<!-- ===== concepts.md ===== -->

# nano-ui Concepts (for AI agents)

Read this before any component doc. Every component doc references these
patterns instead of re-explaining them.

## What nano-ui is

`@kizmann/nano-ui` (npm) is a Vue 3 component library, version `3.0.0`,
optimized for desktop applications with drag-and-drop. It depends only on
`@kizmann/pico-js` (`^2.1.4`, a regular `dependency`, not a peer dependency).
There is **no `moment` dependency** in this version — date/time handling goes
through `@kizmann/pico-js`'s `Now`/`Locale` helpers (see
`src/datetime/js/helper/NDateHelper.ts`). If you find documentation elsewhere
claiming a `moment` peer dependency, treat it as stale.

## The Controller / Data / View pattern

Every component is a set of (usually) four files under
`src/<group>/js/<component-name>/`:

| File | Class | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `N<Comp>.ts` | — (Vue SFC-less component) | `defineComponent()` call: declares `name`, `props`, `emits`, and a `setup()` that wires the other three together. This is the file to read for the public prop/emit contract. |
| `N<Comp>Controller.ts` | extends `ProtoController` | Owns all reactive state, computed-like getters, event handlers, and lifecycle logic that would otherwise live inline in `setup()`. |
| `N<Comp>Data.ts` | extends `ProtoData` | A thin getter/setter facade over the controller's props/state (`this.scope.get(key)` / `this.scope.set(key, value)`). Components read/write through `this.data.foo`, not `this.props.foo` directly. |
| `N<Comp>View.ts` | extends `ProtoView` | The render function (`default()`), plus per-part render helpers (`this.div('part-name', [...])` etc.) building the BEM DOM tree. No reactive logic lives here. |

`N<Comp>.ts`'s `setup(props, context)` always follows this exact shape:

```ts
setup(props, context) {
    let ncx = new N<Comp>Controller(props, context);
    ncx.dispose(() => { ncx = null; });
    return ncx.render();
}
```

`ncx.render()` (defined on `ProtoController`, `src/root/js/proto/ProtoController.ts`)
returns `() => this.view.default()` — i.e. the actual Vue render function.
`ncx.dispose(fn)` registers `fn` to run ~2s after `onUnmounted` (via
`Run.delay`, not immediately) for cleanup.

Some components use a small variation: `GroupController`
(`src/root/js/controller/GroupController.ts`, extends `ProtoController`) adds
`append(child)`/`remove(child)`/`watchChilds(cb)` and a reactive `childs` list —
used by parent components that track child instances registered via
`inject`/`provide` (e.g. group/collection components). Some components also
split into multiple controller variants for different behavior modes (e.g.
`NCheckboxControllerGlobal.ts` / `NCheckboxControllerSingle.ts` — confirm which
applies per usage in that component's own doc).

## `ProtoController` — the shared runtime API

`src/root/js/proto/ProtoController.ts`. Key methods every Controller
subclass inherits (not exhaustive — read the file for full API):

- `get(key, fallback?)` / `set(key, value)` — read/write a reactive value.
  Values not explicitly created via `makeData`/`cloneProp`/`linkProp` fall
  back to reading the prop of the same name (`prop(key, fallback)`).
- `update(key, value)` — `set()` + emits `update:${key}` with the new value.
  This is the standard v-model write path.
- `prop(key, fallback?)` — read a raw prop (unwraps refs).
- `cloneProp(key, options?)` — creates a local reactive copy of a prop that
  stays in sync via a `watch()` (one-way, prop → local).
- `linkProp(key, source?, freeze?)` — creates a `computed()` alias to another
  reactive source (defaults to `this.props`); can point at another
  controller's `.vals` via `source.ncx.vals`.
- `makeData(key, value?)` — creates a plain local `ref()`, independent of any
  prop.
- `compData(key, cb)` — a `computed()` stored in `vals`.
  `watchProp` / `watchData` — watch a prop or a `vals` entry.
- `emit(event, ...args)` — thin wrapper over `context.emit`.
  `pass(keys)` — exposes bound methods onto the instance's public `ctx`
  (what a parent gets via a template ref).
- `injectRef(key, fallback?)` — wraps Vue's `inject`; used by e.g.
  `NFormItem` context injection (`injectRef(['form-item', 'NFormItem'])` runs
  automatically in `ProtoController.setup()` for every component).
- `ncx(key)` — resolves the child component's own Controller instance from a
  template ref registered via `makeRef(key)` (relies on the render-time
  `instance.ncx` back-reference set in `setup()`).
- `dom(key)` / `rel(key)` — resolve a template ref to a DOM element / raw ref.
- `onSignal(event, cb)` / `offSignal(uid)` / `fireSignal(event, ...args)` —
  a global pub/sub bus (backed by pico-js's `Signal`), used for cross-component
  communication that doesn't fit parent/child props (e.g. `Notify`/`Alert`/
  `Confirm`, popover/modal stacking).
- `applyClear()` — resets `modelValue` to the component's `clearValue` prop
  and emits `update:modelValue` — this is what the built-in "clear" (×) button
  calls.
- `attrs` — getter for `context.attrs` (fall-through attributes).

**`superDisabled`** (`ProtoData`, `src/root/js/proto/ProtoData.ts`): a
component is treated as disabled if its own `disabled` prop is true, OR if it
is registered inside an `NFormItem` whose bound model value is falsy/absent in
a specific way — read `ProtoData.superDisabled` before assuming a component's
effective disabled state is just its own `disabled` prop.

## `ProtoData` — the shared data facade

`src/root/js/proto/ProtoData.ts`, `extends ProtoExtend([BaseData, IconData])`.
Provides:

- `classRoot(merge?)` — builds the component's root BEM class list:
  the base BEM class, then conditionally `n-theme-{theme}`, `n-size-{size}`,
  `n-type-{type}`, `n-color-{$color}` (color resolved through
  `Styler.wheel()`), `n-load`, `n-disabled` (from `superDisabled`),
  `n-clearable`, `n-icon-{iconPosition}`.
- `classPart(part, merge?)` — builds a `{bem}__{part}` class for a DOM part.
- Every subclass additionally gets `BaseData`'s getters (`load`, `disabled`,
  `size`, `type`, `color`, `$color`, `theme`, `clearable`, `clearValue`) and
  `IconData`'s getters (`icon`, `iconPosition`, `iconDisabled`) for free —
  these back the shared prop mixins below.

## `ProtoView` — the shared render helpers

`src/root/js/proto/ProtoView.ts`. Every View subclass gets:

- `default()` — override point, the component's actual render tree.
- `slot(key = 'default', ...args)` — renders a named slot if present, else
  `null`.
- `icon(props)` — renders an `<i class="n-icon {icon}">`. Accepts either a
  bare icon string or `{ icon, class, ...attrs }`. **This is the exact
  mechanism the `icon` prop is applied through** — see `ai-docs/icons.md`.
- `comp(el, props?, slot?)` — resolves and renders a globally-registered
  component by tag name (`resolveComponent`), used for the table/info cell
  and filter type registries (`NTableCells`, `NInfoCells`, `NTableFilters`,
  etc. — see each relevant component doc).
- `div(props, slot?, type?)` — renders a BEM-classed element; `props` can be a
  bare string (treated as the `name` for `classPart`) or a full props object.
- `clear(value?)` — renders the built-in clear (×) button when
  `clearable` is true and `value` is non-empty; wired to `applyClear()`.
- `angle()` — renders the built-in dropdown-angle icon.
- `empty(options?)` — renders `<n-empty-icon>` with `emptyText`/`emptyProps`.

## Shared prop mixins (`Props`)

`src/root/index.ts` re-exports every mixin under a single `Props` object:
`Props = { ...BaseProps, ...IconProps, ...AlignProps, ...PositionProps, ...TextProps, ...OptionProps, ...DragProps }`.
Components spread named groups from it, e.g. `...Props.Size, ...Props.Icon`,
instead of redeclaring common props. Full contents (source files under
`src/root/js/prop/`):

**`BaseProps.ts`**

| Export | Prop(s) | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Load` | `load` | `Boolean` | `false` |
| `Disabled` | `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` |
| `Size` | `size` | `String` | `null` |
| `Type` | `type` | `String` | `null` |
| `Color` | `color` | `[String, Number]` | `null` |
| `Clearable` | `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` |
| `ClearValue` | `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` |
| `ThemeNone` | `theme` | `String` | `null` |
| `ThemeDark` | `theme` | `String` | `'dark'` |
| `EmptyPropsInline` | `emptyProps` | `Object` | `{ inline: true }` |
| `EmptyPropsStacked` | `emptyProps` | `Object` | `{ inline: false }` |

`size` and `type` are **not closed enums** — see "Type and Size are open
strings" below.

**`IconProps.ts`**

| Export | Prop(s) | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `icon` | `String` | `''` |
| `IconDisabled` | `iconDisabled` | `Boolean` | `false` |
| `IconPositionBefore` | `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before','after']` | `'before'` |
| `IconPositionAfter` | `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before','after']` | `'after'` |

**`AlignProps.ts`**

| Export | Prop(s) | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AlignHorizontal` | `align` | `String`, validated in `['horizontal','vertical']` | `'horizontal'` |
| `AlignVertical` | `align` | `String`, validated in `['horizontal','vertical']` | `'vertical'` |
| `AlignLeft` | `align` | `String`, validated in `['left','center','right']` | `'left'` |
| `AlignRight` | `align` | `String`, validated in `['left','center','right']` | `'left'` (yes — `AlignRight`'s default is `'left'` in source; not a typo you should "fix") |

**`PositionProps.ts`**

| Export | Prop(s) | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PositionBottomStart` | `position` | `String`, validated against the 12-value popover position set | `'bottom-start'` |
| `PositionBottomCenter` | `position` | same popover set | `'bottom-center'` |
| `PositionDrawer` | `position` | `String`, validated in `['top','bottom','left','right']` | `'right'` |
| `PositionModal` | `position` | same drawer set (`['top','bottom','left','right']`) | `'right'` |

Popover position full set (`PopoverPosition` in `src/root/js/data/PositionData.ts`):
`top-start, top-center, top-end, bottom-start, bottom-center, bottom-end, left-start, left-center, left-end, right-start, right-center, right-end`.

**`TextProps.ts`** — all `String`, all default via `Locale.trans(...)`
(pico-js i18n) so the literal default is a translation lookup, not a fixed
English string:

| Export | Prop | Translation key |
|---|---|---|
| `UndefinedText` | `undefinedText` | `'Undefined'` |
| `EmptyText` | `emptyText` | `'No items'` |
| `TrueText` | `trueText` | `'Yes'` |
| `FalseText` | `falseText` | `'No'` |

**`OptionProps.ts`** — `OptionsObject`: `options` (`Object`, default `{}`),
`optionsValue` (`String`, default `'$index'`), `optionsLabel` (`String`,
default `'$value'`). Always documented together — see "Options resolution"
below. Note the prop is typed `Object` but an Array also works (see below).

**`DragProps.ts`** — `Draglist`, a large mixin (`items`, `current`,
`selected`, `expanded`, `cascade`, `group`, `allowGroups`, `safezone`,
`allowCurrent`, `renderHandle`, `renderExpand`, `renderSelect`, `allowSelect`,
`allowDrag`, `allowDrop`, `transformDrop`, `insertNode`, `removeNode`,
`uniqueProp`, `childProp`, `itemSkip`, `rootSkip` — full defaults in
`src/root/js/prop/DragProps.ts`). Used by `NDraglist`/`NDropzone` — document
exact defaults in `components/draglist.md` rather than repeating here.

## Shared data classes

`src/root/js/data/*.ts` — plain getter/setter classes (`get x() { return
this.scope.get('x') }`) that a component's `N<Comp>Data` class extends
alongside `ProtoData`, mirroring the prop mixin it uses (e.g. a component
using `Props.OptionsObject` extends/mixes in `OptionData` to get `.options`/
`.optionsValue`/`.optionsLabel` getters). `BaseData` and `IconData` are always
present because `ProtoData` itself extends `ProtoExtend([BaseData, IconData])`.

## `ProtoExtend` — the multi-inheritance shim

`src/root/js/proto/ProtoExtend.ts`: `ProtoExtend([A, B, ...])` returns a class
whose prototype has every listed class's prototype merged in (via
`Mix.extend`), constructed as the first class in the list. This is how a
`Data` class can extend `ProtoData` **and** behave as if it also extends e.g.
`AlignData`/`OptionData` — Vue/TS components in this codebase use this instead
of real multiple inheritance. If a component's `Data` class shows
`extends ProtoExtend([ProtoData, OptionData])`-style code, treat it as having
every method/getter from both.

## Type and Size are open strings, not closed enums

`Props.Type` (`type`) and `Props.Size` (`size`) are both declared as plain
`String` with `default: null` — there is no runtime enum/union restricting
values. Confirmed **built-in, styled** values:

- `type`: `primary`, `secondary`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `success`
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`

Any other string is structurally accepted (it becomes `n-type-{value}` /
`n-size-{value}` via `ProtoData.classRoot()`) but has **no default CSS** unless
the consuming app defines it. Document these as `String` with the built-ins
listed as "known defaults," never as a closed union.

## Options resolution (`options` / `optionsValue` / `optionsLabel`)

Any component with an `options` prop always has `optionsValue` and
`optionsLabel` alongside it (fixed trio from `Props.OptionsObject`,
`src/root/js/prop/OptionProps.ts`) plus matching getters from `OptionData`
(`src/root/js/data/OptionData.ts`). Resolution logic lives in
`OptionHelper.getList`/`getFlat` (`src/root/js/helper/OptionHelper.ts`):

1. `options` may be an **Array** or a plain **Object**.
2. `OptionHelper.getList()` walks it and produces `{ $index, $value }` pairs:
   - `$index` = the array position (number) or object key (string) — the
     entry's own key in the `options` structure, never something read out of
     the item itself.
   - `$value` = the entry's own value (the whole item, e.g. the full object).
3. `OptionHelper.getFlat()` then resolves `label`/`value` for each entry via
   `Obj.get(item, optionsLabel)` / `Obj.get(item, optionsValue)`, where `item`
   is the `{ $index, $value }` pair — so an expression like `optionsLabel`
   dots into that pair, e.g. `'$value.foo'` to reach `item.$value.foo`.

Examples:

```js
// options: [{ foo: 'bar' }]
// $index -> 0, $value -> { foo: 'bar' }
// optionsLabel: '$value.foo'  =>  'bar'

// options: { foo1: { foo: 'bar' } }
// $index -> 'foo1', $value -> { foo: 'bar' }
// optionsLabel: '$value.foo'  =>  'bar'
```

Defaults (`optionsValue: '$index'`, `optionsLabel: '$value'`) mean: with no
overrides, the raw index/key is used as the value, and the raw item is used
as the label. <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether `$index` alone (without dotting into
it) is valid as a full optionsLabel/optionsValue expression beyond the
literal default string — confirmed only that the default is exactly `$index`
and `$value` as whole-string values; dotted access (`$value.foo`) is
confirmed via `Obj.get`. -->

## v-model conventions

Standard Vue convention throughout: prop `modelValue`, event
`update:modelValue`, driven by `ProtoController.update('modelValue', value)`.
Confirmed directly for `NInput`, `NSwitch`, `NSelect`, `NModal`, `NTabs`,
`NTransfer`, `NCheckbox` — plain `v-model` works, there are no named-model
variants (`v-model:visible` etc.) on any of these, even where you might
expect one (`NModal`'s open state is a plain boolean `v-model`; `NTabs`'
active tab is a plain string `v-model`, default `'default'`).

`modelValue`'s declared **type varies per component** — always check that
component's own prop table:

| Component | `modelValue` type |
|---|---|
| `NInput` | `[String, Number]` |
| `NSwitch` | `[Number, Boolean, String, Object]` |
| `NTransfer` | `[Array, Object]` |
| `NSelect` | untyped, `default: null` |

**`NCascader` is the one exception found so far**: it emits both
`update:modelValue` and `update:splitValue` — a second bindable value
alongside the main one. See `ai-docs/components/cascader.md` for what each
represents; wiring only `v-model` on `NCascader` misses required state.

Do not assume plain `modelValue`/`update:modelValue` is universal across
every one of the 40+ components without checking — treat it as the strong
default, not a guarantee.

## Icons and app-level config

See `ai-docs/icons.md` and `ai-docs/config.md` — these are cross-cutting
enough to warrant their own files rather than living here.

(2026-08-20) — see `ai-docs/llms.txt` for the full provenance note. They are
**not** derived from `docs/` or any other pre-existing Markdown in this repo;

`ai-docs/` was written directly from `src/`.

<!-- ===== setup.md ===== -->

# Setup

## Install

```bash
npm install @kizmann/nano-ui
# or
yarn add @kizmann/nano-ui
```

Runtime dependency: `@kizmann/pico-js` (`^2.1.4`, listed under
`dependencies` in `package.json` — not `peerDependencies`, npm/yarn will
install it automatically). **There is no `moment` dependency in this
version** (`3.0.0`) — date/time logic uses pico-js's own `Now`/`Locale`
helpers. If other documentation claims a `moment` peer dependency, it's
describing an older/different version than what's in this repo.

## Module usage (ES modules)

```js
import { Install } from "@kizmann/nano-ui";
app.use(Install);
```

```scss
@import "@kizmann/nano-ui/nano/index.scss";
```

`Install`'s second/third parameters (`Icons`, `Settings`) are accepted but
currently inert — see `ai-docs/config.md`. Just call `app.use(Install)` with
no arguments.

## Global `<script>` usage

```html
<script src="//unpkg.com/@kizmann/nano-ui@latest/dist/nano-ui.browser.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="//unpkg.com/@kizmann/nano-ui@latest/dist/nano-ui.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="//unpkg.com/@kizmann/nano-ui@latest/dist/themes/default.css">
```

```js
App.use(nano.Install);
```

Global usage also depends on `@kizmann/pico-js` being loaded first as
`globalThis.pi` — `Install()` early-returns with a console error
(`'pico-js is not available.'`) if `globalThis.pi` is undefined.

## Theme CSS

Two shipped themes under `themes/`: `default` and `webservy`. Each exposes a
single entry stylesheet (`themes/<name>/index.scss`, or the built
`dist/themes/<name>.css`) that `@forward`s every component's theme partial.
Pick one theme's CSS to load — see `ai-docs/theming.md` for how to override
individual CSS custom properties instead of swapping the whole theme.

## ES5/6 precompile (webpack alias workaround)

Only needed if your build does **not** already run the babel plugins in this
repo's own `babel.config.cjs` (class properties, JSX, TS preset, etc. — the
library's source uses modern/TS syntax and is shipped as source under
`src/` as well as pre-built under `dist/`). If your bundler tries to compile
`node_modules/@kizmann/nano-ui/src/...` directly and fails, alias the import
to the pre-built ESM bundle instead:

```js
// webpack.config.js
module.exports = {
    resolve: {
        alias: {
            '@kizmann/nano-ui': '@kizmann/nano-ui/dist/nano-ui.esm.js'
        }
    }
}
```

```js
// webpack.mix.js
mix.webpackConfig({
    resolve: {
        alias: {
            '@kizmann/nano-ui': '@kizmann/nano-ui/dist/nano-ui.esm.js'
        }
    }
});
```

With that alias in place, also point VS Code's autocomplete at the same
target via `jsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "@kizmann/nano-ui": ["node_modules/@kizmann/nano-ui/src/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Demo

A full live demo covering most components: `demos/overview.html` (also
mirrored at https://vankizmann.github.io/nano-ui/demos/overview.html). This
is the source used throughout `ai-docs/components/*.md` for realistic usage
examples.

<!-- ===== config.md ===== -->

# Config

There are two unrelated things named "config" in this codebase — do not
conflate them.

## 1. `App.use(Install, ...)` options — currently inert

`Install` (`src/index.esm.ts`) has this signature:

```ts
export function Install(App, Icons = {}, Settings = {})
```

Confirmed by reading the full function body: **`Icons` and `Settings` are
accepted but never read anywhere inside `Install`, nor passed on to anything
else.** All `Install` actually does is:

- attach `ctor`/`cmer`/`cslo` legacy helpers to `App.config.globalProperties`,
- attach `Notify`/`Alert`/`Confirm`/`trans`/`choice` globals if not already
  present on `App.config.globalProperties` (falling back to `globalThis.*`),
- call every component group's install function (`NanoImports.forEach(m => m(App))`).

**Do not document `App.use(Install, { ...someConfig })` as configuring
locale, default size, default type, z-index, icon prefixes, or anything else
— none of that is implemented.** If you need per-component defaults, set
props explicitly (or via a wrapper component) rather than expecting a global
config object to do it. The parameter exists only for legacy call-site
compatibility (some older integration presumably used to pass something
here); passing anything today has zero observable effect.

If a future version of this library changes `Install`'s body to actually
consume these parameters, this note will be wrong — re-check
`src/index.esm.ts`'s `Install` function body directly if behavior here seems
to contradict what you observe.

## 2. `src/config/` — the `NConfig` component

Unrelated to the above. `src/config/` registers one real Vue component,
`NConfig` (`App.component('NConfig', NConfig)`, confirmed in
`src/config/index.ts`) — see `ai-docs/components/config.md` for its full
prop/usage contract. In short: `<n-config>` is a JSON/object-driven dynamic
render component — you pass it a `config` prop describing a tree of
components/props/events/slots (with `$scope`/`$model`/`$extra`/`$global`
template-variable resolution and `vIf`/`vAwait`/`vShow` conditionals), and it
renders that tree via `h()`. It is not related to installation-time
configuration at all.


---

<!-- ===== icons.md ===== -->

# Icons

See `ai-docs/concepts.md` first for the shared `Props.Icon` mixin and
`ProtoView.icon()`.

## Default: pass a full class string, as-is

The `icon` prop (`Props.Icon`, `src/root/js/prop/IconProps.ts`) is a plain
`String` (`default: ''`). It is **not** resolved through any nano-ui prefix
or name-lookup logic. Whatever string you pass is applied almost verbatim.

Confirmed in `ProtoView.icon()` (`src/root/js/proto/ProtoView.ts`):

```ts
icon(props = undefined) {
    if (!Mix.isObj(props)) props = { icon: props };
    if (!props.icon) return null;
    const [icon, classList] = [Obj.pluck(props, 'icon', ''), Obj.pluck(props, 'class', [])];
    props.class = [`n-icon ${icon}`, ...classList].join(' ');
    return h('i', props);
}
```

So `icon="fa fa-ghost"` renders `<i class="n-icon fa fa-ghost">`. This is
exactly the pattern used in `demos/overview.html`:

```html
<n-message type="primary" icon="fa fa-ghost" title="With title and icon">...</n-message>
<n-tag type="primary" icon="fa fa-ghost">...</n-tag>
```

**Default icon set is Font Awesome** — pass the full FA class string for
whichever FA version/style your app loads (e.g. `fa fa-ghost`,
`fa-solid fa-ghost`, depending on the FA version). There is no nano-ui-side
icon name registry to document — for the actual set of available icon names
and their class syntax, use Font Awesome's own icon reference, not this
library's docs.

There is no separate "icon name" vs. "prefix" concept in nano-ui: don't
document `icon="ghost"` as valid, and don't invent a prefix-resolution
mechanism — none exists for the public `icon` prop.

## Overriding the default icon set: `Styler`

nano-ui's *own internal* chrome (the clear/× button, the dropdown angle, the
search icon inside inputs, calendar/clock icons in date/time pickers, the
default icons used by `Alert`/`Confirm`/`Notify`, etc.) is **not** hardcoded
Font Awesome markup — it's resolved through `Styler.icon()`
(`src/root/js/module/Styler.ts`), which is a static, mutable registry:

```ts
static icons = {
    default: { locate, revert, prev, 'prev-first', next, 'next-last', check,
               'angle-left', 'angle-right', 'angle-up', 'angle-down',
               search, times, minus, clock, calendar, duration },
    preview: { default, video },
    alert: { default, info, success, warning, danger },
    confirm: { /* same as alert */ },
    notify:  { /* same as alert */ },
};

static icon(type, group = 'default', fallback = 'default') {
    if (type == null) type = fallback;
    if (Obj.has(this.icons, [group, type])) return Obj.get(this.icons, [group, type]);
    return Obj.get(this.icons, [group, fallback]);
}
```

Every value in `Styler.icons` is currently a Font Awesome class string (e.g.
`'fa fa-angle-down'`). To switch nano-ui's *internal* iconography away from
Font Awesome (a custom sprite set, Material Icons, etc.), mutate this
registry before/after install:

```js
import { Styler } from '@kizmann/nano-ui'; // exported from src/root/index.ts

Styler.icons.default['angle-down'] = 'my-icons my-icons-chevron-down';
Styler.icons.default['times']      = 'my-icons my-icons-close';
// ...or replace whole groups: Styler.icons.default = { ...myIconMap };
```

`Styler` is also reachable at runtime as `globalThis.NStyler` (set at the
bottom of `src/root/js/module/Styler.ts` if not already defined) — useful in
a plain `<script>` global-usage setup with no module imports available.

There is no separate "register a resolver function" API — `Styler.icon()`
itself is the resolver, and `Styler.icons` is a plain object you overwrite by
key. If you need fully custom resolution logic (not just swapping class
strings), monkey-patch `Styler.icon` itself; there's no built-in hook for
that beyond replacing the static method.

**Important distinction:** this override only changes icons nano-ui renders
*itself* (its internal chrome). It has no effect on values you pass to the
public `icon` prop on `NButton`, `NTag`, `NMessage`, etc. — those are always
applied as-is per the "Default" section above, regardless of `Styler` state.


---

<!-- ===== theming.md ===== -->

# Theming

## Two layers: CSS custom properties, and per-component class props

nano-ui's visual states are driven by **both** mechanisms — it is not
purely one or the other:

1. **CSS custom properties** (`--n-color-*`, `--n-size-*`) supply the actual
   color/size *values*. These are generated once per theme and don't change
   per-component-instance; you override them to reskin the whole library.
2. **Component `type`/`size`/`theme`/`color` props** select *which* CSS class
   (and therefore which custom-property lookup) applies to a given instance —
   e.g. `type="danger"` on any component adds `n-type-danger`, which some
   component's CSS rule then reads `color('danger')` for. Some visual states
   (e.g. `link`/`glass`/`round`/`square` on `NButton`) exist ONLY as boolean
   props with dedicated CSS classes — there is no CSS-variable equivalent for
   "make this button a link-style button."

So: color/size *palettes* are CSS-variable-based and themeable without
touching component code; which palette entry/appearance a specific instance
uses is prop-based and cannot be changed via CSS alone.

## Shipped themes

Two full themes under `themes/`: `default` and `webservy`. Each theme
directory has one `index.scss` that `@forward`s every component's own
`<component>/index` partial (button, input, select, table, ... — one
partial per component group, mirroring `src/`), plus a `root/` directory
holding the actual variable definitions:

```
themes/default/
  index.scss          # forwards every component partial
  root/
    helpers.scss       # css-colors / css-sizes / css-remaps mixins + color()/size() SCSS functions
    vars/
      colors-light.scss        # default light palette
      colors-dark.scss         # dark palette
      colors-light-bluish.scss # alternate light palette
      colors-dark-bluish.scss  # alternate dark palette
      sizes-default.scss       # xs/sm/md/lg/xl size maps
  <component>/index.scss  # e.g. button/, input/, table/, ... — one per group
```

Load a whole theme by including its built CSS (`dist/themes/default.css` or
`dist/themes/webservy.css`), or `@use`/`@import` its `index.scss` from your
own SCSS build.

## The `color()` / `size()` SCSS helpers

`themes/default/root/helpers.scss` defines:

```scss
@function color($color, $opacity: 1) {
  @return rgba(var(--n-color-#{$color}), #{$opacity});
}
@function size($size, $context: '$') {
  @return <substitutes var(--n-size-#{$size}) into $context>;
}
```

Every component's own theme partial calls these, e.g.
`background: color('primary')`, `padding: size('md.pad')`. This is the
actual override surface: **redefine the underlying `--n-color-*`/`--n-size-*`
custom property**, and every component partial that reads it via `color()`/
`size()` picks up the new value automatically — no need to override each
component's CSS individually.

## Color variables

Generated via the `css-colors` mixin from each `colors-*.scss` palette file
(`$color-primary`, `$color-secondary`, `$color-success`, `$color-warning`,
`$color-danger`, `$color-info`, `$color-neutral`, a `$color-gray-05`..
`$color-gray-95` ramp, plus semantic ones like `$color-text`,
`$color-background`, `$color-form`, and a `$color-tag-0`..`$color-tag-N`
wheel used by the `color`/`$color` prop + `Styler.wheel()` for arbitrary
per-item coloring). Each becomes `--n-color-{name}: R, G, B` (channel
components, not a full `rgb()` string — that's why `color()` wraps it in
`rgba(var(--n-color-x), opacity)`), so overriding one is:

```css
:root {
  --n-color-primary: 43, 112, 227; /* R, G, B channels, comma-separated */
}
```

To override for a specific theme variant only, scope it under that theme's
root class/selector instead of bare `:root` (check the built CSS for the
exact selector the theme wraps its `:root` overrides in — `-light`/`-dark`/
`-light-bluish`/`-dark-bluish` variants are all generated from the same
mixin with different `$prefix` values and later remapped onto the plain
`--n-color-*` names via `css-remaps`).

## Size variables

Generated via `css-sizes` from `sizes-default.scss`'s five maps (`$size-xs`,
`$size-sm`, `$size-md`, `$size-lg`, `$size-xl` — matching exactly the five
built-in `Props.Size` values from `ai-docs/concepts.md`). Each map has keys
like `hgt`, `hgt-inline`, `pad`, `pad-vertical`, `fnt`, `fnt-icon`,
`fnt-label`, `fnt-inline`, `rad`, `rad-inline`, `rad-window`, `rad-circle` —
becoming `--n-size-{sizeName}-{key}`, e.g. `--n-size-md-hgt: 32px`. A
`.n-size-{name}` class selector (emitted by `ProtoData.classRoot()` whenever
a component's `size` prop is set) is what activates the correct size's
lookups for that component instance.

**Custom `size`/`type` values** (per `ai-docs/concepts.md`'s "open string"
rule) get a `n-size-{value}`/`n-type-{value}` class applied structurally, but
there is no generated `--n-size-{value}-*`/`--n-color-{value}` variable set
for them — you must define the CSS for a custom value yourself, following
the same variable-naming convention the built-ins use, for existing
component partials to pick it up "for free."

## Practical overrides

- **Reskin one color globally**: override `--n-color-primary` (and friends)
  at `:root` — every component using `type="primary"` shifts together.
- **Add a new `type`/`size` value**: define `--n-color-{name}` /
  `--n-size-{name}-*` variables following the existing naming convention,
  then pass `type="{name}"` / `size="{name}"` — no source changes needed
  since these props are open strings.
- **Swap themes entirely**: load `webservy`'s CSS instead of `default`'s (see
  `demos/overview.html`'s `<n-select>`-driven theme switcher, which swaps the
  `<link id="theme">` stylesheet `href` — theme switching is just swapping
  which compiled CSS file is loaded, not a runtime API call).
- **Icon changes**: not a CSS concern — see `ai-docs/icons.md` (`Styler.icons`).

<!-- ===== patterns.md ===== -->

# Patterns

Realistic multi-component compositions, based on `demos/` usage and the
component pairings confirmed while writing `ai-docs/components/*.md`. Read
`ai-docs/concepts.md` first.

## 1. A validated form

`NForm` + `NFormItem` (`prop` matching a key in the bound `form` object) +
string-array `rules`. Validation is fully automatic (`NFormController`
deep-watches the `form` prop and recomputes on every mutation) — there is
**no** exposed `validate()`/`submit()` method to call manually (confirmed:
`NForm.ts`'s `setup()` never calls `ncx.pass(...)`). Read the computed
error/valid state back out via `NFormItem`'s own state instead of expecting a
programmatic gate.

```vue
<n-form :form="user">
    <n-form-item label="Email" prop="email" :rules="['required', 'email']">
        <n-input v-model="user.email" />
    </n-form-item>
    <n-form-item label="Confirm password" prop="passwordConfirm"
                 :rules="['required', 'same:password']">
        <n-input v-model="user.passwordConfirm" type="password" />
    </n-form-item>
    <n-button type="primary" @click="save(user)">Save</n-button>
</n-form>
```

See `ai-docs/components/form.md` for the full validation-rule reference
(`required`, `required_if:key`, `required_unless:key`, `same:key`,
`diffrent:key` — note the misspelling is intentional, matches the actual
module filename — `value:val`, `email`, `min:n`, `max:n`, `minlength:n`,
`maxlength:n`).

## 2. A draggable/reorderable tree

`NDraglist` with a nested `items` tree (`uniqueProp: 'id'`,
`childProp: 'children'` by default — see `ai-docs/components/draglist.md`
for the exact node shape). Handle `update:items` to persist the reordered
tree, and `move` if you need the specific drop target/mode for a server call.

```vue
<n-draglist
    :items="tree"
    @update:items="tree = $event"
    @move="onMove"
    v-slot="{ item, depth }"
>
    <div :style="{ paddingLeft: depth * 16 + 'px' }">{{ item.label }}</div>
</n-draglist>
```

Cross-container drag needs an `NDropzone` as the second zone; see
`ai-docs/components/dropzone.md` for its `mode` prop (controls copy vs. move
semantics on the source side).

## 3. A modal-driven CRUD flow

`NModal` (plain boolean `v-model`, no `title` prop — build your own header
markup in the `header` slot) wrapping an `NForm`, triggered from an
`NTable` row action:

```vue
<n-table :items="rows" height="400px" :current="current" @update:current="current = $event">
    <n-table-column prop="name" label="Name" />
    <n-table-column prop="active" label="Active" type="boolean" />
    <n-table-column label="" v-slot="{ item }">
        <n-button size="xs" @click="editing = { ...item }; open = true">Edit</n-button>
    </n-table-column>
</n-table>
<n-paginator :total="total" v-model:page="page" />

<n-modal v-model="open" :listen="false">
    <template #header>Edit item</template>
    <n-form :form="editing">
        <n-form-item label="Name" prop="name" :rules="['required']">
            <n-input v-model="editing.name" />
        </n-form-item>
    </n-form>
    <template #footer>
        <n-button @click="open = false">Cancel</n-button>
        <n-button type="primary" @click="save(editing); open = false">Save</n-button>
    </template>
</n-modal>
```

Remember: `NTable` requires an explicit height (its virtual scroller reads
`el.clientHeight`), `NPaginator` is never nested inside `NTable`, and sort/
filter state on `NTable` is presentational only — you must re-fetch/re-derive
`items` yourself in response to its `sort`/`update:filter` events.

## 4. Hierarchical / bulk selection

Two different tools depending on the shape of the choice:

- **`NCascader`** for a single drill-down path through a tree (region →
  city, category → subcategory). Bind `v-model` for the full path array, or
  `v-model:split-value` if you only need to persist the leaf id and let the
  component reconstruct the path from `options` on load (see
  `ai-docs/components/cascader.md`).
- **`NTransfer`** for picking an arbitrary subset out of a flat list (its own
  `labelProp`/`uniqueProp` props, NOT the `optionsValue`/`optionsLabel` trick
  — see `ai-docs/components/transfer.md`).

```vue
<n-cascader v-model="form.categoryPath" v-model:split-value="form.categoryId" :options="categoryTree" />
<n-transfer v-model="form.selectedUsers" :options="allUsers" label-prop="name" unique-prop="id" />
```

## 5. A read-only detail panel reusing table cell types

`NInfo` + `NInfoColumn` reuse `NTable`'s cell-type renderers (`string`,
`boolean`, `datetime`, `image`, `option` — note `select`/`matrix` are NOT
available here, unlike on `NTableColumn`) to render a key-value summary for
one record, typically the `current` row of a table:

```vue
<n-table :items="rows" height="300px" v-model:current="current" />
<n-info :item="current">
    <n-info-column label="Name" prop="name" />
    <n-info-column label="Active" prop="active" type="boolean" />
    <n-info-column label="Created" prop="createdAt" type="datetime" />
</n-info>
```


---

<!-- ===== components/button-group.md ===== -->

# NButtonGroup

A generic visual-grouping wrapper that fuses its children into one connected
row (flush borders, shared corner radius) — use it whenever several controls
(not only buttons) should read as a single control cluster.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **button** group index
(`src/button/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NButtonGroup', NButtonGroup)`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` | Adds `n-load` class to the wrapper `<div>` only. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. Adds `n-size-{size}` to the wrapper only. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`. Adds `n-type-{type}` to the wrapper only. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` | Adds `n-disabled` to the wrapper only (via `superDisabled`). See Gotchas — this does **not** disable children. |

## Events

None — `NButtonGroup.ts` declares no `emits` array, and `NButtonGroupController` never calls `scope.emit(...)`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The controls to group together. |

## Exposed methods

None — `NButtonGroupController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-button-group>
    <n-button>Previous</n-button>
    <n-button>Next</n-button>
</n-button-group>
```

## Realistic example

Pulled directly from `demos/overview.html` — a mixed group of an input, a
date picker, a multi-select, and a button all fused into one row:

```vue
<n-button-group>
    <n-input v-model="n_input.value" v-bind="n_input" type="primary"></n-input>
    <n-datepicker v-bind="n_datepicker"></n-datepicker>
    <n-select v-bind="n_select" :multiple="true" type="primary" :options="icons"></n-select>
    <n-button v-bind="n_button" type="primary">Button</n-button>
</n-button-group>
```

## Required composition

None structurally — `NButtonGroupView` renders a plain `<div>` around
whatever is passed to its default slot, with no child-type registration or
validation. Per the confirmed composition contract for this component,
intended children are: `NButton`, `NCascader`, any input (`NInput`,
`NInputNumber`, `NInputFile`, `NTextarea`), and any date/time picker
(`NDatepicker`, `NTimepicker`, `NDatetimepicker`, `NDurationpicker`) — i.e. a
general grouping wrapper, not button-only. This is corroborated by the real
demo usage above (input + datepicker + select + button in one group).

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `disabled`/`size`/`type` set on `NButtonGroup` cascade down to its children — they don't. `NButtonGroupView.default()` only builds a class list for the wrapper `<div>` itself (`data.classList` = `this.classRoot()`); there is no prop-forwarding to slotted children. Each child must set its own `disabled`/`size`/`type` individually, exactly as shown in the demo above (each child repeats `type="primary"` itself).
- Expecting `NButtonGroup` to emit or expose anything for coordinating children (e.g. a shared active/selected state) — it has no `emits`, no exposed methods, and no child-registration mechanism (`GroupController`'s `append`/`remove`/`watchChilds` from concepts.md is **not** used here; `NButtonGroupController` extends the plain `ProtoController`, not `GroupController`). It is purely a visual wrapper.

## Gotchas

- The name suggests a button-only container, and `NButtonGroupView.ts`'s render logic is fully generic (`h('div', props, [this.slot('default')])`) with zero child-type checks — nothing in the JS restricts membership at all. The one genuinely button-specific rule lives in CSS (`src/button/css/button-group.scss`): `.n-button-group > .n-button { z-index: 5; }` bumps buttons above other children on hover/focus stacking. Everything else in that stylesheet (flex row layout, border-radius trimming on first/last child, `-1px` margin to collapse borders) is written generically against `> *`, so it applies uniformly to any child type — consistent with, not contradicting, the confirmed "general grouping wrapper" rule.
- `theme`, `color`, `clearable`, and `icon` are not declared props on `NButtonGroup` (no matching `Props.*` mixin is spread in), so despite `BaseData`/`IconData` getters existing on the class, passing those attributes has no reactive effect.

## Related components

- `NButton` — the most common child; see `ai-docs/components/button.md`.
- `NInput`, `NInputNumber`, `NInputFile`, `NTextarea` — input-family children.
- `NDatepicker`, `NTimepicker`, `NDatetimepicker`, `NDurationpicker` — date/time-picker children.
- `NCascader` — also a supported child (note its non-standard v-model, see concepts.md).


---

<!-- ===== components/button.md ===== -->

# NButton

A clickable action element (native `<button>` by default) with icon, loading,
and style-modifier support; reach for it for any standalone user action
(submit, trigger, link-styled action) — use `NButtonGroup` only when you need
several controls visually fused into one connected row.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **button** group index
(`src/button/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NButton', NButton)`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` | Adds `n-load` root class (no built-in spinner/pointer-lock in this component — purely a CSS hook). |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl` (see concepts.md). Adds `n-size-{size}`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`. Adds `n-type-{type}`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` | Combined with `superDisabled` (see concepts.md) to set the native `disabled` DOM attribute. |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` | Icon class rendered via `ProtoView.icon()`; see `ai-docs/icons.md`. |
| `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before', 'after']` | `'before'` | `Props.IconPositionBefore` | Whether the icon renders before or after the label. |
| `nativeType` | `String` | `'button'` | local | **Not** the HTML `type` attribute — it is the tag name passed to `h()` as the root element (see Gotchas). |
| `link` | `Boolean` | `false` | local | Adds `n-button--link` modifier class (link-styled button). |
| `glass` | `Boolean` | `false` | local | Adds `n-button--glass` modifier class. |
| `round` | `Boolean` | `false` | local | Adds `n-button--round` modifier class. |
| `square` | `Boolean` | `false` | local | Adds `n-button--square` modifier class **and** suppresses the default-slot content wrapper (see Gotchas). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `click` | the raw `PointerEvent` | Root element's `pointerdown` fires with `e.which === 1` (left button) — bound via `onPointerdown`, not a native `click` listener. |
| `dblclick` | the raw `MouseEvent` | Root element's native `dblclick` fires. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Button label/content. Rendered only if the slot is actually supplied **and** `square` is `false` — when `square` is `true`, the wrapping `<span>` is skipped entirely regardless of slot content. The icon (if any) is rendered outside/alongside this and is unaffected by `square`. |

## Exposed methods

None — `NButtonController` never calls `pass()`, so nothing beyond the standard component instance is exposed on a template ref.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-button>Click me</n-button>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on confirmed usage in `demos/overview.html`:

```vue
<n-button icon="fa fa-paragraph">
    Paragraph
</n-button>

<n-button type="danger" :glass="true" :link="true" size="xs">
    Delete
</n-button>

<n-button type="primary" @click="notify('primary')">
    Notify
</n-button>
```

## Required composition

None — `NButton` is fully standalone. It is commonly placed inside
`NButtonGroup` (see `ai-docs/components/button-group.md`) or a form-item
`action` slot, but neither is required for it to function.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `nativeType` sets the HTML `type` attribute (e.g. `submit`/`reset`) — it doesn't. `NButtonView.default()` passes `data.native` (the `nativeType` prop) as the **tag name** to `h()`; no `type` attribute is ever set on the rendered element. The same pattern is used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `NPreviewView.ts` sets `nativeType: 'a'` to render an anchor tag).
- Assuming `type="link"` is a valid built-in style — it isn't one of the confirmed built-in `type` values (`primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`). The link-styled look is a separate boolean `link` prop (`n-button--link`), not a `type` value. (An older Vue 2 demo, `demos/button/index.html`, uses `type="link"` and an `outline` prop that no longer exists in this source — treat that demo as stale.)
- Assuming plain `@click` on the component reacts to any click — the emit is gated on `pointerdown` with `e.which === 1`, so keyboard-triggered activation (Enter/Space while focused) does not fire nano-ui's `click` event, only real native browser default-button-activation semantics would (via the native `disabled`/form behavior), not this custom emit.
- Expecting slot text to still render when `square` is `true` — `body()` returns `null` in that case; only the icon shows. Pair `square` with `icon` and no meaningful default-slot content.

## Gotchas

- `load`, `disabled`, `size`, `type` all run through the shared `classRoot()` (see concepts.md) even though only `disabled` has any other effect in this component (native `disabled` attribute via `superDisabled`); `load`/`size`/`type` are purely CSS class hooks here.
- `theme`, `color`, and `clearable` are **not** declared props on `NButton` (no `Props.Theme*`/`Props.Color`/`Props.Clearable` mixin is spread in), so passing them has no reactive effect even though `BaseData`'s getters technically exist on the class.
- `demos/button/index.html` is a stale pre-Vue-3 demo (uses Vue 2 global, an `outline` prop, and `size="small"/"default"/"large"` — none of which exist in current source). Prefer `demos/overview.html` usage as ground truth.

## Related components

- `NButtonGroup` — wraps multiple controls (including `NButton`) into one visually connected row.
- `NFormItem` — commonly hosts `NButton` in its `action` slot; also the source of `superDisabled`'s form-context behavior.


---

<!-- ===== components/cascader-panel.md ===== -->

# NCascaderPanel

The cascading tree-list itself (columns of `n-virtualbar` lists, one per
depth) — usable standalone/inline, and also what `NCascader` renders
internally as its popover body.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **cascader** group index
(`src/cascader/index.ts`), which registers both `NCascaderPanel`
(`n-cascader-panel`) and `NCascader` (`n-cascader`) as separate top-level
components in the same call — see cascader.md for the exact snippet.

**Required composition (as given):** `NCascaderPanel` and `NCascader` are
fully independent components despite the shared naming — `NCascaderPanel` is
not required to live inside an `NCascader`. See cascader.md's Gotchas for the
apparent contradiction in the render source (`NCascader` does internally
instantiate an `NCascaderPanel` as its popover content).

`NCascaderPanelController` extends `GroupController`
(`src/root/js/controller/GroupController.ts`), not `NPopoverPanelController`
— unlike `NSelect`/`NCascader`, it renders its own plain root `<div>`
directly (`NCascaderPanelView.default()`), with no popover trigger/display
row of its own. It also does `injectRef(['popover', 'NPopover'])` so that
`updateCascade()` can call `this.ncx('popover')?.superClose()` if it happens
to be rendered inside an `n-popover` (e.g. when embedded by `NCascader`) —
this is a no-op when used standalone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` | Adds `n-load` to the root. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` | Drives `superDisabled`/`n-disabled` class only — not read anywhere else in this component; per-node disabling goes through `disabledProp` instead. |
| `modelValue` | `[Array, Object]` | `null` | Component-local (`NCascaderPanel.ts`) | In practice a `string[]` — the full selected path (one `valueProp` value per depth, root → leaf). |
| `splitValue` | `String` | `null` | Component-local | The single leaf value of the selected path (`Arr.last(modelValue)`) — see cascader.md's Events section for the exact bidirectional-sync semantics, which are identical here (same `NCascaderHelper` functions). |
| `trigger` | `String` | `'hover'` | Component-local | `'hover'`: mouseenter expands a column, click commits the selection. `'click'`: click expands a column, dblclick commits the selection. No runtime validator; any other string disables both expand and commit (see cascader.md Gotchas). |
| `options` | `[Array, Object]` | `() => []` | Component-local | The tree. **Not** `Props.OptionsObject`. See "Options tree shape" below. |
| `labelProp` | `String` | `'label'` | Component-local | Dot-path (`Obj.get`) read on each node for its display label. |
| `valueProp` | `String` | `'value'` | Component-local | **Plain key** (`item[data.valueProp]`, not dot-path) read on each node for its selectable value. |
| `childProp` | `String` | `'children'` | Component-local | Key holding a node's array of child nodes; walked via `Arr.cascadeFind`. |
| `disabledProp` | `String` | `'disabled'` | Component-local | Plain key read on each node; passed straight through as the `disabled` prop of that node's `n-popover-option`. |

### Options tree shape

Same contract as `NCascader` (this is the component that actually implements
the tree walk — `NCascader` only forwards to it):

```ts
interface CascaderNode {
    value: string;      // read via valueProp (plain key, default 'value')
    label: string;       // read via labelProp (Obj.get, default 'label')
    children?: CascaderNode[]; // read via childProp (default 'children')
    disabled?: boolean;  // read via disabledProp (default 'disabled')
}
```

`options` itself can be an Array or Object (typed `[Array, Object]`), walked
by `Arr.cascadeFind(options, childProp, matcherFn)`
(`src/cascader/js/helper/NCascaderHelper.ts`), which returns the array of
nodes forming the path from the root down to the first match — this is what
gets mapped through `valueProp` to build `modelValue`.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `string[]` — full path of `valueProp` values, root → the just-clicked/dblclicked node | `updateCascade(item, depth)` commits a selection (click or dblclick, depending on `trigger`) |
| `update:splitValue` | `string` — `valueProp` of the just-selected node, i.e. `Arr.last(modelValue)` | Same `updateCascade()` call as above, emitted alongside `update:modelValue` in the same handler |

Both events are always emitted together from `updateCascade()` — there is no
path where one fires without the other from a direct user interaction. (They
can, however, become resynchronized independently via the constructor-time
`buildModelFromSplit`/`buildSplitFromModel` calls if only one of the two
props was seeded externally.)

## Slots

None — `NCascaderPanelView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. Each depth column
is rendered via the `n-virtualbar` component's own scoped default slot
(`this.item(value, depth)`), not a slot `NCascaderPanel` exposes to its own
consumer.

## Exposed methods

None — `NCascaderPanelController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-cascader-panel v-model="path" :options="tree"></n-cascader-panel>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<n-cascader-panel
    v-model="path"
    v-model:split-value="cityId"
    :options="locations"
    trigger="click"
    type="primary"
></n-cascader-panel>
```

```ts
// same shape/data as cascader.md's realistic example
const locations = [
    {
        value: 'us', label: 'United States',
        children: [
            {
                value: 'us-ca', label: 'California',
                children: [
                    { value: 'us-ca-sf', label: 'San Francisco' },
                    { value: 'us-ca-la', label: 'Los Angeles' },
                ],
            },
        ],
    },
];
```

## Required composition

None required by the stated rule — `NCascaderPanel` renders its own root
`<div>` with `n-virtualbar` columns and needs no wrapping component to
function; it is usable directly inline (e.g. an always-visible tree browser,
as opposed to `NCascader`'s popover-triggered version). `NButtonGroup`'s
optional-child note (cascader.md) is specific to `NCascader`, not confirmed
for `NCascaderPanel`.

## Common mistakes

- Wiring only `v-model` and skipping `v-model:split-value`, same as
  `NCascader` — see cascader.md's Common mistakes for the exact failure
  mode. It applies identically here since both events fire from the same
  `updateCascade()` path.
- Assuming `valueProp` supports dot-path nesting like `labelProp` does — it
  doesn't (`item[data.valueProp]`, a plain key lookup, not `Obj.get`).
- Passing an `options` shaped for `Props.OptionsObject`
  (`optionsValue`/`optionsLabel`) — this component doesn't use that mixin at
  all; use `labelProp`/`valueProp`/`childProp` instead.

## Gotchas

- This is the component `NCascader` instantiates internally as its popover
  body (see cascader.md's Gotchas for the exact `passProps`/event-forwarding
  code) — so despite being documented and registered as fully independent,
  in practice `NCascaderPanel` is rendered on every `NCascader` instance too,
  just not authored directly by the `NCascader` consumer.
- `injectRef(['popover', 'NPopover'])` makes `updateCascade()`'s
  `this.ncx('popover')?.superClose()` call a safe no-op when
  `NCascaderPanel` is used standalone (no injected popover context) — it
  only actually closes something when nested inside an `n-popover` ancestor
  (which is exactly what happens when `NCascader` renders it).
- Extends `GroupController` (adds `childs`/`append`/`remove`/`watchChilds`),
  but nothing in `NCascaderPanelController`'s own logic calls `append()`/
  `remove()` — <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether some other part of the render tree
  (e.g. `n-popover-option` or `n-virtualbar` instances) registers itself as
  a child via `inject`/`provide` against this controller; not traced for
  this doc. Treat the `GroupController` base as present but functionally
  unused by this component's own code. -->

## Related components

- `NCascader` — the popover-triggered wrapper that renders this component
  internally; see its doc for the full trigger-display/collapse behavior
  this component doesn't have on its own.
- `NSelect` — the flat (non-tree) counterpart, built on
  `NPopoverPanelController`/`NPopoverPanelView` instead of `GroupController`.

<!-- ===== components/cascader.md ===== -->

# NCascader

A dropdown trigger for cascading (tree-shaped) selection — pick a path
through nested `options` (e.g. Country → State → City) via a popover that
internally renders an `NCascaderPanel`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **cascader** group index
(`src/cascader/index.ts`), which registers both `NCascader` (`n-cascader`)
and `NCascaderPanel` (`n-cascader-panel`) as separate top-level components in
the same call:

```ts
App.component(NCascader.name, NCascader);
App.component(NCascaderPanel.name, NCascaderPanel);
```

**Required composition (as given):** `NCascader` and `NCascaderPanel` are
fully independent components despite the shared naming — not a formal
parent/child pair the consumer is required to wire together. See Gotchas for
an apparent contradiction found in the render source.

`NCascader` extends the shared popover-panel stack (`NPopoverPanelController`
/ `NPopoverPanelView`), same as `NSelect`.

## Props

`NCascaderProps` spreads `NCascaderPanelProps` in full, so every
`NCascaderPanel` prop (except its `trigger`, which is also inherited) is also
an `NCascader` prop:

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (via `NCascaderPanelProps`) | Adds `n-load` to the root. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (via `NCascaderPanelProps`) | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (via `NCascaderPanelProps`) | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (via `NCascaderPanelProps`) | Drives `superDisabled`/`n-disabled` class only — see Gotchas. |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` | Shows the built-in clear (×) button. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` | Value used by the clear button / `applyClear()`. |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No items')` | `Props.EmptyText` | Shown by `this.empty()` when `options` is empty. |
| `undefinedText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Undefined')` | `Props.UndefinedText` | Label shown for a selected item whose `labelProp` value is empty (`NCascaderView.item()`). |
| `position` | `String` | `'bottom-start'` | `Props.PositionBottomStart` | Popover position; same 12-value set as `NSelect` (see select.md). |
| `modelValue` | `[Array, Object]` | `null` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | In practice a `string[]` — the full selected **path**, one value (per `valueProp`) per depth level, root → leaf. See "Options tree shape" below. |
| `splitValue` | `String` | `null` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | The single **leaf value** of the selected path — `Arr.last(modelValue)`. See Events for the exact semantics. |
| `options` | `[Array, Object]` | `() => []` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | The tree. **Not** `Props.OptionsObject` — no `optionsValue`/`optionsLabel` here; see "Options tree shape". |
| `labelProp` | `String` | `'label'` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | Dot-path (`Obj.get`) read on each node for its display label. |
| `valueProp` | `String` | `'value'` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | **Plain key** (used as `item[data.valueProp]`, not `Obj.get`) read on each node for its selectable value. |
| `childProp` | `String` | `'children'` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | Key holding a node's array of child nodes; used by `Arr.cascadeFind` to walk the tree. |
| `disabledProp` | `String` | `'disabled'` | `NCascaderPanelProps` (component-local) | Plain key read on each node to disable that individual option in the panel. |
| `collapse` | `Number` | `3` | Component-local (`NCascader.ts`) | Max number of path segments shown in the trigger's display row before collapsing the rest behind a `collapseText` marker. |
| `collapseText` | `String` | `'...'` | Component-local | Text of the collapsed-segment marker, via `Locale.trans()`. |
| `collapseFirst` | `Boolean` | `true` | Component-local | When `true` (default), the first path segment stays visible even when collapsing; when `false`, an extra segment shifts into the collapsed range. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Please select'` | Component-local | Literal default, passed through `Locale.trans()` at render. |

`trigger` (`String`, default `'hover'`) is also present (inherited from
`NCascaderPanelProps`) — it controls the internal panel's interaction mode
(`'hover'` expands on mouseenter and selects on click; `'click'` expands on
click and selects on double-click). It has no runtime enum validator, but
only these two string values have defined behavior in
`NCascaderPanelController`.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `string[]` — the full path of `valueProp` values from the root node down to the just-selected node (e.g. `['country-1', 'state-2', 'city-9']`) | The internal `NCascaderPanel` commits a selection (`updateCascade()`, on click or dblclick depending on `trigger`) and emits `update:modelValue`, which `NCascaderView.panel()`'s `onUpdate:modelValue` handler forwards into `scope.update('modelValue', value)`. Also fired reactively by `NCascaderHelper.buildModelFromSplit()` when only `splitValue` changes externally (`detectModel()`, watched on `splitValue`/`options`). |
| `update:splitValue` | `string` — the single `valueProp` value of the **last (deepest) node in the just-selected path**, i.e. `Arr.last(modelValue)` | Same commit action as above (`updateCascade()` sets both `splitValue` and `modelValue` together from the same click). Also fired reactively by `NCascaderHelper.buildSplitFromModel()` when only `modelValue` changes externally. |

**What `splitValue` represents:** it is not a separate piece of state — it is
a derived, always-in-sync single-value mirror of `modelValue`'s last entry.
`NCascaderController.detectModel()` keeps the two reconciled in both
directions: if `modelValue` is set but `splitValue` is empty,
`buildSplitFromModel()` sets `splitValue = Arr.last(modelValue)`; if
`splitValue` is set but `modelValue` is empty, `buildModelFromSplit()` walks
`options` with `Arr.cascadeFind` to find the node whose `valueProp` equals
`splitValue`, then rebuilds the full path array as `modelValue`. In practice
this means: bind `v-model` (`modelValue`) when you want the full breadcrumb
path, and/or bind `splitValue` (via `v-model:split-value`) when you only want
to persist/read the single terminal (leaf, or deepest-clicked) value — e.g.
storing just a city id in a flat DB column while still letting the component
reconstruct and display the full Country/State/City path from that id alone
via `options`.

## Slots

None — neither `NCascaderView` nor (transitively) the internal
`NCascaderPanelView` calls `this.slot(...)`.

## Exposed methods

None — `NCascaderController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-cascader v-model="path"></n-cascader>
```

## Realistic example

Tree shape confirmed against `demos/overview.html`'s `cascaderData` (which
uses the exact default keys `value`/`label`/`children`):

```vue
<n-cascader
    v-model="path"
    v-model:split-value="cityId"
    :options="locations"
    trigger="click"
    :clearable="true"
    type="primary"
></n-cascader>
```

```ts
interface CascaderNode {
    value: string;
    label: string;
    children?: CascaderNode[];
    disabled?: boolean; // read via disabledProp, default key 'disabled'
}

const locations: CascaderNode[] = [
    {
        value: 'us', label: 'United States',
        children: [
            {
                value: 'us-ca', label: 'California',
                children: [
                    { value: 'us-ca-sf', label: 'San Francisco' },
                    { value: 'us-ca-la', label: 'Los Angeles' },
                ],
            },
        ],
    },
];

// after selecting "San Francisco":
// path   -> ['us', 'us-ca', 'us-ca-sf']   (modelValue)
// cityId -> 'us-ca-sf'                     (splitValue)
```

## Required composition

- `NCascader` is standalone by the stated rule above — it does not require a
  separately-authored `NCascaderPanel` in the template (see Gotchas for the
  internal-render caveat).
- Optional: `NButtonGroup` (`src/button/js/button-group/`) can contain
  `NCascader` as a child — `NButtonGroupView` renders a plain default slot
  (`this.slot('default')`) with no type restriction, so any component
  including `NCascader` may be placed inside `<n-button-group>`. This is
  optional composition, not a requirement in either direction.

## Common mistakes

- **Wiring only `v-model` (i.e. only `modelValue`) and never touching
  `splitValue`.** This is a near-certain mistake for agents porting from
  other cascader-style components: if your app's data model only ever reads
  `splitValue` (e.g. persisting a single leaf id), forgetting
  `v-model:split-value="..."` means that id is silently generated internally
  but never surfaced to your own state, and vice versa — if you seed the
  component with only a `splitValue` and expect `modelValue` to already be
  populated as a plain prop read (rather than after the `Run.frame`-deferred
  `detectModel()` reconciliation), you'll observe a one-frame gap.
- Assuming `options` supports `Props.OptionsObject`'s `optionsValue`/
  `optionsLabel` dotted-path resolution. It doesn't — use `labelProp`/
  `valueProp`/`childProp`/`disabledProp` instead (plain/`Obj.get` key reads,
  not `$index`/`$value` pair wrapping).
- Assuming `valueProp` supports dot-path nesting like `labelProp` does.
  `labelProp` is resolved via `Obj.get(item, labelProp)` (dot-path capable),
  but `valueProp` is read as a **plain key** (`item[data.valueProp]`) in both
  `NCascaderPanelController` and `NCascaderPanelView` — a dotted `valueProp`
  like `'meta.id'` will not resolve.

## Gotchas

- **Apparent contradiction with the stated independence rule:**
  `NCascaderView.panel()` directly renders `n-cascader-panel` as the popover
  body, forwarding `NCascader`'s own current `modelValue`, `splitValue`,
  `options`, `size`, `type`, `disabled`, `load`, `trigger`, `labelProp`,
  `valueProp`, `childProp`, `disabledProp` into it via
  `passProps(props, Mix.keys(NCascaderPanelProps))`, and listening for the
  panel's `update:modelValue`/`update:splitValue` to update its own state:
  ```ts
  props['onUpdate:modelValue'] = (value) => scope.update('modelValue', value);
  props['onUpdate:splitValue'] = (value) => scope.update('splitValue', value);
  return this.comp('n-cascader-panel', props);
  ```
  This is a real internal parent/child render relationship — `NCascader`
  instantiates and drives an `NCascaderPanel` instance under the hood. It
  does not change the consumer-facing rule (you never author
  `<n-cascader-panel>` inside `<n-cascader>` yourself — it's generated), but
  it means the two components are coupled at the implementation level even
  though they are registered and documented as independent, separately
  usable components.
- `NCascaderController` also does `provide('NCascader', this.instance)`, but
  nothing in `NCascaderPanelController` (or elsewhere searched) injects that
  key — it appears unused/vestigial in the current source.
- `disabled` does not appear to be read anywhere in `NCascaderController`,
  `NCascaderView`, or `NCascaderPanelController` to gate opening, hovering,
  or clicking — only `classRoot()` applies the `n-disabled` styling class,
  and per-node disabling goes through `disabledProp` instead (passed as
  `disabled` to each `n-popover-option`). <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether the
  underlying `n-popover`/`n-popover-option` components independently read a
  `disabled` prop to block interaction — not traced into `src/popover/` for
  this doc. -->
- `demos/cascader/index.html` is stale: it loads Vue 2.5.13 off a prebuilt
  `dist/nano-ui.esm.js` and uses `:items="items"` — there is no `items` prop
  anywhere in the current `NCascaderProps`/`NCascaderPanelProps`. Its data
  generator does confirm the tree shape (`label`/`value`/`children`/
  `disabled` keys), which matches current defaults, but do not copy its
  template syntax.
- `trigger`'s two-value behavior (`'hover'` vs `'click'`) is not enforced by
  a prop validator (unlike, e.g., `Props.AlignHorizontal`'s array validator)
  — any other string is structurally accepted but falls through both
  `if` branches in `NCascaderPanelController.onMouseenter`/`onClick`/
  `onDblclick`, effectively disabling expand/select entirely.

## Related components

- `NCascaderPanel` — the tree list `NCascader` renders internally as its
  popover body; also directly usable standalone (e.g. inline, without a
  popover trigger). See cascader-panel.md, including the render-coupling
  gotcha above.
- `NSelect` — the flat counterpart; shares the same
  `NPopoverPanelController`/`NPopoverPanelView` base and the plain
  `update:modelValue` v-model convention (minus `splitValue`).
- `NButtonGroup` — optional container; see Required composition.
