<!-- ===== components/chart-bar.md ===== -->

# NChartBar

A bar-chart wrapper that renders one bar per `NChartItem` child (plus an
optional aggregated "Other" bar), a header showing the average value, and an
optional legend.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **chart** group index
(`src/chart/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NChartBar', NChartBar)`
(alongside `NChartDonut` and `NChartItem` — all three are registered together
by the same install function).

## Props

`NChartBar` itself declares **no data/items/series prop at all**. The chart's
data comes entirely from its `<n-chart-item>` children — see "Required
composition" below and `ai-docs/components/chart-item.md` for the per-item
shape.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. |
| `sort` | `Boolean` | `false` | own (`NChartBarProps`) | When `true`, bars are ordered by `data.value` descending (`Arr.sort(this.childs, 'data.value').reverse()`) instead of DOM/registration order. |
| `limit` | `Number` | `4` | own (`NChartBarProps`) | Max number of individual bars shown; the remainder are summed into one "Other" bar. Pass `null`/`undefined` to disable limiting (`data.limit ?? items.length`). |
| `legend` | `Boolean` | `true` | own (`NChartBarProps`) | Shows/hides the legend list below the bars (rendered inside `n-scrollbar`). |
| `color` | `[Number, String]` | `10` | own (`NChartBarProps`) — **not** `Props.Color` (which defaults to `null`) | Base index into the 20-slot color wheel (`Styler.wheel`, `limitwheel = 19`). Each bar without its own `color` gets `Styler.wheel(Mix.int(color) + index)`, so bars are auto-tinted in sequence starting from this offset. |
| `totalLabel` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Total')` | own (`NChartBarProps`) | Label text next to the header's total tag. |
| `otherLabel` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Other')` | own (`NChartBarProps`) | `axis` label used for the aggregated "Other" bar when `limit` hides items. |
| `minHeight` | `Number` | `5` | own (`NChartBarProps`) | Minimum bar height as a percentage, used in `getHeight()`: `((100 - minHeight) / maxval * value) + minHeight`. |

### Data shape (via `NChartItem` children, not a prop)

Each `<n-chart-item>` child contributes one entry once mounted. The controller
reads it back off the child's own `NChartItemController` as:

```ts
interface ChartItem {
    axis: string;           // NChartItem's `axis` prop, default Locale.trans('Item')
    value: string | number; // NChartItem's `value` prop
    color: string | number | null;
    type: string | null;
}
```

Concrete example:

```vue
<n-chart-bar :color="0" :limit="5">
    <n-chart-item value="4800" axis="Jan"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="2000" axis="Feb"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="800" axis="Mar" type="danger"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-bar>
```

## Events

None — `NChartBar.ts` declares `emits: []` and `NChartBarController` never
calls `scope.emit(...)` or `update(...)`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Where `<n-chart-item>` children are placed. `NChartBarView.default()` renders `this.slot('default')` after the header/body, but the items themselves render nothing visible (`NChartItemView.default()` returns `null`) — their only job is to register with the chart via inject/`append()`. |

## Exposed methods

None — `NChartBarController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-chart-bar>
    <n-chart-item value="40"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-bar>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted directly from `demos/charts.html`:

```vue
<n-chart-bar :color="0" :limit="5" :sort="true" size="sm">
    <n-chart-item value="40"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="25"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="40"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="80"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-bar>
```

`demos/charts.html` also shows explicit per-bar `type`s (bypassing the color
wheel for those bars):

```vue
<n-chart-bar :color="0" :limit="5" :legend="false" size="xs">
    <n-chart-item value="80" type="primary"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20" type="warning"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="25" type="danger"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="40" type="info"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="25" type="success"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="40" type="neutral"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-bar>
```

## Required composition

**Confirmed: `NChartItem` is a required child of a chart-providing ancestor —
either `NChartBar` or `NChartDonut`.** `NChartBarController extends
GroupController` and calls `provide('NChart', this.instance)` during
`setup()`. `NChartItemController.setup()` calls `this.injectRef(['chart',
'NChart'])`, and `onMounted()` calls `this.ncx('chart')?.append(this)`
(`onUnmounted()` calls `.remove(this)`). `NChartBarController.makeDataset()`
then reads its bars straight from `this.childs` (the `GroupController` list
populated by that `append()` call) — there is no other way to feed data into
`NChartBar`.

Without at least one `NChartItem` descendant, `NChartBar` renders its header
and an empty bar frame (`avgval` computes to `NaN` since `total /
this.childs.length` divides by zero). An `NChartItem` rendered with no
`NChart`-providing ancestor mounts silently as a no-op (`this.ncx('chart')` is
`undefined`, so `?.append(this)` never fires) — it produces no visible output
and registers nowhere.

`NChartItem` does not care *which* of the two chart components is its parent
— both provide the same `'NChart'` injection key with an API-compatible
instance (`GroupController.append`/`remove`), so the same `<n-chart-item>`
markup works verbatim under `<n-chart-bar>` or `<n-chart-donut>`.

## Common mistakes

- Looking for an `items`/`data`/`series` prop on `NChartBar` — there isn't
  one. All data must be passed as `<n-chart-item>` children.
- Assuming `NChartItem` renders something on its own outside a chart parent —
  its view always returns `null`; it is purely a data-registration component.
- Passing `color` as a prop on `NChartBar` expecting a CSS color/theme color —
  it's a **numeric wheel offset** (`Styler.wheel`), not a color value; per-bar
  visual color is set via each `NChartItem`'s own `color` or `type` prop.
- Expecting `limit` to drop the excess items — it instead merges them into one
  extra "Other" bar (`otherLabel`), whose `value` is the sum of the hidden
  items' values.

## Gotchas

- `NChartItem`'s `label` prop is declared but never read anywhere in
  `NChartItemData`, `NChartItemController`, or `toItem()` — it currently has
  no effect on rendering. Use `axis` for the bar's label text instead.
- If an item sets an explicit `type`, that takes priority over the color
  wheel entirely — the bar/legend swatch gets `n-type-{type}` instead of
  `n-color-{n}`, and the item's own `color` prop is ignored in that case (see
  `NChartBarView.bar()`: `if (!item.type) { …n-color… } else { …n-type… }`).
- The built-in "Other" bucket is styled with `type: 'neutral'` internally —
  `neutral` is a real, working `n-type-*` value for chart items even though
  it isn't in the concepts.md list of globally "known styled" `type` values;
  it's specific to the chart components' own stylesheet.
- The legend is always sorted by value descending (`Arr.sort(scope.childs,
  'data.value').reverse()`) regardless of the `sort` prop, which only affects
  bar order — `sort` and legend order can visually disagree when `sort` is
  `false`.

## Related components

- `NChartItem` — required data-carrying child; see
  `ai-docs/components/chart-item.md`.
- `NChartDonut` — the other chart type sharing the same `NChartItem` child
  contract and most of the same props (`sort`, `limit`, `legend`, `color`,
  `totalLabel`, `otherLabel`); see `ai-docs/components/chart-donut.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/chart-donut.md ===== -->

# NChartDonut

A donut/ring-chart wrapper that renders one arc per `NChartItem` child (plus
an optional aggregated "Other" arc), a centered total label, and an optional
legend.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **chart** group index
(`src/chart/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NChartDonut', NChartDonut)`
(alongside `NChartBar` and `NChartItem` — all three are registered together
by the same install function).

## Props

`NChartDonut` itself declares **no data/items/series prop at all**. The
chart's data comes entirely from its `<n-chart-item>` children — see
"Required composition" below and `ai-docs/components/chart-item.md` for the
per-item shape.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. |
| `sort` | `Boolean` | `false` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | When `true`, arcs are ordered by `data.value` descending instead of DOM/registration order. |
| `limit` | `Number` | `4` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | Max number of individual arcs shown; the remainder are summed into one "Other" arc. Pass `null`/`undefined` to disable limiting. |
| `legend` | `Boolean` | `true` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | Shows/hides the legend list below the ring (rendered inside `n-scrollbar`). |
| `color` | `[Number, String]` | `10` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) — **not** `Props.Color` (which defaults to `null`) | Base index into the 20-slot color wheel (`Styler.wheel`, `limitwheel = 19`). Each arc without its own `color` gets `Styler.wheel(Mix.int(color) + index)`. |
| `totalLabel` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Total')` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | Label shown centered in the ring alongside the summed total (`--n-chart-label` CSS var). |
| `otherLabel` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Other')` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | `axis` label used for the aggregated "Other" arc when `limit` hides items. |
| `width` | `Number` | `10` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | Stroke width of the ring, applied as the `--n-stroke-width` CSS var and used in `getDistance()`'s gap math. |
| `overlap` | `Boolean` | `false` | own (`NChartDonutProps`) | When `false` (default), a small gap is subtracted between adjacent arcs (`dasharr - width*1.5`, offset shifted by `-width*0.5`) so arcs don't visually touch; when `true`, arcs render edge-to-edge and the root gets an extra `n-chart-donut--overlap` class. |

### Data shape (via `NChartItem` children, not a prop)

Identical contract to `NChartBar` — each `<n-chart-item>` child contributes:

```ts
interface ChartItem {
    axis: string;           // NChartItem's `axis` prop, default Locale.trans('Item')
    value: string | number; // NChartItem's `value` prop
    color: string | number | null;
    type: string | null;
}
```

Concrete example:

```vue
<n-chart-donut :width="8" :color="0" :limit="5">
    <n-chart-item value="500" color="9"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20" color="10"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="25" color="11"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="40" color="12"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-donut>
```

## Events

None — `NChartDonut.ts` declares `emits: []` and `NChartDonutController` never
calls `scope.emit(...)` or `update(...)`. `onPointerenter`/`onPointerleave`
(fired from arc hover, see below) only write directly to a template-ref DOM
node's inline style — they do not emit anything to the parent.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Where `<n-chart-item>` children are placed. `NChartDonutView.default()` renders `this.slot('default')` after the SVG ring/legend, but the items themselves render nothing visible (`NChartItemView.default()` returns `null`) — their only job is to register with the chart via inject/`append()`. |

## Exposed methods

None — `NChartDonutController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-chart-donut>
    <n-chart-item value="40"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-donut>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted directly from `demos/charts.html`:

```vue
<n-chart-donut :width="8" :color="0" :limit="5" :overlap="true" size="xs">
    <n-chart-item value="80" type="primary"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20" type="warning"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="25" type="success"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="40" type="danger"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-donut>
```

## Required composition

**Confirmed: `NChartItem` is a required child of a chart-providing ancestor —
either `NChartDonut` or `NChartBar`.** `NChartDonutController extends
GroupController` and calls `provide('NChart', this.instance)` during
`setup()`. `NChartItemController.setup()` calls `this.injectRef(['chart',
'NChart'])`, and `onMounted()` calls `this.ncx('chart')?.append(this)`
(`onUnmounted()` calls `.remove(this)`). `NChartDonutController.makeDataset()`
/`makeTotal()`/`makeMaxval()` then read straight from `this.childs` (the
`GroupController` list populated by that `append()` call) — there is no other
way to feed data into `NChartDonut`.

Without at least one `NChartItem` descendant, the ring renders just its base
circle with `total`/`maxval` computed from an empty array (`total: 0`,
`maxval: Number.MIN_VALUE`). An `NChartItem` rendered with no
`NChart`-providing ancestor mounts silently as a no-op — it produces no
visible output and registers nowhere.

`NChartItem` does not care *which* of the two chart components is its parent
— both provide the same `'NChart'` injection key with an API-compatible
instance (`GroupController.append`/`remove`), so the same `<n-chart-item>`
markup works verbatim under `<n-chart-donut>` or `<n-chart-bar>`.

## Common mistakes

- Looking for an `items`/`data`/`series` prop on `NChartDonut` — there isn't
  one. All data must be passed as `<n-chart-item>` children.
- Assuming `width` controls the SVG element's pixel size — the `<svg>` is
  hard-coded to `width="600" height="600" viewBox="0 0 140 140"`; `width` is
  the ring's **stroke** width only.
- Expecting hover state (`onPointerenter`) to update reactive component state
  or emit an event — it directly mutates a DOM node's inline CSS custom
  properties (`--n-chart-label`, `--n-chart-value`) via `this.dom('text')`,
  bypassing Vue reactivity entirely.
- Passing `color` as a prop on `NChartDonut` expecting a CSS color/theme color
  — it's a **numeric wheel offset** (`Styler.wheel`), not a color value;
  per-arc visual color is set via each `NChartItem`'s own `color` or `type`
  prop.

## Gotchas

- `NChartItem`'s `label` prop is declared but never read anywhere in
  `NChartItemData`, `NChartItemController`, or `toItem()` — it currently has
  no effect on rendering. Use `axis` for the arc's label text instead.
- If an item sets an explicit `type`, that takes priority over the color
  wheel entirely — the arc/legend swatch gets `n-type-{type}` instead of
  `n-color-{n}`, and the item's own `color` prop is ignored in that case.
- The built-in "Other" bucket is styled with `type: 'neutral'` internally —
  `neutral` is a real, working `n-type-*` value for chart items even though
  it isn't in the concepts.md list of globally "known styled" `type` values;
  it's specific to the chart components' own stylesheet.
- `overlap: false` (the default) shrinks each arc's dash length and shifts its
  offset to create a visible gap between arcs; with many very small values
  this can make thin slices disappear entirely (`Math.max(dasharr -
  width*1.5, 0)`).
- The legend is always sorted by value descending regardless of the `sort`
  prop, which only affects arc draw order — `sort` and legend order can
  visually disagree when `sort` is `false`.

## Related components

- `NChartItem` — required data-carrying child; see
  `ai-docs/components/chart-item.md`.
- `NChartBar` — the other chart type sharing the same `NChartItem` child
  contract and most of the same props (`sort`, `limit`, `legend`, `color`,
  `totalLabel`, `otherLabel`); see `ai-docs/components/chart-bar.md`.

<!-- ===== components/chart-item.md ===== -->

# NChartItem

A headless (renders nothing itself) data-carrier component: each instance
represents one bar/arc's data and registers itself with an ancestor chart
(`NChartBar` or `NChartDonut`) via inject/provide.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **chart** group index
(`src/chart/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NChartItem', NChartItem)`
(alongside `NChartBar` and `NChartDonut` — all three are registered together
by the same install function).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`, plus `neutral` (used internally by the parent chart's own "Other" bucket, but usable directly — see `demos/charts.html`). When set, this bar/arc renders with `n-type-{type}` and its own/wheel-derived `color` is ignored (see the parent chart docs' Gotchas). |
| `color` | `[String, Number]` | `null` | `Props.Color` | Explicit color-wheel index/value for this item. When `null` (default), the parent chart derives one from its own `color` prop plus this item's position: `Styler.wheel(Mix.int(parentColor) + index)`. Ignored if `type` is also set. |
| `value` | `[String, Number]` | `null` | own (`NChartItemProps`) | The numeric value this bar/arc represents. Read via `Mix.num`/`Num.float` by the parent for height/arc-length math and summed for totals/averages. |
| `axis` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Item')` | own (`NChartItemProps`) | The label shown in the popover (bar chart) / legend / hover tooltip (donut chart) for this item. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | own (`NChartItemProps`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED as intentionally functional --> Declared but **never read** anywhere in `NChartItemData`, `NChartItemController`, or `toItem()` — currently has no effect on rendering. Do not rely on it; use `axis` instead. |

### Data shape this item contributes to its parent

Once mounted, `toItem()` is what the parent chart actually consumes for each
child:

```ts
interface ChartItem {
    axis: string;
    value: string | number;
    color: string | number | null;
    type: string | null;
}
```

Concrete example (a single item inside a chart):

```vue
<n-chart-item value="4800" axis="Jan" type="primary"></n-chart-item>
```

## Events

None — `NChartItem.ts` declares no `emits` array at all, and
`NChartItemController` never calls `scope.emit(...)` or `update(...)`.

## Slots

None. `NChartItemView.default()` returns `null` unconditionally — the
component renders no DOM and therefore has no slot outlets.

## Exposed methods

None — `NChartItemController` never calls `pass()`. It does define
`toItem()`, `onMounted()`, and `onUnmounted()` as regular (non-exposed)
methods, called only by the item itself and read by the parent chart via its
own `childs` array of controller instances (not via a template-ref API).

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-chart-bar>
    <n-chart-item value="10"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-bar>
```

`NChartItem` is never used standalone — see "Required composition" below.

## Realistic example

From `demos/charts.html`, a full donut dataset with explicit numeric colors:

```vue
<n-chart-donut :width="8" :color="0" :limit="5" size="sm">
    <n-chart-item value="500" color="9"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20" color="10"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="25" color="11"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="40" color="12"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="80" color="13"></n-chart-item>
    <n-chart-item value="20" color="14"></n-chart-item>
</n-chart-donut>
```

(the source demo also passes a `linecap="normal"` attribute on `n-chart-donut`
— that is not a declared prop of `NChartDonut`, so it falls through as a
plain, no-op DOM attribute; omitted here.)

## Required composition

**Confirmed: `NChartItem` requires a parent that `provide()`s the `'NChart'`
injection key — currently only `NChartBar` and `NChartDonut` do this.**

`NChartItemController.setup()` calls `this.injectRef(['chart', 'NChart'])`
(reading whatever ancestor called `provide('NChart', ...)`), and:

```ts
onMounted() { this.ncx('chart')?.append(this); }
onUnmounted() { this.ncx('chart')?.remove(this); }
```

Both `NChartBarController` and `NChartDonutController` extend
`GroupController` and call `provide('NChart', this.instance)` in their own
`setup()`, giving them `append(child)`/`remove(child)`/`watchChilds(cb)` and a
reactive `childs` list (see concepts.md's `GroupController` section). This is
exactly and only how a chart's data set is built — there is no
`items`/`data`/`series` prop on either chart component.

`NChartItem` itself renders nothing (`view.default()` returns `null`) and
performs no visual role on its own — outside a `NChart`-providing parent, it
silently registers nowhere (`this.ncx('chart')` is `undefined`, so
`?.append(this)` never fires) and has zero effect. It is **not** independent;
treat it as a required, chart-scoped child of `NChartBar` or `NChartDonut`
(interchangeably — the injection contract is identical for both).

## Common mistakes

- Using `<n-chart-item>` outside `<n-chart-bar>`/`<n-chart-donut>` expecting
  it to render a standalone bar or badge — it renders nothing by itself, ever.
- Setting `label` expecting it to appear as the item's display text — it's
  unused; use `axis`.
- Setting both `color` and `type` and expecting `color` to still apply as a
  fallback tint — `type`, if present, fully overrides the color-wheel/`color`
  path in the parent's render logic (`if (!item.type) { …color… } else {
  …type… }`).
- Binding `v-model` on `NChartItem` — it has no `modelValue` prop and is not
  a v-model-style component at all; it's a one-shot data descriptor read once
  per render via `toItem()`.

## Gotchas

- There is no reactive update path from prop changes on an already-mounted
  `NChartItem` back to a visible re-render trigger beyond normal Vue
  reactivity — the parent's `makeDataset()`/`makeMaxval()`/`makeTotal()` are
  only explicitly re-run on `watchChilds` (mount/unmount) and on the parent's
  own `limit` prop changing; changing an item's `value` prop while mounted
  still flows through because `data.visible`/`data.hidden` hold live
  `NChartItemController` references (`item.data.value` is read live at
  render time), but derived aggregates like `avgval`/`maxval`/`total` are
  **not** wrapped in a `computed()` — they're plain `set()` calls run only
  from the watchers above, so they will not update on an in-place `value`
  change alone. <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact Vue reactivity edge case here; confirmed only that makeMaxval/makeAvgval/makeTotal are imperative methods invoked from watchProp('limit')/watchChilds(), not computed(). -->
- `uid` (used internally for `append`/`remove`/dataset filtering) comes from
  `this.makeUID()` in `setup()`, not from any prop — there's no way to pass a
  stable custom key for an item.

## Related components

- `NChartBar` — bar-chart parent; see `ai-docs/components/chart-bar.md`.
- `NChartDonut` — donut-chart parent; see `ai-docs/components/chart-donut.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/checkbox-group.md ===== -->

# NCheckboxGroup

A container that tracks which of its child `NCheckbox` items are checked as a single array `v-model`, and provides aggregate "all checked"/"some checked" state for a "check all" checkbox.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/checkbox/index.ts` (`App.component(NCheckboxGroup.name, NCheckboxGroup)`). Source: `src/checkbox/js/checkbox-group/{NCheckboxGroup,NCheckboxGroupController,NCheckboxGroupData,NCheckboxGroupView}.ts`. `NCheckboxGroupController extends GroupController` (see concepts.md) for `childs`/`append`/`remove`, and `provide('NCheckboxGroup', this.instance)` so children can `inject` it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Not read directly by `NCheckboxGroupData`, but flows through `classRoot()` as `n-size-{size}` on the group root — children read their own `size` prop independently. |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same as above — styles the group root only. |
| `align` | `String`, validated in `['horizontal','vertical']` | `'horizontal'` | `Props.AlignHorizontal` (`AlignProps.ts`) | Layout direction of the children; adds a `{bem}--{align}` class. |
| `modelValue` | `Array` | `() => []` | local (`NCheckboxGroup.ts`) | The array of checked children's `value`s. This **is** the group-level v-model — array type, not boolean. |
| `view` | `String` (known: `'checkbox'`, `'button'`) | `'checkbox'` | local (`NCheckboxGroup.ts`) | Visual style, applied to every child (children's own `view` prop is overridden — see `checkbox.md` Gotchas). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `any[]` | `NCheckboxGroupController.superToggle(child)` (a non-global child checkbox was clicked — value added/removed via `Arr.toggle`), or `superGlobal()` (the `global` checkbox was clicked — either all children's values are added, or the array is cleared to `[]`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The child `NCheckbox` items. |

## Exposed methods

`ncx.pass({ global: 'superGlobal', toggle: 'superToggle' })`:

- `.global()` — no arguments; runs the same check-all/uncheck-all logic as clicking a `global` child checkbox. Practically callable from a template ref.
- `.toggle(child)` — expects an actual child `NCheckboxController` instance (as produced internally via `ncx('...')`); not practically callable from outside the library's own render tree. Prefer a child `NCheckbox`'s own exposed `.toggle()` (see `checkbox.md`) to toggle one item programmatically.

Additionally, via `exposeData('checked')` / `exposeData('intermediate')`, a template ref on the group exposes two **reactive values** (not methods):

- `checked: boolean` — `Arr.lengths(model, childs)` <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact boolean semantics of pico-js's `Arr.lengths` helper not confirmed from this repo's source; behaviorally it is used as "are all registered children checked" (compared against the checked/unchecked icon and `n-checked` class on the `global` checkbox). --> — true once every registered child is checked.
- `intermediate: boolean` — `!Mix.isEmpty(model)`, i.e. true whenever the array is non-empty (at least one child checked, including the all-checked case).

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-checkbox-group v-model="selected">
    <n-checkbox value="foo">Foo</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="bar">Bar</n-checkbox>
  </n-checkbox-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const selected = ref([]);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on `demos/checkbox/index.html` (vertical group with a "check all" checkbox) and `demos/overview.html`'s button-view variant:

```vue
<template>
  <n-checkbox-group align="vertical" v-model="form.options">
    <n-checkbox :global="true">Check all</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="foo">Foo</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="bar">Bar</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="james">James</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="bond">Bond</n-checkbox>
  </n-checkbox-group>

  <n-checkbox-group align="horizontal" view="button" v-model="form.options">
    <n-checkbox :global="true">Check all</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="foo">Foo</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="bar">Bar</n-checkbox>
  </n-checkbox-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ options: [] });
</script>
```

## Required composition

Must contain `NCheckbox` children to be useful (an empty group just renders an empty wrapper `div`). Per the confirmed composition rule: `NCheckboxGroup` may only contain `NCheckbox` — nesting any other component as a direct child is not a supported pattern (no other component reads/provides the `NCheckboxGroup` inject key).

## Common mistakes

- Binding `v-model` to a boolean, matching the mental model of a single checkbox: `NCheckboxGroup`'s `modelValue` is always an **array** of the checked children's `value`s, default `[]`.
- Expecting the group's `size`/`type` props to cascade into each child's own styling automatically: they only style the group's own root element (`classRoot()` on `NCheckboxGroupData`) — each `NCheckbox` child still needs its own `size`/`type` if per-item styling is desired (only `view` is actually forced from parent to child, per `NCheckboxData.view`).
- Calling the group's exposed `.toggle()` directly expecting to pass a checkbox's `value`: it expects a live child controller instance, not a value — use the child checkbox's own `.toggle()` instead, or `.global()` for check-all/none.

## Gotchas

- The group's `view` prop is inherited by every child regardless of what `view` the child itself declares (see `checkbox.md` Gotchas: `NCheckboxData.view` prefers `ncx('group')?.data.view`).
- `checked`/`intermediate` (exposed via `exposeData`) are the same aggregate values a `global` child checkbox links to (`linkProp`) — if you don't want a visible "check all" checkbox but want the aggregate state (e.g. for a custom header), read these off a template ref instead of adding a `global` `NCheckbox`.

## Related components

- `NCheckbox` — the required child; see `checkbox.md` for the two Controller variants (`global` vs. default).
- `NRadioGroup` — mutually-exclusive counterpart; see `radio-group.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/checkbox.md ===== -->

# NCheckbox

A single boolean (or grouped/"select-all") checkbox — usable standalone with its own `v-model`, or nested inside `NCheckboxGroup` to toggle membership in a shared array.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/checkbox/index.ts` (`App.component(NCheckbox.name, NCheckbox)`), alongside `NCheckboxGroup` from the same group index. Source: `src/checkbox/js/checkbox/{NCheckbox,NCheckboxController,NCheckboxControllerGlobal,NCheckboxControllerSingle,NCheckboxData,NCheckboxView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the `n-disabled` class (via `classRoot`/`superDisabled`) — see Gotchas, it does **not** block clicks by itself. |
| `modelValue` | `[Number, Boolean]` | `false` | local (`NCheckbox.ts`) | The checked state when the checkbox is used standalone (or with `global`, is read-only — see Controller fork below). |
| `value` | `[Number, Boolean, String]` | `null` | local (`NCheckbox.ts`) | The value this checkbox represents inside an `NCheckboxGroup`'s array. Ignored when the checkbox is standalone. |
| `allowUncheck` | `Boolean` | `false` | local (`NCheckbox.ts`) | When the checkbox is both checked and `disabled`, this removes the `n-disabled` class (see `NCheckboxData.classList`) so it still reads as interactive — see Gotchas for what this does and doesn't actually gate. |
| `global` | `Boolean` | `false` | local (`NCheckbox.ts`) | Selects which Controller class is instantiated — see Controller fork below. This is the "check all / uncheck all" checkbox for a group. |
| `view` | `String` (known: `'checkbox'`, `'button'` — confirmed via `n-checkbox--button` in `themes/default/checkbox/src/checkbox/checkbox.scss`) | `'checkbox'` | local (`NCheckbox.ts`) | Visual style. **Ignored when nested inside an `NCheckboxGroup`** — the group's own `view` prop always wins (see Gotchas). |

## Controller fork (important)

`NCheckbox.ts`'s `setup()` picks the Controller class at instantiation time based on the `global` prop:

```ts
let name : any = NCheckboxControllerSingle;
if ( props.global ) { name = NCheckboxControllerGlobal; }
let ncx = new name(props, context);
```

- **`global: false` (default) → `NCheckboxControllerSingle`.** `modelValue` is a local reactive clone (`cloneProp('modelValue')`) — the checkbox owns its own state and works with no ancestor group at all. If an ancestor `NCheckboxGroup` *is* found (via `injectRef(['group','NCheckboxGroup'])`), it additionally: registers itself with the group (`onMounted` → `group.append(this)`), derives its own `modelValue` from whether the group's array contains this checkbox's `value` (`watchModel`/`updateModel`, using `Arr.has`), and on click (`superToggle`) both tells the group to add/remove its value (`group.superToggle(this)`, which updates the group's array and emits the **group's** `update:modelValue`) *and* flips its own local `modelValue` (emitting its **own** `update:modelValue` too).
- **`global: true` → `NCheckboxControllerGlobal`.** Requires an ancestor `NCheckboxGroup` — `setup()` throws `Error('NCheckboxGroup is required on global!')` if `injectRef` finds none. Its `modelValue` and `intermediate` are **read-only computed aliases** (`linkProp`) to the group's own `checked`/`intermediate` state (see `checkbox-group.md`) — clicking it never calls `this.update('modelValue', ...)` on itself; it only calls `this.ncx('group').superGlobal()`, which recomputes the group's array (checking all children, or clearing it) and emits `update:modelValue` **on the group**. A `global` checkbox therefore never fires its own `update:modelValue` — don't wire a `v-model` to it.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `boolean` | **Single controller only.** `NCheckboxControllerSingle.superToggle()` runs on click, flipping the local boolean via `this.update('modelValue', !this.data.model)`. Declared in `emits` for both controller variants, but the Global variant never actually calls `update()` on itself (see Controller fork above) — only the parent `NCheckboxGroup` emits in that case. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Rendered inside `.n-checkbox__label`, next to the checkbox box — the visible label text. |

## Exposed methods

`ncx.pass({ toggle: 'superToggle' })` — a template ref exposes `.toggle()`, which runs the exact same logic as a click (flips state and, if grouped, notifies the group). Works with no arguments for both controller variants.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-checkbox v-model="checked">Accept terms</n-checkbox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const checked = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on `demos/checkbox/index.html` and the `NCheckbox` section of `demos/overview.html` (standalone usage plus a group with a `global` "check all" checkbox):

```vue
<template>
  <n-checkbox v-model="form.option" size="md" type="primary" :allow-uncheck="true">
    Enable notifications
  </n-checkbox>

  <n-checkbox-group v-model="form.options" align="vertical">
    <n-checkbox :global="true">Check all</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="foo">Foo</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="bar">Bar</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="james">James</n-checkbox>
    <n-checkbox value="bond">Bond</n-checkbox>
  </n-checkbox-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ option: false, options: [] });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — `NCheckbox` works standalone with its own `v-model`. Optionally nested inside `NCheckboxGroup` for group-array behavior. **Exception:** an `NCheckbox` with `global="true"` requires an ancestor `NCheckboxGroup` and throws at setup otherwise (see Controller fork).

## Common mistakes

- Assuming every `NCheckbox` inside a group needs its own `v-model`: inside `NCheckboxGroup`, checked state is derived from whether the group's array contains this checkbox's `value` prop — a separate `v-model` on the child is redundant (though harmless for the Single controller, since it mirrors the derived state).
- Using `global="true"` on a checkbox with no surrounding `NCheckboxGroup`, expecting it to just act as a normal checkbox — it throws `NCheckboxGroup is required on global!` at setup instead.
- Wiring `v-model="x"` onto a `global` checkbox expecting it to reflect/control that variable directly — its `modelValue` is a read-only alias to the group's aggregate `checked` state; it never emits its own `update:modelValue`.
- Setting `view="button"` on an individual `NCheckbox` that lives inside an `NCheckboxGroup` and expecting it to render as a button: the group's `view` prop always wins for grouped children (see Gotchas).

## Gotchas

- **`disabled` is styling-only in the shipped theme.** `NCheckboxView.default()` binds `onClick` unconditionally (no guard for `data.disabled`/`superDisabled`); disabling only adds the `n-disabled` class via `classRoot()`. `themes/default/checkbox/src/checkbox/checkbox.scss` has no `pointer-events` rule, so a disabled checkbox is still clickable/toggleable in JS unless the consuming app's own CSS blocks pointer events.
- `allowUncheck` interacts with the point above: it only removes the `n-disabled` class when the checkbox is checked (`NCheckboxData.classList`) — it doesn't change click behavior (which was never blocked to begin with). Its practical effect is purely visual: an already-checked, disabled checkbox no longer *looks* disabled.
- **`view` is decided by the parent when grouped.** `NCheckboxData.view` getter: `this.scope.ncx('group')?.data.view || this.scope.get('view')` — if an ancestor `NCheckboxGroup` exists, its `view` prop is used regardless of what this checkbox's own `view` prop says.
- Global checkbox's own icon reflects the group's "all checked" boolean (`data.model`, aliased to the group's `checked`), and its `n-intermediate` class reflects the group's `intermediate` state (true whenever the group's array is non-empty) — both classes can be present simultaneously (e.g. when all items are checked, `checked` and non-empty are both true).

## Related components

- `NCheckboxGroup` — the container that gives `value`/`global` meaning; see `checkbox-group.md`.
- `NRadio`/`NRadioGroup` — mutually-exclusive counterpart; see `radio.md`/`radio-group.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/collapse-item.md ===== -->

# NCollapseItem

A single panel within an `NCollapse`: renders a clickable header (icon,
label, optional action slot, angle indicator) and a content area whose
mount/visibility behavior is governed by `lazy`/`keep`, driven entirely by
the parent `NCollapse`'s `modelValue`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally alongside `NCollapse` via `App.use(Install)` from the
**collapse** group index (`src/collapse/index.ts`), which calls
`App.component('NCollapseItem', NCollapseItem)`. The two are always
registered together — see `ai-docs/components/collapse.md`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sort` | `[Number, String]` | `null` | Component-local (`NCollapseItem.ts`) | Intended sort key. <!-- Currently unused by the render path — see collapse.md Gotchas: `NCollapseView.default()` never consumes the `sorted` list. --> |
| `name` | `String` | `'default'` | Component-local | The identity used for open/closed membership in the parent's `modelValue` array (`Arr.has`/`Arr.toggle`). Give every item in a given `NCollapse` a distinct value — see collapse.md Gotchas. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | Component-local | Header text, only used when no `label` slot is provided. |
| `icon` | `String` | `null` | Component-local | Icon name rendered before the label via `this.icon(data.icon)` (`ai-docs/icons.md` mechanism); omitted entirely (`null` render) when empty. |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `null` | Component-local | `null` = inherit the parent `NCollapse`'s `scrollbar` prop. Explicit `true`/`false` overrides it for this item only. |
| `lazy` | `Boolean` | `null` | Component-local | `null` = inherit the parent's `lazy`. See collapse.md Gotchas for the `lazy`/`keep` interaction. |
| `keep` | `Boolean` | `null` | Component-local | `null` = inherit the parent's `keep`. See collapse.md Gotchas. |

Note: `NCollapseItem` does **not** spread any of the shared `Props.*` mixins
(no `load`/`size`/`type`/`disabled`/etc.) — its prop list above is exhaustive.
`inheritAttrs: false` is also set on the component.

## Events

None — `NCollapseItem.ts` declares an empty `emits: []` array, and
`NCollapseItemController` never calls `this.emit(...)`. Its `superToggle()`/
`superOpen()`/`superClose()` methods delegate directly to the parent's
`ncx('collapse').superToggle(name)`, which is what actually fires the
parent's `update:modelValue`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The panel's body content. Only rendered while `isActive()` is true (see collapse.md's `lazy`/`keep` breakdown); hidden with inline `display:none` while mounted-but-closed. |
| `label` | none | Overrides the `label` prop as the header text. Checked directly via `context.slots.label ? context.slots.label() : data.label` (not through the `this.slot()` helper, but functionally equivalent — renders nothing extra if absent). |
| `action` | none | Extra content in the header's action area (e.g. a button), rendered only if the slot is actually provided (`context.slots.action` truthiness check gates it, unlike `label`/`default`). |

## Exposed methods

None — `NCollapseItemController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-collapse v-model="openPanels">
    <n-collapse-item name="panel-1" label="Panel 1">
        Content 1
    </n-collapse-item>
</n-collapse>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<n-collapse v-model="openPanels" :keep="true">
    <n-collapse-item name="details" icon="info-circle" :lazy="false">
        <template v-slot:label>
            <strong>Order details</strong>
        </template>
        <template v-slot:action>
            <n-button size="xs" type="secondary" @click.stop="refresh">Refresh</n-button>
        </template>
        <pre>{{ order }}</pre>
    </n-collapse-item>
</n-collapse>
```

## Required composition

**Strict pairing, same pattern as `NRadio`/`NRadioGroup`**: `NCollapseItem`
cannot be used outside an `NCollapse` ancestor (it `inject`s the `NCollapse`
context and dereferences it unconditionally in `setup()` — see
`ai-docs/components/collapse.md`'s "Required composition" for the exact
mechanism), and `NCollapse` should only contain `NCollapseItem` children.

## Common mistakes

- Relying on the `action` slot for something that must always render — it's
  gated by a slot-presence check and produces no wrapper element at all if
  omitted (unlike `label`, which always has the `label` prop as a fallback).
- Using `NCollapseItem` standalone (outside `<n-collapse>`) — it will error
  when `NCollapseItemController.setup()` tries to read
  `collapse.data.scrollbar` off an `undefined` inject result.
- Forgetting that clicking the header itself toggles the panel
  (`onPointerdown` on the whole header element) — nesting another clickable
  control (like the `action` slot's button) without `@click.stop` will also
  toggle the panel when that control is clicked.

## Gotchas

- `sort` is accepted as a prop and fed into `NCollapse`'s internal `sorted`
  computation, but that computation is never used to order the rendered
  output — see `ai-docs/components/collapse.md` Gotchas. Don't rely on it
  for visual ordering today.
- `name` defaults to the literal string `'default'`, not `null` or an
  auto-generated id — easy to miss if you copy an item without setting
  `name` explicitly.
- `disabled`/`size`/`type`/`color`/`theme` are not declared props here at
  all (no `Props.*` mixin spread), unlike most other nano-ui components —
  don't expect them to have any effect if passed.

## Related components

- `NCollapse` — the only valid parent; see `ai-docs/components/collapse.md`
  for the open/closed model, `sort` caveat, and `lazy`/`keep` semantics.

<!-- ===== components/collapse.md ===== -->

# NCollapse

The multi-panel accordion container: tracks which panel names are open as an
array `v-model`, and provides context (`NCollapse` inject key) that its
`NCollapseItem` children read to know if they're open and how to render.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **collapse** group index
(`src/collapse/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NCollapse', NCollapse)`
and `App.component('NCollapseItem', NCollapseItem)` together — both are
always registered as a pair.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` | Adds `n-load` to the root. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`. |
| `modelValue` | `Array` | `() => []` | Component-local (`NCollapse.ts`) | The list of currently-open panel `name`s. **Always multi-open** — see "Single vs. multiple open panels" below. |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `true` | Component-local | Default for child items' `scrollbar` (wraps panel content in `n-scrollbar` instead of a plain `<div>`). Each `NCollapseItem` can override this individually. |
| `lazy` | `Boolean` | `true` | Component-local | Default for child items' `lazy` (content isn't mounted until first opened). See gotchas on `lazy`/`keep` interaction. |
| `keep` | `Boolean` | `false` | Component-local | Default for child items' `keep` (once opened, content stays mounted — hidden via `display:none` rather than destroyed — when the panel closes). |
| `dragOpen` | `Boolean` | `true` | Component-local | If true, dragging something over a closed item's header (native `dragenter`) auto-opens that panel (`superFixed`, opens-only, never closes). Desktop drag-and-drop UX. |

## Single vs. multiple open panels

`NCollapse` **only supports multiple open panels** — there is no accordion /
single-open mode and no prop to switch modes. `modelValue` is always an
`Array` of open panel `name` strings. Toggling a panel
(`NCollapseController.superToggle(name)`) calls `Arr.toggle(clone(model),
name)` — i.e. it adds/removes just that one name from the array, with no
logic anywhere that closes other open panels. To emulate accordion (single-
open) behavior yourself, listen to `update:modelValue` and truncate the
array to its last entry before writing it back, or otherwise manage the
array externally.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `string[]` — the full new list of open panel names | A panel header is clicked (`superToggle`, via `NCollapseItem`'s `superToggle()` → `collapse.superToggle(name)`), or a drag-enter auto-opens a closed panel (`superFixed`, only adds, never removes). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Place `NCollapseItem` children here. Rendered as-is via `this.slot('default')` — see Gotchas about visual ordering. |

## Exposed methods

None — `NCollapseController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-collapse v-model="openPanels">
    <n-collapse-item name="panel-1" label="Panel 1">
        Content 1
    </n-collapse-item>
    <n-collapse-item name="panel-2" label="Panel 2">
        Content 2
    </n-collapse-item>
</n-collapse>
```

## Realistic example

Built from source (no demo files reference `n-collapse`/`n-collapse-item`):

```vue
<n-collapse v-model="openPanels" :keep="true" size="sm">
    <n-collapse-item name="general" label="General" icon="cog" sort="1">
        <n-input v-model="form.name" placeholder="Name"></n-input>
    </n-collapse-item>
    <n-collapse-item name="advanced" label="Advanced" icon="sliders" sort="2" :lazy="false">
        <template v-slot:action>
            <n-button size="xs" type="danger">Reset</n-button>
        </template>
        <n-input v-model="form.token" placeholder="API token"></n-input>
    </n-collapse-item>
</n-collapse>
```

```js
openPanels = ['general'];
```

## Required composition

**Strict pairing, same pattern as `NRadio`/`NRadioGroup`**: `NCollapse` may
only contain `NCollapseItem` children, and `NCollapseItem` cannot be used
outside an `NCollapse` ancestor. This is enforced structurally by
`inject`/`provide`: `NCollapseController.setup()` calls
`provide('NCollapse', this.instance)`, and `NCollapseItemController.setup()`
calls `this.injectRef(['collapse', 'NCollapse'])` and then immediately reads
`collapse.data.scrollbar`/`.lazy`/`.keep` — if no ancestor `NCollapse`
provided that key, `collapse` is `undefined` and this throws.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a `type`/`mode` prop (e.g. `accordion`) to restrict to one open
  panel at a time — no such prop exists; see "Single vs. multiple open
  panels" above.
- Assuming the `sort` prop on `NCollapseItem` controls visual order — it
  doesn't, in the current render path. See Gotchas.
- Putting non-`NCollapseItem` content directly in the default slot — nothing
  throws, but it won't participate in the open/close model or header/content
  chrome, and breaks the confirmed composition contract.

## Gotchas

- **`sort` / the `sorted` computed list appear to be dead code in the current
  render path.** `NCollapseController` maintains a `sorted` data value
  (`Arr.sort(this.childs, 'data.sort')`, updated via `watchChilds`/
  `watchData('modelValue', ...)`), and `NCollapseView` has an `items()` method
  that maps `data.sorted` to `item.view.display(scope)` — but
  `NCollapseView.default()` never calls `items()`; it renders
  `this.slot('default')` directly. So visual order is whatever DOM/template
  order you write `<n-collapse-item>` children in, **not** the `sort` prop
  value. <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether this is intentional (sort reserved for a
  future/alternate render path) or a bug — flagging per instructions rather
  than guessing. -->
- **`lazy`/`keep` interact non-trivially** (`NCollapseItemController.isActive()`):
  - `lazy: true, keep: false` (the defaults): content mounts on first open,
    unmounts (destroyed) when closed, and remounts fresh (loses state) next
    time it's opened.
  - `keep: true`: once opened, content stays mounted permanently (hidden with
    inline `display: none` when closed) — preserves component state (e.g. a
    form inside a panel) across collapses.
  - `lazy: false`: content mounts immediately on `NCollapse` render
    (regardless of open state), also without ever unmounting — functionally
    similar to `keep: true` but skips the "not yet opened" gate entirely.
- Per-item `scrollbar`/`lazy`/`keep` props default to `null`, which is a
  sentinel meaning "inherit from the parent `NCollapse`'s prop of the same
  name" (`NCollapseItemController.setup()` copies the parent's value in only
  when the local prop is `null`). Passing an explicit `true`/`false` on the
  item overrides the parent.
- `NCollapseItem`'s `name` prop defaults to the literal string `'default'`
  for every instance. If you don't give each item a distinct `name`, they
  all share `'default'` and open/close as one (`Arr.has`/`Arr.toggle`
  operate on that shared string), since the open/closed model is entirely
  name-based membership in the `modelValue` array.

## Related components

- `NCollapseItem` — the only valid child; see `ai-docs/components/collapse-item.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/config.md ===== -->

# NConfig

A JSON/object-driven dynamic renderer: pass a `config` tree describing
components, props, events, and slots, and `<n-config>` renders it via `h()` —
useful for server-driven or fully data-defined UI. Not related to the
`App.use(Install, ...)` install options — see `ai-docs/config.md` for that
distinction.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from `src/config/index.ts`
(`App.component('NConfig', NConfig)`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `modelValue` | `Object` | `null` | local | The data model made available to bound expressions as `$model`. |
| `extraValue` | `Object` | `null` | local | Extra context data made available as `$extra`. |
| `config` | `Object` | `null` | local | The render tree to interpret. Each key is an "alias" (the tag name to render, e.g. `'div'`, `'n-button'`, or `'my-alias: n-button'` — text after `:` is stripped before resolving the component, letting the same tag repeat under different keys), and each value is either a primitive/render-tree (nested `config`) or an object shaped `{ binds, props, events, content, slots, vIf, vAwait, vShow }`. |

`config` node shape (from `NConfigView.setup()`):

```ts
interface ConfigNode {
  binds?: Record<string, string | { value: string; fallback?: any }>; // two-way bound props: reads/writes into $scope/$model/$extra/$global
  props?: Record<string, any>;   // static or resolved props (see expression rules below)
  events?: Record<string, Function>; // handler always called with `this` = the NConfig-bound `scope` prop
  content?: ConfigNode | ConfigNode[] | string | Function; // default slot
  slots?: Record<string, ConfigNode | Function>;           // named slots
  vIf?: any;    // gate on NConfigController.propExists
  vAwait?: any; // gate on NConfigController.propAwait
  vShow?: any;  // if falsy, sets `style="display: none;"` instead of skipping render
}
```

Expression resolution (`NConfigController.getProp`/`getInput`/`getString`):
- A prop key starting with `!` is treated as a raw function passed through
  as-is (bound to call with `this.data.self` — see `scope` prop below).
- A string value containing `$scope`, `$model`, or `$global` is resolved
  against `{ $scope: <scope prop>, $model: <modelValue>, $extra: <extraValue>, $global: globalThis }`
  via `Obj.get`. Prefixing with `!!` coerces to boolean; `!` alone negates.
- A plain string with no `$`-prefix and no `@` prefix is used as a literal.
  A string starting with `@` is translated via `Locale.trans()` (pico-js
  i18n) — `@` itself is escaped as `\@`.
- A function value is called as `fn.call(this.data.self, this.data.model, fallback)`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `Object` | `null` | local | The `this` context (`$scope`) used when resolving `!`-prefixed functions/expressions and event handlers. |

## Events

None (`emits: []`).

## Slots

None — `NConfig` has no template-authored slots of its own; its entire
output comes from interpreting the `config` prop.

## Exposed methods

None.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-config :config="{ div: { content: 'Hello' } }" />
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<n-config
    :model-value="user"
    :scope="this"
    :config="{
        'n-button': {
            props: { type: 'primary', disabled: '$model.locked' },
            events: { click: onSave },
            content: '@Save',
            vIf: '$model.id',
        },
    }"
/>
```

## Required composition

None — standalone.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `config` is a plain Vue render-fn replacement with normal prop
  binding syntax — it isn't; static-looking prop values are still run
  through `getProp()`'s `$scope`/`$model`/`$global`/`@`-translation rules, so
  a literal string that happens to start with `@` or contain `$model` will
  be interpreted, not passed through literally.
- Forgetting `scope` — event handlers and `!`-prefixed expressions are bound
  to `this.data.self` (the `scope` prop), not to the calling component.

## Gotchas

- `content`/each `slots` entry accepts a bare string (rendered via
  `getString`, so `@`-prefixed strings translate), a function, or a nested
  config node/array — `NConfigView.child()` decides which based on type.
- Built-in raw tags `div`, `a`, `p`, `span`, `iframe` skip `resolveComponent`
  entirely; every other alias must resolve to a globally registered
  component or `NConfigView.setup()` returns `null` silently.

## Related components

None specific — this is a general-purpose dynamic renderer, unrelated to any
other component group.


---

<!-- ===== components/datepicker-panel.md ===== -->

# NDatepickerPanel

The calendar grid UI (month/year/date views, single or range selection) — confirmed to be **both** a standalone, directly-usable inline-calendar component **and** the exact component `NDatepicker`/`NDatetimepicker` render internally inside their popovers.

Confirmation: `demos/overview.html` uses it standalone, outside any popover, at top level (`<n-datepicker-panel v-bind="n_datepicker" min-date="now" :panels="2" :range="true">`). Separately, `NDatepickerView.panel()` (`src/datetime/js/datepicker/NDatepickerView.ts`) and `NDatetimepickerView.datepicker()` (`src/datetime/js/datetimepicker/NDatetimepickerView.ts`) both render it via `this.comp('n-datepicker-panel', props)` inside their own popovers, forwarding a subset of their own props straight through.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/datetime/index.ts` as `NDatepickerPanel` (`App.component(NDatepickerPanel.name, NDatepickerPanel)`). Source: `src/datetime/js/datepicker-panel/{NDatepickerPanel,NDatepickerPanelController,NDatepickerPanelData,NDatepickerPanelView}.ts`. `NDatepickerPanelController` extends `GroupController` (`src/root/js/controller/GroupController.ts`, see concepts.md) — note it never actually calls `append`/`remove`/`watchChilds` itself (see "Gotchas").

## Props

`NDatepickerPanelProps` (`src/datetime/js/datepicker-panel/NDatepickerPanel.ts`):

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shows the built-in loading state. |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Subject to `superDisabled` (concepts.md). |
| `modelValue` | `[Array, String]` | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | A formatted date string in single mode, or `[arriveString, departString]` in `range` mode. See `datepicker.md`'s "Common mistakes" — same rule applies here. |
| `arrive` | `[String]` | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Independently-bindable range start value. |
| `clearArrive` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Reserved for consumers wiring their own clear UI (the panel itself has no built-in clear button — that lives on `NDatepicker`). |
| `depart` | `[String]` | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Independently-bindable range end value. |
| `clearDepart` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Same note as `clearArrive`. |
| `range` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Enables two-click range selection in the day grid instead of single-click date selection. |
| `panels` | `Number` | `1` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Number of side-by-side month grids rendered. |
| `format` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Format `modelValue`/`arrive`/`depart` are written back as when a day is clicked. |
| `minDate` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Earliest selectable day; disabled days below it get an `n-disabled` class (no click handler is removed — see "Gotchas"). |
| `maxDate` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanel.ts` (own prop) | Latest selectable day, same caveat as `minDate`. |

Note: `NDatepickerPanel` has **no** `clearable`/`clearValue`/`position`/`placeholder*`/`displayFormat`/`icon` props — those are `NDatepicker`-only, added on top when it wraps this panel in a popover+text-input.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | formatted date string (single mode) or `[arriveString, departString]` (range mode) | Single mode: clicking any day (`setRangeDate(date)` → `setModelDate(date)`). Range mode: clicking the second day of a range (`setRangeDate(date)` → `setModelRange(temp)`). |
| `update:arrive` | formatted date string | Range mode only, fired together with `update:modelValue` from `setModelRange(dates)` when the second day of a range is clicked. |
| `update:depart` | formatted date string | Range mode only, fired together with `update:modelValue` from `setModelRange(dates)`, same trigger as `update:arrive`. |

Clicking a month (in the "months" sub-view) or a year (in the "years" sub-view) does **not** emit any `update:*` event — it only calls `setPanelDate(item)`, which repositions the visible calendar and switches back to the "dates" view; it does not select/commit a value.

## Slots

None. `NDatepickerPanelView` never calls `this.slot(...)`.

## Exposed methods

None. `NDatepickerPanelController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-datepicker-panel v-model="date" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const date = ref(null);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` — a standalone inline range calendar with two month panels and a floor date:

```vue
<template>
  <n-datepicker-panel
    v-model:arrive="stay.arrive"
    v-model:depart="stay.depart"
    min-date="now"
    :panels="2"
    :range="true"
    size="md"
    type="primary"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const stay = reactive({ arrive: null, depart: null });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — usable standalone (as shown above), with no required parent. It is also composed internally, without any special setup required from the consumer, by `NDatepicker` (inside a popover, single or two-input mode) and by `NDatetimepicker` (inside a popover, alongside `NTimepickerPanel`). Optionally, like other pickers, an app can nest it (or its `NDatepicker` wrapper) inside `<n-button-group>` purely for grouped layout — not a requirement.

## Common mistakes

- **Assuming `modelValue` is a `Date` object.** As with `NDatepicker`, it is always a **string** (or a 2-string array in `range` mode), formatted per the `format` prop (default `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'`) — never a `Date`, and not affected by `displayFormat` (this component doesn't have a `displayFormat` prop at all; that's `NDatepicker`-only).
- **Expecting a single click to finish a range.** In `range: true` mode, the first click only stages `ranges`/`hovers` locally — no `update:*` fires until the second click resolves the pair via `setModelRange`.
- **Expecting `minDate`/`maxDate` to block clicks.** They only add an `n-disabled` CSS class to out-of-bounds days (`NDatepickerPanelView.date()`); the `onPointerdown` handler is still attached, so blocking the actual click is left to CSS (`pointer-events`) in the consuming app's theme, not JS.

## Gotchas

- `NDatepickerPanelController.onMousedown(item)` exists but is **dead code** — no element in `NDatepickerPanelView` wires up `onPointerdown`/`onClick` to call it. The real per-day click handler is `setRangeDate(date)` (bound in `NDatepickerPanelView.date()`).
- `NDatepickerPanelController` extends `GroupController` (adds `childs`/`append`/`remove`/`watchChilds`), but this file never calls any of those — <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether this base class choice is vestigial or used by some other integration point not present in this file. -->
- The header's month/year labels are clickable and switch `view` to `'months'`/`'years'` respectively; a "Go back" footer button (rendered via `this.comp('n-button', ...)`, calling `onRevert()`) only appears once you're in one of those sub-views — it resets `view` back to `'dates'` and re-centers on `displays[0]`'s original position via `setDisplayDates()`.
- `range` selection swaps arrive/depart order automatically if you click an earlier date second (`if (date.before(temp[0])) temp = temp.reverse()` in `setRangeDate`), so `arrive` is always guaranteed ≤ `depart` regardless of click order.

## Related components

- `NDatepicker` — wraps this panel in a popover with a text input; see `datepicker.md`.
- `NDatetimepicker` — composes this panel together with `NTimepickerPanel` inside one popover; see `datetimepicker.md`.
