<!-- ===== components/datepicker.md ===== -->

# NDatepicker

A text-input date field that opens a popover calendar (internally an `NDatepickerPanel`) for picking a single date or a `arrive`/`depart` date range.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/datetime/index.ts` as `NDatepicker` (`App.component(NDatepicker.name, NDatepicker)`). Source: `src/datetime/js/datepicker/{NDatepicker,NDatepickerController,NDatepickerData,NDatepickerView}.ts`. `NDatepickerController` extends `NPopoverPanelController` (`src/popover/js/popover-panel/NPopoverPanelController.ts`) — the same base used by `NSelect`/other popover-driven inputs (see concepts.md's Controller/Data/View section for the shared `ProtoController` API this inherits, e.g. `applyClear()`, `onFocus`/`onBlur`).

## Props

`NDatepickerProps` (`src/datetime/js/datepicker/NDatepicker.ts`) is built from `...NDatepickerPanelProps` (see `datepicker-panel.md`) plus its own additions below. The full effective prop set is the union of both tables.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (via `NDatepickerPanelProps`) | Shows the built-in loading state. |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (via `NDatepickerPanelProps`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (via `NDatepickerPanelProps`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (via `NDatepickerPanelProps`) | Subject to `superDisabled` (concepts.md). |
| `modelValue` | `[Array, String]` | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` (own decl there) | See "Common mistakes" — always read back as a **formatted string** (single mode) or a **2-element array of formatted strings** (`range: true`), never a `Date`. |
| `arrive` | `[String]` | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | The range's start-date v-model (formatted string). Only meaningful when `range: true`. |
| `clearArrive` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | Value `arrive` resets to on clear, in range mode. |
| `depart` | `[String]` | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | The range's end-date v-model (formatted string). Only meaningful when `range: true`. |
| `clearDepart` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | Value `depart` resets to on clear, in range mode. |
| `range` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | Switches from a single date field to two (`arrive`/`depart`) inputs plus range-selection behavior in the panel. |
| `panels` | `Number` | `1` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | Number of side-by-side month panels rendered in the popover calendar. |
| `format` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | The format `modelValue`/`arrive`/`depart` are **written back** as (via `Now#format()`). Distinct from `displayFormat` below — see "Gotchas". |
| `minDate` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | Earliest selectable date. Accepts anything `Now.make()` accepts (`Date`, `Now` instance, ISO string, or a pico-js relative expression like `"now"` — confirmed via `demos/overview.html`'s `min-date="now"`). |
| `maxDate` | any | `null` | `NDatepickerPanelProps` | Latest selectable date, same accepted forms as `minDate`. |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (own spread) | Shows the built-in clear (×) button when a value is present. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (own spread) | Non-range clear target for `modelValue` (see `applyClear()`; in range mode `clearArrive`/`clearDepart` are used instead). |
| `position` | `String`, validated against the 12-value popover position set | `'bottom-start'` | `Props.PositionBottomStart` (own spread) | Popover placement; full enum in concepts.md. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Select date'` | `NDatepicker.ts` (own prop) | Placeholder for the single (non-range) input. |
| `placeholderArrive` | `String` | `'Start date'` | `NDatepicker.ts` (own prop) | Placeholder for the `arrive` input in range mode. |
| `placeholderDepart` | `String` | `'End date'` | `NDatepicker.ts` (own prop) | Placeholder for the `depart` input in range mode. |
| `rangeSeperator` | `String` | `'-'` | `NDatepicker.ts` (own prop) | Text rendered between the arrive/depart inputs in range mode. |
| `displayFormat` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD'` | `NDatepicker.ts` (own prop) | Format used to **parse the typed text** and to **render the text field(s)**. Distinct from `format` — see "Gotchas". |
| `icon` | `String` | `() => Styler.icon('calendar')` | `NDatepicker.ts` (own prop, **not** `Props.Icon`) | Icon shown in the field handle; rendered via `NPopoverPanelView.handle()`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | a formatted date string, or `[arriveString, departString]` when `range: true` | User presses Enter in the text input (`onInput()`), commits an arrive/depart input (`onArrive()`/`onDepart()`, which also re-emits `modelValue` as the pair), clicks the clear button (`applyClear()`), or picks a date in the internal calendar panel (bubbled from `NDatepickerPanel`'s own `update:modelValue`). |
| `update:arrive` | formatted date string | Only in `range: true` mode: user commits the arrive text input (`onArrive()`), calls clear (`applyClear()`), or picks a range start/end in the panel (bubbled from `NDatepickerPanel`). |
| `update:depart` | formatted date string | Only in `range: true` mode: user commits the depart text input (`onDepart()`), calls clear (`applyClear()`), or completes a range pick in the panel (bubbled from `NDatepickerPanel`). |

## Slots

None. `NDatepickerView` overrides `NPopoverPanelView.panel()` to always render the internal `n-datepicker-panel` component directly — it does not fall through to `this.slot('panel')` like the base `NPopoverPanelView` does.

## Exposed methods

None. `NDatepickerController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-datepicker v-model="date" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const date = ref(null);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/datepicker/index.html` and `demos/overview.html` — a single date field with clear, and a separate arrive/depart range field:

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item label="Date">
      <n-datepicker v-model="form.date" :clearable="true" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Stay">
      <n-datepicker
        v-model:arrive="form.arrive"
        v-model:depart="form.depart"
        :range="true"
        :clearable="true"
      />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';

const form = reactive({
  date: 'now+2days',
  arrive: 'now',
  depart: 'now+2days',
});
</script>
```

Note: `demos/datepicker/index.html` is a legacy Vue 2 demo and uses `:arrive.sync="form.arrive"` — the Vue 3 equivalent shown above is `v-model:arrive`/`v-model:depart`.

## Required composition

None required — `NDatepicker` is self-contained (it renders its own internal popover and calendar panel). Optionally, it can be placed inside `<n-button-group>` alongside `NTimepicker`/other pickers purely for grouped visual layout (confirmed pattern in `demos/overview.html`: `<n-button-group><n-datepicker .../><n-timepicker .../></n-button-group>`) — this is not a requirement of either component.

## Common mistakes

- **Assuming `modelValue` is a `Date` object.** It is not. Every write-back (`onInput`, `onArrive`, `onDepart`, `applyClear`, or a panel click) sets `modelValue` to a **string** formatted via `format` (default `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'`), or to a **2-element string array** `[arrive, depart]` when `range: true`. You may hand it a `Date`, a pico-js `Now` instance, or a compatible string on the way in (`NDateHelper.getDate`/`getDates` pass it through `Now.make()`), but always expect a string/array back out.
- **Confusing `format` with `displayFormat`.** `displayFormat` (default `'YYYY-MM-DD'`) controls what's shown in the text input and how typed text is parsed (`Now.make(data.input, data.displayFormat)`). `format` (default `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'`) controls what's actually written to `modelValue`/`arrive`/`depart`. With the defaults, typing `2026-08-25` and pressing Enter emits `"2026-08-25 00:00:00"`, not `"2026-08-25"`.
- **Wiring only `v-model` in range mode.** `range: true` needs `arrive`/`depart` handled too if you want the two text fields to be independently bindable — `modelValue` alone still receives `[arriveString, departString]`, but `update:arrive`/`update:depart` are separate events (`v-model:arrive`, `v-model:depart`).

## Gotchas

- Reading an externally-supplied `modelValue`/`arrive`/`depart` string always goes through `NDateHelper.getDate`/`getDates`, which calls `Now.make(value)` **without** passing the `format` prop — parsing relies on pico-js's default format (`'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'`) plus its ISO-date/relative-expression detection, not on your custom `format` value. <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact fallback parsing behavior for a customized `format` whose string doesn't match the default pattern or ISO — confirmed only that the `format` prop itself is never passed into these `Now.make()` calls. -->
- `minDate`/`maxDate` accept pico-js relative-date expressions (e.g. `"now"`), not just literal date strings/`Date` objects — see `demos/overview.html`'s `min-date="now"`.
- In range mode, the popover requires two day-clicks to commit a range; the first click only updates internal hover/preview state (no `update:*` emitted) — see `datepicker-panel.md`'s Gotchas for the full click sequence.
- Pressing Tab in the `depart` input blurs/closes the popover (`onBlur()`); pressing Tab in the `arrive` input does not — only Enter commits the arrive value.

## Related components

- `NDatepickerPanel` — the calendar UI `NDatepicker` renders inside its popover (also usable standalone; see `datepicker-panel.md`).
- `NDatetimepicker` — the date+time counterpart, composing `NDatepickerPanel` and `NTimepickerPanel` together (see `datetimepicker.md`).
- `NTimepicker` — analogous single-purpose time field, commonly paired with `NDatepicker` inside `NButtonGroup`.


---

<!-- ===== components/datetimepicker.md ===== -->

# NDatetimepicker

A text-input date-and-time field that opens a popover containing an internal `NDatepickerPanel` (calendar) and `NTimepickerPanel` (time list) side by side; no range mode (no `arrive`/`depart`).

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/datetime/index.ts` as `NDatetimepicker` (`App.component(NDatetimepicker.name, NDatetimepicker)`). Source: `src/datetime/js/datetimepicker/{NDatetimepicker,NDatetimepickerController,NDatetimepickerData,NDatetimepickerView}.ts`. `NDatetimepickerController` extends `NPopoverPanelController` (same base as `NDatepicker`; see `datepicker.md` and concepts.md).

## Props

`NDatetimepickerProps` (`src/datetime/js/datetimepicker/NDatetimepicker.ts`):

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Subject to `superDisabled` (concepts.md). |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shows the built-in clear (×) button. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Value `modelValue` resets to on clear; also forwarded as-is into both internal panels. |
| `position` | `String`, validated against the 12-value popover position set | `'bottom-start'` | `Props.PositionBottomStart` (`PositionProps.ts`) | Popover placement; full enum in concepts.md. |
| `modelValue` | untyped (no `type` key) | `null` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | See "Common mistakes" — always read back as a **formatted string**, never a `Date`, despite the untyped declaration. |
| `minDate` | any | `null` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | Earliest selectable date/time; forwarded to the internal `NDatepickerPanel`. Accepts anything `Now.make()` accepts, including relative expressions like `"now"`. |
| `maxDate` | any | `null` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | Latest selectable date/time, same as `minDate`. |
| `panels` | `Number` | `1` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | Number of side-by-side month grids in the internal calendar panel. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Select datetime'` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | Placeholder for the text input. |
| `format` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | Format `modelValue` is **written back** as. Forwarded unchanged to both the internal `NDatepickerPanel` and `NTimepickerPanel`, so it must contain both date and time tokens for both sub-panels to parse/format it meaningfully. |
| `displayFormat` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop) | Format used to parse the typed text and render the text field. Unlike `NDatepicker`, this defaults to the **same** value as `format` (both full date+time). |
| `icon` | `String` | `() => Styler.icon('calendar')` | `NDatetimepicker.ts` (own prop, **not** `Props.Icon`) | Icon shown in the field handle. |

Note: unlike `NDatepicker`, `NDatetimepickerProps` does **not** spread `NDatepickerPanelProps` — it declares its own `modelValue`/`minDate`/`maxDate`/`panels`/`format`/`displayFormat`, and has no `range`/`arrive`/`depart`/`rangeSeperator`/`placeholderArrive`/`placeholderDepart` props at all.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | a formatted datetime string | User presses Enter in the text input (`onInput()`), clicks the clear button (`applyClear()`, inherited from `ProtoController`), picks a date in the internal calendar (bubbled from `n-datepicker-panel`'s `update:modelValue`), or picks a time in the internal time list (bubbled from `n-timepicker-panel`'s `update:modelValue`). |

This is the only emit declared (`emits: ['update:modelValue']`) — there is no `update:arrive`/`update:depart` on this component.

## Slots

None. `NDatetimepickerView` overrides `NPopoverPanelView.panel()` to always render its own `datepicker()` + `timepicker()` pair directly — it does not fall through to `this.slot('panel')`.

## Exposed methods

None. `NDatetimepickerController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-datetimepicker v-model="value" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const value = ref(null);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html`'s options pattern (size/type/clearable/disabled all bindable):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item label="Appointment">
      <n-datetimepicker
        v-model="form.appointment"
        size="md"
        type="primary"
        :clearable="true"
      />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ appointment: 'now+2days' });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None required from the consumer — `NDatetimepicker` is self-contained: it composes `NDatepickerPanel` and `NTimepickerPanel` internally inside its own popover (`NDatetimepickerView.panel()` renders both, forwarding `modelValue`/`clearValue`/`format` — plus `panels`/`minDate`/`maxDate` to the date side only). Optionally, like `NDatepicker`, it can be placed inside `<n-button-group>` alongside other pickers purely for grouped layout — not a requirement, and not directly demonstrated for this specific component in `demos/`.

## Common mistakes

- **Assuming `modelValue` is a `Date` object.** The prop is declared with no `type` restriction at all (`{ default: null }`), which can read as "accepts anything," but the only value the component ever actually writes back via `update:modelValue` is a **string**, formatted per the `format` prop (default `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'`). Feed it a `Date`/`Now`/compatible string on the way in; expect a string on the way out.
- **Setting `format`/`displayFormat` to a date-only pattern (e.g. `'YYYY-MM-DD'`).** Both default to a full date+time pattern and both are forwarded to the internal `NTimepickerPanel`; a date-only `format` would strip time information out of every written value.
- **Expecting a `range` prop.** `NDatetimepicker` has no range mode — use `NDatepicker` with `range: true` for a date range, or two separate `NDatetimepicker`s if you need a datetime range.

## Gotchas

- The same `modelValue` (and `clearValue`/`format`) is passed straight through to **both** internal panels (`NDatepickerPanelView`'s date grid and `NTimepickerPanel`'s time list) — each panel parses out and updates only the portion it cares about, but both receive the whole formatted string on every change, and either one's click can independently trigger `update:modelValue` on the outer `NDatetimepicker`.
- As with `NDatepicker`, reading an externally-supplied `modelValue` goes through `NDateHelper.getDate()`, which calls `Now.make(value)` without passing the `format` prop — parsing relies on pico-js's default format/relative-expression detection, not your custom `format`. <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact fallback parsing behavior for a customized `format` that doesn't match ISO or the default pattern. -->
- `minDate`/`maxDate` are only forwarded to the date panel, not the time panel — there is no way to restrict selectable *times* on a given day through this component's props.

## Related components

- `NDatepickerPanel` — the calendar half of the internal popover; see `datepicker-panel.md`.
- `NDatepicker` — the date-only counterpart (also supports `range`); see `datepicker.md`.
- `NTimepickerPanel` / `NTimepicker` — the time-selection half composed inside this component's popover (documented separately, outside this batch).

<!-- ===== components/draglist.md ===== -->

# NDraglist

A virtualized, drag-and-drop-enabled tree/list view (also usable as a grid via `grid: true`) for reordering, nesting, selecting, and expanding hierarchical items.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally as `NDraglist` (template tag `<n-draglist>`) by
`src/draggable/index.ts` via `App.component(NDraglist.name, NDraglist)`.
Source: `src/draggable/js/draglist/NDraglist.ts` (`defineComponent`),
`NDraglistController.ts`, `NDraglistData.ts`, `NDraglistView.ts` — see
`ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern.

There is no separate `NDraggrid` registration — "grid mode" is the same
`NDraglist` component with `grid: true`. Internally the View switches its BEM
root from `n-draglist`/`n-draglist-item` to `n-draggrid`/`n-draggrid-item`
when `data.grid` is true (`NDraglistView.ts` `default()`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See `ai-docs/concepts.md` ("Type and Size are open strings"). |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same as above. |
| `items` | `Array` | `() => []` | `Props.Draglist` (`DragProps.ts`) | The tree data. See "Items tree shape" below. |
| `current` | `Object` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | Currently-focused/active node's raw item object. `v-model:current`-able (`update:current` is emitted, but see the Events table — one reset path does **not** emit). Cloned locally via `cloneProp` at setup. |
| `selected` | `Array` | `() => []` | `Props.Draglist` | Array of selected node **uids** (the value of `uniqueProp` for each selected item, not the item objects themselves). `v-model:selected`-able. |
| `expanded` | `Array` | `() => []` | `Props.Draglist` | Array of expanded node uids (controls which children are visible — see `NVirtualHelper.visibles()`). `v-model:expanded`-able. |
| `cascade` | `Array` | `() => []` | `Props.Draglist` | Array of uids describing the "path" to the current node (root → leaf), used to derive/restore `current` on mount and updated on click/keyboard nav. `v-model:cascade`-able. |
| `group` | `Array` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | Drag-group identity/identities this list belongs to; if `null`, defaults to `[this.uid]` (a component-generated unique id) at setup — see `NDraglistController.setup()`. |
| `allowGroups` | `Array` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | Groups this list will *accept drops from*; if `null`, defaults to the resolved `group` value at setup. A drag from a source list is rejected outright (`onDragmove` returns early) unless `Arr.has(config.group, data.allowGroups)` is true. |
| `safezone` | `Number \| Function` | `0.6` | `Props.Draglist` | Fraction of a node's height/width (or a custom `(size, ...) => number` function) treated as the "before/after" edge band vs. the "inside" center band when computing drop mode — see `NDragReciever.getMode()`. |
| `allowCurrent` | `Boolean` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Whether the `n-current` CSS class is applied to the node matching `current` (purely a rendering toggle in `NDraglistView.node()`, does not block the `current` update itself). |
| `renderHandle` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Renders a dedicated `__handle` drag-grip element per node and moves `draggable` off the row root onto the handle. See "Gotchas" — the `header_handle()` header counterpart is dead code. |
| `renderExpand` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Renders a per-node expand/collapse angle icon (only for nodes with children — see `value.childs` on the virtual node). |
| `renderSelect` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Renders a per-node checkbox. **Does not** render a "select all" header checkbox in the current build — see "Gotchas". |
| `allowSelect` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Gates whether a node's checkbox is interactive (`n-disabled` class applied via `nodeAllowSelect()` when false). When a function: called as `allowSelect({ value, item })`. <!-- UNVERIFIED: `nodeAllowSelect()` only calls the function form after first checking `data.relation.depth` matches the node's depth — cross-depth selection is blocked structurally regardless of `allowSelect`'s return value, so `allowSelect` only fine-tunes within-depth selectability. --> |
| `allowDrag` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Gates the DOM `draggable` attribute per node (and per handle, when `renderHandle` is true). When a function: called as `allowDrag({ value })`. |
| `allowDrop` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Gates whether a pending drop is accepted (sets `result.mode = 'deny'` when false). When a function: called once per dragged item as `allowDrop(node, target, mode)` where `node = { value, item }` (dragged item) and `target` is the same shape for the hovered node (or `null` for a root/append drop); **all** dragged items must pass for the drop to be allowed (`nodeAllowDrop()` in `NDraglistController.ts`). |
| `transformDrop` | `Function` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | `(item) => item`, applied to each dragged item's raw data right before it's spliced into the target tree on drop (`onDragdrop()`); e.g. reassigning a fresh id so a "copy" doesn't collide. If not a function, defaults to identity. |
| `insertNode` | `Boolean` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | If false, `NDragHelper`'s append/inside/before/after operations become no-ops (item is not spliced into the destination tree) — use to build a drop target that only reports the event without mutating the list. |
| `removeNode` | `Boolean` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | If false, `NDragHelper.unlinkNodes()`/`removeNodes()` become no-ops (dragged item is not stripped out of the source tree) — pairs with `insertNode: false` on the source to implement copy-instead-of-move. |
| `uniqueProp` | `String` | `'id'` | `Props.Draglist` | Dot-path key read off each raw item to get its unique id. |
| `childProp` | `String` | `'children'` | `Props.Draglist` | Dot-path key read off each raw item to get its child array. |
| `itemSkip` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | If true, `nodeDragmove()` short-circuits and returns the raw zone-level result unchanged — effectively disables node-level (before/inside/after) drop targeting, leaving only zone-level `append` drops. |
| `rootSkip` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | If true, `onDragmove()` skips computing the zone-level `append` fallback result — effectively disables dropping directly onto the list's empty/root area, leaving only node-level drops. |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No items')` | `Props.EmptyText` (`TextProps.ts`) | Passed through to the internal `n-virtualbar`'s empty state. |
| `emptyProps` | `Object` | `{ inline: false }` | `Props.EmptyPropsStacked` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Passed through to the internal `n-virtualbar`'s empty state. |
| `grid` | `Boolean` | `false` | Local (`NDraglist.ts`) | Switches BEM root/behavior to grid mode (`n-draggrid`) and is forwarded to the drag-mode calculation (`grid` affects axis used in `NDragReciever.getMode()` — X axis in grid mode vs. Y axis in list mode). |
| `itemHeight` | `Number` | `32` | Local | Row height forwarded to the internal `n-virtualbar` for virtualization math. |
| `itemWidth` | `Number` | `120` | Local | Grid cell width, forwarded to `n-virtualbar`; also used to compute per-depth indentation is **not** this — indentation uses `itemOffset`, not `itemWidth`. |
| `itemOffset` | `Number` | `30` | Local | Pixels of left-indent per tree depth level (`node_spacer()`), and also used as the drop-target's horizontal offset compensation for indented rows during drag (`nodeDragmove()`). |
| `scrollPortal` | `Boolean` | `false` | Local | Forwarded to the internal `n-virtualbar` (controls whether its scrollbar renders through a teleport/portal). <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact `n-virtualbar` behavior — out of scope for this doc. --> |

### Items tree shape

Each entry in `items` (and recursively in each entry's `childProp`, `'children'` by default) is a plain object with at least:

```ts
interface DraglistNode {
    [uniqueProp]: string | number;   // default key: 'id' — must be unique across the whole tree
    [childProp]?: DraglistNode[];    // default key: 'children' — omit or [] for leaf nodes
    // ...any other fields your row template needs
}
```

Concrete example (confirmed real usage, `demos/overview.html`):

```js
const virtualTree = [
    {
        id: 'a1b2c3',          // uniqueProp
        label: 'Item 1',
        value: 'a1b2c3',
        matrix: 10,
        image: 'https://picsum.photos/600/600.jpg',
        enabled: true,
        children: [            // childProp
            { id: 'd4e5f6', label: 'Item 2', children: [] },
            { id: 'g7h8i9', label: 'Item 3', children: [] },
        ],
    },
    // ...more root nodes
];
```

Internally, `NVirtualHelper.virtuals()` walks this tree once (on `items`
change) into a flat list of lightweight "virtual" node descriptors —
`{ uid, index, depth, route, cascade, parent, childs, total }` — where
`route` is the exact array-index path into `items` (e.g.
`['items', 0, 'children', 1]`) used internally to read/write the real node
via `Obj.get`/`Obj.set`. This flat list (`data.virtuals`, further filtered by
`expanded` into `data.visibles`) is what actually drives rendering and drop
math — the raw `items` tree is only spliced into at drop-time.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:items` | `(items: DraglistNode[])` — a full clone of the tree after mutation | A drop is accepted and mutates the tree (`onDragdrop`, when `result.mode` is one of `append`/`inside`/`before`/`after`), and also when a drag that originated from this list ends inside a *different* zone (`onDragend`, to strip the moved nodes out of the source). |
| `move` | `(uid, ids, options)` — see below | Only from `onDragdrop` (the *destination* list/dropzone of a successful drop), right after `update:items`. |
| `update:selected` | `(uids: (string\|number)[])` | Checkbox click (`onSelectclick`), select-all (`selectAll()`), and reset to `[]` after any successful drop or drag-end. |
| `update:current` | `(item: object)` | Row click (`onCurrentclick`), keyboard up/down/left/right navigation (`setPrevCurrent`/`setNextCurrent`), `setTotalCurrent()`, and internal cascade-restore (`buildCurrent()`). **Not** fired when `current` is reset to `null` after a drop/drag-end — that reset uses the non-emitting `set()`, not `update()`, so `v-model:current` will appear "stuck" showing the old item's data even though internal state is `null`. |
| `update:expanded` | `(uids: (string\|number)[])` | Expand/collapse angle click (`onExpandclick`). |
| `update:cascade` | `(cascade: (string\|number)[])` | Row click when the clicked node's ancestor path differs from the current `cascade` (`onCurrentclick`), and keyboard/`setTotalCurrent` navigation. |
| `row-click` | `(item: object, e: MouseEvent)` | Any row is clicked. `item` is `data.current` **read immediately after** the click also ran `onCurrentclick`, so in practice it is the just-clicked item's raw data. |
| `node-click` | `({ value, item }, e: MouseEvent)` | Same click, richer payload: `value` is the clicked node's virtual descriptor (`uid`/`index`/`depth`/`route`/`cascade`/`parent`/`childs`/`total`), `item` is the same raw data as `row-click`'s payload. |
| `row-dblclick` | `(item: object, e: MouseEvent)` | Any row is double-clicked (fires alongside the two preceding `click`/`row-click` events per normal DOM dblclick semantics). |
| `node-dblclick` | `({ value, item }, e: MouseEvent)` | Same double-click, richer payload (same shape as `node-click`). |

### `move` event payload detail

Emitted as `emit('move', targetUid, ids, options)` from `onDragdrop` in
`NDraglistController.ts`:

- `targetUid` — for `inside`/`before`/`after` drops, the **uid of the node the
  drop was targeted at** (the new parent, for `inside`; the new sibling
  reference point, for `before`/`after`). For an `append` drop (dropped onto
  empty zone space, no specific node target), this is instead whatever uid
  was recorded at drag-start — in practice the **source** zone's own
  component uid, not an item id. <!-- UNVERIFIED: this asymmetry is traced
  directly from `config.uid` reuse in `onDragdrop()`, but its intended
  semantics for `append` mode aren't documented in source — treat `targetUid`
  as reliable only for `inside`/`before`/`after`. -->
- `ids` — array of the **uids of the dragged items** (`config.items` mapped
  through `value.uid`), i.e. what moved.
- `options` — `{ uids: {zone, item}, mode, target, grid, type, group, items, item }`:
  - `mode`: `'append' | 'inside' | 'before' | 'after'` (the only modes that
    reach `move` — `deny`/`self`/`ignore` never get this far).
  - `group`: the dragged group id(s) (clone of the source's `group` prop at drag-start).
  - `items`: array of `{ value, item }` pairs for every dragged node (richer than `ids`).
  - `item`: the resolved target item object — the new parent object for
    `inside`, the parent of the reference sibling for `before`/`after`, or
    `null`/`fallback` for `append` (root-level drop).

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | `{ value, item }` — `value` is the node's virtual descriptor (`uid`, `index`, `depth`, `route`, `cascade`, `parent`, `childs`, `total`); `item` is the raw tree-node object (`Obj.get(data, value.route)`) | Renders the content of each row/cell. Called once per **visible** node (`data.visibles`, i.e. respecting `expanded`), via the internal `n-virtualbar`'s virtualized item slot. There is no separate header/footer slot. |

No other slots exist. `NDraglistView.node_element()` builds a local `passed`
object that additionally includes `copy()`/`remove()` callbacks, but **they
are never passed to the slot** — only `{ value, item }` reaches
`context.slots.default(...)`. Do not rely on `copy`/`remove` in your slot
template (see "Gotchas").

## Exposed methods

None. No `pass()`/`context.expose()` calls exist in `NDraglistController.ts`,
so a template `ref` on `<n-draglist>` does not get bound access to controller
methods like `getItemById`/`getParentById`/`selectAll`/`scrollToIndex` in the
current Vue 3 build. <!-- UNVERIFIED: the legacy Vue 2 demo
(`demos/draggable/index.html`) calls `this.$refs.drag.getParentById(...)`
directly, which implies some prior build exposed the controller on the
template ref (or exposed it by default under Vue 2's options-API instance
model). That demo also references `n-draglist-tree`, `slot-scope`, and props
(`viewport-height`, `threshold`) that do not exist anywhere in the current
`src/`, so it reflects a different, older API surface — do not treat it as
current behavior. -->

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
    <n-draglist v-model:items="items">
        <template #default="{ item }">
            {{ item.label }}
        </template>
    </n-draglist>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const items = ref([
    { id: '1', label: 'First', children: [] },
    { id: '2', label: 'Second', children: [] },
]);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Nested tree with drag handles, expand/collapse, checkboxes, and a `move`
listener (shape closely follows `demos/overview.html`):

```vue
<template>
    <n-draglist
        v-model:items="tree"
        v-model:selected="selected"
        v-model:expanded="expanded"
        :group="['project-tree']"
        :render-handle="true"
        :render-expand="true"
        :render-select="true"
        :safezone="0.3"
        :item-offset="24"
        style="height: 400px;"
        @move="onMove"
    >
        <template #default="{ value, item }">
            <div :style="{ lineHeight: '32px' }">
                {{ item.label }} <small v-if="value.childs">({{ value.childs }})</small>
            </div>
        </template>
    </n-draglist>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const tree = ref([
    {
        id: 'folder-1',
        label: 'Folder 1',
        children: [
            { id: 'file-1', label: 'File 1', children: [] },
            { id: 'file-2', label: 'File 2', children: [] },
        ],
    },
    { id: 'file-3', label: 'File 3', children: [] },
]);

const selected = ref([]);
const expanded = ref(['folder-1']);

function onMove(targetUid, ids, options) {
    console.log('moved', ids, 'to', targetUid, options.mode);
}
</script>
```

## Required composition

None confirmed. `NDraglist` runs standalone via the global `NDragHandler`
pub/sub (window-level `dragover`/`drop` listeners registered once,
`src/draggable/js/drag/NDragHandler.ts`) and its own internal
`NDragReciever` per instance — it does not require an `NDropzone` ancestor or
sibling to function; multiple `NDraglist`/`NDropzone` instances interoperate
purely by sharing a `group` string. `provide('NDraglist', this.instance)` is
called in `setup()`, but no other component in `src/` was found injecting
that key. <!-- UNVERIFIED: could not find a confirmed consumer of the
`'NDraglist'` provide/inject key in the current source tree. -->

## Common mistakes

- **Wrong child-key name.** If your data uses `subItems`/`items`/`nodes`
  instead of `children`, you must pass `child-prop="subItems"` — otherwise
  every node is treated as a leaf (no drop-inside target, no expand arrow).
- **Wrong id-key name.** Similarly, if your unique identifier field isn't
  literally `id`, pass `unique-prop="..."`. `selected`/`expanded`/`cascade`
  all store *this* value, not the item object.
- **Assuming `selected`/`expanded`/`cascade` hold items.** They hold arrays
  of uid values (`uniqueProp` values), not the tree-node objects themselves.
- **Relying on `copy`/`remove` in the default slot.** They are built
  internally (`NDraglistView.node_element()`) but never actually forwarded to
  the slot call — only `{ value, item }` is. A disabled demo block
  (`demos/overview.html`, `v-if="false"`) still shows this pattern; it does
  not work against current source.
- **Expecting `update:current` after a drop.** `current` is reset to `null`
  after a successful drop/drag-end via `set()`, which does not emit — a
  `v-model:current` binding will silently retain the previous value.
- **Two lists dragging into each other but nothing happens.** Check `group`/
  `allowGroups` — a drop is rejected outright unless the dragged item's
  `group` intersects the target list's `allowGroups`.

## Gotchas

- **Select-all header is dead code.** `NDraglistView.header()` and its
  `header_handle()`/`header_expand()`/`header_select()` helpers build a
  header row with a select-all checkbox bound to `scope.selectAll()`, but
  `default()` never calls `this.header()` — nothing in the current render
  tree invokes it. `renderSelect: true` only renders the **per-node**
  checkbox (`node_select()`); there is no working select-all UI without
  building your own (you can still call the underlying logic — see
  `selectState()`/`selectAll()` in `NDraglistController.ts` — but there is no
  exposed way to call them from outside per "Exposed methods" above).
- **`NDragHandler`/`NDragCounter`/`NDragIndicator`/`NDragReciever` are
  internal-only.** They are exported as named exports from
  `src/draggable/index.ts` (not registered as Vue components) and implement
  the shared cross-instance drag machinery: `NDragHandler` is a global
  singleton wiring `window` `dragover`/`drop`/`dragend` listeners and routing
  them to the right zone's `NDragReciever` (one instance per mounted
  `NDraglist`/`NDropzone`, created in `onMounted()` via
  `NDragHandler.append(uid, config)`); `NDragCounter` renders the floating
  "N items" drag-ghost badge that follows the cursor; `NDragIndicator`
  renders the floating drop-position outline box. None of these are meant to
  be instantiated or rendered directly in application templates — treat them
  as implementation detail, not public API. `NDropTarget.ts` in the same
  folder is an empty file (no exported symbol) as of this source snapshot.
- **Keyboard navigation is global-ish.** Arrow-key handling is bound via a
  global `Pointer.bind(uid, 'keydown', ...)` scoped to `[dropzone="${uid}"]`
  — it requires the event target to be inside the list's DOM subtree, not
  full page-level capture.
- **`mode: 'self'`/`'ignore'`/`'deny'` never reach `move`/`update:items`.**
  See the `move` payload note above — only `append`/`inside`/`before`/`after`
  produce a tree mutation and a `move` event.

## Related components

- `NDropzone` (`ai-docs/components/dropzone.md`) — a simpler single-item drop
  target sharing the same underlying drag machinery (`NDragHandler`,
  `NDragReciever`) and `group`/`allowGroups`/`allowDrop` conventions.


---

<!-- ===== components/drawer.md ===== -->

# NDrawer

An edge-anchored panel toggled by a plain boolean `v-model`; shares almost all of its Data/View/backend logic with `NModal` but slides in from a side instead of centering.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/modal/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NDrawer', NDrawer);
```

Source: `src/modal/js/drawer/NDrawer.ts` (+ `NDrawerController.ts`, `NDrawerData.ts` extends `NModalData`, `NDrawerView.ts` extends `NModalView`). See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the loading state/class from `ProtoData.classRoot()`. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `primary`, `secondary`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `success`. |
| `theme` | `String` | `'dark'` | `Props.ThemeDark` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Default is `'dark'`, not `null`. |
| `position` | `String`, validated in `['top','bottom','left','right']` | `'right'` | `Props.PositionDrawer` (`PositionProps.ts`) | **Full enum: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`.** Controls which edge the drawer slides from; adds a `{bem}--{position}` modifier class via the inherited `NModalData.classList`. |
| `modelValue` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Open/closed state. Plain `v-model`. |
| `mode` | `String` | `'modal'` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | **Declared but currently unused.** Grepping `src/modal/js/drawer/` and `NDrawerData.ts` finds no `get mode()` getter and no other read of `this.scope.get('mode')` anywhere — it has no observable effect on rendering or behavior in this version. Do not rely on it to change modal-vs-inline behavior. |
| `listen` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Same trigger auto-binding mechanism as `NModal` — see `ai-docs/components/modal.md` Gotchas. |
| `closable` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Gates escape-key and outside-click closing, same as `NModal`. |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Wraps default-slot content in `n-scrollbar` when `true` (inherited `NModalView.content()`). |
| `width` | `String \| Number` | `null` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Inline `style.width` on the frame; numbers get `px` appended. |
| `height` | `String \| Number` | `null` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Inline `style.height` on the frame. Declared as `[String, Number]` in the prop type even though its JSDoc says `PropType<string>`. |
| `target` | `String` | `null` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | CSS selector for the trigger; auto-resolves to the previous DOM sibling if left `null` (same as `NModal`). |
| `beforeOpen` | `Function` | `null` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Same gating semantics as `NModal`'s `beforeOpen`. |
| `beforeClose` | `Function` | `null` | `NDrawer.ts` (own) | Same gating semantics as `NModal`'s `beforeClose`. |

**There is no `keep` prop on `NDrawer`**, unlike `NModal`. `NDrawerData` inherits `NModalData`'s `get keep()` getter (`this.scope.get('keep')`), but since `keep` is not declared in `NDrawerProps`, that always resolves falsy — so the inherited `NModalView.body()` check `if (!data.keep && !data.model) return null;` always behaves as `if (!data.model) return null;` for `NDrawer`. In practice this means `NDrawer`'s content is **always unmounted while closed** — there is no keep-alive option.

**Confirmed: there is no `title` prop.** `NDrawerProps` has no `title` entry and none of `NDrawerData`/`NDrawerView` (nor the inherited `NModalData`/`NModalView`) read one. Use the `header` slot instead.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `boolean` | `ProtoController.update('modelValue', value)`, fired from `onOpen()`/`onClose()` when the internal `NModalElement` opens/closes. |
| `open` | none | Fired in `NDrawerController.onOpen()`, right after `update:modelValue` is emitted `true`. |
| `close` | none | Fired in `NDrawerController.onClose()`, right after `update:modelValue` is emitted `false`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `header` | none | Rendered inside `{bem}__header`, only if present (inherited `NModalView.body()`). |
| `default` | none | Main content, wrapped in `n-scrollbar` (or plain `div` if `scrollbar: false`). |
| `footer` | none | Rendered inside `{bem}__footer`, only if present. |
| `raw` | `{ props }` (the frame's `{ name: 'frame', style }` object) | If present, bypasses header/default/footer and hands you the whole frame. |

No slot receives a `close()` function or any other scoped helper — same as `NModal`.

## Exposed methods

Exposed via `ncx.pass({ open: 'superOpen', close: 'superClose' })` in `NDrawer.ts`'s `setup()`:

- `open()` — calls `NModalElement.open()` with no arguments (no `silent` parameter is forwarded, unlike `NModal.superOpen`).
- `close(forceClose = false)` — calls `NModalElement.close(forceClose)`. There is no `silent` parameter exposed here either (unlike `NModal.superClose`'s two-argument form) — `NDrawerController.superClose` only forwards `forceClose`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-button @click="open = true">Open drawer</n-button>
  <n-drawer v-model="open" :listen="false">
    Hello!
  </n-drawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const open = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (header/footer slots, `position` driven by a select) and the nested-drawer pattern in `demos/drawer.html` (`listen="false"`, chained `v-model`s):

```vue
<template>
  <n-button @click="showDrawer1 = true">Open Drawer 1</n-button>

  <n-drawer v-model="showDrawer1" :listen="false" position="right" :width="640">
    <template #header>
      Edit item
    </template>

    <n-form>
      <n-form-item label="Name">
        <n-input placeholder="Fill me" />
      </n-form-item>
    </n-form>

    <n-button @click="showDrawer2 = true">Open Drawer 2</n-button>

    <template #footer>
      Im the footer
    </template>
  </n-drawer>

  <n-drawer v-model="showDrawer2" :listen="false">
    Foobar
  </n-drawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const showDrawer1 = ref(false);
const showDrawer2 = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — `NDrawer` is standalone. Its content is whatever you put in the `header`/`default`/`footer`/`raw` slots.

## Common mistakes

- **Assuming a `title` prop exists.** It does not (confirmed above) — use the `header` slot.
- **Assuming `v-model:visible` instead of plain `v-model`.** `NDrawer` uses `modelValue`/`update:modelValue`, exactly like `NModal`.
- **Assuming slot-scoped close props exist.** No slot receives any scope; close it by writing `false` to your own `v-model` ref (as `demos/drawer.html` does, always with `:listen="false"` and no `target`) or by calling the exposed `close()` method.
- **Assuming the `mode` prop does something.** It is declared (`default: 'modal'`) but not read anywhere in `NDrawerData`/`NDrawerController`/`NDrawerView` in this version — treat it as inert.
- **Assuming `keep` works on `NDrawer` like it does on `NModal`.** It doesn't exist as a prop here; content always unmounts on close (see Props above).

## Gotchas

- **`listen`/trigger auto-binding** works identically to `NModal` — see `ai-docs/components/modal.md` Gotchas for the full mechanism (previous-sibling auto-`target`, global `mousedown`/`keyescape` handlers, shared `NModalHandler`/`NModalElement`). All of `demos/drawer.html`'s examples explicitly set `:listen="false"` and drive the drawer purely through `v-model`, presumably because the trigger buttons there aren't structured as the drawer's immediate previous sibling.
- **No `watchProp('modelValue', ...)` in `NDrawerController`, unlike `NModalController`.** Confirmed by reading both controllers' `setup()`: `NModalController.setup()` registers `this.watchProp('modelValue', (value) => value ? this.modal.open() : this.modal.close())`; `NDrawerController.setup()` has no equivalent call anywhere. `NDrawerController.onMounted()` only checks the *initial* `data.model` once (`if (data.model) this.modal.open();`). Practical effect: the drawer's visibility class/content-mount is driven directly and reactively off the `modelValue` prop in the shared `NModalView` (so toggling `v-model` from outside still shows/hides it visually), but toggling `v-model` from outside **after mount does not re-enter `NModalElement`** — it will not register with `NModalHandler`'s backdrop/z-index stack, will not arm the escape-key/outside-click `Pointer.prevent` chain for that instance, and will not re-fire `beforeOpen`/`beforeClose` or the `open`/`close` events. Prefer the exposed `open()`/`close()` methods (via a template ref) or the trigger/`listen` mechanism over raw external `v-model` writes if you need those side effects; plain internal toggling (button-inside-the-drawer calling `open = false`, or the default trigger click path) is unaffected since it always goes through `NModalElement` directly.
- **Z-index/backdrop stacking, `beforeOpen`/`beforeClose` promise-gating, and the shared global handler** all work exactly as documented for `NModal` — `NDrawer` reuses `NModalHandler`/`NModalElement` verbatim (`src/modal/js/drawer/NDrawerController.ts` imports them from `../handler/`).

## Related components

- `NModal` — nearly identical implementation (`NDrawerData extends NModalData`, `NDrawerView extends NModalView`); differs mainly in default `position`-driven layout (edge slide-in vs. centered), the missing `keep` prop, and the `watchProp('modelValue', ...)` asymmetry noted above.
- `n-scrollbar` — used internally for default-slot content when `scrollbar: true`.
- `NPreview`, `NAlert`/`NConfirm` (`src/preview`, `src/signal`) — also built on the same `NModalHandler`/`NModalElement` stacking backend.

<!-- ===== components/dropzone.md ===== -->

# NDropzone

A single-item drag-and-drop target that captures whatever node is dropped on it into a `v-model:item`, without itself holding or rendering a list.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally as `NDropzone` (template tag `<n-dropzone>`) by
`src/draggable/index.ts` via `App.component(NDropzone.name, NDropzone)`.
Source: `src/draggable/js/dropzone/NDropzone.ts` (`defineComponent`),
`NDropzoneController.ts`, `NDropzoneData.ts`, `NDropzoneView.ts` — see
`ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern.

Note: `NDropzone` does **not** use `Props.Draglist` — it declares its own
small, local prop set (only `item`, `allowGroups`, `allowDrop`, `mode`, plus
`Props.Size`/`Props.Type`). It shares drag *mechanics* with `NDraglist`
(same `NDragHandler`/`NDragReciever` machinery) but not the item-tree props.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See `ai-docs/concepts.md` ("Type and Size are open strings"). Not otherwise used by `NDropzoneData`/`NDropzoneView` beyond `classRoot()`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same as above. |
| `item` | `Object` | `null` | Local (`NDropzone.ts`) | The captured item's raw data. `v-model:item`-able — set via `update:item` whenever a valid drop lands (`NDropzoneController.onDragdrop`). Not cloned/synced any other way; read-mostly from the parent's perspective. |
| `allowGroups` | `Array` | `null` | Local | Groups this zone accepts drops from. If `null`, defaults to `[this.uid]` (a component-generated unique id) at setup — meaning **with no `group`-matching source list, an `NDropzone` with default `allowGroups` will reject everything**, since no external `NDraglist`/`NDropzone` will share its auto-generated uid. Always set this explicitly to match a source list's `group`. |
| `allowDrop` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | Local | Gates whether a pending drop is accepted (`result.mode` forced to `'deny'` when false). When a function: called once per dragged item as `allowDrop(node, target, mode)` where `node = { value, item }` for the dragged item and `target` is always `null` for `NDropzone` (there is no concept of a per-node hover target inside a dropzone — `onDragmove` always resolves to `{ target: els.zone, mode: 'append' }`). All dragged items must pass (`nodeAllowDrop()` in `NDropzoneController.ts`). |
| `mode` | `String` | `null` | Local | Declared as `type: [String]` (the source's JSDoc comment says `PropType<object>`, which is stale/incorrect — the runtime type is `String`). When set, **overrides** the computed drop result's `mode` in both `onDragdrop()` and `onDragend()` — i.e. it is reported back to the *source* list as the drop outcome. Not a validated enum; structurally any string works, but only values meaningful to `NDraglist`'s own handling do anything useful — confirmed useful value: `'ignore'` (source list's `onDragend` treats `'ignore'`, like `'deny'`, as "do not remove the dragged item from my tree", turning the interaction into a non-destructive **copy** rather than a move). <!-- UNVERIFIED: no other `mode` string was found exercised against `NDropzone` in `demos/` beyond `'ignore'`; `'deny'` set on this prop technically would only matter if it also reached `onDragmove`, but `onDragmove` doesn't read `data.mode`, so `mode="deny"` on this prop is a no-op for the drop-acceptance decision (only `allowDrop:false` produces that) — it would just make `onDragdrop`/`onDragend` unnecessarily report a mode value of `'deny'` when a drop already succeeded. -->|

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:item` | `(item: object)` — the raw data of the **first** dragged node (`Arr.first(config.items).item`) | A drop is accepted. Fired from `NDropzoneController.onDragdrop()`, which only runs if the drag wasn't already denied at the `dragmove` stage (`allowGroups` mismatch or `allowDrop` false both prevent `onDragdrop` from running at all — see "Gotchas"). If more than one item is dragged (multi-select drag from an `NDraglist`), only the first is captured; the rest are silently dropped from this event (no truncation warning). |

There is no `move`/`row-click`/etc. — `NDropzone` is deliberately minimal: it
has no internal list, no selection, no keyboard nav, no tree.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | The raw `item` value directly (**not** wrapped in an object) — i.e. `v-slot="item"` binds `item` itself, or `v-slot="{ ...fields }"` destructures the item's own fields if it's a plain object | Renders the zone's content — typically showing whatever was last dropped (`data.item`), or empty-state markup when `item` is `null`. Called via `this.scope.context.slots?.default(this.scope.data.item)` in `NDropzoneView.body()`. |

This differs from `NDraglist`'s default slot, which passes `{ value, item }`
— `NDropzone` passes the item value alone, with no virtual-node metadata
(there is no virtual node; a dropzone isn't a list).

## Exposed methods

None. No `pass()`/`context.expose()` calls exist in `NDropzoneController.ts`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
    <n-dropzone v-model:item="droppedItem" :allow-groups="['project-tree']">
        <template #default="item">
            <div v-if="item">{{ item.label }}</div>
            <div v-else>Drop here</div>
        </template>
    </n-dropzone>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const droppedItem = ref(null);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Paired with an `NDraglist` sharing a `group`, using `allow-drop` and `mode`
to build a non-destructive "drop to copy" trash/favorites-style target
(shape follows the confirmed usage in `demos/overview.html`):

```vue
<template>
    <n-draglist v-model:items="tree" :group="['project-tree']" style="height: 300px;">
        <template #default="{ item }">
            <div style="line-height: 32px;">{{ item.label }}</div>
        </template>
    </n-draglist>

    <n-dropzone
        v-model:item="favorite"
        :allow-groups="['project-tree']"
        :allow-drop="true"
        mode="ignore"
        style="width: 200px; height: 200px; border: 2px dashed #999;"
    >
        <template #default="item">
            <div v-if="item" style="padding: 8px;">
                Favorited: {{ item.label }}
            </div>
            <div v-else style="padding: 8px; opacity: 0.5;">
                Drag an item here to favorite it
            </div>
        </template>
    </n-dropzone>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const tree = ref([
    { id: 'file-1', label: 'File 1', children: [] },
    { id: 'file-2', label: 'File 2', children: [] },
]);

const favorite = ref(null);
</script>
```

With `mode="ignore"` above, dropping a node onto the zone captures it into
`favorite` **and** tells the source `NDraglist` not to remove it from `tree`
(the drag effectively copies a reference rather than moving the node).
Without `mode` set, the source list's default drag-end handling for a
cross-zone drop still only removes the node if `removeNode` is true on the
source list **and** the reported mode isn't `deny`/`ignore` — a plain
`NDropzone` drop (no `mode` prop) reports whatever `onDragmove` computed
(`'append'`), so the source *will* remove the dragged node by default.
<!-- UNVERIFIED: "the source will remove the node by default" is inferred
from `NDraglistController.onDragend()`'s `Arr.has(['deny','ignore'],
result.mode)` early-return guard combined with `NDragHelper.unlinkNodes`/
`removeNodes` being gated only by `removeNode`; not independently observed
running in a browser. -->

## Required composition

None structurally — `NDropzone` renders and mounts standalone (it doesn't
need an `NDraglist` ancestor or descendant). It is only *useful* paired with
at least one `NDraglist` (or another drag source) sharing a compatible
`group`/`allowGroups`, since it has no way to initiate a drag itself.

## Common mistakes

- **Leaving `allow-groups` unset.** Its default is `[this.uid]` (a private,
  auto-generated id), so with no explicit `allow-groups`, the zone silently
  rejects every drop from every other component — nothing will ever appear
  to work. Always pass `allow-groups` matching the source list(s)' `group`.
- **Expecting all dragged items.** Multi-select drags from an `NDraglist`
  only surface their **first** item via `update:item`; there is no array
  form of this event.
- **Confusing this component's `mode` prop with `NDraglist`'s drop-result
  `mode` values.** They're related but not the same axis: this prop
  *overrides what gets reported back*, it does not change whether
  `allowDrop` accepts the drop in the first place.
- **Assuming the default slot scope matches `NDraglist`'s.** It's the bare
  item (or `null`), not `{ value, item }`.

## Gotchas

- **`NDragHandler`/`NDragCounter`/`NDragIndicator`/`NDragReciever` are
  internal-only.** Same shared machinery documented in
  `ai-docs/components/draglist.md` — `NDropzone` creates its own
  `NDragReciever` in `onMounted()` exactly like `NDraglist` does
  (`NDragHandler.append(uid, config)`), and relies on the same global
  `NDragHandler` singleton for `window`-level `dragover`/`drop` routing.
  `NDropTarget.ts` (`src/draggable/js/drag/NDropTarget.ts`) is an empty file
  in this source snapshot — no exported symbol, nothing to document.
- **No node-level drop targeting.** Unlike `NDraglist`, there's no
  before/inside/after distinction — every accepted drop resolves to a single
  `'append'`-style result (`onDragmove` always sets `target: els.zone, mode:
  'append'`), then `mode` (the prop) can stomp that value afterward purely
  for what's *reported*, not for how the drop itself was resolved.
- **A drag started from a plain `NDropzone` isn't possible.** There's no
  `dragstart` wiring here (no draggable element, no `nodeDragstart`
  equivalent) — `NDropzone` is a pure target, never a source.

## Related components

- `NDraglist` (`ai-docs/components/draglist.md`) — the tree/list drag
  source (and equally valid drop target) sharing the same `NDragHandler`/
  `NDragReciever` machinery and `group`/`allowGroups`/`allowDrop`
  conventions.


---

<!-- ===== components/durationpicker.md ===== -->

# NDurationpicker

A text-input-plus-popover picker for a relative duration, bound as a plain
**integer number of seconds** — not a date, not an object, and not
minutes. Confirmed via `demos/overview.html` (`modelValue: 124521`, a raw
seconds count) and `@kizmann/pico-js`'s `PicoNowDuration.safeDuration()`/
`diffrence()` (`safeDuration(3661) => { dates:0, hours:1, minutes:1,
seconds:1 }`; `diffrence` returns whole seconds), which
`NDateHelper.getDurationData`/`getDurationString`/`getDurationNumber`
(`src/datetime/js/helper/NDateHelper.ts`) build directly on.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/datetime/index.ts`:
`App.component('NDurationpicker', NDurationpicker)`. Source:
`src/datetime/js/durationpicker/NDurationpicker.ts`. Controller
(`NDurationpickerController`) extends `NPopoverPanelController`
(`src/popover/js/popover-panel/NPopoverPanelController.ts`), same base as
`NTimepicker`.

`NDurationpicker.ts` also exports `NDurationpickerOptions` — the default
`options` array (below) — importable directly if you need the raw preset
seconds values.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` (open string) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Known defaults: `primary, secondary, info, warning, danger, success`. |
| `size` | `String` (open string) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Known defaults: `xs, sm, md, lg, xl`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Disables input + popover trigger. |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shows the built-in × clear button. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Value `modelValue` resets to via `applyClear()`. |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No items')` | `Props.EmptyText` (`TextProps.ts`) | Shown (via `this.empty()`) when `options` resolves to an empty list. |
| `position` | `String` (popover position enum) | `'bottom-start'` | `Props.PositionBottomStart` (`PositionProps.ts`) | Popover placement. |
| `modelValue` | **untyped** (no `type:` key — any value passes Vue's prop validation) | `null` | own declaration | **Runtime shape: a plain integer number of seconds** (e.g. `3600` = 1 hour). See "Common mistakes." |
| `options` | `[Array, Object]` | `NDurationpickerOptions` — 21 preset seconds values from `300` (5 min) up to `604800` (7 days) | own declaration | Selectable presets shown in the popover list; each entry is itself a raw seconds number. |
| `minDuration` | untyped | `null` | own declaration | **Declared but not read anywhere in `NDurationpickerController`/`NDurationpickerView`/`NDateHelper` — currently has no effect.** |
| `maxDuration` | untyped | `null` | own declaration | **Same — declared, unused, no effect in this version.** |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Select duration'` | own declaration | Shown in the text input when empty. |
| `negativeText` | `String` | `'Negative duration'` | own declaration | **Declared but not referenced anywhere in the component's own code — no effect found.** |
| `format` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | own declaration | **Declared but not consumed by any duration logic** (`NDateHelper`'s duration helpers never read `scope.data.format`) — appears reserved/unused in this version. |
| `dates` | `String` | `':count Day\|:count Days'` | own declaration | Pluralized display/parse pattern for the "days" part of a duration (`:count` is the numeric placeholder). |
| `hours` | `String` | `':count Hour\|:count Hours'` | own declaration | Same, for hours. |
| `minutes` | `String` | `':count Minute\|:count Minutes'` | own declaration | Same, for minutes. |
| `seconds` | `String` | `':count Second\|:count Seconds'` | own declaration | Same, for seconds. |
| `icon` | `String` | `Styler.icon('duration')` | `NDurationpicker`'s own declaration (not the `Props.Icon` mixin) | Leading icon; no matching `iconPosition`/`iconDisabled`. |

`dates`/`hours`/`minutes`/`seconds` are used **both ways**: for display
(`NDateHelper.getDurationString` picks the right plural form via
`Locale.choice`) and for parsing typed free text back into seconds
(`NDateHelper.getDurationNumber`/`getDurationMatch` builds a regex from
each pattern, replacing `:count` with a capture group).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `number` (seconds), or `clearValue` on clear | (1) user edits the free-text input and presses Enter/blurs such that the text changed — `onInput()` calls `NDateHelper.getDurationNumber(this, data.input)` and emits the resulting seconds count; (2) user presses Enter without changing the recognizable text — `applyIndex()` emits the seconds value at the currently scrolled `options` index; (3) user clicks a preset row in the popover list — `NDurationpickerView.item()`'s `onClick` calls `scope.update('modelValue', value.value)` directly with that preset's raw seconds number; (4) the clear (×) button (`applyClear()`, inherited). |

## Slots

None — `NDurationpickerView` never calls `this.slot(...)` (uses `this.empty()` for the empty-options state instead of a slot).

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()`/`context.expose` calls in `NDurationpickerController`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-durationpicker v-model="duration"></n-durationpicker>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<!-- adapted from demos/overview.html -->
<n-durationpicker
  v-model="form.duration"
  size="md"
  type="primary"
  :clearable="true"
></n-durationpicker>
```

```js
// demos/overview.html initializes it as:
data.n_durationpicker = {
    size: 'md', type: 'primary', clearable: true,
    disabled: false, modelValue: 124521, // seconds — 1 day, 10:35:21
};
```

## Required composition

None required standalone. Optional: `NButtonGroup` (generic
`this.slot('default')` container) can wrap an `NDurationpicker` alongside
other controls, same as any other component — not a required or
component-specific pairing.

## Common mistakes

- **Getting the `modelValue` shape wrong.** It is a **plain integer number
  of seconds** — not an `{ hours, minutes, seconds }` object, not a
  `Date`, and not minutes. `60 * 5` (`300`) is 5 minutes; the built-in
  `options` preset list is itself just an array of such seconds integers
  (`NDurationpickerOptions`, e.g. `[300, 600, 900, 1800, ..., 604800]`).
  Passing an object or a `Date` will not work with the internal
  `Now.make().safeDuration(value)`/`diffrence()` logic this component is
  built on.
- Assuming `format`, `negativeText`, `minDuration`, or `maxDuration` do
  anything — all four are declared props with no code path reading them
  in this version (confirmed by grep across
  `src/datetime/js/durationpicker/` and `NDateHelper.ts`). Setting them is
  a silent no-op.
- Passing a negative number expecting a "negative duration" UI: internally
  `NDateHelper.getDurationData` takes the absolute value
  (`if (value < 0) value = value * -1`) before formatting, so negative
  seconds display the same as their positive counterpart rather than using
  `negativeText` (which, per above, isn't wired to anything anyway).

## Gotchas

- `NDurationpickerView.input()` checks `if (data.range) return null` to
  hide the text input, but `NDurationpickerData` (and its mixins
  `NPopoverPanelData`/`PositionData`/`TextData`) never define a `range`
  getter — this is dead code copied from `NDatepicker`/`NSlider` (which do
  have a real `range` prop/getter). It always evaluates falsy, so the
  input always renders; there is no way to hide it via a `range` prop.
- Free-text parsing (`onInput` → `getDurationNumber`) only works for
  strings matching the `dates`/`hours`/`minutes`/`seconds` patterns
  (default English `:count Day(s)/Hour(s)/Minute(s)/Second(s)`); typing
  something else silently resolves to whichever `options` preset is
  currently scrolled to (`applyIndex()`), not necessarily `0`.
- `options` accepts an `Object` as well as an `Array` per its prop type,
  following the shared `Props.OptionsObject`-style resolution described in
  `ai-docs/concepts.md` — but note `NDurationpicker` does **not** actually
  use `Props.OptionsObject`/`OptionHelper`; it declares its own local
  `options` prop and reads entries directly as raw values (`Arr.each(data.options, (value) => ({ value }))`
  in the View), so there's no `optionsValue`/`optionsLabel` pair here
  despite the "options" naming similarity to that shared pattern.

## Related components

- `NTimepicker` / `NTimepickerPanel` — sibling `src/datetime/` components
  with a completely different `modelValue` shape (a formatted date+time
  string, not seconds).
- `NDatepicker`, `NDatetimepicker` — other `src/datetime/` pickers (not
  covered in this doc batch).


---

<!-- ===== components/empty-icon.md ===== -->

# NEmptyIcon

A small "no data" placeholder — an icon slot plus optional text — rendered automatically by other components' empty states via `ProtoView.empty()`, and usable directly.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/empty/index.ts` (`App.component(NEmptyIcon.name, NEmptyIcon)`). Source: `src/empty/js/empty-icon/{NEmptyIcon,NEmptyIconController,NEmptyIconData,NEmptyIconView}.ts`. See concepts.md for `ProtoView.empty(options)`, which is how most consumers actually reach this component (as `<n-empty-icon>` resolved via `this.comp(...)`, not hand-authored in templates).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `image` | `[String]` | `'default'` | local (`NEmptyIcon.ts`) | Adds a `n-empty-icon--{image}` modifier class (`NEmptyIconData.classList`). No built-in modifier styling ships for any value in `src/empty/css/empty-icon.scss` (only the `--inline` modifier for the `inline` prop exists there) — treat `image` as a hook for consumer-supplied CSS/background-image variants, not a closed set of shipped looks. |
| `inline` | `[Boolean]` | `false` | local (`NEmptyIcon.ts`) | Lays the icon and text out in a row (`flex-direction: row`, smaller icon box) instead of the default stacked column layout. This is exactly what `Props.EmptyPropsInline`/`Props.EmptyPropsStacked` (concepts.md) set via the `emptyProps` prop on a *consuming* component (`{ inline: true }` vs `{ inline: false }`). |
| `emptyText` | `[String]` | `null` | local (`NEmptyIcon.ts`) | **Not** the shared `Props.EmptyText` mixin — this is its own locally-declared prop with a plain `null` default (no automatic `Locale.trans('No items')` fallback at the prop-default level). The raw value is still passed through `Locale.trans()` at render time in `NEmptyIconView.body()` if non-empty. |

## Events

None — `emits: []` in `NEmptyIcon.ts`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `icon` | none | Rendered inside `.n-empty-icon__type` — the icon/graphic area. Empty by default (no fallback icon is rendered if omitted); consuming code typically leaves this empty and styles `.n-empty-icon__type` via the `image` modifier class instead, or fills it with an `<i class="n-icon ...">`/image explicitly. |
| `default` | none | Fallback body text, rendered inside `.n-empty-icon__text` **only when `emptyText` is empty** (`NEmptyIconView.body()`: `emptyText` takes priority over the `default` slot when both are present). |

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()`/`context.expose` call in `NEmptyIconController` or `NEmptyIcon.ts`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-empty-icon empty-text="No items"></n-empty-icon>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

`NEmptyIcon` has no direct usage in `demos/` — it's invoked internally by other components' empty states. This mirrors that path (`ProtoView.empty()`, see concepts.md), which any component extending `ProtoView` can call from its own render tree, e.g. inside a custom list/table View:

```ts
// inside a custom N<Comp>View extends ProtoView
body() {
    const { data } = this.scope;

    if ( !data.items.length ) {
        return this.empty({ inline: false });
    }

    return this.list(data.items);
}
```

Direct template usage, matching what `ProtoView.empty()` produces under the hood:

```vue
<template>
  <n-empty-icon :empty-text="'No results found'" :empty-props="{ inline: true }" v-bind="emptyProps"></n-empty-icon>
</template>
```

## Required composition

None — `NEmptyIcon` is a leaf component with no required parent/child wiring.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `emptyText`'s default to already be a translated `'No items'` string like other components' `emptyText` props (`Props.EmptyText`) — `NEmptyIcon`'s own `emptyText` prop defaults to plain `null`; the `'No items'` default lives on the *consuming* component's own `emptyText` prop (e.g. `NVirtualbar`), which is what actually gets passed down via `ProtoView.empty()`.
- Expecting the `default` slot and `emptyText` to combine (e.g. `emptyText` as a heading plus slot content below) — only one is ever rendered; `emptyText`, when non-empty, fully replaces the `default` slot.
- Setting `image="illustration"` (or any custom value) and expecting a built-in graphic to appear — no shipped CSS backs any `image` value in this repo; you must supply your own `.n-empty-icon--illustration` CSS rule (e.g. a `background-image`) for it to render anything visible.

## Gotchas

- **This is the component behind every other component's empty state.** `ProtoView.empty(options)` (inherited by every `View` subclass) renders `<n-empty-icon>` with props built as `{ emptyText: scope.get('emptyText'), ...scope.get('emptyProps'), ...options }` — i.e. it reads `emptyText`/`emptyProps` off the *calling* component's own props, not off `NEmptyIcon`'s. Confirmed callers: `NVirtualbar`, `NSelect`, `NCascader`, `NInfo`, `NDurationpicker` (grep `this.empty(` under `src/`).
- `.n-empty-icon__type` has no intrinsic content — it's a plain box (`display: block`, sized via CSS) with a `content: '\00a0'` spacer pseudo-element purely to preserve its aspect ratio (`padding-bottom: 100%` trick), not a default icon glyph. If nothing is passed via the `icon` slot and no CSS background is set for the current `image` value, the icon area renders as an invisible empty square.
- `.n-empty-icon.n-disabled .n-empty-icon__type { display: none; }` — if a consuming component's own `disabled`/`superDisabled` state ends up applied to `<n-empty-icon>` itself (e.g. via `emptyProps`), the icon area disappears entirely while the text remains.

## Related components

- Every list/select/table-like component with an `emptyText`/`emptyProps` pair (`NVirtualbar`, `NSelect`, `NCascader`, `NInfo`, `NDurationpicker`, etc.) — see concepts.md's `ProtoView.empty()` section.


---

<!-- ===== components/form-bag.md ===== -->

# NFormBag

A flat, click-to-jump list of every current validation message across all `NFormItem`s registered on the nearest ancestor `NForm` — typically dropped inside an `NPopover` as an "errors summary" panel.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/form/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NFormBag', NFormBag);
```

Source: `src/form/js/form-bag/NFormBag.ts` (+ `NFormBagController.ts`, `NFormBagData.ts`, `NFormBagView.ts`). `NFormBagController extends ProtoController` directly. See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern.

## Props

None. `NFormBagProps = {}` in `src/form/js/form-bag/NFormBag.ts` — the component takes no props at all.

## Events

None. `emits: []` in `NFormBag.ts`, and no `this.emit(...)` call anywhere in `NFormBagController`.

## Slots

None. `NFormBagView.default()` builds its entire tree programmatically from the injected `NForm`'s registered fields — there is no `this.slot(...)` call anywhere in `NFormBagView.ts`.

## Exposed methods

None. `NFormBag.ts` never calls `ncx.pass(...)`, and `NFormBagController` defines no additional methods beyond what it inherits.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item prop="email" label="Email" :rules="['required', 'email']">
      <n-input v-model="form.email" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-bag />
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ email: '' });
</script>
```

## Realistic example

`demos/form.html` places it directly as the first child inside an `NFormFrame`'s body (`<n-form-frame ...><n-form-bag></n-form-bag> ... </n-form-frame>`) — no `NPopover` wrapper in that demo. `NFormBagController` also does `injectRef(['popover', 'NPopover'])` purely so it can auto-close an ancestor popover on click if one happens to be present (see Required composition); wrapping it in one is optional, e.g.:

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-frame>
      <n-form-bag />

      <n-form-item prop="teststring" label="Teststring" :rules="['required', 'minlength:3']">
        <n-input v-model="form.teststring" />
      </n-form-item>
    </n-form-frame>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ teststring: '' });
</script>
```

Clicking an entry in the list calls `field.superView()` (scrolls the field into view, opening any ancestor `NTabsItem`/`NCollapseItem`/`NFormGroup`) and, if an ancestor `NPopover` was injected, closes it (`scope.ncx('popover')?.superClose()`).

## Required composition

Requires an `NForm` ancestor somewhere in the tree (not necessarily a direct parent — resolved via `injectRef(['form', 'NForm'])`, i.e. Vue's `provide`/`inject`). Confirmed directly from source: `NFormBagView.default()` reads `scope.ncx('form')?.data.messages` and, if that is empty (including when there is no `NForm` ancestor at all, since the optional-chain then reads `undefined`), returns `null` and renders nothing. It also optionally injects `NPopover` (`injectRef(['popover', 'NPopover'])`) purely to auto-close that popover on item click — an `NPopover` ancestor is not required for `NFormBag` to render or function, just for that one convenience.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting `NFormBag` to render anything without an `NForm` ancestor.** It silently renders `null` — no warning, no error, no placeholder.
- **Expecting it to render when there are zero validation messages.** Same code path (`Mix.isEmpty(errors)` check) — an all-valid form means `NFormBag` renders nothing, which is by design for an "errors summary" widget but easy to mistake for a bug while testing with valid data.
- **Passing props or slot content to `<n-form-bag>`.** Both are silently ignored/discarded — it takes no props and renders no slots.

## Gotchas

- `NFormBag` itself is not disable-aware in the `ProtoData.superDisabled`/`injectRef(['form-item', ...])` sense described in `ai-docs/concepts.md` — it has no `disabled` prop and doesn't render inputs, only a read-only list of message text and click targets.
- The list is built fresh on every render from `scope.ncx('form').childs` (every currently-mounted `NFormItem`), filtered to those whose `prop` key has entries in `data.messages` — a field with no `prop` set (see `ai-docs/components/form-item.md`) never appears here, since it can never have a keyed message.

## Related components

- `NForm` (`ai-docs/components/form.md`) — required ancestor; source of `childs` and `data.messages`.
- `NFormItem` (`ai-docs/components/form-item.md`) — each rendered row corresponds to one field's `prop`/`label`/messages, and clicking it calls the field's `superView()`.
- `NPopover` — optional ancestor; `NFormBag` auto-closes it on item click if present. Typically the actual host of `NFormBag`'s content, per `demos/form.html`'s usage pattern.


---

<!-- ===== components/form-frame.md ===== -->

# NFormFrame

A scrollable layout shell for long forms: splits into a sidebar (built from every registered `NFormGroup` child, as click-to-jump links) and a scrollable body for the actual form content.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/form/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NFormFrame', NFormFrame);
```

Source: `src/form/js/form-frame/NFormFrame.ts` (+ `NFormFrameController.ts`, `NFormFrameData.ts`, `NFormFrameView.ts`). `NFormFrameController extends GroupController` — tracks a `childs` list of registered `NFormGroup`s (populated by `NFormGroupController.onMounted`: `this.ncx('form-frame')?.append(this)`). See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared pattern.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
