| `showSearch` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NFormFrame.ts` (own) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / dead prop: declared but never read by `NFormFrameController`, `NFormFrameData`, or `NFormFrameView` in this commit. `NFormFrameView.side()` calls `this.search()` unconditionally — the search input renders regardless of this prop's value. See Gotchas. --> |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Search ...'` | `NFormFrame.ts` (own) | Placeholder text passed to the always-rendered search `n-input` (`NFormFrameView.search()`). |

## Events

None. `emits: []` in `NFormFrame.ts`, and no `this.emit(...)` call anywhere in `NFormFrameController`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The scrollable body content — typically `NFormGroup`/`NFormItem`/`NTabs`/`NCollapse` trees (`NFormFrameView.body()`: wrapped in an `n-scrollbar`). |

## Exposed methods

None (`NFormFrame.ts` never calls `ncx.pass(...)`). Internally, `NFormFrameController` defines `superView(group)` (smooth-scrolls the frame's body to the given `NFormGroupController`'s DOM node via `[data-ncx="${group.uid}"]`, then calls `group.superView()` to expand it if collapsed) — called from the sidebar link's click handler, not reachable from a template ref.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-form-frame style="height: 60vh;">
    <n-form-group label="Section 1" icon="fa fa-star">
      <n-form-item label="Name">
        <n-input />
      </n-form-item>
    </n-form-group>
  </n-form-frame>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/form.html` — nested under `NForm`, containing an `NFormBag` and multiple `NFormGroup`s reachable via the sidebar:

```vue
<template>
  <n-form kind="fieldset" :form="form">
    <n-form-frame style="height: 80vh; border: 1px solid #eee;" :show-search="true">
      <n-form-bag />

      <n-form-group label="General" icon="fa fa-star">
        <n-form-item prop="teststring" label="Teststring" :rules="['required', 'minlength:3']">
          <n-input v-model="form.teststring" />
        </n-form-item>
      </n-form-group>

      <n-form-group label="Advanced" icon="fa fa-ghost" :collapse="true">
        <n-form-item prop="testbool" label="Testbool">
          <n-switch v-model="form.testbool">Testbool</n-switch>
        </n-form-item>
      </n-form-group>
    </n-form-frame>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ teststring: '', testbool: false });
</script>
```

Clicking "General" or "Advanced" in the auto-generated sidebar smooth-scrolls the body to that group (expanding it first if collapsed).

## Required composition

Per this library's composition rules, `NFormFrame` expects an `NForm` ancestor somewhere in the tree (not necessarily a direct parent). Note the source-level nuance for Gotchas: `NFormFrameController.setup()` does **not** itself call `injectRef(['form', 'NForm'])` or read anything from an `NForm` instance — it only does `provide('NFormFrame', this.instance)` for its own `NFormGroup` children to inject. There is no direct code-level dependency from `NFormFrame` on `NForm` found in this commit; the requirement is a structural/usage convention (it is meant to be the layout shell for content living inside an `NForm`, and its `NFormGroup` children do separately read `NForm.kind` — see `ai-docs/components/form-group.md`) rather than an enforced runtime check.

## Common mistakes

- **Relying on `show-search` to hide the search box.** It renders unconditionally regardless of this prop's value — see Props/Gotchas.
- **Typing in the search box and expecting the sidebar links or body content to filter.** Nothing in `NFormFrameController`/`NFormFrameView` filters `childs`/`links()` by the typed text — see Gotchas.
- **Expecting `NFormGroup`s outside of `NFormFrame` to still show up in a sidebar.** There is no global registry — only `NFormGroup`s that are actual descendants of a given `NFormFrame` (and thus successfully `injectRef`/`append` into it) appear in that frame's `links()` list.

## Gotchas

- **The search box is non-functional as of this commit.** `NFormFrameView.search()` renders an `n-input` bound to `data.search` and wires `onInput` to `scope.set('search', e.target.value)` — but `NFormFrameController.setup()` never calls `makeData('search', ...)`, and `NFormFrameData` has no `search` getter at all. `scope.set('search', value)` still succeeds silently (`ProtoController.set()` just assigns into the internal `vals` plain object even without a prior `makeData` call), but `data.search` used as the input's bound `modelValue` always reads `undefined` (no getter), so the field visually never reflects what you typed past the DOM's own uncontrolled state, and — more importantly — nothing filters `links()`'s output using it. `showSearch` and `placeholder` exist, suggesting a filter-the-sidebar feature was intended, but it is not wired up in this commit.
- The sidebar (`side()`) is always rendered (search box included) — there is no prop to hide the sidebar entirely, only content is driven by however many `NFormGroup` children happen to register.
- `NFormFrameController.superView(group)` resolves the group's DOM node by a `data-ncx` attribute (`NFormGroupView.default()` sets `props['data-ncx'] = scope.uid`) via its own `body` ref's `.scrollTo(selector, options)` — this relies on `n-scrollbar`'s own API (`this.ncx('body')?.scrollTo(...)`), not a plain DOM `scrollIntoView` (contrast with `NFormItemController.superView()`/`NFormGroupController.superView()`, which do use `el.scrollIntoView(...)` directly).

## Related components

- `NForm` (`ai-docs/components/form.md`) — conventional ancestor (no direct code dependency found — see Required composition).
- `NFormGroup` (`ai-docs/components/form-group.md`) — registers itself into this component's `childs`, producing one sidebar link per group.
- `NFormBag` (`ai-docs/components/form-bag.md`) — commonly placed as a direct child inside the frame body, per `demos/form.html`.


---

<!-- ===== components/form-group.md ===== -->

# NFormGroup

A labeled, optionally collapsible section grouping related `NFormItem`s under a legend/header, and (when nested in an `NFormFrame`) contributing a jump-to-section link in that frame's sidebar.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/form/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NFormGroup', NFormGroup);
```

Source: `src/form/js/form-group/NFormGroup.ts` (+ `NFormGroupController.ts`, `NFormGroupData.ts`, `NFormGroupView.ts`). `NFormGroupController extends GroupController` (it tracks its own `childs`, though nothing in this component's own code reads that list back — see Gotchas). See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared pattern.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | Rendered before the label text if non-empty (`NFormGroupView.label_icon()`). |
| `modelValue` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | The expanded/collapsed state, only meaningful when `collapse: true` — see below. |
| `nativeType` | `String` | `'div'` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | Root element tag (`h(data.native, ...)`). |
| `kind` | `String` | `null` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | Pushes a `{bem}--{kind}` modifier class. When unset (`null`), falls back to the nearest ancestor `NForm`'s own `kind` prop (`NFormGroupData.superKind`, reads `this.scope.ncx('form')?.get('kind')`) — if there's no `NForm` ancestor either, no modifier class is added. Confirmed styled values (from `src/form/css/form-group.scss`): `classic`, `fieldset`. |
| `align` | `String` | `null` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | Pushes a `{bem}--{align}` modifier class if set. **Not** the shared `Props.AlignHorizontal`/`AlignVertical` mixin from `ai-docs/concepts.md` — it's `NFormGroup`'s own plain-string prop with no validator and a `null` default (unlike `NForm`'s `align`, which defaults to `'vertical'`). `demos/form/index.html` (legacy demo) passes `align="horizontal"`. |
| `name` | `String` | `() => Hash.uuid()` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | Declared but not read by `NFormGroupController`/`NFormGroupData`/`NFormGroupView` in this commit. <!-- UNVERIFIED: likely intended as a stable identifier for future use (e.g. matching `NTabsItem`/`NCollapseItem` `name` conventions elsewhere in the library), but no such usage found in `src/form/`. --> |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | The section heading text. |
| `grid` | `String \| Number` | `null` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | When set, adds `n-grid gap-{grid}` to the body wrapper's class list (`NFormGroupView.body()`), for laying out the default-slot children in a CSS grid. |
| `collapse` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NFormGroup.ts` (own) | Enables the collapse/expand toggle (clicking the header, or calling `superToggle()`/`superOpen()`/`superClose()`) and renders the collapse-angle icon (`NFormGroupView.collapse()`). When `false`, `modelValue` still governs visibility (see below) but there is no way to toggle it from the UI. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `boolean` | Standard v-model write path, fired by `superToggle()`/`superOpen()`/`superClose()` — but **only when `collapse: true`**; all three methods guard on `if (this.data.collapse) { this.update(...) }` and are otherwise no-ops. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The group's body content, rendered inside `{bem}__body` (`NFormGroupView.body()`). |
| `action` | none | Rendered inside `{bem}__header`'s `{bem}__action`, next to the label — only if the slot is actually provided (`NFormGroupView.action()` checks `context.slots.action`). Used in `demos/form.html` for a header-corner button: `<template #action><n-button ...>Action</n-button></template>`. |

## Exposed methods

None (`NFormGroup.ts` never calls `ncx.pass(...)`). Internally, `NFormGroupController` defines `superToggle()`, `superOpen()`, `superClose()` (all `collapse`-gated, see Events) and `superView()` (opens any ancestor `NTabsItem`/`NCollapseItem` and smooth-scrolls this group into view — called both by `NFormItem.superView()`'s chain and by `NFormFrame`'s sidebar link click), but none are reachable from a template ref.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-form-group label="Contact">
    <n-form-item label="Name">
      <n-input v-model="form.name" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form-group>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/form.html` — a collapsible group with an icon, inside a tab, plus one with an `action` slot:

```vue
<template>
  <n-tabs model-value="general">
    <n-tabs-item name="general" label="General">
      <n-form-group label="Redirect" icon="fa fa-directions" :collapse="true" :model-value="false">
        <n-form-item prop="testbool" label="Testbool">
          <n-switch v-model="form.testbool">Testbool</n-switch>
        </n-form-item>
      </n-form-group>
    </n-tabs-item>
  </n-tabs>

  <n-form-group label="Advanced" icon="fa fa-ghost" type="danger">
    <template #action>
      <n-button type="auto" size="xs">Reset</n-button>
    </template>

    <n-form-item label="Danger zone">
      <n-input />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form-group>
</template>
```

## Required composition

Per this library's composition rules, `NFormGroup` expects an `NForm` ancestor somewhere in the tree (not necessarily a direct parent). See Gotchas for the precise, source-confirmed nuance: the actual hard structural dependency in `NFormGroupController` is on an ancestor **`NFormFrame`** (via `injectRef(['form-frame', 'NFormFrame'])` + `append(this)`/`remove(this)` on mount/unmount, which is what populates `NFormFrame`'s sidebar link list), while the `NForm` injection (`injectRef(['form', 'NForm'])`) is used only for the optional `kind` style fallback described in the Props table.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting `collapse="false"` (the default) to hide `NFormGroup`'s toggle icon but still allow collapsing via `v-model`.** With `collapse: false`, `superToggle`/`superOpen`/`superClose` are all no-ops — `modelValue` can still be set directly by the parent (it still governs the `n-hidden` class), but nothing inside the component will ever change it.
- **Passing `legend`/`checkable` props**, seen in the older `demos/form/index.html` (a stale, pre-current-API demo). Neither prop exists on the current `NFormGroupProps` — the equivalent of `legend` is `label`; there is no `checkable` equivalent at all.
- **Assuming `align` behaves like `NForm.align`.** It's a separate, unvalidated plain string prop with a `null` default (see Props) — passing an arbitrary value produces a `{bem}--{value}` class with no guarantee of matching CSS.

## Gotchas

- `NFormGroupController extends GroupController` and does track a live `childs` array (any component that calls `this.append(this)`/appends itself into an injected `'form-group'` — see `NFormItemController.onMounted`: `this.ncx('form-group')?.append(this)`), but nothing in `NFormGroup`'s own `Data`/`View` code reads `this.childs` back. It exists purely so descendant `NFormItem`s have somewhere to register themselves as a side effect of injection — no visible per-group feature (like a group-level "first error" jump) currently consumes it.
- The `kind`/`NForm` relationship is a **soft, cosmetic** dependency only — `NFormGroupData.superKind` degrades gracefully (`this.kind || ncx?.get('kind')`) to no modifier class at all if there is no `NForm` ancestor, rather than throwing or misbehaving.
- The `NFormFrame`/`append` relationship is a **structural** dependency for the sidebar-navigation feature specifically — an `NFormGroup` with no `NFormFrame` ancestor still renders and functions completely normally as a standalone collapsible section, it simply never appears in any sidebar link list (because there is no `NFormFrame` to append to).
- `superDisabled`/`injectRef(['form-item', 'NFormItem'])` (from `ai-docs/concepts.md`) is inherited by every component including `NFormGroup`, but `NFormGroup` never reads `superDisabled` in its own `Data`/`View` code — it has no `disabled` prop of its own and does not visually disable itself based on an enclosing `NFormItem`.

## Related components

- `NForm` (`ai-docs/components/form.md`) — optional ancestor for `kind` fallback.
- `NFormFrame` (`ai-docs/components/form-frame.md`) — required ancestor for the sidebar jump-link feature; `NFormGroup` registers itself into `NFormFrame`'s `childs`.
- `NFormItem` (`ai-docs/components/form-item.md`) — typical direct/descendant content; its `superView()` chain calls this group's `superView()`/opens it when jumping to a field inside a collapsed group.


---

<!-- ===== components/form-item.md ===== -->

# NFormItem

A single labeled field wrapper: renders a label, the default-slot input, an optional per-field validation error message, and (optionally) a toggle for making the field conditional/skippable.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/form/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NFormItem', NFormItem);
```

Source: `src/form/js/form-item/NFormItem.ts` (+ `NFormItemController.ts`, `NFormItemData.ts`, `NFormItemView.ts`). `NFormItemController extends ProtoController` directly (not `GroupController` — it has no `childs` of its own). See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `modelValue` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | The field's enabled/visible state, only meaningful when `conditional: true` (see below). Local copy via `cloneProp('modelValue')`. **No explicit `emits` array is declared** on `NFormItem.ts` (unlike `NForm`/`NFormGroup`) — `update:modelValue` is still fired (via `ProtoController.update()`), just not statically declared, so `v-model` still works. |
| `rules` | `Array` | `() => []` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | The field's validation rules — see "Validation rules" below for the exact shape and every available rule. |
| `conditional` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | When `false` (the default), `NFormItemController.setup()` force-sets `modelValue` to `true` on creation, and the label-row toggle control is never rendered. When `true`, the field renders an "Enable field"/"Disable field" toggle row (`NFormItemView.cond()`) that flips `modelValue` via `superToggle()`. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | Rendered inside `{bem}__label`. |
| `prop` | `String` | `null` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | The key path into the ancestor `NForm`'s `form` object this field validates/displays errors for (`Obj.get(form, prop)`). Required for `rules`/`errors` to do anything — see `ai-docs/components/form.md`. |
| `tooltip` | `String` | `null` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / dead prop: declared but never read by `NFormItemController`, `NFormItemData`, or `NFormItemView` in this commit — no tooltip is actually rendered for the label. `demos/form/index.html` (a legacy demo) passes `tooltip="Im a label tooltip"`, but against the current component that's a no-op falling through as a plain DOM attribute. --> |
| `conditionOn` | `String` | `null` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / dead prop: declared but never read anywhere in `src/form/`. --> |
| `conditionOff` | `String` | `null` | `NFormItem.ts` (own) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / dead prop: declared but never read anywhere in `src/form/`. --> |

`NFormItem` does **not** spread any `Props.*` mixins from `ai-docs/concepts.md`'s shared `Props` object — every prop above is its own declaration.

### Validation rules (`rules` prop)

Shape: `Array<string>`, each entry formatted as `"ruleKey"` or `"ruleKey:arg"` (a single colon-delimited argument — no rule currently takes more than one). Parsed in `NFormRuleHandler.test()` (`src/form/js/form-rules/NFormRuleHandler.ts`):

```ts
let [name, ...args] = rule.split(':');
// this.rules[name].validate(scope /* NFormController */, field /* NFormItemController */, value, ...args)
```

`value` is always `Obj.get(scope.data.form, field.data.prop)` — the field's current value read from the ancestor `NForm`'s `form` object. A rule "fails" when `validate(...)` returns falsy, and its `message(...)` return value is pushed into `NForm`'s `data.checks[prop]`. Re-evaluated automatically on every `form` mutation (see `ai-docs/components/form.md`) — no manual trigger needed.

New rules can be registered at runtime via `NFormRuleHandler.register(key, ruleModule)`.

Every rule module lives in `src/form/js/form-rules/module/`:

| Rule key | Module | Argument | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `required` | `NFormRuleRequired.ts` | none | Passes if the value is boolean `true`, or (for non-booleans) not empty (`!Mix.isEmpty(value)`). |
| `required_if` | `NFormRuleRequiredIf.ts` | `key` — another field's `prop` | Looks up `target = form[key]`. If `target` is empty, or not "true-ish" (`!Mix.isTrue(target)`), the rule passes unconditionally (field not required). Otherwise falls through to the same check as `required` (boolean `true`, or non-empty). |
| `required_unless` | `NFormRuleRequiredUnless.ts` | `key` — another field's `prop` | Looks up `target = form[key]`. If `target` is **not** empty, or is "true-ish" (`Mix.isTrue(target)`), the rule passes unconditionally (field not required). Otherwise falls through to the `required` check. |
| `same` | `NFormRuleSame.ts` | `key` — another field's `prop` | Passes if `value === form[key]` (strict equality). Typical use: "confirm password" fields. |
| `diffrent` | `NFormRuleDiffrent.ts` | `key` — another field's `prop` | Passes if `value !== form[key]`. **Note the key is spelled `diffrent`, not `different`** — this is the exact registered rule name; using `different:` silently no-ops (unknown rule names are skipped: `if (!this.rules[name]) return;`). |
| `value` | `NFormRuleValue.ts` | `val` — a literal string | Passes if `Mix.str(value) === val` (string-coerced strict equality against a literal). |
| `email` | `NFormRuleEmail.ts` | none | Passes if the value is empty, or matches `/^.*?@.*?\.[a-z]{2,}$/`. |
| `min` | `NFormRuleMin.ts` | `min` — a number | Passes if the value is empty, or (for numeric values) `value >= min`. Non-numeric non-empty values fail. |
| `max` | `NFormRuleMax.ts` | `max` — a number | Passes if the value is empty, or (for numeric values) `value <= max`. Non-numeric non-empty values fail. |
| `minlength` | `NFormRuleMinlength.ts` | `min` — a number | Passes if the value is empty, or (for strings/arrays) `length > min` — **strictly greater than**, not `>=`. |
| `maxlength` | `NFormRuleMaxlength.ts` | `max` — a number | Passes if the value is empty, or (for strings/arrays) `length < max` — **strictly less than**, not `<=`. |

All 11 modules are pre-registered in `NFormRuleHandler.rules` (`src/form/js/form-rules/NFormRuleHandler.ts`) — this is the complete built-in set as of this commit.

Real usage (`demos/form.html`):

```html
<n-form-item prop="testselect" label="Testselect" :rules="['required_unless:teststring', 'value:primary']">
  <n-select v-model="n_testform.testselect" :options="types" :clearable="true"></n-select>
</n-form-item>

<n-form-item prop="teststring" label="Teststring" :rules="['required', 'minlength:3', 'diffrent:testselect']">
  <n-input v-model="n_testform.teststring"></n-input>
</n-form-item>
```

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `boolean` | Standard v-model write path, fired from `NFormItemController.superToggle()` when the "Enable field"/"Disable field" toggle row is clicked (only rendered/active when `conditional: true`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The field's input control(s), rendered inside `{bem}__input` (`NFormItemView.input()`). |

## Exposed methods

None (`NFormItem.ts` never calls `ncx.pass(...)`). Internally `NFormItemController` defines `superToggle()` (flips `modelValue` when `conditional`) and `superView()` (opens any ancestor `NTabsItem`/`NCollapseItem`/`NFormGroup` and smooth-scrolls the field into view — used by `NForm.gotoFirstError()`/`NFormBag`'s click-to-jump list), but neither is reachable from a template ref.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-form-item label="Name">
    <n-input v-model="form.name" />
  </n-form-item>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Standalone, with no `NForm` ancestor at all (fully valid per Required composition below) — just a labeled wrapper:

```vue
<template>
  <n-form-item label="Search" tooltip="Ignored, see Gotchas">
    <n-input v-model="query" clearable />
  </n-form-item>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const query = ref('');
</script>
```

Nested under `NForm` with validation (adapted from `demos/form.html`):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item prop="teststring" label="Teststring" :rules="['required', 'minlength:3', 'diffrent:testselect']">
      <n-input v-model="form.teststring" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item prop="testbool" label="Testbool" conditional :rules="['required_if:teststring']">
      <n-switch v-model="form.testbool">Testbool</n-switch>
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ teststring: '', testselect: '', testbool: false });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None in either direction. `NFormItem` works **fully standalone** with no `NForm` ancestor (`injectRef(['form', 'NForm'])` resolves to `null`; `onMounted`/`onUnmounted` guard the `append`/`remove` calls with `?.`, and `NFormItemView.error()` defaults `errors` to `{}` when there's no `NForm` to read messages from) — in that case it's just a label+input wrapper with no validation. It also works with an `NForm` ancestor and **no** `NFormGroup`/`NTabsItem`/`NCollapseItem` ancestor (those are all optional `injectRef` lookups used only for `superView()`'s auto-expand-and-scroll behavior).

## Common mistakes

- **Setting `rules` without `prop`.** Rules are evaluated against `Obj.get(form, field.data.prop)` — with no `prop`, the value is always read from an undefined path and errors never attach to this field (nor merge from the `errors` prop).
- **Expecting the `tooltip`/`conditionOn`/`conditionOff` props to do anything.** They don't in this commit — see the prop table above.
- **Using `different:` instead of `diffrent:`** in a `rules` entry. The registered key is `diffrent` (misspelled in source) — an unrecognized rule name is silently skipped, no error, no console warning.
- **Assuming `conditional` fields start disabled.** The default `modelValue` is `true` — a conditional field starts *enabled* and must be explicitly toggled off, or mounted with `:model-value="false"`.

## Gotchas

- `NFormItemController.setup()` calls `provide('NFormItem', this.instance)` — this is exactly the injection point every other component's `ProtoController.setup()` reads via the automatic `injectRef(['form-item', 'NFormItem'])` call described in `ai-docs/concepts.md`. Concretely: put any input component (e.g. `NInput`, `NSelect`, `NSwitch`) inside an `NFormItem`'s default slot, and that input's `ProtoData.superDisabled` getter becomes `this.scope.get('disabled') || !(!ncx || ncx?.data.model)` — i.e. it treats itself as disabled whenever the enclosing `NFormItem`'s `modelValue` (`data.model`) is falsy, on top of its own `disabled` prop. This is how `conditional` `NFormItem`s disable their contents when toggled off, and it's automatic — nothing in the child input needs to opt in.
- The per-field error shown by `NFormItemView.error()` only reads from the **nearest injected `NForm`** (`scope.ncx('form')?.data.messages`) — if there's no `NForm` ancestor, `errors` defaults to `{}` and no error node is ever rendered, silently.
- `is-disabled` is added to the root class list whenever `!data.model` (i.e., a toggled-off conditional field), independent of/in addition to `superDisabled`-driven `n-disabled` classes on child inputs.

## Related components

- `NForm` (`ai-docs/components/form.md`) — optional ancestor; owns `form`/`errors` and computes `messages`.
- `NFormGroup` (`ai-docs/components/form-group.md`) — optional ancestor; `superView()` will open a collapsed group to reveal this field.
- `NFormBag` (`ai-docs/components/form-bag.md`) — lists this field's messages and can trigger `superView()` on click.


---

<!-- ===== components/form.md ===== -->

# NForm

The root form container: tracks a bound `form` data object, auto-computes validation `checks`/`messages` for every registered `NFormItem`, and merges in server-side `errors`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/form/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NForm', NForm);
```

Source: `src/form/js/form/NForm.ts` (+ `NFormController.ts`, `NFormData.ts`, `NFormView.ts`). `NFormController extends GroupController` (not plain `ProtoController`) — it tracks a reactive `childs` list of every mounted `NFormItem` via `append(child)`/`remove(child)` (called from `NFormItemController.onMounted`/`onUnmounted`). See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern and `GroupController`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds `n-load` via `ProtoData.classRoot()`. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `primary`, `secondary`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `success`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds `n-disabled` via `superDisabled`/`classRoot()`. Not otherwise read by `NFormController`/`NFormData` — it does not itself force-disable descendant inputs (each input reads its own `superDisabled`, which only checks a *direct* `NFormItem` ancestor's `modelValue`, not `NForm.disabled` — see `ai-docs/concepts.md`'s `ProtoData.superDisabled`). |
| `align` | `String`, validated in `['horizontal','vertical']` | `'vertical'` | `Props.AlignVertical` (`AlignProps.ts`) | Pushes a `{bem}--{align}` class (`NFormData.classList`). `src/form/css/form-item.scss` styles `.n-form--vertical .n-form-item` / `.n-form--horizontal .n-form-item` (label-above vs. label-beside layout). |
| `form` | `Object` | `null` | `NForm.ts` (own) | The bound form-data object. Deep-watched (`watchProp('form', ...)`) — every nested mutation re-runs `compareChange()` (dirty tracking) and `extractChecks()` (re-validates every registered `NFormItem` against its `rules`). This is what rule modules read via `Obj.get(scope.data.form, field.data.prop)`. |
| `dirty` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NForm.ts` (own) | Local copy via `cloneProp('dirty')`. Auto-flips to `true` the first time the `form` object's content hash changes from its initial value (`NFormController.compareChange()`, hashed with `Hash.object`). Emits `update:dirty` — see Events. |
| `errors` | `Object` | `null` | `NForm.ts` (own) | Server/manual errors, merged into the auto-computed `checks`. Shape: `{ [prop: string]: string \| string[] }` — see "The `messages`/`checks`/`errors` merge" below. |
| `nativeType` | `String` | `'div'` | `NForm.ts` (own) | The native element tag rendered as root (`h(data.native, ...)`, `NFormView.default()`). Set to `'form'` to get a real `<form>` element; nothing in `NFormController`/`NFormView` currently attaches a `submit` DOM listener to it regardless of tag — see Gotchas. |
| `kind` | `String` | `'classic'` | `NForm.ts` (own) | Pushes a `{bem}--{kind}` class. Confirmed styled values from `src/form/css/form-group.scss`: `classic`, `fieldset`. `NFormGroup.kind` falls back to this value when its own `kind` prop is unset (`NFormGroupData.superKind`). |
| `square` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NForm.ts` (own) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / dead prop: declared here but never read by NFormController, NFormData, or NFormView, and not part of any inherited BaseData/IconData getter. No visible effect as of this commit. --> |

There is no `rules` prop on `NForm` itself — validation rules are declared per-field on `NFormItem` (see `ai-docs/components/form-item.md`'s "Validation rules" section for the full `rules` shape and every `NFormRule*` module).

### The `messages`/`checks`/`errors` merge

- `data.checks` — auto-computed by `NFormController.extractChecks()` (runs whenever `form` changes): for every registered child `NFormItem`, runs `NFormRuleHandler.test(this, child)` against that field's `rules` prop and the current value at `Obj.get(form, child.data.prop)`, collecting failing rules' messages into `checks[prop] = string[]`. Entries with zero messages are filtered out (`Obj.filter(checks, v => v.length > 0)`).
- `data.messages` — `NFormController.getMessages()`: clones `data.checks`, then for every key in the `errors` prop, merges (`Arr.merge`) the errors prop's value (coerced to an array via `Arr.all`) onto any existing rule-check messages for that same key. This is what `NFormItemView.error()` and `NFormBagView` read to display per-field error text.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:dirty` | `boolean` | Standard v-model write path (`ProtoController.update('dirty', ...)`), fired from `NFormController.compareChange()` the first time the `form` prop's content hash diverges from its initial value (only while `data.dirty` is still `false` and `data.form` is truthy). |
| `submit` | — | <!-- UNVERIFIED / dead emit: declared in `emits: ['update:dirty', 'submit']` on `NForm.ts`, but no call site anywhere in `NFormController`/`NFormView` (or elsewhere in `src/`) actually does `this.emit('submit')`, and no native `submit` DOM listener is attached to the rendered root element regardless of `nativeType`. Treat as currently non-functional/reserved rather than a working submit hook. --> |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The form body — `NFormItem`/`NFormGroup`/`NFormFrame`/`NFormBag`/arbitrary content (`NFormView.default()`: `this.slot('default')`). |

## Exposed methods

None. `NForm.ts`'s `setup()` never calls `ncx.pass(...)` (contrast with e.g. `NModal.ts`'s `ncx.pass({ open: 'superOpen', close: 'superClose' })`), so a template ref on `<n-form ref="formRef">` does **not** get a `validate()`/`submit()`-style method. `NFormController` does define `gotoFirstError()` (scrolls/opens the first field with a validation message, via `child.superView()`) and `getMessages()`, but neither is called from anywhere else in `src/` and neither is exposed to a template ref — they are effectively internal/dead from a public-API standpoint as of this commit. Validation itself needs no manual trigger: it recomputes automatically and reactively (see the `form` prop's deep-watch above) as the bound `form` object's fields change.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item label="Name">
      <n-input v-model="form.name" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ name: '' });
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/form.html` (real prop usage: `kind`, `errors`, `rules` array strings):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form kind="fieldset" :form="form" :errors="{ email: 'Already taken' }">
    <n-form-item prop="email" label="Email" :rules="['required', 'email']">
      <n-input v-model="form.email" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item prop="password" label="Password" :rules="['required', 'minlength:8']">
      <n-input v-model="form.password" type="password" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item prop="confirm" label="Confirm password" :rules="['same:password']">
      <n-input v-model="form.confirm" type="password" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';

const form = reactive({
  email: '', password: '', confirm: '',
});
</script>
```

Any failing rule (or the `errors.email` entry) surfaces automatically under the corresponding `NFormItem` — no manual validate call is needed.

## Required composition

None — `NForm` is the root/ancestor component. `NFormItem` works both nested inside it and standalone (see `ai-docs/components/form-item.md`); `NFormBag`, `NFormGroup`, and `NFormFrame` each expect `NForm` somewhere above them in the tree (not necessarily as a direct parent — resolved via Vue `provide`/`inject`, `provide('NForm', this.instance)` here).

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting a `validate()`/`submit()` method on a template ref.** There isn't one — see Exposed methods. Read `form.checks`/`form.messages`-equivalent state reactively (there is no direct prop exposing `data.messages` outward either; it is only consumed internally by `NFormItem`/`NFormBag`) or gate your own submit handler on whatever validity signal your app tracks.
- **Listening for `@submit`.** The declared `submit` emit is never fired by the component — see Events.
- **Passing a non-reactive plain object as `form`.** `watchProp('form', ...)` deep-watches it; if it's not reactive (not created with `reactive()`/`ref()`), mutations won't be observed and `checks`/`dirty` won't update.
- **Forgetting `prop` on `NFormItem`.** Rules and error-message lookups are keyed by `NFormItem`'s `prop`, which must match a real key path on `form` (`Obj.get(scope.data.form, field.data.prop)`); an `NFormItem` with no `prop` never participates in validation or `errors` display.

## Gotchas

- Every `ProtoController` (every component in the tree, not just form components) runs `injectRef(['form-item', 'NFormItem'])` in its own `setup()` — this is unrelated to `NForm`'s own `provide('NForm', ...)`/`injectRef(['form', 'NForm'])` pair, but it's the mechanism that makes any input's `superDisabled` getter check its nearest `NFormItem` ancestor's `modelValue` (see `ai-docs/concepts.md`). `NForm` itself does not participate in that specific chain — only `NFormItem` provides `'form-item'`.
- `dirty` is a one-way ratchet in this version: `compareChange()` only ever flips it from `false` to `true` (`if (data.dirty || !data.form) return;` short-circuits once dirty is already true), and only compares against the hash captured the first time `compareChange()` ran. There is no built-in way to reset `dirty` back to `false` other than writing to it yourself via `v-model:dirty`.
- `nativeType: 'form'` gives you a real `<form>` element, but combined with the dead `submit` emit (see Events) you'll still need your own native `@submit.prevent` handling strategy — nothing in `NForm` calls `preventDefault()` or emits on a native submit event.

## Related components

- `NFormItem` (`ai-docs/components/form-item.md`) — the field wrapper `NForm` tracks in `childs`; owns the `rules` prop and per-field error display.
- `NFormGroup` (`ai-docs/components/form-group.md`) — collapsible/legend-style section grouping, reads `NForm.kind` as a style fallback.
- `NFormFrame` (`ai-docs/components/form-frame.md`) — scrollable layout shell with a jump-to-section sidebar built from `NFormGroup` children.
- `NFormBag` (`ai-docs/components/form-bag.md`) — renders a flat list of every current validation message across all registered `NFormItem`s, typically inside an `NPopover`.


---

<!-- ===== components/info-column.md ===== -->

# NInfoColumn

A single labeled field within an `NInfo` panel: reads one property off the
parent's `item` (via `prop`) and renders it through a cell-type renderer
resolved from the shared `NInfoCells` registry.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally alongside `NInfo` via `src/info/index.ts`
(`App.component('NInfoColumn', NInfoColumn)`). Its `type` prop selects a
renderer from `globalThis.NInfoCells`, a registry built by that same
`src/info/index.ts` by **re-registering the table module's cell renderers**
(`src/table/js/table-cell/*.ts`) under the `NInfoCells` global instead of
`NTableCells`:

```ts
globalThis.NInfoCells = {
    'string': NTableCellString, 'boolean': NTableCellBoolean,
    'datetime': NTableCellDatetime, 'image': NTableCellImage,
    'option': NTableCellOption,
};
```

`NInfoColumnView.resolve(type)` looks up `globalThis.NInfoCells[type]`,
falling back to the `'string'` renderer if the key isn't found:

```ts
resolve(type, scope = 'NInfoCells') {
    if ( globalThis[scope][type] ) return globalThis[scope][type];
    return globalThis[scope]['string'];
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` | `'string'` | Component-local (`NInfoColumn.ts`) | **Cell renderer selector.** Full enumerated list, exactly the `NInfoCells` registry keys: `'string'`, `'boolean'`, `'datetime'`, `'image'`, `'option'`. Any other value (including `'select'` or `'matrix'`, which exist as `NTableColumn` cell types) silently falls back to the `'string'` renderer via `resolve()` — there is no error, just a likely-wrong render. Also used verbatim in the root element's modifier class: `n-info-column--{type}`. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | Component-local | Text rendered in the field's label part (`n-info-column__label`). No label slot exists — this prop is the only way to set it. |
| `prop` | `String` | `null` | Component-local | Dot-path read off the parent `NInfo`'s `item` via `Obj.get(item, prop)` — this is the value handed to the cell renderer as `input`. |
| `data` | `Object` | `null` | Component-local | Renderer-specific config object, read by individual cell renderers via `column.get('data')` (e.g. `NTableCellImage` reads `data.thumbProp` from it) — mirrors `NTableColumn`'s own `data` prop for the same cell components. |
| `datetimeFormat` | `String` | `'LTSD'` | Component-local | Format token string passed to `Now.make(input).format(...)` by the `'datetime'` cell renderer only. |
| `trueText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Yes')` | `Props.TrueText` (`TextProps.ts`) | Used by the `'boolean'` cell renderer (`NTableCellBoolean`) via `column.data.trueText`. |
| `falseText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No')` | `Props.FalseText` (`TextProps.ts`) | Used by the `'boolean'` cell renderer via `column.data.falseText`. |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No items')` | `Props.EmptyText` (`TextProps.ts`) | Declared via the shared mixin; <!-- UNVERIFIED: no direct read of `data.emptyText` found in `NInfoColumnController`/`View` or in the reused table-cell renderers — likely reserved for parity with `NTableColumn`, not observed to affect `NInfoColumn`'s own render path. --> |
| `undefinedText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Undefined')` | `Props.UndefinedText` (`TextProps.ts`) | Used by the `'option'` cell renderer (`NTableCellOption`) as the fallback label when `getOption(input)` resolves to `null`. |
| `options` / `optionsValue` / `optionsLabel` | `Object` (Array also works) / `String` / `String` | `{}` / `'$index'` / `'$value'` | `Props.OptionsObject` (`OptionProps.ts`) | Standard options trio (see concepts.md "Options resolution"). Consumed by the `'option'` cell renderer via `column.getOption(input)` / `column.data.undefinedText`. |
| `modelValue` | any | `null` | Component-local | Declared but <!-- UNVERIFIED: no getter in `NInfoColumnData`, no read/write anywhere in `NInfoColumnController`/`View` — this prop is currently a no-op. Do not rely on `v-model` doing anything on `NInfoColumn`. --> |

Note: `type` here is **not** `Props.Type` from `BaseProps` (that's an open
styling string, default `null`) — it's a component-local prop with a
different meaning and a different default (`'string'`). See `info.md`'s
"Common mistakes" for the naming collision with `NInfo`'s own `type` prop.

## Events

None. `NInfoColumn.ts` doesn't declare an `emits` array at all (not even an
empty one), and `NInfoColumnController` never calls `this.emit(...)` or
`this.update(...)`.

## Slots

None. `NInfoColumnView` never calls `this.slot(...)` — the label comes from
the `label` prop only, and the field is always rendered through the resolved
cell-type component, not slot content.

## Exposed methods

None — `NInfoColumnController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-info :item="user">
    <n-info-column label="Name" prop="name"></n-info-column>
</n-info>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<n-info :item="user">
    <n-info-column label="Name" type="string" prop="name"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column
        label="Avatar"
        type="image"
        prop="avatar"
        :data="{ thumbProp: 'avatarThumb' }"
    ></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column label="Joined" type="datetime" prop="joinedAt" datetime-format="LL"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column label="Active" type="boolean" prop="active" true-text="Enabled" false-text="Disabled"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column
        label="Role"
        type="option"
        prop="roleId"
        :options="[{ value: 1, name: 'Admin' }, { value: 2, name: 'Member' }]"
        options-value="$value.value"
        options-label="$value.name"
        undefined-text="Unknown role"
    ></n-info-column>
</n-info>
```

## Required composition

**Confirmed from source: `NInfoColumn` must be a descendant of `NInfo`.**
`NInfoColumnController.setup()` calls
`this.injectRef(['info', 'NInfo'])`, and its `onMounted()`/`onUnmounted()`
hooks call `this.ncx('info')?.append(this)` / `?.remove(this)` — registering
itself into the parent `NInfo`'s (`GroupController`) child list. More
importantly, `NInfoColumnView.field()` reads the actual value to render via:

```ts
const item = Obj.get(scope.ncx('info'), ['data', 'item'], {});
const input = Obj.get(item, data.prop);
```

Outside an `NInfo` ancestor, `inject('NInfo', null)` resolves to `null`, so
`scope.ncx('info')` is `undefined` — the optional chaining means **no hard
runtime error is thrown** (unlike e.g. `NCollapseItem`, which does error
standalone), but `item` silently falls back to `{}` and `input` is always
`undefined`, so every column renders empty/blank. Functionally, `NInfoColumn`
outside `NInfo` is inert, even though it won't crash.

## Common mistakes

- Passing `type="select"` or `type="matrix"` expecting it to work like
  `NTableColumn` — **confirmed not supported**: `NInfoCells` only registers
  `string`/`boolean`/`datetime`/`image`/`option` (5 of the 7 `NTableColumn`
  cell types). Both `select` and `matrix` silently fall back to the
  `'string'` renderer via `resolve()`'s registry-miss branch, producing a
  raw stringified value instead of the expected control.
- Using `NInfoColumn` outside `<n-info>` — no error is thrown, but every
  field renders blank because `item`/`input` resolve to `{}`/`undefined`
  (see "Required composition" above).
- Expecting `v-model="..."` on `NInfoColumn` to do anything — `modelValue`
  is declared but never read or written; this component is display-only.
- Confusing this `type` prop (cell renderer choice) with the shared
  `Props.Type` styling prop used elsewhere in the library — they don't
  overlap in meaning or accepted values.

## Gotchas

- `data` is a generic per-renderer config bag, not itself typed per cell
  type — check the specific `NTableCell*.ts` source (`src/table/js/table-cell/`)
  for what keys a given `type` actually reads from it (e.g. only
  `'image'` reads `data.thumbProp`).
- The root element's class includes `n-info-column--{type}` using the raw
  `type` string, so an unsupported value like `type="matrix"` still produces
  a `n-info-column--matrix` class even though it renders with the `string`
  cell component underneath — the class and the actual renderer can disagree.
- `emptyText` is declared (via `Props.EmptyText`) but not observed to be
  consumed anywhere in this component's own render path or by any of the
  five reused cell renderers — don't rely on it doing anything here.
- `datetimeFormat` defaults to `'LTSD'`, not a plain date pattern — it's a
  pico-js `Now`/`Locale` token string (see concepts.md's note on the
  `Now`/`Locale` datetime helpers replacing `moment`).

## Related components

- `NInfo` (`ai-docs/components/info.md`) — the required parent; provides
  `item` and the injection context this component depends on.
- `NTableColumn` / `NTable` — owns the original `string`/`boolean`/
  `datetime`/`image`/`option`/`select`/`matrix` cell-renderer set under
  `src/table/js/table-cell/`; `NInfoColumn` reuses 5 of those 7 renderer
  components directly (not reimplementations) via the `NInfoCells` registry.
  `select` and `matrix` remain table-only.


---

<!-- ===== components/info.md ===== -->

# NInfo

A read-only key-value detail panel: renders a single `item` object through
its `NInfoColumn` children, or a built-in empty state when no item is set.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `src/info/index.ts`'s install function
(`App.component('NInfo', NInfo)`), which also registers `NInfoColumn` in the
same call. That same file additionally builds the shared cell-renderer
registry that `NInfoColumn` reads from:

```ts
globalThis.NInfoCells = {
    'string':   NTableCellString,
    'boolean':  NTableCellBoolean,
    'datetime': NTableCellDatetime,
    'image':    NTableCellImage,
    'option':   NTableCellOption,
};
```

These are the **same renderer components the table module uses**
(`src/table/js/table-cell/*.ts`, imported directly), re-keyed under
`NInfoCells` instead of `NTableCells`. `NInfo` itself doesn't touch this
registry — it's `NInfoColumn` that resolves a cell type through it (see
`ai-docs/components/info-column.md`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string — see concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings." Applied via `classRoot()` as `n-size-{size}`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string, styling only (`n-type-{type}`) — unrelated to `NInfoColumn`'s own `type` prop (cell-renderer selector). |
| `item` | `Object` | `null` | Component-local (`NInfo.ts`) | The data object being displayed. Each child `NInfoColumn` reads one field out of it via its own `prop`. When falsy, `NInfo` renders the empty state instead of its children. |
| `syncEvent` | `Function` | `null` | Component-local | Stored and exposed via `data.syncEvent`, but <!-- UNVERIFIED: no call site found anywhere in `src/info/` — `NInfoController`/`NInfoView` never invoke it. Its purpose could not be confirmed from source; treat as reserved/unused in this version. --> |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `false` | Component-local | When `true`, wraps the body in an `n-scrollbar` component (`this.comp('n-scrollbar', ...)`) instead of a plain `div`. |
| `renderEmpty` | `Boolean` | `true` | Component-local | Declared and exposed via `data.renderEmpty`, but <!-- UNVERIFIED: `NInfoView.body()` branches only on `data.item` truthiness, never reads `data.renderEmpty` — the prop currently has no observed effect on the render path. --> |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No item')` | Component-local (overrides `Props.EmptyText`'s `'No items'` key) | Text shown in the empty state (`n-empty-icon`) when `item` is falsy. Note the singular wording differs from the shared `Props.EmptyText` default used elsewhere in the library. |

`NInfo` does **not** spread `Props.Load`/`Disabled`/`Color`/`Clearable`/etc. —
only `Size` and `Type` from `BaseProps`. Its prop list above is exhaustive.

## Events

None. `NInfo.ts` declares `emits: []`, and `NInfoController` never calls
`this.emit(...)` or `this.update(...)`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Rendered inside the body wrapper only while `item` is truthy (`this.div('body', [this.slot()])` in `NInfoView.body()`). This is where `NInfoColumn` children go. |

## Exposed methods

None — `NInfoController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-info :item="user">
    <n-info-column label="Name" prop="name"></n-info-column>
</n-info>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted directly from `demos/overview.html` (the `n-info` block bound to a
table's current row):

```vue
<n-info :item="user" :scrollbar="true" style="width: 300px; height: 500px;">
    <n-info-column label="Name" type="string" prop="name"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column label="Avatar" type="image" prop="avatar"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column label="Joined" type="datetime" prop="joinedAt"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column label="Active" type="boolean" prop="active"></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column
        label="Role"
        type="option"
        prop="roleId"
        :options="[{ value: 1, name: 'Admin' }, { value: 2, name: 'Member' }]"
        options-value="$value.value"
        options-label="$value.name"
    ></n-info-column>
    <n-info-column label="ID" type="string" prop="id"></n-info-column>
</n-info>
```

## Required composition

`NInfo` is the parent side of the pair: it `provide('NInfo', this.instance)`
in `NInfoController.setup()` and is a `GroupController` (tracks appended
children via `append`/`remove`, though `NInfoView` doesn't currently iterate
`childs` itself — the default slot renders whatever markup is passed in).
`NInfo` has no dependency on `NInfoColumn` existing — an `NInfo` with no
column children (or arbitrary other content in its default slot) still
renders fine, showing the empty state only when `item` itself is falsy.
See `ai-docs/components/info-column.md` for the child-side requirement.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `renderEmpty: false` to suppress the empty state — it has no
  observed effect; the empty state is driven purely by `item` truthiness.
- Assuming `type`/`size` restrict to a fixed set of values — see concepts.md,
  they're open strings with only `xs/sm/md/lg/xl` (size) and
  `primary/secondary/info/warning/danger/success` (type) styled by default.
- Confusing `NInfo`'s `type` prop (visual style) with `NInfoColumn`'s `type`
  prop (which cell renderer to use) — they are unrelated props that happen
  to share a name.

## Gotchas

- `syncEvent` and `renderEmpty` are both declared, plumbed through to
  `NInfoData` getters, but have no confirmed consumer in the current source
  — don't assume passing them changes behavior.
- The empty state uses `this.empty({ inline: false })` (`ProtoView.empty()`),
  which reads `emptyText`/`emptyProps` directly off `scope` rather than
  `data` — `NInfo` doesn't declare an `emptyProps` prop at all, so it always
  renders with `{}` merged under the `{ inline: false }` override.
- `scrollbar` changes the root wrapper component (`n-scrollbar` vs plain
  `div`) but not the BEM class list — `classList` is computed once and
  passed to whichever wrapper is used.

## Related components

- `NInfoColumn` (`ai-docs/components/info-column.md`) — the only documented
  way to render fields inside `NInfo`; required child-side `inject` of this
  component's provided context.
- `NTable` / `NTableColumn` — the cell-type rendering system
  (`string`/`boolean`/`datetime`/`image`/`option`) that `NInfoColumn` reuses
  verbatim from `src/table/js/table-cell/*.ts` is otherwise documented under
  the table component's own docs.

<!-- ===== components/input-file.md ===== -->

# NInputFile

A file-picker control composed from a read-only `NInput` (display) and an `NButton` (trigger) wrapping a hidden native `<input type="file">`; reach for this over the other input variants whenever the bound value needs to be one or more native `File` objects rather than text.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/input/index.ts` as `NInputFile` (`App.component(NInputFile.name, NInputFile)`). Source: `src/input/js/input-file/{NInputFile,NInputFileController,NInputFileData,NInputFileView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md. |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Not read directly by `NInputFileController`/`NInputFileView` (the trigger `NButton` and display `NInput` are not individually given a `disabled` prop), but it still works: `classList` calls the shared `classRoot()` (see concepts.md), which adds `n-disabled` to the root element whenever `superDisabled` is true, and the global rule `.n-disabled:not(.n-draglist-item,.n-resizer) { pointer-events: none; }` (`src/index.scss`) then blocks all clicks inside — including the hidden file input and the trigger button. Effective, but via generic CSS rather than component-specific JS logic. |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: available via `IconData` but never read in `NInputFileView` — no visible effect found. --> |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (`BaseProps.ts`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / confirmed non-functional here: `NInputFileView.default()` never calls `this.clear(...)`, unlike `NInput`/`NInputNumber`. Setting `clearable` renders no clear button on this component. --> |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same caveat — unreachable without a rendered clear control; `applyClear()` is never triggered by this component's own UI. |
| `modelValue` | untyped (no `type` key), `default: null` | `null` | `NInputFile.ts` (own prop) | See "The modelValue shape" below — this is the one prop on this component you must get exactly right. |
| `multiple` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NInputFile.ts` (own prop) | Enables multi-file selection (sets `multiple` on the native `<input type="file">`) and changes both the `modelValue` shape and the display text pluralization. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `''` | `NInputFile.ts` (own prop) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: declared and exposed via `NInputFileData.placeholder`, but never passed to the inner `n-input` component or read anywhere in `NInputFileView` — the display `NInput`'s `modelValue` prop is always the resolved file name/count instead. No visible effect found. --> |
| `glass` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NInputFile.ts` (own prop) | Forwarded as the `glass` prop to the inner trigger `NButton` (`this.comp('n-button', { glass: data.glass }, ...)`). |
| `buttonText` | `String` | `'Select file'` | `NInputFile.ts` (own prop) | Text of the trigger button, resolved through `Locale.trans(data.buttonText)` (pico-js i18n) — treat the default as a translation-key lookup, not a fixed literal. |
| `countText` | `String` | `':count File|:count Files'` | `NInputFile.ts` (own prop) | Pluralization template resolved via `Locale.choice(countText, model?.length)` (pico-js i18n pluralization: `singular|plural` split on `\|`) — only used when `multiple` is true. |

### The `modelValue` shape

`modelValue` is **not** a `FileList`, and **not** a URL/filename string. `NInputFileController.updateModel()` (triggered by the hidden native input's `input` event) does exactly this:

```ts
let files = [...this.rel('input')?.files];   // spreads the native FileList into a plain array of File objects

if ( Mix.isEmpty(files) ) {
    return;                                   // no files selected (e.g. user cancelled the picker) -> no update at all, modelValue is left untouched
}

if ( !data.multiple ) {
    files = Arr.first(files);                 // single-select: unwrap to just the first File object
}

this.update('modelValue', files);
```

So, concretely:

- `multiple: false` (the default) → `modelValue` is a single native `File` object (or stays whatever it was before — including the initial `null` — if the selection is empty).
- `multiple: true` → `modelValue` is an `Array<File>` (native `File` objects, in the order the browser reports them).
- The initial/default `modelValue` is `null` — code consuming this component must handle `null` before the user has picked anything, regardless of `multiple`.
- The display `NInput` reads `Obj.get(data.model, 'name')` (the `.name` property off the `File` object, or off the first `File` when computing the count) — this only makes sense for `File`/`File[]`; passing a plain string/URL as `modelValue` yourself will not display as expected.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | a `File` (single) or `File[]` (multiple) — see above | The hidden native `<input type="file">` fires its native `input` event and the resulting `FileList` is non-empty. |

`emits` is declared as exactly `['update:modelValue']` — there is no separate `input`/`change`/`focus`/`blur` re-emission on this component (unlike `NInput`/`NTextarea`/`NInputNumber`).

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| none | — | `NInputFileView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NInputFileController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-input-file v-model="file" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const file = ref(null); // will become a File object once selected
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (`n_preview.file` usage):

```vue
<template>
  <n-input-file v-model="preview.file" />
  <p v-if="preview.file">Selected: {{ preview.file.name }} ({{ preview.file.size }} bytes)</p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const preview = reactive({ file: null });
</script>
```

Multi-file variant (not found in demos — built from source props):

```vue
<template>
  <n-input-file v-model="files" :multiple="true" button-text="Select files" />
  <ul v-if="files">
    <li v-for="f in files" :key="f.name">{{ f.name }}</li>
  </ul>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const files = ref(null); // becomes File[] once selected, still null until then
</script>
```

## Required composition

None required — standalone (it internally composes `NInput` for display and `NButton` for the trigger, but consumers just use `<n-input-file>` as a single tag). Optional: can be placed inside `NButtonGroup` (confirmed composition pairing).

## Common mistakes

- Treating `modelValue` as a `FileList`: it is a plain `File` (single) or `Array<File>` (multiple), already unwrapped from the native `FileList` — do not call `.item(0)` or iterate it as a `FileList`.
- Assuming `multiple: false` always yields the *first* file the user visually selected in the OS dialog: `Arr.first(files)` takes the first entry of the spread `FileList`, whose order is browser/OS-dependent, not necessarily selection order.
- Relying on `clearable`/`clearValue` to work the same way they do on `NInput`/`NInputNumber`: neither is wired up in this component's `View`/`Controller` — see the UNVERIFIED notes in the props table. (`disabled` *does* work, but via the generic `n-disabled`/`pointer-events: none` CSS mechanism, not component-specific logic — see the Props table entry.)
- Expecting selecting the *same* file twice in a row to fire `update:modelValue` again: the hidden `<input type="file">`'s value is never reset by this component, so re-picking an identical file may not fire a native `input` event the second time (standard browser file-input behavior, not something this component works around).

## Gotchas

- The rendered "input" the user sees typing/reading into is actually a disabled, read-only `NInput` (`disabled: true` is hardcoded in `NInputFileView.input()`) showing either the file name (`Obj.get(data.model, 'name')`) or, when `multiple`, a pluralized count string built from `countText`/`Locale.choice`. It is not connected to `modelValue` for writing — only for display.
- The actual file-selection UI is a visually hidden native `<input type="file">`, clicked programmatically via the trigger `NButton`'s `onClick` (`scope.rel('input')?.click()`).
- No built-in way to clear the selection from the rendered UI — `clearable` has no effect (see Common mistakes); clearing must be done by setting `modelValue` to `null` (or `[]`) from the parent yourself.

## Related components

`NInput` (plain string variant, and what this component uses internally for display), `NInputNumber` (numeric variant), `NTextarea` (multi-line variant), `NFormItem` (form-layout wrapper providing labels/validation context).


---

<!-- ===== components/input-number.md ===== -->

# NInputNumber

A numeric text input with increase/decrease stepper buttons and a display-format string, bound via `v-model`; reach for this over plain `NInput` whenever the value must be clamped to a `min`/`max` range or formatted (currency, units) for display.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/input/index.ts` as `NInputNumber` (`App.component(NInputNumber.name, NInputNumber)`). Source: `src/input/js/input-number/{NInputNumber,NInputNumberController,NInputNumberData,NInputNumberView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the `n-load` loading class. |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md. |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Subject to `superDisabled`. |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Renders the built-in `×` clear button (`this.clear()` is called unconditionally in the render tree, between the input and the increase button). |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Value `modelValue` resets to via `applyClear()`. |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: prop is mixed in and available via `IconData`, but `NInputNumberView` never calls `this.icon(...)` for the model's own icon (it only uses hardcoded `fa fa-minus`/`fa fa-plus` icons for the stepper buttons). No visible effect found in this component's own render tree. --> |
| `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before','after']` | `'before'` | `Props.IconPositionBefore` (`IconProps.ts`) | Same caveat as `icon` — not read in `NInputNumberView`. |
| `iconDisabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.IconDisabled` (`IconProps.ts`) | Same caveat — not read in this component's source. |
| `modelValue` | `[String, Number]` | `''` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | Declared type allows `String` or `Number`, but internally treated as numeric (`Mix.isNum` checks, `min`/`max` clamping). Cloned locally via `cloneProp('modelValue')`. |
| `min` | `Number` | `0` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | Lower clamp bound, enforced in `applyFormat()`, `decreaseNumber()`, `increaseNumber()`. |
| `max` | `Number` | `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | Upper clamp bound, same enforcement points. |
| `stepSize` | `Number` | `1` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | <!-- UNVERIFIED / confirmed dead prop: declared and exposed via `NInputNumberData.stepSize` getter/setter, but `decreaseNumber()`/`increaseNumber()` hardcode `value -= 1` / `value += 1` and never read `data.stepSize`. Setting `stepSize` currently has no effect on the stepper buttons — the step is always exactly 1 regardless of this prop. `demos/overview.html` even has a commented-out example passing `:step-size="0.1"`, suggesting this was intended to work but does not in the current source. --> |
| `precision` | `Number` | `0` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | Decimal precision. `precision > 0` parses the typed value with `Locale.num()` (decimal-aware); `precision < 1` (i.e. `0` or negative) parses with `Locale.int()`. Also passed to `Str.number(model, precision)` for display formatting. |
| `format` | `String` | `':count'` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | Display template resolved via `Locale.replace(format, { count })` — `:count` is replaced with the formatted number. E.g. `format=":count USD"` displays `"42 USD"`. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `''` | `NInputNumber.ts` (own prop) | Native placeholder text. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | new `number` | **Not** fired on every keystroke (see Gotchas). Fired by `applyFormat()` (on `Enter` keydown or on `blur`), and immediately by `decreaseNumber()`/`increaseNumber()` when the stepper buttons are used. |
| `input` | native `Event` | Native `input` event on the `<input>` element — fired on every keystroke, but this does **not** update `modelValue` by itself. |
| `keydown` | native `KeyboardEvent` | Native `keydown`. If the key is Enter (`e.which === 13`), `applyFormat(e.target.value)` runs first, then this emits. |
| `keyup` | native `KeyboardEvent` | Native `keyup`. |
| `focus` | native `FocusEvent` | Native `focus` (sets internal focus state). |
| `blur` | native `FocusEvent` | Native `blur` — `applyFormat(e.target.value)` runs first (committing/clamping the typed value), then this emits. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| none | — | `NInputNumberView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NInputNumberController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-input-number v-model="value" :min="0" :max="100" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const value = ref(0);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (currency-formatted, clamped-range field with a `:clearable` companion pair of min/max controls):

```vue
<template>
  <n-input-number v-model="minValue" :min="-100" :max="100" placeholder="Min. Value" />
  <n-input-number v-model="maxValue" :min="-100" :max="100" placeholder="Max. Value" />

  <n-input-number
    v-model="price"
    :min="minValue"
    :max="maxValue"
    :precision="2"
    :clearable="true"
    format=":count USD"
    type="primary"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const minValue = ref(-100);
const maxValue = ref(100);
const price = ref(0);
</script>
```

## Required composition

None required — standalone. Optional: can be placed inside `NButtonGroup` (confirmed composition pairing).

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `modelValue` updates live as the user types: it does not. Typing only emits a plain `input` event; `update:modelValue` is only fired on `Enter` or `blur` (via `applyFormat()`), or immediately when the stepper buttons are clicked. Code that reads `v-model` reactively while the user is mid-typing (e.g. computed validation on every keystroke) will see stale values until the field loses focus or Enter is pressed.
- Passing `:step-size` expecting the stepper buttons to move by that amount: `stepSize` is a declared, gettable/settable prop with no runtime effect — `decreaseNumber()`/`increaseNumber()` always move by exactly `1`. Treat this as a confirmed dead prop, not a misconfiguration on the consumer's side.
- Passing a non-numeric string as `modelValue` (e.g. `''` — the declared default): display falls back to an empty string (`Mix.isNum(data.model)` guard in `NInputNumberView.input()`), which is expected, but any arithmetic done against the raw prop before the first user interaction should guard against non-numeric values.

## Gotchas

- The `format` prop's `:count` placeholder is resolved via `Locale.replace()` (pico-js i18n), not a plain string replace — templates without a literal `:count` token simply never interpolate the number.
- `icon`/`iconPosition`/`iconDisabled` are present in the props table (inherited via `Props.Icon`/`Props.IconPositionBefore`/`Props.IconDisabled`) but `NInputNumberView` never renders a user-supplied icon or reads `iconDisabled` — only the hardcoded stepper icons (`fa fa-minus`/`fa fa-plus`) appear.
- Holding down the increase/decrease button (`pointerdown`) triggers one immediate step, then after a 500 ms delay starts auto-repeating every 120 ms until `pointerup` — a press-and-hold acceleration behavior that isn't obvious from the props alone.
- The clear button (`this.clear()`) is rendered unconditionally in the DOM tree between the input and the increase button, but — per `ProtoView.clear()` — only actually shows when `clearable` is true and the model is non-empty.
- There is no `nativeType` prop on this component (unlike `NInput`). The native `<input>`'s `type` attribute is set to `data.type` — i.e. the **visual** `type` prop (`primary`/`danger`/etc., or `null`). Browsers silently fall back to `type="text"` behavior for unrecognized values, so this has no visible effect in practice, but it means the styling `type` prop and the native input attribute are (harmlessly) the same underlying value, not independent concerns.

## Related components

`NInput` (plain string variant, no clamping/formatting), `NInputFile` (file selection variant), `NTextarea` (multi-line variant), `NFormItem` (form-layout wrapper providing labels/validation/`superDisabled` context).


---

<!-- ===== components/input.md ===== -->

# NInput

A single-line text input bound via `v-model`; reach for this over `NInputNumber` (numeric formatting/stepper) or `NTextarea` (multi-line) whenever you need a plain string/number field with optional icon-button and inline label.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/input/index.ts` as `NInput` (`App.component(NInput.name, NInput)`). Source: `src/input/js/input/{NInput,NInputController,NInputData,NInputView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the `n-load` loading class (see concepts.md). |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Subject to `superDisabled` (concepts.md). |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shows the built-in `×` clear button (`ProtoView.clear()`) when the model is non-empty. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Value `modelValue` is reset to by `applyClear()`. |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | When non-empty, renders a clickable icon "button" part alongside the input. |
| `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before','after']` | `'before'` | `Props.IconPositionBefore` (`IconProps.ts`) | Side the icon button renders on. |
| `iconDisabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.IconDisabled` (`IconProps.ts`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: declared and available via `IconData`, but not read anywhere in `NInputView`/`NInputController` — the icon button click handler does not check it. May currently have no visible effect on `NInput` specifically; do not assume it disables the icon click. --> |
| `modelValue` | `[String, Number]` | `''` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | v-model value. Confirmed exactly as concepts.md states. Cloned locally via `cloneProp('modelValue')`. |
| `nativeType` | `String` | `'text'` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | Passed straight through as the native `<input type="...">` attribute (e.g. `'text'`, `'password'`, `'email'`) — any valid HTML input type string works, not a closed enum. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `''` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | Native placeholder text. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | Inline label rendered next to the input; not rendered at all when empty (`Mix.isEmpty`). |
| `labelPosition` | `String` | `'before'` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | Open string; only the literal values `'before'`/`'after'` are handled in `NInputView.default()`. Any other value means the label is never rendered even if `label` is set — see Common mistakes. |
| `onButtonClick` | `Function` | `null` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | Not manually invoked in source — its presence only toggles an `n-has-event` class on the icon button. The actual click handling is via the `button-click` event (see Gotchas). |
| `onButtonDblclick` | `Function` | `null` | `NInput.ts` (own prop) | Same caveat as `onButtonClick`, for the `button-dblclick` event. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | new `string` value (`e.target.value`) | Native `input` event on the `<input>` element (`scope.update('modelValue', e.target.value)`). |
| `input` | native `Event` | Alongside `update:modelValue`, on every native input event. |
| `keydown` | native `KeyboardEvent` | Native `keydown` on the `<input>`. |
| `keyup` | native `KeyboardEvent` | Native `keyup` on the `<input>`. |
| `focus` | native `FocusEvent` | Native `focus` on the `<input>` (also sets internal focus state for the `n-focus` class). |
| `blur` | native `FocusEvent` | Native `blur` on the `<input>` (clears the focus state). |
| `button-click` | native `PointerEvent` | `pointerdown` on the icon-button part (only rendered when `icon` is set). **Not declared in the component's `emits` array** — see Gotchas. |
| `button-dblclick` | native `MouseEvent` | `dblclick` on the icon-button part. Also **not declared in `emits`**. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| none | — | `NInputView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NInputController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-input v-model="value" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const value = ref('');
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (type variants) and `demos/input/index.html` (icon-button + native-type toggle pattern, rewritten to the current `button-click` event since the demo's own `@icon-click` no longer exists in source — see Gotchas):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item label="Name">
      <n-input v-model="form.name" type="primary" placeholder="Fill me" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Disabled">
      <n-input v-model="form.name" :disabled="true" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Password">
      <n-input
        v-model="form.password"
        :native-type="nativeType"
        :icon="icon"
        @button-click="toggleNativeType"
      />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive, ref, computed } from 'vue';

const form = reactive({ name: '', password: '' });
const nativeType = ref('password');
const icon = computed(() => nativeType.value === 'text' ? 'fa fa-eye-slash' : 'fa fa-eye');

function toggleNativeType() {
  nativeType.value = nativeType.value === 'text' ? 'password' : 'text';
}
</script>
```

## Required composition

None required — standalone. Optional: can be placed inside `NButtonGroup` (confirmed composition pairing) to render alongside buttons as a segmented control-style group.

## Common mistakes

- Setting `labelPosition` to anything other than `'before'`/`'after'`: the label silently never renders, even with a non-empty `label` prop — it's an open string but only those two literal values are branch-matched in the view.
- Binding `@icon-click` (seen in the older `demos/input/index.html` demo file): this event does not exist in the current source. The actual events are `button-click` / `button-dblclick`.
- Expecting `iconDisabled` to disable the icon-button's clickability on `NInput`: it's not read anywhere in this component's Controller/View — it has no confirmed effect here (see UNVERIFIED note in Props).
- Expecting `modelValue` to stay a `Number` when bound to numeric data: the native `<input>` always emits `e.target.value`, a `string`; use `NInputNumber` if you need numeric coercion.

## Gotchas

- `button-click` and `button-dblclick` are emitted via `scope.emit(...)` but are **not** listed in `NInput`'s `emits: [...]` array. They still work when bound with `@button-click`/`:on-button-click`, because Vue resolves emit-to-listener by matching `onButtonClick`/`onButtonDblclick` against whatever is declared as a prop (which `NInput.ts` does explicitly) — but this is easy to miss since the emits array undersells the component's real event surface.
- The icon/button part only renders at all when `icon` is non-empty (`Mix.isEmpty(data.icon)` guard) — setting only `onButtonClick`/`iconPosition` without an `icon` value produces no visible button and no way to trigger `button-click`.
- The built-in clear (`×`) button only shows when `clearable` is true **and** the current model value is non-empty (`ProtoView.clear(value)`); it is unrelated to `disabled`.

## Related components

`NInputNumber` (numeric variant with stepper), `NInputFile` (file selection variant), `NTextarea` (multi-line variant), `NFormItem` (form-layout wrapper providing labels/validation/`superDisabled` context).
