<!-- ===== components/loader.md ===== -->

# NLoader

A wrapper that overlays a spinner on top of its default-slot content while `visible`, with debounced show/hide timing to avoid flicker on fast async operations.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/loader/index.ts` (`App.component(NLoader.name, NLoader)`). Source: `src/loader/js/loader/{NLoader,NLoaderController,NLoaderData,NLoaderView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings"; styles the spinner color. |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule; styles the spinner size. |
| `visible` | `[Boolean]` | `false` | local (`NLoader.ts`) | Whether the loading overlay should be shown. Not applied to the DOM directly — see the `minimum`/`debounce` timing logic below and in Gotchas. |
| `minimum` | `[Number]` | `120` | local (`NLoader.ts`) | Minimum milliseconds the spinner stays visible once shown, even if `visible` flips back to `false` almost immediately — prevents a flash-then-vanish spinner for very fast operations. |
| `debounce` | `[Number]` | `120` | local (`NLoader.ts`) | Extra milliseconds to wait, after `visible` becomes `false` and the `minimum` has already elapsed, before actually removing the spinner. |

## Events

None — `emits: []` in `NLoader.ts`; no v-model, no custom events.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The content the loader overlays (e.g. a form, a panel) — `NLoaderView.default()` renders only `this.slot()` inside the root div; the actual spinner graphic comes from the `n-load` CSS class (see Gotchas), not from a rendered child node. |

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()`/`context.expose` call in `NLoaderController` or `NLoader.ts`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-loader :visible="loading">
    <p>Content that may still be loading…</p>
  </n-loader>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const loading = ref(true);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on the `NLoader` section of `demos/overview.html`:

```vue
<template>
  <n-loader :visible="isLoading" size="md" type="primary" style="min-height: 200px; padding: 20px;">
    <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit…</p>
  </n-loader>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const isLoading = ref(true);
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — `NLoader` is a standalone wrapper around arbitrary slot content.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting the spinner to appear/disappear the instant `visible` toggles — by design it doesn't: a show is applied immediately, but a hide is delayed by up to `minimum + debounce` milliseconds total (see Gotchas) to avoid flicker on quick toggles.
- Assuming `visible` is reflected as a prop straight onto a DOM attribute/class you can target — the actual active state is the internal `active` value (`n-load` class), derived from `visible` through the timer logic, not `visible` itself.
- Toggling `visible` on/off in a tight loop expecting each toggle to restart a fresh full-length overlay — `applyTimer()` resets `this.timing` and clears any pending hide-timer on every `visible` change, but the effective on-screen duration is still governed by the same `minimum`/`debounce` math, not a naive per-toggle reset.

## Gotchas

- **The spinner graphic is pure CSS, not a rendered element.** `NLoaderView.default()` only ever renders the default slot; the visual spinner comes from `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements keyed off the `n-load` class in `src/loader/css/loader.scss` (`.n-load:before`, `.n-load:after`, and nested-loader overrides `.n-load .n-load:before/:after`). If you don't load the shipped CSS, `NLoader` renders as an inert wrapper with no visible overlay.
- **Timing algorithm (`NLoaderController`):** turning `visible` on immediately sets `active = true` (`this.set('active', this.data.visible)` inside `applyTimer()`), so *showing* is instant. Turning `visible` off does not immediately clear `active` — `startTimer()` checks how long the loader has been visible (`Date.now() - this.timing`); if that's under `minimum`, it delays via `restartTimer()` until `minimum` has elapsed, *then* re-runs `startTimer()`, which finally schedules the actual `active = false` after `debounce` more milliseconds. Net worst-case hide delay is roughly `minimum + debounce` (240ms with the defaults) after `visible` goes false, not `debounce` alone.
- Because the entire visible/active distinction is timer-driven rather than purely reactive, rapidly toggling `visible` from application code (e.g. inside a fast polling loop) can keep `active` pinned `true` far longer than any single `visible=true` window actually lasted.
- `NLoaderData.classList` only ever adds the plain `n-load` class (no `n-load-{type}`/`n-load-{size}` variant class) — `type`/`size` styling is expected to be implemented in CSS purely off the standard `n-type-{value}`/`n-size-{value}` classes from `classRoot()`, same as every other component using those mixins.

## Related components

- None directly — `load`/`n-load` is also a shared `Props.Load` boolean used by many other components (see concepts.md `BaseProps.ts`) to show their *own* inline loading state; `NLoader` is the standalone wrapper version of the same visual class.

<!-- ===== components/map-marker.md ===== -->

# NMapMarker

A single draggable/positionable pin on a geographic `NMap` (Google Maps JavaScript API marker), two-way-bound to `lat`/`lng` coordinate props — not a generic image/coordinate-grid marker.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/map/index.ts` as `NMapMarker` (`App.component(NMapMarker.name, NMapMarker)`), alongside `NMap` in the same file. Source: `src/map/js/map-marker/{NMapMarker,NMapMarkerController,NMapMarkerData,NMapMarkerView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lat` | `Number` | `0` | `NMapMarker.ts` (own prop, not from shared `Props` mixins) | Marker latitude. Reactively watched (`watchProp('lat', ...)`) — changes after mount call `marker.marker.setPosition({ lat, lng })` on the underlying Google Maps marker. |
| `lng` | `Number` | `0` | `NMapMarker.ts` (own prop) | Marker longitude. Reactively watched the same way as `lat`. |
| `drag` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NMapMarker.ts` (own prop) | Passed to the Google Maps marker as `draggable`. When `true`, dragging the pin fires `position_changed` on the marker, which (debounced 500ms) writes the new coordinates back via `update('lat', ...)`/`update('lng', ...)`. |
| `options` | `Object` | `{}` | `NMapMarker.ts` (own prop) | Raw options object merged into the Google Maps marker options: `{ ...options, lat, lng, draggable: drag }` — `lat`/`lng`/`draggable` from the dedicated props always win over anything with the same key inside `options`. <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact accepted keys inside `options` beyond `lat`/`lng`/`draggable`/`html` — this is passed straight into pico-js's `Map.createMarker(uid, options)`, whose own option schema lives outside src/ and is out of scope per task instructions. --> |

Coordinate shape: both `lat` and `lng` are plain numbers (coerced via pico-js's `Num.float()` before being handed to the map), not a combined `{lat, lng}` object prop — e.g. `:lat="53.55" :lng="9.99"` or `v-model:lat="form.lat" v-model:lng="form.lng"`. Internally they are read/written as a `{ lat: number, lng: number }` object only at the Google Maps API boundary (`marker.marker.setPosition({ lat, lng })` / `.getPosition().lat()`/`.lng()`).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:lat` | `number` — new latitude | The marker is dragged (if `drag` is `true`) and its Google Maps `position_changed` listener fires, debounced 500ms; `NMapMarkerController.updatePosition()` calls `this.update('lat', this.marker.marker.getPosition().lat())`. |
| `update:lng` | `number` — new longitude | Same trigger as above; `updatePosition()` also calls `this.update('lng', this.marker.marker.getPosition().lng())` in the same debounced callback. |

`NMapMarker.ts` declares **no `emits` array at all** (unlike `NMap.ts`, which at least declares `emits: []`). The `update:lat`/`update:lng` events still work because `ProtoController.update()` calls `context.emit()` directly — Vue allows emitting undeclared events, it just skips the (irrelevant here) prop-type validation and attribute-fallthrough exclusion emits declaration normally provides.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none (no scope object passed) | Not rendered visibly — the marker's root `<div>` is `style="display: none;"`. If a default slot is present, `NMapMarkerController.initMarker()` instead reads `this.el.innerHTML` and passes it as `options.html` to `map.createMarker(uid, options)`, i.e. the slot content becomes the custom HTML content of the Google Maps marker overlay (see the "Huhu!" yellow box example in `demos/map/index.html`). |

## Exposed methods

| Public name | Internal method | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | `superAddress` | `(address: string) => void` | Wired via `ncx.pass({ 'address': 'superAddress' })` in `NMapMarker.ts`'s `setup()`. Calling it (via a template ref, e.g. `markerRef.value.address('some street')`) calls `this.ncx('map').map.setMarkerByAddress(this.uid, address)`, and on success calls `this.ncx('map').map.superFocus()` (geocodes the address and recenters/focuses the parent map on it). |

`pass()`'s mapping is `{ [publicName]: 'internalMethodName' }` (see `src/root/js/proto/ProtoController.ts`), so the exposed public method name is **`address`**, not `setMarkerByAddress` — see Gotchas: `demos/map/index.html` calls `this.$refs.marker.setMarkerByAddress(...)`, which is stale against the current source.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-map :lat="53.55" :lng="9.99" :zoom="9">
    <n-map-marker :lat="53.55" :lng="9.99" />
  </n-map>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (draggable marker, two-way-bound coordinates displayed in disabled inputs):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form>
    <n-form-item label="Lat">
      <n-input v-model="location.lat" :disabled="true" />
    </n-form-item>
    <n-form-item label="Lng">
      <n-input v-model="location.lng" :disabled="true" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>

  <n-map :lat="location.lat" :lng="location.lng" :zoom="9">
    <n-map-marker v-model:lat="location.lat" v-model:lng="location.lng" :drag="true" />
  </n-map>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const location = reactive({ lat: 53.55, lng: 9.99 });
</script>
```

Adapted from `demos/map/index.html` (custom marker HTML content via default slot, plus the `address` exposed method — updated here to the current `address(...)` name rather than the demo's stale `setMarkerByAddress(...)` call, see Gotchas):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form-item :label="trans('Address')">
    <n-button-group>
      <n-input v-model="address" />
      <n-button @click="markerRef.address(address)">{{ trans('Set marker') }}</n-button>
    </n-button-group>
  </n-form-item>

  <n-form-item>
    <n-map>
      <n-map-marker ref="markerRef" v-model:lat="form.lat" v-model:lng="form.lng" :drag="true">
        <div style="padding: 20px; background: yellow; color: red;">Huhu!</div>
      </n-map-marker>
    </n-map>
  </n-form-item>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ lat: 53.565, lng: 10.04228 });
const address = ref('');
const markerRef = ref(null);
</script>
```

## Required composition

`NMapMarker` cannot stand alone — it requires an `NMap` ancestor. Mechanically: `NMapController.setup()` calls `provide('NMap', this.instance)`; `NMapMarkerController.setup()` calls `this.injectRef(['map', 'NMap'])` (i.e. `this.refs['map'] = inject('NMap', null)`) and then immediately does `this.ncx('map').append((map) => this.initMarker(map))`. If there is no ancestor `NMap` providing `'NMap'`, `inject` resolves to `null`, `ncx('map')` returns `undefined`, and calling `.append(...)` on `undefined` throws a `TypeError` during `NMapMarker`'s own `setup()` — i.e. rendering `<n-map-marker>` outside `<n-map>` fails immediately, not silently.

## Common mistakes

- Calling `$refs.marker.setMarkerByAddress(...)`, as `demos/map/index.html` does: the current source exposes this as `address(...)`, not `setMarkerByAddress(...)` (see Exposed methods / Gotchas).
- Using `:draggable="true"` (as the stale `demos/map/index.html` shows) instead of the actual prop name `:drag="true"`.
- Expecting a combined `position` or `coordinates` object prop: there is no such prop — `lat` and `lng` are always separate `Number` props/v-models.
- Placing `<n-map-marker>` outside of `<n-map>` (e.g. rendering it conditionally in a sibling tree, or via `<teleport>`): this throws at setup time — see Required composition.
- Assuming `options` can override `lat`/`lng`/`draggable`: `initMarker()` spreads `data.options` first, then `{ lat, lng }`, then `draggable: data.drag` — the dedicated props always take precedence over the same keys inside `options`.

## Gotchas

- `demos/map/index.html` is stale relative to current source in three ways: it uses `:lat.sync`/`:draggable` (Vue-2-era API) instead of `v-model:lat`/`:drag`, and it calls the exposed method as `setMarkerByAddress(...)` instead of the current `address(...)` (from `pass({ 'address': 'superAddress' })`). Prefer `demos/overview.html` and the current source for the accurate contract.
- `update:lat`/`update:lng` only fire when `drag` is `true` and the user actually drags the pin (or something else moves the underlying Google Maps marker and fires `position_changed`) — setting `lat`/`lng` programmatically does not create an event loop, but also means a non-draggable marker (`drag: false`, the default) never emits position updates at all; it only ever reads `lat`/`lng` in one direction (prop → marker, via `importPosition()`/`watchProp`).
- The `position_changed` handler is debounced 500ms (`Run.debounce(..., 500)`), so `update:lat`/`update:lng` (and thus a bound `v-model`) lag behind the visual drag by up to half a second.
- The component's own root element is always `display: none` — `NMapMarkerView` never renders a visible marker itself; the actual pin/overlay is painted by the Google Maps API via `map.createMarker(...)`. If `context.slots.default` exists, that hidden div's `innerHTML` becomes the marker's custom HTML content at creation time only (`initMarker()` reads `this.el.innerHTML` once) — updating slot content later does not update an already-created marker's HTML. <!-- UNVERIFIED: no watcher on slot content was found in NMapMarkerController.ts, but this is a negative/absence finding rather than a directly-quoted confirmation. -->

## Related components

- `NMap` — required parent, see "Required composition" above and `ai-docs/components/map.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/map.md ===== -->

# NMap

A geographic map (latitude/longitude, not an image/coordinate grid) that wraps `@kizmann/pico-js`'s `Map` class, which in turn wraps the Google Maps JavaScript API (`google.maps` — see `demos/map/index.html` and `demos/overview.html`, both of which load `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js`).

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/map/index.ts` as `NMap` (`App.component(NMap.name, NMap)`), alongside `NMapMarker` in the same file. Source: `src/map/js/map/{NMap,NMapController,NMapData,NMapView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lat` | `Number` | `0` | `NMap.ts` (own prop, not from shared `Props` mixins) | Initial map-center latitude, read once when the underlying Google `Map` is constructed. |
| `lng` | `Number` | `0` | `NMap.ts` (own prop) | Initial map-center longitude, read once at construction. |
| `zoom` | `Number` | `15` | `NMap.ts` (own prop) | Initial zoom level, read once at construction. |

`NMapProps` does not spread any group from the shared `Props` object (`src/root/index.ts`) — there is no `size`/`type`/`color`/`disabled`/`theme` prop on `NMap`. `NMapData.classList` calls `this.classRoot([])` with no extra modifier classes, so the root element only ever gets the base `n-map` BEM class (plus whatever `n-theme-*`/`n-disabled` `classRoot` derives from `BaseData` defaults, which are all `null`/`false` since nothing sets them).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|

`NMap.ts` declares `emits: []` — literally no emits, and `NMapController` never calls `this.emit(...)` or `this.update(...)`. Changing `:lat`/`:lng`/`:zoom` after mount does **not** recenter or re-zoom the map and there is no event to bind back to (see Gotchas).

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none (no scope object passed) | Rendered as children of the same `<div>` element that is passed to `new Map(el, {...})` as the map container — normally one or more `<n-map-marker>` elements. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NMapController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

`NMapController` does expose an internal (non-public-API) `append(cb: Function)` method used by child `NMapMarker` instances via `provide('NMap', this.instance)` / `inject`/`ncx('map')` — this is the parent/child wiring described in "Required composition" below, not something a template consumer calls directly.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-map :lat="53.55" :lng="9.99" :zoom="9" />
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (draggable marker two-way-bound to the map's displayed coordinates):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form>
    <n-form-item label="Lat">
      <n-input v-model="location.lat" :disabled="true" />
    </n-form-item>
    <n-form-item label="Lng">
      <n-input v-model="location.lng" :disabled="true" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>

  <n-map :lat="location.lat" :lng="location.lng" :zoom="9">
    <n-map-marker v-model:lat="location.lat" v-model:lng="location.lng" :drag="true" />
  </n-map>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const location = reactive({ lat: 53.55, lng: 9.99 });
</script>
```

## Required composition

`NMap` is the required parent for `NMapMarker` — see `ai-docs/components/map-marker.md` for the precise rule and failure mode. `NMap` itself has no required parent or child; it renders standalone (an empty `<n-map>` is valid, just an empty Google Map canvas).

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `:lat`/`:lng`/`:zoom` to be reactive props that recenter/rezoom the live map: `NMapController.onMounted()` reads `this.data.lat/lng/zoom` exactly once to build `new Map(this.rel('el'), {...})`. There is no `watchProp` on any of the three in `NMapController.ts`. Changing them after mount has no effect on the map view.
- Binding `v-model` on `NMap` itself: it has no `modelValue` prop and `emits: []`. Position two-way-binding happens on `NMapMarker` (`v-model:lat` / `v-model:lng`), not on `NMap`.
- Forgetting to load the Google Maps JS API script (`<script src="https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js?key=...">`) in the host page — both demos load it explicitly; nothing in `NMap`/`NMapController` injects it for you. <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether pico-js's `Map` class lazily loads the Google Maps script itself in some code path not visible in src/map/*.ts — not confirmed either way from this repo's source alone, since `Map` itself lives in the `@kizmann/pico-js` dependency, out of scope per task instructions. -->

## Gotchas

- The container `<div>` (`ref="el"`) serves double duty: it's both the literal DOM node handed to `new Map(el, {...})` (so Google Maps may inject its own canvas/controls as further children) and the Vue slot host rendering `<n-map-marker>` children (which themselves render `display: none` placeholder divs — see map-marker.md). Do not assume the rendered child markup is what visually represents the map; the visible map surface is painted by the Google Maps API into that same element.
- `demos/map/index.html` is written against an older/Vue-2-flavored API (`:lat.sync`, `:draggable`) that does not match the current source (`v-model:lat`, prop `drag` not `draggable`, `emits: []` on `NMap`). Treat `demos/overview.html` as the more current reference; see map-marker.md for the specific exposed-method mismatch this causes.
- `NMap` has no `disabled`/`size`/`type`/`color`/`theme` styling props at all — do not assume every nano-ui component gets these for free just because `ProtoData`/`classRoot` support them; a component only gets them if it spreads the relevant `Props.*` mixin, and `NMap` doesn't.

## Related components

- `NMapMarker` — the only component designed to be nested inside `NMap`; see `ai-docs/components/map-marker.md`.

<!-- ===== components/message.md ===== -->

# NMessage

A dismissible inline banner/alert box with an optional icon, title, and animated collapse-on-close transition.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/visuals/index.ts` as `NMessage` (`App.component(NMessage.name, NMessage)`). Source: `src/visuals/js/message/{NMessage,NMessageController,NMessageData,NMessageView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Size modifier, see concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known built-ins: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Styles the message via `n-type-{type}`. Demo (`demos/overview.html`) only uses `type="primary"`. |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | Rendered inside a dedicated `.n-message__symbol` wrapper — only rendered at all if `icon` is truthy (`NMessageView.symbol()` returns `null` otherwise). |
| `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before','after']` | `'before'` | `Props.IconPositionBefore` (`IconProps.ts`) | Declared via the mixin, but <!-- UNVERIFIED/dead: `NMessageView` never reads `data.iconPosition` — the icon symbol is always rendered as the first child of `.n-message__wrapper`, before `body()`, regardless of this prop's value. Treat `iconPosition` as currently inert on `NMessage`. --> |
| `modelValue` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NMessage.ts` (own prop) | Controls visibility. `true` = shown/active (adds `n-active` class); the internal close button sets it to `false` via `update()`. Cloned locally via `cloneProp('modelValue')` in `NMessageController.setup()`. |
| `closable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NMessage.ts` (own prop) | Shows/hides the built-in close (×) button (`NMessageView.close()`). |
| `title` | `String` | `null` | `NMessage.ts` (own prop) | Optional title line, rendered above the default-slot body; also adds a `with-title` class when set. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `false` | The built-in close (×) button (rendered only when `closable` is `true`) is pointer-pressed (`onPointerdown` in `NMessageView.close()`), calling `scope.update('modelValue', false)`. Note `NMessage.ts` declares `emits: []` — the event still fires functionally through `ProtoController.update()` → `context.emit()`, but is not declared in the component's `emits` option. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The message body content, rendered inside `.n-message__text` (below the title, if any). |

## Exposed methods

None. `NMessageController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-message v-model="visible" type="primary" closable>
    Something happened.
  </n-message>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const visible = ref(true);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` — with/without title and icon:

```vue
<template>
  <n-message v-bind="n_tags" type="primary" title="With title">Foo askd kasjdbnjka sjdkna</n-message>
  <n-message v-bind="n_tags" type="primary" icon="fa fa-ghost" title="With title and icon">Foo askd kasjdbnjka sjdkna</n-message>
  <n-message v-bind="n_tags" type="primary">Foo askd kasjdbnjka sjdkna</n-message>
  <n-message v-bind="n_tags" type="primary" icon="fa fa-ghost">Foo askd kasjdbnjka sjdkna</n-message>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const n_tags = reactive({ size: 'md' });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — independent, standalone component.

## Common mistakes

- Relying on `iconPosition` to move the icon after the content: it's declared as a prop (inherited from `Props.IconPositionBefore`) but `NMessageView` never reads it — the icon is always the first element in the wrapper.
- Expecting `emits` to list `update:modelValue`: `NMessage.ts` declares an empty `emits: []` array even though the close button does emit `update:modelValue` at runtime via `ProtoController.update()`. `v-model="visible"` on `<n-message>` still works (Vue only warns about undeclared emits in dev, it doesn't block them), but strict prop/emit validation tooling may flag it.
- Assuming `modelValue: false` unmounts/removes the component from the DOM: it doesn't — it only toggles the `n-active` class and (via the `ResizeObserver` + `--n-message-height` CSS var wiring in `NMessageController`) drives a height-collapse transition. The element stays mounted.

## Gotchas

- `NMessageController` wires a `ResizeObserver` on the root element (`onMounted`) that continuously writes `--n-message-height` as a CSS custom property whenever content size changes (except mid-transition, tracked via `transitionrun`/`transitionend` listeners on the same element) — this is what enables the smooth open/close height animation. The observer is disconnected in `onUnmounted`.
- `modelValue` is cloned locally (`cloneProp('modelValue')`), meaning `NMessageData.model`/`classList` reactively track the prop, but the actual close action writes back through `update()` (the standard prop → v-model round trip) rather than mutating the local clone directly.
- The close button's handler is bound to `onPointerdown`, not `onClick` — relevant if you're attaching your own click-based test/interaction logic on top of it.

## Related components

None — NMessage has no composition relationship with NTag, NRating, or NProgress; documented independently per task scope.

<!-- ===== components/modal.md ===== -->

# NModal

An overlay dialog toggled by a plain boolean `v-model`, rendered into `document.body` and stacked/backdropped through a shared global handler.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/modal/index.ts`:

```ts
App.component('NModal', NModal);
```

Source: `src/modal/js/modal/NModal.ts` (+ `NModalController.ts`, `NModalData.ts`, `NModalView.ts`). See `ai-docs/concepts.md` for the shared Controller/Data/View pattern this file assumes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the loading state/class from `ProtoData.classRoot()`. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string, not a closed enum — see `ai-docs/concepts.md`. Known styled values: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `primary`, `secondary`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `success`. |
| `theme` | `String` | `'dark'` | `Props.ThemeDark` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Note the default is `'dark'`, not `null` — `NModal` uses `ThemeDark`, not `ThemeNone`. |
| `position` | `String`, validated in `['top','bottom','left','right']` | `'right'` | `Props.PositionModal` (`PositionProps.ts`) | Adds a `{bem}--{position}` modifier class (`NModalData.classList`). Same 4-value set as `NDrawer`'s `position`, despite the name suggesting a popover-style set. |
| `modelValue` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NModal.ts` (own) | The open/closed state. Plain `v-model` — see Events below. |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NModal.ts` (own) | When `true`, the default-slot content is wrapped in an `n-scrollbar` component (`NModalView.content()`); when `false`, a plain `div`. |
| `keep` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NModal.ts` (own) | When `true`, the body/content DOM is kept mounted even while closed (`NModalView.body()`: `if (!data.keep && !data.model) return null;`). Default `false` unmounts content on close. |
| `listen` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NModal.ts` (own) | Enables the auto trigger-binding mechanism — see Gotchas. |
| `closable` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NModal.ts` (own) | When `false`, escape-key and outside-click/backdrop clicks no longer close the modal (`NModalElement.onMousedown`/`onEscape`). Explicit `close()` calls (e.g. `force: true`) still work. |
| `width` | `String \| Number` | `null` | `NModal.ts` (own) | Applied as inline `style.width` on the frame element; numbers are suffixed with `px` (`NModalData.safeWidth`). |
| `height` | `String \| Number` | `null` | `NModal.ts` (own) | Same as `width`, for `style.height`. |
| `target` | `String` | `null` | `NModal.ts` (own) | CSS selector for the trigger element. If left `null`, the trigger auto-resolves to the modal's previous DOM sibling — see Gotchas. |
| `beforeOpen` | `Function` | `null` | `NModal.ts` (own) | Called before opening. May return `false`/`Promise` to block/delay the open — see Gotchas. |
| `beforeClose` | `Function` | `null` | `NModal.ts` (own) | Same as `beforeOpen`, called before closing. |

**Confirmed: there is no `title` prop.** `NModalProps` (`src/modal/js/modal/NModal.ts`) has no `title` entry, and `NModalData`/`NModalView` never read one. `demos/modal/index.html` (a legacy Vue-2-era demo) does write `<n-modal ref="modal" title="Modal :)">`, but against the current component that `title` attribute just falls through as a plain HTML attribute — it is not consumed by the component and renders no heading. Use the `header` slot instead (see Slots).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `boolean` | Standard v-model write path (`ProtoController.update('modelValue', value)`), fired from `onOpen()`/`onClose()` whenever the internal `NModalElement` actually opens or closes (trigger click, outside click, escape key, or the exposed `open()`/`close()` methods). |
| `open` | none | Fired in `NModalController.onOpen()`, right after `update:modelValue` is emitted with `true`. |
| `close` | none | Fired in `NModalController.onClose()`, right after `update:modelValue` is emitted with `false`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `header` | none | Rendered inside `{bem}__header` above the default content, only if the slot is present (`slots.header` check in `NModalView.body()`). |
| `default` | none | Main content, wrapped in `n-scrollbar` (or a plain `div` if `scrollbar: false`) inside `{bem}__frame > {bem}__content`. |
| `footer` | none | Rendered inside `{bem}__footer` below the default content, only if present. |
| `raw` | `{ props }` where `props` is the frame's `{ name: 'frame', style }` object | Escape hatch: if present, `NModalView.body()` returns `slots.raw({ props })` directly and skips header/default/footer entirely — you own the whole frame markup. |

No slot passes a `close()` function or any other scoped helper for dismissing the modal. Closing is done exclusively by driving `v-model` to `false` (or calling the exposed `close()` method — see below), typically from a button inside your own slot content wired to your own state/ref.

## Exposed methods

Exposed via `ncx.pass({ open: 'superOpen', close: 'superClose' })` in `NModal.ts`'s `setup()`, reachable on a template ref:

- `open(silent = false)` — calls the internal `NModalElement.open(silent)`. `silent: true` still opens (and still runs `beforeOpen`), but skips the internal `onOpen` callback entirely — meaning `update:modelValue`/`open` are **not** emitted for a silent open (`NModalElement.openRun`: `if (!silent && this.options.onOpen) { this.options.onOpen(); }`).
- `close(force = false, silent = false)` — calls `NModalElement.close(force, silent)`. `force: true` bypasses `Pointer.blocked(uid)` checks (parent-chain blocking) and closes anyway; `silent: true` likewise skips the `onClose` callback, so `update:modelValue`/`close` are not emitted.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-button @click="open = true">Open modal</n-button>
  <n-modal v-model="open">
    Hello!
  </n-modal>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const open = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (header/footer slots, sizing/theme props driven reactively) and `demos/overview.html`'s `beforeClose` usage:

```vue
<template>
  <n-button>Open modal</n-button>
  <n-modal
    v-model="showModal"
    size="md"
    theme="auto"
    :width="640"
    :before-close="confirmClose"
  >
    <template #header>
      Edit item
    </template>

    <n-form>
      <n-form-item label="Name">
        <n-input v-model="form.name" placeholder="Fill me" />
      </n-form-item>
    </n-form>

    <template #footer>
      <n-button @click="showModal = false">Cancel</n-button>
      <n-button type="primary" @click="save">Save</n-button>
    </template>
  </n-modal>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue';

const showModal = ref(false);
const form = reactive({ name: '' });

function save() {
  showModal.value = false;
}

// beforeClose may return false, a boolean, or a Promise to gate closing —
// see demos/overview.html: `() => window.Confirm.make('blabla', 'danger')`
function confirmClose() {
  return window.Confirm.make('Discard changes?', 'danger');
}
</script>
```

Note: `<n-button>Open modal</n-button>` immediately precedes `<n-modal>` with no explicit `target`/`listen="false"` — this relies on the default trigger auto-binding described in Gotchas, exactly as shown in `demos/overview.html`.

## Required composition

None — `NModal` is standalone. Its content is whatever you put in the `header`/`default`/`footer`/`raw` slots; there is no required child component.

## Common mistakes

- **Assuming a `title` prop exists.** It does not (confirmed above). Use the `header` slot.
- **Assuming `v-model:visible` instead of plain `v-model`.** `NModal` uses the standard `modelValue`/`update:modelValue` pair — a plain `v-model="open"` is correct, matching `ai-docs/concepts.md`'s v-model conventions section.
- **Assuming slot-scoped close props exist** (e.g. expecting `<template #default="{ close }">`). No slot receives any scope — see Slots above. Close it by writing to your own `v-model` ref, or via the `close()` exposed method on a template ref.
- Forgetting that `keep: false` (the default) unmounts slot content while closed — don't rely on child component state persisting across opens unless `keep` is `true`.

## Gotchas

- **`listen` / trigger auto-binding**, confirmed via `src/modal/js/handler/NModalElement.ts`: when a `NModal` mounts, its `NModalElement` wrapper resolves a `target` — if the `target` prop is left `null` (the default), it auto-resolves to **the modal's previous DOM sibling element** (`Dom.find(el).prev().get(0)`, `NModalElement` constructor). With `listen: true` (the default), a global `mousedown` handler (bound once via `Pointer.bind('NModal', 'mousedown', ...)` in `NModalHandler.init()`) checks every click: if it lands inside the resolved `target`, the modal opens (if closed); if it lands outside both the `target` and the modal's own frame while the modal is open, the modal closes (subject to `closable`). This is exactly the `<n-button>Open modal</n-button><n-modal>...</n-modal>` sibling pattern used throughout `demos/overview.html`. Set `listen="false"` to disable this entirely and drive the modal purely via `v-model`/exposed methods (as `demos/drawer.html` does for `NDrawer`), or set an explicit `target="#some-selector"` to bind to a specific element instead of the previous sibling.
- **Escape key and outside-click** close behavior is also gated by `closable` (default `true`) and goes through the same global `Pointer`-bound handlers (`NModalHandler.escape`/`.mousedown`), which are registered **once** for the whole app and iterate every currently-mounted `NModalElement` (shared by `NModal`, `NDrawer`, and also `NPreview`/`NAlert`/`NConfirm`, which reuse the same `NModalHandler`/`NModalElement` classes).
- **Z-index/backdrop stacking**: opening a modal calls `NModalHandler.open(uid, zindex)` (`zindex` from `Pointer.zindex()`), which raises a shared `.n-modal-backdrop` element and adds an `n-backdrop` class to `<body>`. Closing pops it back to the next-topmost modal's z-index, or removes the backdrop entirely when none remain.
- **`beforeOpen`/`beforeClose`** (`NModalElement.onPromise`): if the function returns `false`, the open/close is cancelled; if it returns a `Promise`, the transition is deferred (and the modal is frozen against further open/close calls) until the promise settles; if it returns `null`/`undefined`, the transition proceeds immediately. `demos/overview.html` uses this to gate closing on a `Confirm` dialog: `beforeClose: () => window.Confirm.make('blabla', 'danger')`.
- **External `v-model` writes are watched and drive the real open/close machinery**: `NModalController.setup()` calls `this.watchProp('modelValue', (value) => value ? this.modal.open() : this.modal.close())`, so setting the bound ref from outside (not just clicking the trigger) correctly re-enters `NModalElement`, updates the backdrop/z-index stack, and fires `open`/`close`. (Contrast with `NDrawer` — see `ai-docs/components/drawer.md` Gotchas, which has no equivalent watcher.)

## Related components

- `NDrawer` — same Controller/View lineage (`NDrawerData extends NModalData`, `NDrawerView extends NModalView`), same `NModalHandler`/`NModalElement` stacking backend, but slides from an edge instead of centering.
- `n-scrollbar` — used internally to wrap default-slot content when `scrollbar: true` (the default).
- `NPreview`, `NAlert`/`NConfirm` (`src/preview`, `src/signal`) — also built on `NModalHandler`/`NModalElement`, so they share the same escape-key/outside-click/z-index stacking behavior described above.


---

<!-- ===== components/paginator.md ===== -->

# NPaginator

A pagination bar (limit selector, item count, "go to page" select, and page-number buttons) with no data-fetching logic of its own — purely a controlled UI over `page`/`limit`/`total`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/table/index.ts` as `NPaginator` (tag `<n-paginator>`). Source: `src/table/js/paginator/NPaginator.ts` / `NPaginatorController.ts` / `NPaginatorData.ts` / `NPaginatorView.ts`.

## Props

Spreads `Props.Size`, `Props.Type` (open strings — see concepts.md), plus its own props declared in `NPaginator.ts`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string, see concepts.md. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string, see concepts.md. |
| `page` | `Number` | `1` | own | Current page (1-indexed). Cloned locally (`cloneProp('page')`) and written via `update('page', value)`. |
| `limit` | `Number` | `100` | own | Rows-per-page. Cloned locally, written via `update('limit', value)`. |
| `limitOptions` | `Array` | `[25, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2500]` (`NPaginatorLimits`, exported from `NPaginator.ts`) | own | Options for the limit `<n-select>`. |
| `total` | `Number` | `0` | own | Total row count across all pages — used to compute `pageOptions` (`Num.ceil(total / limit)` pages) and the count text. |
| `maxPages` | `Number` | `5` | own | How many numbered page buttons to show around the current page in the `'pages'` layout slot. |
| `layout` | `Array` | `['limit', 'count', 'spacer', 'goto', 'pages']` (`NPaginatorLayout`, exported from `NPaginator.ts`) | own | Ordered list of which built-in sections to render (or a custom slot name — see Slots below). |
| `limitText` | `String` | `':count item|:count items'` | own | pico-js `Locale.choice` pluralization template for the limit-select option labels. |
| `countText` | `String` | `'No items|Total :count item|Total :count items'` | own | `Locale.choice` template (0 / singular / plural forms) for the `'count'` layout section. |
| `buttonProps` | `Object` | `null` | own | Extra props spread onto every page-number `<n-button>` (`NPaginatorView.page()`). |

There is no row-data or column prop here — `NPaginator` never touches `NTable`'s `items`; it only emits page/limit changes for your own fetch/filter logic to react to.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:page` | `(page: number)` | User picks a page from the "go to page" select (`slot_goto`) or clicks a page-number button (`page()`, on `pointerdown`) — both call `scope.update('page', index)`. |
| `update:limit` | `(limit: number)` | User picks a new page size from the limit select (`slot_limit`) — calls `scope.update('limit', value)`. |
| `paginate` | — | **Declared in `emits` but never emitted anywhere in source** (`grep` of `src/table/js/paginator` finds no `emit('paginate', ...)`/`this.emit(` call at all). Do not build logic around it — react to `update:page`/`update:limit` instead. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| any name listed in `layout` that isn't one of the 5 built-ins (`'limit'`, `'count'`, `'spacer'`, `'goto'`, `'pages'`) | none (`this.slot(key)`, no scope object passed) | `NPaginatorView.resolve(key)` looks for a `slot_${camelCase(key)}` method first; if none exists, it falls through to `slot_custom(key)`, which wraps `this.slot(key)` (a plain, unscoped named slot) in a `.n-paginator__pages` div — i.e. you can inject arbitrary custom sections into `layout` by name. |

## Exposed methods

None (`ctx.pass([...])` is never called for this component).

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-paginator :page="1" :limit="25" :total="264" />
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<template>
  <div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 500px;">
    <n-table :items="rows" style="flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0;">
      <n-table-column prop="name" label="Name" />
      <n-table-column prop="email" label="Email" />
    </n-table>

    <n-paginator
      :page="page"
      :limit="limit"
      :total="total"
      style="flex: 0 0 auto;"
      @update:page="onPage"
      @update:limit="onLimit"
    />
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const rows = ref([]);
const total = ref(0);
const page = ref(1);
const limit = ref(25);

async function fetchPage() {
  // NPaginator does not fetch or slice data itself — you own this call.
  const res = await fetch(`/api/users?page=${page.value}&limit=${limit.value}`);
  const data = await res.json();
  rows.value = data.items;
  total.value = data.total;
}

function onPage(value) {
  page.value = value;
  fetchPage();
}

function onLimit(value) {
  limit.value = value;
  page.value = 1;
  fetchPage();
}

fetchPage();
</script>
```

## Required composition

`NPaginator` has no parent/child relationship with `NTable` at all — no `inject`/`provide` wiring connects them (confirmed: `NPaginatorController` never calls `injectRef`/`provide` for an `NTable` context, unlike `NTableColumn`). **Per project convention, `NPaginator` must never be nested inside `NTable`'s default slot** — use it as a sibling element adjacent to the table (e.g. below it, as in the realistic example), wiring `page`/`limit`/`total` to your own data-fetching logic and, typically, to `NTable`'s `items`/`sortProp`/`sortDir`/`filter`.

## Common mistakes

- Waiting for a `paginate` event — it's declared but dead code; use `update:page`/`update:limit`.
- Expecting `NPaginator` to slice/paginate an `items` array for you, or to talk to a sibling `NTable` automatically — it has zero awareness of `NTable`; all page/limit/total state and the resulting refetch/reslice is entirely your app's responsibility.
- Nesting `<n-paginator>` inside `<n-table>`'s slot — don't; keep them siblings (see "Required composition").

## Gotchas

- `total` is a plain row count, not a page count — `pageOptions`/`maxPages` math derives the page count from `Num.ceil(total / limit)` internally.
- `layout` accepts arbitrary custom slot names beyond the 5 built-ins — see Slots above.

## Related components

- `NTable` — commonly paired with, but structurally independent; must be a sibling, never a child.


---

<!-- ===== components/popover-group.md ===== -->

# NPopoverGroup

A styled section label/divider rendered inside an `NPopover`'s option list (e.g. `"Group 02"` between blocks of `NPopoverOption`s).

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/popover/index.ts` as `NPopoverGroup` (`<n-popover-group>`), alongside `NPopover` and `NPopoverOption`. All three are installed together — there is no way to register one without the others.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Only affects `NPopoverGroup`'s own root class (`n-disabled` via `ProtoData.classRoot()`/`superDisabled`) — see Gotchas for what it does *not* do. |

`NPopoverGroupProps` spreads **only** `Props.Disabled` — no `Size`, `Type`, `Color`, `Icon`, etc.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|

None — `NPopoverGroup.ts` declares no `emits` array at all.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The group's label/content, rendered inside a `<span>` (`NPopoverGroupView.default()`: `h('span', null, [this.slot()])`). |

## Exposed methods

None. (No `pass(...)`/`ctx` exposure calls in `NPopoverGroupController`.)

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-button>Menu</n-button>
  <n-popover v-model="open">
    <n-popover-group>
      Section label
    </n-popover-group>
    <n-popover-option>Item</n-popover-option>
  </n-popover>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const open = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html`, used to separate blocks of menu options inside a dropdown:

```vue
<template>
  <n-button icon="fa fa-paragraph">
    Paragraph
  </n-button>

  <n-popover trigger="click" position="bottom-start">
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-paragraph">Demotext</n-popover-option>
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-paragraph">Paragraph</n-popover-option>

    <n-popover-group>
      Headings
    </n-popover-group>

    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading">Headline H3</n-popover-option>
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading">Headline H4</n-popover-option>

    <n-popover-group disabled>
      Coming soon
    </n-popover-group>
  </n-popover>
</template>
```

## Required composition

Per this doc's ground truth: **`NPopoverGroup` requires `NPopover` as its parent — it cannot be used standalone.** Render it only inside an `<n-popover>`'s `default` slot, alongside `NPopoverOption`s. See Gotchas, however, for what the source actually enforces (nothing, at runtime).

## Common mistakes

- Using `<n-popover-group>` outside of `<n-popover>` — it is intended purely as a section divider *within* a popover's option list, not a standalone component (see Required composition and Gotchas).
- Assuming `disabled` on `NPopoverGroup` disables/grays out the `NPopoverOption`s that follow it — it does not; there is no parent/child relationship or prop propagation between them at all (see Gotchas). `disabled` here only toggles `NPopoverGroup`'s own `n-disabled` class.
- Assuming `NPopoverGroup` behaves like a real "group" container (e.g. `NRadioGroup`/`NCheckboxGroup`, which track child instances via `GroupController`) — it doesn't track, count, or relate to any children at all; it renders its slot content and nothing else.

## Gotchas

- **The "requires `NPopover`" rule is a usage convention, not an enforced runtime dependency.** `NPopoverGroupController.setup()` does call `this.injectRef(['popover', 'NPopover'])`, but `injectRef` falls back to `null` (not a throw) when no ancestor `NPopover` provided the `'NPopover'` injection key — and, unlike e.g. `NTabsItem` (which unconditionally dereferences its injected parent and throws if it's `null`), `NPopoverGroupController`/`NPopoverGroupData`/`NPopoverGroupView` **never read the injected value anywhere else**. Rendering `<n-popover-group>` outside an `<n-popover>` will not throw and will render identically (just as an unstyled-context `<div class="n-popover-group"><span>...</span></div>`). Follow the stated composition rule anyway — it's the component's only intended usage — but don't expect a crash as a safety net if it's violated.
- **Despite the name, `NPopoverGroupController` extends plain `ProtoController`, not `GroupController`** (`src/root/js/controller/GroupController.ts`, described in concepts.md) — it has no `append()`/`remove()`/`childs` tracking of the `NPopoverOption`s that happen to follow it. It is a pure visual label/divider, not a functional grouping container.
- `disabled` only ever affects `NPopoverGroup`'s own root class list via `classRoot()`/`superDisabled` (see concepts.md `ProtoData`/`ProtoController`) — there's no mechanism by which it reaches sibling or nested `NPopoverOption`s.

## Related components

- `NPopover` — the required parent; see `ai-docs/components/popover.md`.
- `NPopoverOption` — the clickable-item counterpart typically used alongside `NPopoverGroup` inside the same popover. See `ai-docs/components/popover-option.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/popover-option.md ===== -->

# NPopoverOption

A single clickable menu item rendered inside an `NPopover`'s option list, with an optional icon, and optional auto-close-on-click behavior.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/popover/index.ts` as `NPopoverOption` (`<n-popover-option>`), alongside `NPopover` and `NPopoverGroup`. All three are installed together — there is no way to register one without the others.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shared disabled flag; only affects the root `n-disabled` class (see Gotchas — clicks are **not** actually blocked). |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | Icon rendered via `this.icon(data.icon)` (see `ai-docs/icons.md`), before the label `<span>`. |
| `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before', 'after']` | `'after'` | `Props.IconPositionAfter` (`IconProps.ts`) | Note: **this prop is declared but not actually read anywhere in `NPopoverOptionView`** — the icon is always rendered before the label span regardless of its value; see Gotchas. |
| `focus` | `Boolean` | `false` | own (`NPopoverOption.ts`) | Adds the `n-focus` class. Not managed internally — must be set by the consumer (e.g. for keyboard-navigation highlighting). |
| `active` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | Adds the `n-active` class. Not managed internally — must be set by the consumer (e.g. to mark the currently selected item). |
| `clickClose` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Whether clicking (or double-clicking) this option auto-closes the ancestor `NPopover`. See Gotchas. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `click` | `(e: MouseEvent)` | The option's root `<div>` receives a native `click` — `NPopoverOptionController.onClick(e)` runs the auto-close logic first (if applicable), then always calls `this.emit('click', e)`. |
| `dblclick` | `(e: MouseEvent)` | The option's root `<div>` receives a native `dblclick` — same auto-close-then-emit pattern via `onDblclick(e)`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The option's label content, rendered in a `<span>` next to the icon (`NPopoverOptionView.default()`). |

## Exposed methods

None. (No `pass(...)`/`ctx` exposure calls in `NPopoverOptionController`.)

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-button>Menu</n-button>
  <n-popover v-model="open">
    <n-popover-option @click="onSelect">
      Item
    </n-popover-option>
  </n-popover>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const open = ref(false);
function onSelect() { /* ... */ }
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` (that demo also passes an `image="..."` prop, which doesn't exist on `NPopoverOptionProps` — see Gotchas — omitted below), a dropdown menu built from `NPopoverOption`/`NPopoverGroup`:

```vue
<template>
  <n-button icon="fa fa-paragraph">
    Paragraph
  </n-button>

  <n-popover trigger="click" position="bottom-start">
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-paragraph" @click="insertParagraph">
      Demotext
    </n-popover-option>

    <n-popover-group>
      Headings
    </n-popover-group>

    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading" :active="level === 3" @click="setHeading(3)">
      Headline H3
    </n-popover-option>
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading" :active="level === 4" @click="setHeading(4)">
      Headline H4
    </n-popover-option>

    <!-- keeps the menu open after clicking, e.g. because it opens its own submenu -->
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-ellipsis" :click-close="false" @click="toggleSubmenu">
      More options
    </n-popover-option>

    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-trash" :disabled="!canDelete" @click="removeBlock">
      Delete
    </n-popover-option>
  </n-popover>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const level = ref(3);
const canDelete = ref(true);

function insertParagraph() { /* ... */ }
function setHeading(n) { level.value = n; }
function toggleSubmenu() { /* ... */ }
function removeBlock() { /* ... */ }
</script>
```

## Required composition

Per this doc's ground truth: **`NPopoverOption` requires `NPopover` as its parent — it cannot be used standalone.** It's meant to be rendered directly (optionally alongside `NPopoverGroup` section dividers) inside an `<n-popover>`'s `default` slot, where clicking it can auto-close the ancestor popover. See Gotchas for what actually happens if this rule is violated.

## Common mistakes

- Using `<n-popover-option>` outside of `<n-popover>` — it's designed as a dropdown-menu item for a popover's content, not a standalone clickable element (see Gotchas for what specifically stops working: only the auto-close behavior, not the click event itself).
- Assuming `disabled` prevents the `click`/`dblclick` handlers from firing — it does not (see Gotchas); it only changes the CSS class.
- Not setting `:click-close="false"` on an option that needs to stay open after being clicked (e.g. one that toggles a nested submenu popover or a form control) — with the default `clickClose: true`, any click closes the ancestor `NPopover` immediately.
- Expecting `iconPosition="before"` to move the icon after the label — it has no effect at all (see Gotchas).

## Gotchas

- **The "requires `NPopover`" rule degrades gracefully rather than breaking.** `NPopoverOptionController.setup()` calls `this.injectRef(['popover', 'NPopover'])`, which resolves to `null` (not a throw) when there's no ancestor `NPopover`. `onClick`/`onDblclick` both guard with `if (popover && this.get('clickClose'))` before calling `popover.ncx.superClose()` — so without an ancestor `NPopover`, the component still renders and still emits `click`/`dblclick` normally; it just silently skips the auto-close call. The composition rule is about preserving the intended dropdown-menu-item behavior, not a hard runtime dependency.
- **`disabled` does not block clicks.** Unlike most nano-ui interactive components, `NPopoverOptionView` never checks `data.disabled`/`superDisabled` before wiring `onClick`/`onDblclick` — the handlers are always attached. `disabled` only adds the `n-disabled` CSS class (via `classRoot()`); actually preventing interaction (e.g. via `pointer-events: none`) is left entirely to CSS, not JS.
- **`iconPosition` is a dead prop here.** `NPopoverOptionProps` spreads `Props.IconPositionAfter` (giving `iconPosition` a default of `'after'`, validated in `['before', 'after']`), but `NPopoverOptionView.default()` always renders `this.icon(data.icon)` immediately before the label `<span>`, regardless of `data.iconPosition`'s value — the prop is declared and validated but never actually consulted anywhere in the View.
- **Auto-close uses `superClose()` with no arguments** (`force: false, silent: false`), i.e. the same as calling the exposed `close()` method on `NPopover` with defaults — it respects the "blocked while something is stacked open on top of it" guard (`Pointer.blocked`), so clicking an option won't force-close a popover that currently has a nested submenu popover open on top of it.
- `demos/overview.html` passes an `image="https://picsum.photos/..."` prop on several `<n-popover-option>`s — this is **not** a declared prop on `NPopoverOptionProps`, and since the component doesn't set `inheritAttrs: false`, it just falls through as an inert `image` attribute on the root `<div>` (no `<img>` is ever rendered from it). Treat it as stale demo markup, not part of the current API.

## Related components

- `NPopover` — the required parent; see `ai-docs/components/popover.md`.
- `NPopoverGroup` — the section-divider counterpart typically used alongside `NPopoverOption` inside the same popover. See `ai-docs/components/popover-group.md`.

<!-- ===== components/popover.md ===== -->

# NPopover

Floating, positioned panel anchored to a trigger element (click/hover/right-click), used as the root container for dropdown-menu content (`NPopoverOption`/`NPopoverGroup`) or arbitrary custom content.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/popover/index.ts` as `NPopover` (`<n-popover>`), alongside `NPopoverGroup` and `NPopoverOption`. All three are installed together by the same plugin entry point (there is no way to register only one).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shared loading-state flag; see concepts.md. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `xs, sm, md, lg, xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `primary, secondary, info, warning, danger, success`. |
| `theme` | `String` | `'dark'` | `Props.ThemeDark` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Note: `ThemeDark`, not `ThemeNone` — `NPopover` defaults to the dark theme, unlike most components (see concepts.md `Props` table). |
| `position` | `String` | `'bottom-center'` | `Props.PositionBottomCenter` (`PositionProps.ts`) | Full 12-value popover position enum: `top-start, top-center, top-end, bottom-start, bottom-center, bottom-end, left-start, left-center, left-end, right-start, right-center, right-end`. |
| `modelValue` | `Boolean` | `false` | own (`NPopover.ts`) | Open/closed state. Plain `v-model` (see concepts.md v-model conventions — confirmed directly: `ProtoController.update('modelValue', ...)` in `onOpen`/`onClose`). |
| `width` | `Number` | `null` | own | Pixel width of the popped panel. Special value **`-1`** makes the panel match the trigger/target element's exact width (`NPopoverElement.renderBox()`: `if (width === -1) style.width = target.width() + 'px'`) — see Gotchas. |
| `target` | `String` | `null` | own | CSS selector (or element) used as the popover's anchor **and** interaction source. If left `null`, `NPopoverElement`'s constructor defaults it to the DOM element immediately preceding the popover's own root node in the DOM (`Dom.find(el).prev().get(0)`) — see Gotchas. |
| `trigger` | `String` | `'click'` | own | Open string (no validator), but only `'hover'` and `'context'` get distinct handling in `NPopoverElement`; any other value (including the default `'click'`) is treated as a left-click trigger. See Gotchas for exact per-value behavior. |
| `toggle` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | Changes what happens when the trigger is interacted with again while already open — see Gotchas. |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | When `true`, wraps the `default` slot body in an `n-scrollbar` component instead of a plain div. |
| `escapeClose` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Whether pressing Escape closes the popover (global key listener via `NPopoverHandler`/`Pointer`). |
| `scrollClose` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Whether scrolling closes the popover — see Gotchas for the exact "inside vs. outside" rule. |
| `multiClose` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Whether opening this popover force-closes other, unrelated open popovers elsewhere on the page (single-dropdown-at-a-time behavior). Popovers nested inside this one's own content share its "group" and are exempt. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `(value: boolean)` | The underlying `NPopoverElement` fires its own `'open'`/`'close'` event (from user interaction, programmatic `open()`/`close()`, Escape, scroll, etc.) — `NPopoverController.onOpen()`/`onClose()` call `this.update('modelValue', true/false)`. |
| `open` | none | Immediately after `update:modelValue` is emitted with `true`, in `onOpen()`. |
| `close` | none | Immediately after `update:modelValue` is emitted with `false`, in `onClose()`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `raw` | none | If present, **completely bypasses** `header`/`default`/`footer` and the built-in frame wrapper — `NPopoverView.frame()` returns `slots.raw()` directly. Used internally by `NPopoverPanel` (see Gotchas) to render a fully custom panel body. |
| `header` | none | Rendered above the body, wrapped in `.n-popover__header`. Only rendered if the slot is present. |
| `default` | none | The main body content. Wrapped in `.n-popover__body` (or an `n-scrollbar` component if `scrollbar` is `true`). |
| `footer` | none | Rendered below the body, wrapped in `.n-popover__footer`. Only rendered if the slot is present. |

The whole `frame()` (header/body/footer, or `raw`) only renders while the popover is open (`data.model` true) — closed popovers render an empty, hidden `n-hidden` root div.

## Exposed methods

Exposed onto the component's public `ctx` via `ncx.pass({ open: 'superOpen', close: 'superClose' })` in `NPopover.ts`'s `setup()` — accessible through a template ref:

| Method | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | `(silent = false)` | Calls the internal `NPopoverElement.open(silent)` directly. `silent: true` skips firing the `onOpen` callback (and therefore the `open`/`update:modelValue` events). |
| `close` | `(force = false, silent = false)` | Calls `NPopoverElement.close(force, silent)`. `force: true` bypasses the internal "blocked while a nested/stacked popover is open on top of it" guard (`Pointer.blocked(uid)`); `silent: true` skips firing `onClose`/events. |

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-button>Menu</n-button>
  <n-popover v-model="open">
    Hello from the popover.
  </n-popover>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const open = ref(false);
</script>
```

Note the `<n-button>` immediately precedes `<n-popover>` as a sibling — with no `target` prop set, the popover auto-anchors to (and listens on) whichever element comes right before it in the DOM.

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html`'s dropdown-menu example (that demo also uses an `:always-render="true"` attribute and an `image` prop on `n-popover-option` — neither exists in current source, see Gotchas — both are omitted below):

```vue
<template>
  <n-button icon="fa fa-paragraph">
    Paragraph
  </n-button>

  <n-popover trigger="click" :width="200" type="primary" position="bottom-start" :multi-close="false" :toggle="true">
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-paragraph">
      Demotext
    </n-popover-option>
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-paragraph">
      Paragraph
    </n-popover-option>
    <n-popover-group>
      Group 02
    </n-popover-group>
    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading">
      Headline H3
    </n-popover-option>

    <!-- a popover nested directly after an option auto-targets that option,
         forming a hover-triggered submenu (see Gotchas) -->
    <n-popover trigger="hover" position="right-start">
      <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading">
        Submenu item
      </n-popover-option>
    </n-popover>

    <n-popover-option icon="fa fa-heading">
      Headline H4
    </n-popover-option>
  </n-popover>
</template>
```

## Required composition

`NPopover` has no required parent — it can be used standalone anywhere. It is, however, the **required parent** for `NPopoverGroup` and `NPopoverOption` (see those components' docs).

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `target` to be required — it is optional and, unset, auto-resolves to the previous DOM sibling, which is the common case (a trigger button placed right before `<n-popover>`). Explicit `target` (a CSS selector) is only needed when the trigger element isn't the popover's immediate previous sibling.
- Assuming `trigger` is a closed enum — it's a plain `String`; anything other than `'hover'`/`'context'` silently behaves like `'click'`, so typos (e.g. `trigger="clicked"`) fail silently rather than throwing.
- Treating `width: -1` as an invalid/ignored value — it's a deliberate special case meaning "match the target's width."
- Forgetting `theme` defaults to `'dark'` here (unlike most components, which default `theme` to `null`).

## Gotchas

- **`target` auto-detection**: `NPopoverElement`'s constructor sets `target` to `Dom.find(el).prev().get(0)` when the prop is `null` — i.e., the DOM node immediately before the popover's own (initially in-place, later moved-to-`<body>`) root element at mount time. This is what makes the common `<n-button>...</n-button><n-popover>...</n-popover>` sibling pattern work without an explicit `target`.
- **Nested popovers as submenus**: because of the above, a `<n-popover>` placed as a sibling immediately after an `<n-popover-option>` (both inside an outer `<n-popover>`'s body) auto-targets that specific option, and shares the outer popover's stacking "group" (found via the nearest ancestor `[data-popover]` element) so opening/closing the submenu doesn't fight with the parent's `multiClose` logic. This pattern is inferred directly from `NPopoverElement`'s source and mirrors `demos/overview.html`'s structure, but the demo itself uses some props (`image`, `always-render`) that don't exist in current source — treat the *nesting structure* as reliable, not every prop in that demo.
- **`toggle` semantics**: with `toggle: false` (default), clicking the trigger again while the popover is already open does nothing (`getEventEls` finds the click still inside `target`/the popover itself, so `state()` stays idle) — it only closes via an outside click, Escape, scroll-away, or (for `NPopoverOption`) `clickClose`. With `toggle: true`, clicking the *target/trigger element* again while open closes it, but clicking *inside the popover's own rendered content* does not (`state = src`, where `src` matches only the popover's own element, not the external `target`).
- **`scrollClose` "inside vs. outside" rule**: `NPopoverElement.onScroll()` only keeps the popover open if the scroll event carries `event.detail.target` and that target is contained within the popover's own root element (i.e., a scroll originating from the popover's own internal `n-scrollbar`, which dispatches a custom `virtualscroll` event with `detail.target`). Any plain native `scroll` event (page/ancestor scrolling) has no `event.detail`, so it always closes the popover when `scrollClose` is `true` (the default).
- **`escapeClose`**: Escape only closes the popover when `escapeClose` is `true` (default); when `false`, Escape is a no-op (not a "prevent all closing" flag for other close paths).
- **`NPopoverPanel` is an internal-only base component**: `src/popover/js/popover-panel/NPopoverPanel.ts` defines an `NPopoverPanel` component (BEM `n-popover-panel`) that wraps an `<n-popover>` as a `raw`-slot panel with a display/handle/clear/angle row — but it is **not** registered by `src/popover/index.ts` and never appears as `<n-popover-panel>` in any demo. Its `Controller` is instead used as a **base class** that other components' own controllers extend directly (`NSelectController`, `NCascaderController`, `NDatepickerController`, `NTimepickerController`, `NDurationpickerController`, `NDatetimepickerController` all reference `NPopoverPanelController`/`NPopoverPanelData`/`NPopoverPanelView`) to get a consistent "form-field that opens a popover panel" shape. Do not expect to use `<n-popover-panel>` directly in a template.
- `demos/overview.html`'s popover example passes `:always-render="true"` on `<n-popover>` and `image="..."` on `<n-popover-option>` — neither is a declared prop in current source (`NPopoverProps`/`NPopoverOptionProps`). Since neither component sets `inheritAttrs: false`, these just fall through as inert DOM attributes on the root `<div>`; they have no functional effect. Treat them as stale/leftover demo markup, not part of the current API.

## Related components

- `NPopoverGroup` — a labeled section/divider inside a popover's option list; requires `NPopover` as parent. See `ai-docs/components/popover-group.md`.
- `NPopoverOption` — a clickable menu item inside a popover; requires `NPopover` as parent. See `ai-docs/components/popover-option.md`.
