<!-- ===== components/preview.md ===== -->

# NPreview

An inline thumbnail component for a file/image/video/URL that opens a shared fullscreen lightbox (with prev/next paging across a `group`) when clicked.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/preview/index.ts` (`App.component(NPreview.name, NPreview)`), which also seeds `globalThis.NPreviewModules = { text: NPreviewFileModule, image: NPreviewImageModule, video: NPreviewVideoModule }`. Source: `src/preview/js/preview/{NPreview,NPreviewController,NPreviewData,NPreviewView}.ts`, `src/preview/js/preview-module/{NPreviewFileModule,NPreviewImageModule,NPreviewVideoModule}.ts`, `src/preview/js/handler/{NPreviewElement,NPreviewHandler}.ts`, `src/preview/js/helper/NPreviewHelper.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Standard load-state class from `classRoot()`. |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `theme` | `String` | `null` | `Props.ThemeNone` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Root theme class. |
| `file` | `any` | `null` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | The full-resolution source: a `File`/`Blob` (rendered via `FileReader`), a URL string (image/video/pdf/etc.), or a YouTube/Vimeo URL (detected by `NPreviewHelper.youtube`/`vimeo` and rendered as an embedded `<iframe>`). Used for the fullscreen portal. |
| `thumb` | `any` | `null` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | The thumbnail source shown in the inline (non-fullscreen) body. Falls back to `file` if omitted (`safeThumb = thumb ?? file`), and vice versa (`safeFile = file ?? thumb`). |
| `title` | `[String]` | `null` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Caption rendered under the inline thumbnail (`NPreviewView.title()`); hidden when empty. |
| `index` | `[Number]` | `null` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | This item's position within its `group` for prev/next ordering in the lightbox. If omitted, `NPreviewHandler.append()` assigns `previews.length * 10`. Changing `index` at runtime re-registers the item (`watchProp('index', onChange)` tears down and re-mounts its handler registration). |
| `group` | `[String]` | `() => Hash.uuid()` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Groups multiple `NPreview` instances into one lightbox gallery — prev/next only cycles items sharing the same `group` string. Defaults to a fresh UUID per instance, i.e. **standalone by default** — set the same `group` string on sibling `NPreview`s to link them. |
| `fit` | `[String]` | `'contain'` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Inline thumbnail `object-fit`. Confirmed styled values in `src/preview/css/preview.scss`: `contain` (default), `cover`, applied via `n-preview--{fit}`. |
| `mime` | `[String]` | `null` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: declared prop, but not read anywhere in NPreviewController/Data/View — mime type is instead always derived at render time via `NPreviewHelper.mime(safeFile/safeThumb)`. Appears unused. --> |
| `forceFile` | `[Boolean]` | `false` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: declared prop, not read anywhere in NPreviewController/Data/View. Appears unused. --> |
| `preview` | `[Boolean]` | `true` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Enables the click-to-open lightbox and the hover overlay icon. When `false`, the component just renders a static thumbnail with no click handler and no hover affordance. |
| `previewTypes` | `[Array]` | `() => ['text', 'image']` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Which resolved type categories are allowed to render their *real* thumbnail inline; any type not in this list is forced to `'text'` (generic file display) for the inline body only — see "Module-type selector" below. The fullscreen portal always uses the file's real resolved type regardless of this prop. |
| `showPath` | `[Boolean]` | `true` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Shows the filename (path tail) in the fullscreen meta list. |
| `linkText` | `[String]` | `'Download file'` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Label for the fullscreen download link, passed through `Locale.trans()`. |
| `showLink` | `[Boolean]` | `true` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Shows a download link (`n-button`, `href` = `file`, `target="_blank"`) in the fullscreen meta list. Only rendered when `file` is a string (`Mix.isStr`). |
| `onFocus` | `[Function]` | `null` | local (`NPreview.ts`) | Called (not emitted) when this preview becomes the focused slide in the lightbox — see Events. |

## Module-type selector (`previewTypes` / resolved type)

There is no closed `type`-selector prop on `NPreview` itself; instead each file's display type is *computed* by `NPreviewHelper.type()` from its extension (or detected as a YouTube/Vimeo URL), and only the categories listed in `previewTypes` are allowed to render inline as their real module — the rest are forced to `'text'` for the inline thumbnail.

Full category list produced by `NPreviewHelper.type()` (`NPreviewMimes` map in `src/preview/js/helper/NPreviewHelper.ts`):

- `image` — extensions `jpg, jpeg, gif, svg, png, bmp`
- `video` — extensions `mp4, webm, mov`, plus any detected YouTube/Vimeo URL
- `audio` — extensions `mp3, aac`
- `font` — extensions `woff, ttf, otf`
- `text` — extensions `csv, txt, html`, and the fallback when nothing matches
- `application` — extensions `pdf, doc, xls`

Of these, only three have an actual rendering module registered in `globalThis.NPreviewModules`: `'text'`, `'image'`, `'video'`. `NPreviewView.resolve(type)` looks up `globalThis.NPreviewModules[type]` and **falls back to `'text'`** for any unregistered type — so `audio`, `font`, and `application` files always render through `NPreviewFileModule` (a generic meta list: mime type, path, optional download link), never a native player.

`previewTypes`'s default `['text', 'image']` means: only images render their real thumbnail inline by default; video files show as a generic file entry inline (still open the real `<video>`/YouTube/Vimeo player when clicked, since the fullscreen portal is unaffected by `previewTypes`).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `focus` | — | Declared in `emits: ['focus']`, but `NPreviewController` never calls `this.emit('focus', ...)`. <!-- UNVERIFIED / apparent dead declaration --> The actual "this slide became focused" hook is the `onFocus` **prop** (a plain callback, not a Vue event): `focusPortal()` calls `this.get('onFocus')?.()` directly. Fired by `NPreviewHandler.next()`/`.prev()` calling `this.el.focus()` on the newly active `NPreviewElement`, which in turn calls the `onFocus` handler registered in `NPreviewController.onMounted()`. |

## Slots

None — `NPreview` has no `this.slot(...)` calls in `NPreviewView`; content comes entirely from the `file`/`thumb` props and the registered preview module.

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()`/`context.expose` call in `NPreviewController` or `NPreview.ts`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-preview file="https://picsum.photos/1920/1920.jpg" style="width: 160px;"></n-preview>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on the `NPreview` section of `demos/overview.html` — a mixed gallery grouping images, a YouTube link, a Vimeo link, a video, and a PDF into one lightbox via a shared `group`, with explicit `index` to control paging order:

```vue
<template>
  <div class="n-grid gap-10">
    <n-preview
      group="gallery"
      :index="0"
      file="https://picsum.photos/1920/1920.jpg?a"
      thumb="https://picsum.photos/300/300.jpg?a"
      title="Photo A"
      style="width: 160px;"
    ></n-preview>

    <n-preview
      group="gallery"
      :index="1"
      file="https://picsum.photos/1920/1920.jpg?b"
      thumb="https://picsum.photos/300/300.jpg?b"
      title="Photo B"
      style="width: 160px;"
    ></n-preview>

    <n-preview
      group="gallery"
      :index="2"
      file="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m_Nw_BF90_4"
      thumb="https://via.placeholder.com/100/000/fff.jpg?text=Youtube"
      style="width: 160px;"
    ></n-preview>

    <n-preview
      group="gallery"
      :index="3"
      file="https://www.w3schools.com/html/mov_bbb.webm"
      title="Sample video"
      style="width: 160px;"
    ></n-preview>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Required composition

None — every `NPreview` instance registers itself with the internal `NPreviewHandler` singleton on mount and needs no wrapping component. Grouping into one gallery is done purely by giving multiple instances the same `group` string prop, not by nesting them inside a parent component.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a JS API like `NPreview.open(...)` (à la `Notify`/`Alert`/`Confirm`) — there isn't one. `NPreview` is a template component; you drop `<n-preview>` where the thumbnail should appear, and clicking it (when `preview` is `true`, the default) opens the lightbox itself.
- Omitting `group` on related images and expecting prev/next to cycle between them — each `NPreview` defaults `group` to its own random UUID, so without an explicit shared `group` string every instance is its own single-item gallery.
- Assuming `previewTypes` changes what the fullscreen lightbox can play — it only controls whether the *inline* thumbnail shows the real preview (e.g. an actual `<video>` element) vs. a generic file icon. The fullscreen portal always resolves the real type.
- Setting `mime` or `forceFile` expecting them to affect rendering — neither prop is read anywhere in the component; the mime type and displayed module are always derived from `file`/`thumb` via `NPreviewHelper`.
- Relying on the `focus` emit (`@focus="..."`) — it is declared but never fired; use the `onFocus` prop (a plain function) instead.

## Gotchas

- **Invocation model: inline template component, not a global handler.** Unlike `Alert`/`Confirm`/`Notify`, there is no global function you call to show a preview — `<n-preview>` renders its own inline thumbnail in place, and internally uses a global singleton (`NPreviewHandler`, `src/preview/js/handler/NPreviewHandler.ts`) purely as **internal plumbing** to coordinate a shared fullscreen `<div class="n-preview-modal">` overlay (built once, appended to `document.body`, layered via `NModalHandler.open(uid, zIndex)` so it stacks correctly with real `NModal`s) and to support prev/next paging across every mounted `NPreview` sharing a `group`. You never call `NPreviewHandler` yourself.
- Clicking a thumbnail calls `scope.openPreview()`, which defers to `Pointer.wait(...)` before calling `NPreviewHandler.open(this.preview)` — this is a drag-vs-click disambiguation guard (from `Pointer`, `@kizmann/pico-js`), not an animation delay.
- The lightbox listens globally for `Escape` (close), `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` (prev/next), and a `mouseup` on its own backdrop (`n-preview-modal__frame`) to close — these are bound once at `NPreviewHandler.init()` module-load time, not per-instance.
- `NPreviewHandler.next()`/`.prev()` are throttled by a `blocked` flag while the slide-out CSS transition (`transitionend` on `.n-animate-left`/`.n-animate-right`) is running, so rapid arrow-key presses are naturally debounced rather than queued.
- `previewTypes`'s type check (`Arr.has(data.previewTypes, display.type)`) only applies "when `data.preview` is true" — i.e. it's specifically about deciding whether to render the real preview element behind the click-affordance; with `preview: false` the raw resolved type is always used for the (now unclickable) inline thumbnail.
- `linkText` and `emptyText`-style props here go through `Locale.trans()` even though `linkText`'s own default is a hardcoded literal `'Download file'` (not sourced from `Props.EmptyText`-style i18n mixins) — the literal string is itself passed through translation at render time via the `$linkText` getter.

## Related components

- `NModalHandler`/`NModal` (`src/modal/`) — the fullscreen lightbox reuses `NModalHandler.open(uid, zIndex)`/`.close(uid)` purely for z-index stacking with other modals; it does not render an `NModal` instance itself.
- `n-button` — used for the fullscreen download link (`NPreviewView.link()`).

<!-- ===== components/progress.md ===== -->

# NProgress

A horizontal progress bar whose fill percentage and status color are driven by a numeric value plus a numeric `state` enum.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/visuals/index.ts` as `NProgress` (`App.component(NProgress.name, NProgress)`). Source: `src/visuals/js/progress/{NProgress,NProgressController,NProgressData,NProgressView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds `n-size-{size}` when non-null (`NProgressData.classList` checks `this.size != null` explicitly, unlike most components which delegate entirely to `classRoot()`). |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known built-ins: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Base color when `state === 1` (or falls back to the literal string `'primary'` if `type` is unset). **Overridden entirely for `state` values `0`, `2`, `3`** — see the `state` row below. |
| `modelValue` | `Number` | `0` | `NProgress.ts` (own prop) | The progress percentage. Clamped to `[0, 100]` in `NProgressData.value` (`Math.min(100, Math.max(0, model))`) and written to the CSS custom property `--n-progress-width` on the bar element. Cloned locally via `cloneProp('modelValue')`; there is no interaction that writes back to it (no `update()` calls anywhere in `NProgressController`/`NProgressView` — it is one-way, parent → display only). |
| `state` | `Number` | `0` | `NProgress.ts` (own prop) | Status enum controlling both the bar's color and a status CSS class. Exact mapping, read directly from `NProgressData.classList` in `src/visuals/js/progress/NProgressData.ts`:<br>• **`0`** — pending/awaiting: color forced to `'neutral'` (`n-type-neutral`, regardless of the `type` prop), adds class `n-await`.<br>• **`1`** — active/in-progress: color is whatever `type` resolves to (`type` prop, or `'primary'` if unset) — the only state that respects the `type` prop, adds class `n-active`.<br>• **`2`** — done/success: color forced to `'success'` (`n-type-success`, regardless of `type`), adds class `n-done`.<br>• **`3`** — aborted/error: color forced to `'danger'` (`n-type-danger`, regardless of `type`), adds class `n-abort`.<br>Any other numeric value falls through all four `if` checks: no `n-await`/`n-active`/`n-done`/`n-abort` class is added, and the color falls back to whatever `type` resolves to (same as state `1`'s color logic, but without the `n-active` class). |
| `changeState` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NProgress.ts` (own prop) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: declared as a prop but not read anywhere in NProgressController/NProgressData/NProgressView. Appears to currently have no effect in this source; do not assume it drives automatic state transitions despite the name suggesting that. --> |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | `NProgress.ts` declares `emits: []`. Nothing in `NProgressController`/`NProgressView` calls `update()` or `emit()` — `NProgress` is a purely presentational, one-way display component; `modelValue`/`state` are meant to be driven from the parent, not written back. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | None. `NProgressView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NProgressController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-progress :model-value="45" />
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` — the four `state` values in sequence:

```vue
<template>
  <n-progress v-bind="n_progress" type="primary" :model-value="30" :state="0"></n-progress>
  <n-progress v-bind="n_progress" type="primary" :model-value="40" :state="1"></n-progress>
  <n-progress v-bind="n_progress" type="primary" :model-value="20" :state="2"></n-progress>
  <n-progress v-bind="n_progress" type="primary" :model-value="20" :state="3"></n-progress>
</template>
```

Note: `demos/overview.html` binds `v-bind="n_progress"` but never defines an `n_progress` key in its `data()` (only `n_tags`, `n_rating`, etc. are defined) — <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether this is a stale/incomplete demo binding; `n_progress` resolves to `undefined` there, which Vue's `v-bind` treats as binding nothing. Not a reason to omit `v-bind` in your own usage, just noting the demo itself appears incomplete on this point. -->

## Required composition

None — independent, standalone component.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `state` and `type` combine additively: for `state` `0`, `2`, and `3`, the `type` prop's color is **completely overridden** (forced to `neutral`/`success`/`danger` respectively) — only `state: 1` actually uses the `type` prop's value for color. Setting `type="danger"` with `state="2"` still renders as success-green.
- Expecting `modelValue` to be settable via `v-model`: there is no `update:modelValue` emit anywhere in this component — it's a display-only value, not a v-model target, despite the prop being named `modelValue`.
- Expecting `changeState` to do something (e.g. auto-cycle or animate state changes): it's declared but never read anywhere in the Controller/Data/View of this source — currently inert.
- Passing a `state` value outside `0`–`3` expecting a sensible fallback class: no status class (`n-await`/`n-active`/`n-done`/`n-abort`) is added at all for out-of-range values, only the color-class fallback (equivalent to state `1`'s color, minus the `n-active` class).

## Gotchas

- `modelValue` is silently clamped into `[0, 100]` (`NProgressData.value`) before being written to `--n-progress-width` — passing `150` or `-10` will not overflow or empty the bar, it clamps to `100`/`0`.
- `size` is applied with an explicit `this.size != null` guard directly in `NProgressData.classList` rather than going through the shared `classRoot()` helper used by most other components (see concepts.md) — functionally equivalent for this prop, but worth knowing if you're comparing class-building logic across components.
- The bar fill itself is a nested `<div class="n-progress__bar">` with its width driven purely by the `--n-progress-width` CSS custom property — there's no width-transition/animation logic in the JS layer; any animated-fill behavior would come entirely from CSS (out of scope for this doc).

## Related components

None — NProgress has no composition relationship with NTag, NRating, or NMessage; documented independently per task scope.

<!-- ===== components/radio-group.md ===== -->

# NRadioGroup

The container and single source of truth for a mutually-exclusive set of `NRadio` options.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/radio/index.ts` (`App.component(NRadioGroup.name, NRadioGroup)`). Source: `src/radio/js/radio-group/{NRadioGroup,NRadioGroupController,NRadioGroupData,NRadioGroupView}.ts`. `NRadioGroupController extends GroupController` (see concepts.md), and `provide('NRadioGroup', this.instance)` so children can `inject` it — required, since every `NRadio` throws without it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Styles the group root only (`classRoot()`); not read directly by `NRadioGroupData`. Children read their own `size` prop independently. |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same as above — group root only. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Styles the group root via `superDisabled`/`classRoot()`; each child `NRadio` still has its own separate `disabled` prop (not cascaded). |
| `align` | `String`, validated in `['horizontal','vertical']` | `'horizontal'` | `Props.AlignHorizontal` (`AlignProps.ts`) | Layout direction of the children; adds a `{bem}--{align}` class. |
| `modelValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `''` | local (`NRadioGroup.ts`) | The selected value — this is the actual v-model; individual `NRadio`s only read it via a linked alias (see `radio.md`). |
| `view` | `String` (known: `'checkbox'`, `'button'`) | `'checkbox'` | local (`NRadioGroup.ts`) | Visual style, applied to every child (a child's own `view` prop is always overridden — see `radio.md` Gotchas). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `string \| number \| boolean` (whatever the selected child's `value` is) | `NRadioGroupController.superApply(child)` runs — triggered when any child `NRadio` is clicked (`NRadioController.superApply()` → `ncx('group').superApply(this)`) or its exposed `.apply()` is called directly. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The child `NRadio` items. |

## Exposed methods

`ncx.pass({ apply: 'superApply' })` — a template ref exposes `.apply(child)`, but it expects an actual child `NRadioController` instance (as obtained internally via `ncx('...')`), not a plain value — not practically callable from outside the library's own render tree. To select an option programmatically, prefer a specific `NRadio`'s own exposed `.apply()` (see `radio.md`, which takes no arguments), or simply set the group's `v-model` value directly.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-radio-group v-model="selected">
    <n-radio value="foo">Foo</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="bar">Bar</n-radio>
  </n-radio-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const selected = ref('');
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on `demos/radio/index.html` and `demos/overview.html`'s button/vertical variants:

```vue
<template>
  <n-radio-group v-model="form.option" size="md" type="primary" align="vertical">
    <n-radio value="test1">Foobar 1</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test2">Foobar 2</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test3">Foobar 3</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test4">Foobar 4</n-radio>
  </n-radio-group>

  <n-radio-group v-model="form.option" view="button" align="horizontal">
    <n-radio value="test1">Foobar 1</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test2">Foobar 2</n-radio>
  </n-radio-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ option: 'test1' });
</script>
```

## Required composition

Must contain `NRadio` children — an `NRadio` cannot exist outside of it (throws at setup), and per the confirmed composition rule, `NRadioGroup` may only contain `NRadio` (no other component reads/provides the `NRadioGroup` inject key). An empty `NRadioGroup` renders but has nothing selectable.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting the group's `disabled` prop to cascade and disable every child `NRadio`: it only styles the group's own root — each `NRadio` needs its own `disabled` prop set individually.
- Trying to call the group's exposed `.apply(child)` with a plain value (e.g. `groupRef.apply('foo')`) to select an option: it expects a live child controller instance. Set `form.option = 'foo'` directly, or call the specific child radio's own `.apply()` instead.
- Initializing `modelValue` to `null`/`undefined` and expecting the first radio to show as selected: the declared default is an empty string `''`, and selection is strict-`===` against each child's `value` — no radio is selected until the model matches a real child value.

## Gotchas

- The group's `view` prop is inherited by every child regardless of what `view` each child declares — see `radio.md` Gotchas (`NRadioData.view` prefers `ncx('group')?.data.view`, and since a group is mandatory, the child's own `view` prop is unreachable in practice).
- Because `NRadio` requires a group to even mount, all of the actual `update:modelValue` traffic for this pair originates from `NRadioGroupController`, not from any `NRadio` instance — despite `NRadio.ts` also declaring `emits: ['update:modelValue']` (dead declaration, see `radio.md`).

## Related components

- `NRadio` — the required child; see `radio.md`.
- `NCheckboxGroup`/`NCheckbox` — non-exclusive counterpart, and unlike this pair, `NCheckbox` can stand alone outside `NCheckboxGroup`. See `checkbox-group.md`/`checkbox.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/radio.md ===== -->

# NRadio

A single option within an `NRadioGroup` — mutually exclusive selection. Unlike `NCheckbox`, it cannot be used standalone.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/radio/index.ts` (`App.component(NRadio.name, NRadio)`), alongside `NRadioGroup` from the same group index. Source: `src/radio/js/radio/{NRadio,NRadioController,NRadioData,NRadioView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the `n-disabled` class — see Gotchas, it does **not** block clicks by itself. |
| `value` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `'undefined'` (the literal string, **not** JS `undefined` — see Gotchas) | local (`NRadio.ts`) | The value this radio represents; compared against the group's `modelValue` with strict `===` to determine `n-checked`. |
| `view` | `String` (known: `'checkbox'`, `'button'` — confirmed via `n-radio--button` in `themes/default/radio/src/radio/radio.scss`) | `'checkbox'` | local (`NRadio.ts`) | Declared but effectively dead when used correctly — see Gotchas (`NRadio` always has a group, so the group's `view` always wins). |

**Note:** `NRadio` does **not** declare its own `modelValue` prop at all — see Events below.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | declared in `emits: ['update:modelValue']`, but **`NRadio` never actually calls `this.update('modelValue', ...)` on itself.** | Selection is driven by `NRadioController.superApply()`, which calls `this.ncx('group').superApply(this)` — the **group** (`NRadioGroupController.superApply(child)`) is what calls `this.update('modelValue', child.data.value)` and emits `update:modelValue`. Bind `v-model` to `NRadioGroup`, not to individual `NRadio`s. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Rendered inside `.n-radio__label`, next to the radio dot — the visible label text. |

## Exposed methods

`ncx.pass({ apply: 'superApply' })` — a template ref exposes `.apply()` (no arguments), which selects this radio exactly as a click would (tells the group to set its `modelValue` to this radio's `value`).

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-radio-group v-model="selected">
    <n-radio value="foo">Foo</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="bar">Bar</n-radio>
  </n-radio-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const selected = ref('');
</script>
```

*(`NRadio` cannot be rendered outside an `NRadioGroup` — see Required composition.)*

## Realistic example

Modeled on `demos/radio/index.html` and the `NRadio` section of `demos/overview.html`:

```vue
<template>
  <n-radio-group v-model="form.option" size="md" type="primary" align="vertical">
    <n-radio value="test1">Foobar 1</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test2">Foobar 2</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test3">Foobar 3</n-radio>
    <n-radio value="test4">Foobar 4</n-radio>
  </n-radio-group>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ option: 'test1' });
</script>
```

## Required composition

**`NRadio` cannot stand alone.** `NRadioController.setup()` calls `injectRef(['group', 'NRadioGroup'])` and throws `Error('NRadioGroup is required in radio!')` if no ancestor `NRadioGroup` provides that inject key. It must always be a child of `NRadioGroup`.

## Common mistakes

- Rendering a bare `<n-radio value="x">Foo</n-radio>` outside of `<n-radio-group>`, expecting it to behave like a standalone toggle (as `NCheckbox` can) — it throws at setup instead.
- Putting `v-model` on individual `<n-radio>` elements: `NRadio` has no `modelValue` prop of its own; the v-model belongs on the parent `NRadioGroup`.
- Omitting `value` on an `<n-radio>` and expecting it to be selectable by binding the group's model to `undefined`: the prop's actual default is the *string* `'undefined'`, not the JS value `undefined` — a group `modelValue` of real `undefined` will never strictly-equal it.

## Gotchas

- **`disabled` is styling-only in the shipped theme**, same as `NCheckbox`: `NRadioView.default()` binds `onClick` unconditionally; `themes/default/radio/src/radio/radio.scss` has no `pointer-events` rule, so a "disabled" radio is still clickable in JS unless the app's own CSS enforces it.
- **The `view` prop on `NRadio` is effectively dead code in normal usage.** `NRadioData.view` getter: `this.scope.ncx('group')?.data.view || this.scope.get('view')`. Since `NRadio` always requires a group (throws otherwise), `ncx('group')` is always present, so the group's `view` always wins — an individual radio's own `view` prop can never take effect.
- `value`'s default is the literal string `'undefined'` (`type: [String,Number,Boolean], default: 'undefined'`), not the JS `undefined` value — worth being explicit about this in generated code since it reads like a typo but is the real declared default.
- Checked-state comparison (`this.model === this.value` in `NRadioData.classList`) is strict `===`, so a group `modelValue` of `'1'` (string) will not mark a radio with `:value="1"` (number) as checked.

## Related components

- `NRadioGroup` — required parent; owns the actual `modelValue`/`update:modelValue`. See `radio-group.md`.
- `NCheckbox`/`NCheckboxGroup` — non-exclusive counterpart that, unlike `NRadio`, can stand alone. See `checkbox.md`/`checkbox-group.md`.


---

<!-- ===== components/rating.md ===== -->

# NRating

A read-only star-rating display that renders a row of stars (full/half/empty) plus a pluralized text label for a numeric value.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/visuals/index.ts` as `NRating` (`App.component(NRating.name, NRating)`). Source: `src/visuals/js/rating/{NRating,NRatingController,NRatingData,NRatingView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Size modifier, see concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known built-ins: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Styles the filled stars via `n-type-{type}`. Demo (`demos/overview.html`) uses `primary`/`secondary`/`success`/`warning`/`danger`/`info` — all confirmed built-ins, no `neutral` usage for `NRating`. |
| `modelValue` | `[String, Number]` | `0` | `NRating.ts` (own prop) | The rating value. Coerced to a number via `Mix.num()` (pico-js) in `NRatingData.value`. |
| `closestValue` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NRating.ts` (own prop) | When `true` (default), the displayed numeric label uses `closest` (the value rounded to the nearest `stepSize` increment) instead of the raw `modelValue`. |
| `stepSize` | `Number` | `0.5` | `NRating.ts` (own prop) | Increment used both for rounding the displayed value (`closest = Math.round(value / stepSize) * stepSize`) and for star half-fill thresholds (`closest >= index - 0.5`). |
| `decimals` | `Number` | `1` | `NRating.ts` (own prop) | Decimal places used when formatting the numeric label (`Str.number(value, decimals, 'en')`). |
| `stars` | `Number` | `5` | `NRating.ts` (own prop) | Number of star elements rendered. |
| `starsText` | `String` | `'No stars\|:count Star\|:count Stars'` | `NRating.ts` (own prop) | Pluralized label template passed to pico-js `Locale.choice(starsText, value, { count })`. See Gotchas — the placeholder must be `:count`, not `:value`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | `NRating.ts` declares `emits: []`. Nothing in `NRatingController`/`NRatingView` calls `update()`, `emit()`, or attaches any pointer/click handlers — `NRating` is a purely presentational, read-only display in this source. There is no way for a user to change the rating by interacting with the component. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | None. `NRatingView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NRatingController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-rating :model-value="3.5" />
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` — a grid of ratings across the confirmed built-in `type` values:

```vue
<template>
  <n-rating :model-value="3.3" v-bind="n_rating" type="primary" />
  <n-rating :model-value="3.5" v-bind="n_rating" type="secondary" />
  <n-rating :model-value="3.8" v-bind="n_rating" type="success" />
  <n-rating :model-value="0" v-bind="n_rating" type="warning" />
  <n-rating :model-value="1" v-bind="n_rating" type="danger" />
  <n-rating :model-value="3" v-bind="n_rating" type="info" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
// demo's n_rating also sets a custom `choice` key, which is not an NRating
// prop at all (the real prop is `starsText`) — see Gotchas.
const n_rating = reactive({
  size: 'md',
  choice: 'No stars|:value star|:value stars',
  disabled: false,
});
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — independent, standalone component.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `v-model="rating"` to make the stars clickable/editable: `NRating` has no emits and no interaction handlers at all in this source. It is display-only; despite having a `modelValue` prop (which invites a v-model mental model), there is no `update:modelValue` path.
- Using `:value` as the pluralization placeholder in a custom `starsText`, as `demos/overview.html`'s `n_rating.choice` does (`'No stars|:value star|:value stars'`): the actual replace map built in `NRatingView.value()` only sets a `count` key (`{ count: Str.number(value, ...) }`), and pico-js `Locale.choice()` only auto-fills a `count` placeholder by default. A `:value` placeholder in a custom string will **not** be interpolated — use `:count`. Also note the demo's `choice` key on `n_rating` is not even the right prop name (`starsText` is), so that override has no effect on `NRating` at all as bound in the demo.
- Assuming `stars` determines the max rating value for clamping: `NRatingData` performs no clamping of `modelValue`/`value` against `stars`— a `modelValue` greater than `stars` will simply overflow the rendered star row's "full" state logic (all stars render full, no error).

## Gotchas

- `closest` (used for both the half/full star fill and, by default, the displayed number) is computed as `Math.round(value / stepSize) * stepSize` — with the default `stepSize` of `0.5`, this rounds to the nearest half-star, which is also exactly the granularity the star fill logic (`closest >= index - 0.5`) can visually represent.
- `decimals` only affects the text-label formatting (`Str.number`), not the star fill visualization, which is inherently step-quantized by `stepSize`.
- `starsText` uses pico-js's `Locale.choice()` 2- or 3-part pipe syntax (`'No stars|:count Star|:count Stars'`) — see `NRatingView.value()`; the exact `count` placeholder name is load-bearing (see Common mistakes above).

## Related components

None — NRating has no composition relationship with NTag, NMessage, or NProgress; documented independently per task scope.

<!-- ===== components/resizer.md ===== -->

# NResizer

A flex/box panel with a draggable edge handle that resizes its own width by pointer-dragging, optionally syncing its resulting width to other `NResizer`s sharing a `group`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/resizer/index.ts` (`App.component(NResizer.name, NResizer)`). Source: `src/resizer/js/resizer/{NResizer,NResizerController,NResizerData,NResizerView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds `n-disabled` via `classRoot()`. <!-- UNVERIFIED: `NResizerController.onPointerdown` has no explicit `disabled`/`superDisabled` guard, so this appears styling-only, same pattern as NCheckbox's `disabled` — not independently confirmed by a runtime check in this component. --> |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `modelValue` | `[Number]` | `null` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | The resized width in pixels, as a v-model. Cloned locally (`cloneProp('modelValue')`); updated on drag-release and whenever a `group` signal fires (see Events). |
| `width` | `[Number]` | `null` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | The **live** width in pixels, updated continuously while dragging (unlike `modelValue`, which only settles on drag-release/group-sync). Also cloned locally and re-emitted on every `ResizeObserver` tick (`observeOffset()`). |
| `minWidth` | `[Number]` | `40` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | Clamp floor applied in `detectOffset()`. |
| `maxWidth` | `[Number]` | `null` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | Clamp ceiling applied in `detectOffset()`; no ceiling when `null`. |
| `group` | `[Array]` | `null` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | An array of group-key strings. When one resizer in a shared group finishes a drag, every other `NResizer` whose own `group` array contains a matching key (`Arr.has`) snaps its `width`/`modelValue` to the dragged resizer's resulting width (see Events). Defaults to `[this.uid]` (i.e. its own random UID, not shared with anything) when left `null` — **not shared by default**. |
| `flex` | `[String]` | `''` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | Raw CSS `flex` shorthand applied inline, used as a fallback layout size only while no `modelValue`/drag-derived width is set — see Gotchas for the exact precedence. |
| `direction` | `[String]` | `'right'` | local (`NResizer.ts`) | Which edge the drag handle is on and which way growing the width points. Confirmed values (both explicitly branched in `NResizerController.detectOffset()`/`NResizerData.classList`): `'right'`, `'left'`. Any other string falls through the `if` branches with no offset computed for `detectOffset()`, and no `n-resizer--{direction}` modifier class is added for anything besides these two (open string, but only these two are functional). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `number` (pixels) | Fired via `this.update('width', ...)`/`this.update('modelValue', ...)` in `onGroupSignal()` — i.e. **only** when a *different* resizer in the same `group` finishes dragging and fires the `NResizer` pico-js signal; a resizer's own drag-release does not itself emit `update:modelValue` on itself (only `update:width`, see below). |
| `update:width` | `number` (pixels) | Fired continuously from `observeOffset()` (called on every `ResizeObserver` tick on the root element) via `this.update('width', this.data.width)`, and also from `onGroupSignal()` when a same-group peer finishes dragging. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The panel's own content, rendered alongside the drag handle inside the root `<div>`. |

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()`/`context.expose` call in `NResizerController` or `NResizer.ts`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-resizer v-model="width" :min-width="300" :max-width="800">
    <div style="width: 600px;">Resizable content</div>
  </n-resizer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const width = ref(600);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on `demos/resizer/index.html` (scrollable content inside a fixed-frame resizer) and the grouped pair in `demos/test.html` (two resizers on opposite sides syncing through a shared `group` key):

```vue
<template>
  <div style="border: 2px solid #000; overflow: hidden;">
    <div style="position: relative; width: 600px; height: 400px; overflow: auto;">
      <n-resizer :width="600" :min-width="300" :max-width="800">
        <div style="width: 600px; height: 1200px;">Scrollable panel content</div>
      </n-resizer>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div style="display: flex; flex-direction: row;">
    <n-resizer :group="['pair']" flex="0 0 60%" direction="right" style="height: 200px;">
      Left panel
    </n-resizer>
    <n-resizer :group="['pair']" flex="0 0 40%" direction="left" style="height: 200px;">
      Right panel
    </n-resizer>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Required composition

None — a single `NResizer` works standalone. `group` composition is optional (multiple `NResizer`s sharing the same key string synchronize their widths, but neither requires a parent/wrapper component — they just need the same literal string somewhere in each one's `group` array).

## Common mistakes

- Passing a plain string to `group` (e.g. `group="pair"`) — the prop type is `Array`; it must be an array of key strings (e.g. `:group="['pair']"`), matched via `Arr.has`.
- Relying on `update:modelValue` to track width live while dragging — it only fires on drag-release via a group signal from a *different* resizer, not from the panel's own drag. Use `update:width` (or `v-model:width`) for live updates during a drag of the same instance.
- Passing an HTML `dropzone="true"` attribute (seen in `demos/test.html`) expecting drag-and-drop file behavior — `NResizer` has no drag/drop props or logic; this is a plain fall-through DOM attribute with no special handling in this component.
- Expecting `flex` to keep controlling layout after the panel has been resized once — once `modelValue`/drag-derived width exists, `style.flex` is overwritten to `0 0 {model}px`, overriding the `flex` prop (see Gotchas).

## Gotchas

- **Style precedence in `NResizerView.default()`:** if `data.model` (aka `modelValue`) is a number, `style.width = '{model}px'` is set; if there's no `style.width` *and* `flex` is truthy, `style.flex = data.flex`; then, unconditionally, if `data.model` is truthy, `style.flex` is overwritten again to `'0 0 {model}px'`. Net effect: a set `modelValue` always wins for both `width` and `flex`, and the `flex` prop only has any visible effect before a resize has ever produced a `modelValue`.
- Only `direction: 'right'`/`'left'` are handled by the offset math — no `'top'`/`'bottom'` vertical resizing exists despite `direction` being an open `String` prop.
- Group syncing goes through the same pico-js `Signal` bus documented in concepts.md (`onSignal('NResizer', ...)`/`fireSignal('NResizer', group)`) — it's global, not scoped to a parent component, so two unrelated `NResizer`s anywhere in the app sharing the same `group` key string will sync even without a common ancestor.
- The `ResizeObserver` bound in `onMounted()` fires `observeOffset()` (which recomputes offset from actual `getBoundingClientRect()` layout, not from any pointer event) on *every* layout-affecting size change of the root element — including ones caused by external CSS/layout changes unrelated to a user drag.

## Related components

- `NScrollbar`/`NVirtualbar` — commonly wrap or are wrapped by `NResizer` panels for scrollable resizable regions (see `demos/test.html`).


---

<!-- ===== components/scrollbar.md ===== -->

# NScrollbar

A drop-in scroll container that hides the native scrollbar and renders custom draggable overlay track(s) instead, tracking content size via `ResizeObserver`/`MutationObserver`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/scrollbar/index.ts` (`App.component(NScrollbar.name, NScrollbar)`), alongside `NVirtualbar` from the same group index. Source: `src/scrollbar/js/scrollbar/{NScrollbar,NScrollbarController,NScrollbarData,NScrollbarView}.ts`, plus the shared runtime `src/scrollbar/js/handler/{NScrollbarElement,NScrollbarHelper}.ts` (also used by `NVirtualbar`, see `virtualbar.md`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `overflowX` | `[Boolean]` | `true` | local (`NScrollbar.ts`) | Enables the horizontal overlay track (`n-overflow-x` class) and appends the `.n-scrollbar-h` bar element. |
| `overflowY` | `[Boolean]` | `true` | local (`NScrollbar.ts`) | Enables the vertical overlay track (`n-overflow-y` class) and appends the `.n-scrollbar-v` bar element. |
| `wrapClass` | `[String]` | `':bem__wrap'` | local (`NScrollbar.ts`) | Class applied to the innermost wrapper `<div>` (around the default slot). `:bem` is replaced with the component's BEM root (`n-scrollbar`), so the literal default resolves to `n-scrollbar__wrap`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `ready` | `this` (the `NScrollbarController` instance) | `NScrollbarController.onMounted()` constructs the underlying `NScrollbarElement` with `onReady: () => this.emit('ready', this)`, which `NScrollbarElement`'s constructor calls synchronously after it finishes its initial `makePseudo()`/`detectRect()`/`observeBox()` setup. |
| `scroll` | — | Declared in `emits: ['ready', 'scroll']`, but `NScrollbarController` never calls `this.emit('scroll', ...)` anywhere. <!-- UNVERIFIED / apparent dead declaration --> The actual scroll signal is a plain DOM `CustomEvent` named `virtualscroll` fired on `window` by `NScrollbarElement.fireScroll()` (throttled via `Run.framerate(..., 24)` on the content's native `scroll`/`wheel` events) — listen for that on `window`, not a Vue `@scroll` handler on `<n-scrollbar>`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The scrollable content, rendered inside `.n-scrollbar-content > [wrapClass]`. |

## Exposed methods

None via `pass()`/`context.expose` — `NScrollbar.ts`'s `setup()` calls no `ncx.pass(...)`. However, `NScrollbarController` does define two public instance methods, reachable from a parent through the `ncx(refKey)` mechanism (`ProtoController.ncx()`, see concepts.md) on a template ref, exactly as real call sites in this codebase do (e.g. `NSelectController`/`NDurationpickerController` calling `this.ncx('scrollbar')?.scrollTo(...)`):

- `scrollTo(selector, options = {})` — scrolls the viewport just enough to bring the element matching `selector` (resolved via `this.dom('el').find(selector)`) into view, with an optional `padding` (default `0`) kept clear below it. No-ops (with a `console.warn`) if the element or the viewport isn't found/ready.
- `scrollCenter(selector, options = {})` — same lookup, but centers the target element in the viewport instead of just bringing it into view.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-scrollbar style="max-height: 300px;">
    <p>Long content that needs to scroll…</p>
  </n-scrollbar>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Modeled on `demos/flex-basis.html` and `demos/test.html` — constraining both axes, and combining with `NResizer` for a resizable scrollable region:

```vue
<template>
  <n-scrollbar style="max-height: 200px; max-width: 200px;">
    <div style="width: 500px;">
      Wide content that scrolls both horizontally and vertically.
    </div>
  </n-scrollbar>

  <n-scrollbar>
    <div style="width: 1800px;">
      <n-resizer direction="right" flex="0 0 60%" style="height: 200px;">
        Resizable content
      </n-resizer>
    </div>
  </n-scrollbar>
</template>
```

## Required composition

None — `NScrollbar` is a standalone wrapper; it just needs default-slot content wider/taller than its own box to show a track.

## Common mistakes

- Binding `@scroll="..."` on `<n-scrollbar>` expecting it to fire — the declared `scroll` emit is never actually dispatched; listen for the `virtualscroll` `CustomEvent` on `window` instead (or measure scroll position yourself via a template ref into the slotted content).
- Calling `.scrollTo()`/`.scrollCenter()` on a plain template ref (`$refs.bar.scrollTo(...)`) — these are Controller methods, not exposed via `pass()`, so they're only reachable through the `ncx()` resolution path (`this.ncx('bar')?.scrollTo(...)` from inside another component's own Controller), not as a directly callable method on the component's public instance from arbitrary consumer code.
- Expecting `wrapClass` to replace the whole class list — it's a single class string with a `:bem` token substitution, not a `class` object/array merge.

## Gotchas

- The custom scrollbar tracks are **not** rendered by Vue — `NScrollbarElement` builds and manages `.n-scrollbar-spacer`/`.n-scrollbar-h`/`.n-scrollbar-v` as raw DOM nodes (`Dom.make`) appended directly to the root element, entirely outside the Vue render tree. Inspecting the rendered VDOM won't show them.
- `NScrollbarHelper.detectNative()` runs once at module load and flags `native = true` when the OS/browser already reserves layout space for scrollbars (offsetHeight/Width differ from clientHeight/Width in the *absence* of a scrollbar) — in that case `n-scrollbar--native` is added and the custom track styling defers to the platform's own bars via CSS, without changing the Vue-facing API.
- `overflowX`/`overflowY` only gate whether the corresponding *drag handle bar* is appended to the DOM (`if (overflowX) this.hbar.appendTo(portal)`) — they do not set `overflow-x`/`overflow-y` CSS directly; actual scroll capability still depends on the component's own CSS and content sizing.
- Destruction order matters if you unmount quickly after mount: `onBeforeUnmount` calls `this.scrollbar.destroy()` unconditionally, which will throw if `onMounted` never ran (e.g. component destroyed before its first paint) since `this.scrollbar` would still be `undefined`.

## Related components

- `NVirtualbar` (`virtualbar.md`) — shares the same underlying `NScrollbarElement`/`NScrollbarHelper` runtime, adding item virtualization on top.
- `NResizer` (`resizer.md`) — commonly nested inside an `NScrollbar` for resizable scrollable panels (see `demos/test.html`).
- `NSelect`, `NDurationpicker`, `NDraglist` — internally hold an `NScrollbar`/`NVirtualbar` child and drive it via `this.ncx('scrollbar')?.scrollTo(...)` / `this.ncx('virtualbar')?.scrollTo(...)`.

<!-- ===== components/select.md ===== -->

# NSelect

A searchable dropdown picker (single or multiple selection) backed by a
virtualized option list, with optional free-text option creation.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally via `App.use(Install)` from the **select** group index
(`src/select/index.ts`), which calls `App.component('NSelect', NSelect)`
(tag `n-select`). Self-contained — no companion component to register
alongside it (unlike `NCascader`/`NCascaderPanel`).

`NSelect` extends the shared popover-panel stack: its Controller extends
`NPopoverPanelController`, its View extends `NPopoverPanelView`
(`src/popover/js/popover-panel/*`), so it renders as a display trigger plus
an `n-popover` internally.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` | Adds `n-load` to the root. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string; known styled values `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string; known styled values `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` | Drives `superDisabled`; applied directly to the underlying `<input>`'s `disabled` attribute in `NSelectView.input()`. |
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` | Shows the built-in clear (×) button (`this.clear()` in the `display()` render), wired to `applyClear()`. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` | Value `modelValue` is reset to by the clear button, and the value `applyModel()` falls back to when the selection becomes empty. |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No items')` | `Props.EmptyText` | Text shown by `this.empty()` when the (searched) option list is empty. |
| `undefinedText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Undefined')` | `Props.UndefinedText` | Passed to `OptionHelper.getCombineList` as the label for model values that don't exist in `options` and `allowCreate` is `false`. |
| `position` | `String` | `'bottom-center'` | `Props.PositionBottomCenter` | Popover position; full 12-value set: `top-start`, `top-center`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-end`, `left-start`, `left-center`, `left-end`, `right-start`, `right-center`, `right-end`. |
| `options` | `Object` (Array also accepted) | `{}` | `Props.OptionsObject` | See "Options resolution" in concepts.md. Walked by `OptionHelper.getList`/`getFlat` into `{ label, value }` pairs. |
| `optionsValue` | `String` | `'$index'` | `Props.OptionsObject` | Dot-path (via `Obj.get`) into the `{ $index, $value }` pair to resolve each option's `value`. |
| `optionsLabel` | `String` | `'$value'` | `Props.OptionsObject` | Dot-path into the `{ $index, $value }` pair to resolve each option's `label`. |
| `modelValue` | `any` | `null` | Component-local (`NSelect.ts`) | Untyped (matches concepts.md's confirmed entry). A single option **value** when `multiple` is `false`; an array of values when `multiple` is `true`. |
| `multiple` | `Boolean` | `false` | Component-local | Switches selection mode; changes `modelValue` shape from scalar to array and switches the display from a single input to a tags row. |
| `allowCreate` | `Boolean` | `false` | Component-local | Lets Enter commit the raw search text (`data.search`) as a new option value when nothing in the list matches (`onEnter()`); also lets values in `modelValue` that aren't in `options` render with their own string as the label instead of `undefinedText` (`OptionHelper.getCombineList`). |
| `collapse` | `Boolean` | `true` | Component-local | Multi-select only: when `true`, only the first selected tag is shown plus a `+:count` summary; when `false`, all tags render. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Please select'` | Component-local | Literal default string, passed through `Locale.trans()` at render (`NSelectView.input()`). |
| `collapseText` | `String` | `'+:count item\|+:count items'` | Component-local | `Locale.choice()` plural-form template used for the multi-select collapse summary; `:count` is substituted with `model.length - 1`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | New model value — a scalar (single mode) or filtered/deduped array (multiple mode), or `clearValue` if the selection became empty | Any option click (`item()`'s `onClick` → `applyModel(value)`), pressing Enter in the input (`onEnter()` → `applyModel(model)`), removing a tag's × icon (`tag()`'s `onClick` → `applyModel(value)`), or the built-in clear button (`applyClear()`, inherited from `ProtoController`) |

## Slots

None — `NSelectView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. It overrides both
`display()` and `panel()` from `NPopoverPanelView`, so even the inherited
`panel()` slot (`this.slot('panel')`) is unreachable; the dropdown body is
always the internal virtualized option list (`n-virtualbar` +
`n-popover-option`), not consumer-supplied content.

## Exposed methods

None — `NSelectController` never calls `pass()`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-select v-model="value" :options="{ mike: 'Mike', alex: 'Alex', hans: 'Hans' }"></n-select>
```

## Realistic example

Grounded in `demos/overview.html`'s current (non-stale) usage, which passes
plain key→label objects straight through the `Props.OptionsObject` defaults
(`optionsValue: '$index'`, `optionsLabel: '$value'` — no override needed):

```vue
<n-select
    v-model="size"
    :options="{ xs: 'XS', sm: 'SM', md: 'MD', lg: 'LG', xl: 'XL' }"
    size="md"
></n-select>

<n-select
    v-model="selectedIcons"
    :multiple="true"
    :collapse="false"
    :clearable="true"
    type="primary"
    :options="icons"
></n-select>
```

```js
// icons: array form also works (OptionHelper.getList accepts Array or Object)
icons = [
    { value: 'fa fa-ghost', label: 'Ghost' },
    { value: 'fa fa-directions', label: 'Directions' },
];
```

```vue
<!-- array form needs explicit optionsValue/optionsLabel since the defaults
     ($index/$value) would otherwise resolve to the array index and the
     whole item object -->
<n-select
    v-model="iconValue"
    :options="icons"
    options-value="$value.value"
    options-label="$value.label"
></n-select>
```

## Required composition

None — `NSelect` is self-contained, like `NTransfer`. It internally renders
an `n-popover` with an `n-virtualbar`/`n-popover-option` list as its dropdown
body, but none of that is authored by the consumer.

## Common mistakes

- Passing an **Array** of plain value/label objects without setting
  `optionsValue`/`optionsLabel`. With the defaults (`$index`/`$value`), an
  array's resolved `value` is the **array index**, not `item.value` — see the
  realistic example above.
- Assuming `modelValue` is always an array. It's a scalar unless `multiple`
  is `true` (`NSelectData.model` calls `Arr.first(model)` in single mode).
- Expecting the built-in clear button to appear without also setting
  `clearable="true"` — `Props.Clearable` defaults to `false`.
- Relying on a `panel`/`default` slot to customize the option list — there
  isn't one (see Slots).

## Gotchas

- `options` is declared `type: Object` but `OptionHelper.getList()` (via
  `Arr.each`) accepts an Array just as well — concepts.md's "options may be
  an Array or Object" note applies directly here.
- Values present in `modelValue` but absent from `options` still render (via
  `OptionHelper.getCombineList`): as their own string label if `allowCreate`
  is `true`, otherwise as `undefinedText`. This means an "orphaned" selected
  value doesn't silently disappear from the display.
- `collapseText` uses pico-js's `Locale.choice()` pluralization syntax
  (`'singular|plural'` with a `:count` placeholder), not a plain
  `Locale.trans()` lookup like `emptyText`/`undefinedText`.
- The dropdown popover width is fixed via `popoverConfig.width = -1` in
  `NSelectView` (overriding `NPopoverPanelView`'s default `width: 1`) —
  <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact semantics of the `width` popover config value (e.g.
  whether `-1` means "match trigger width" vs `1` meaning something else) —
  not traced into the `n-popover` component itself for this doc. -->

## Related components

- `NCascader` — the tree-shaped counterpart; also built on the same
  `NPopoverPanelController`/`NPopoverPanelView` base, but uses a
  `labelProp`/`valueProp`/`childProp` tree contract instead of
  `Props.OptionsObject`.
- `NTransfer` — a different flat-list picker (dual-list, not
  dropdown-based), also does not use `Props.OptionsObject`.

<!-- ===== components/signal.md ===== -->

# Signal globals: Alert, Confirm, Notify

`Alert`, `Confirm`, and `Notify` are global JS objects (not Vue components) for
firing one-off alert/confirm/notification popups from anywhere in JS — call
`Alert.make(...)`, `Confirm.make(...)`, `Notify.make(...)` directly, no
template tag, no `import`. Each `make()` builds a plain DOM element with
`@kizmann/pico-js`'s `Dom.make`, not a Vue-rendered component tree. See
`ai-docs/concepts.md` for the `ProtoController`/`onSignal`/`fireSignal` pub/sub
bus these globals sit alongside conceptually (cross-component signalling
outside props/emits) — the handlers here don't build on `ProtoController`
themselves (they predate/bypass the Controller/Data/View pattern entirely),
but `Alert`/`Confirm`/`Notify` are exactly the kind of thing that bus exists to
support decoupled triggering of. See `ai-docs/icons.md` for `Styler.icons`'
`alert`/`confirm`/`notify` groups, which supply each one's default status icon.

## Import / Registration

Source: `src/signal/index.ts`. This module's default export (the function
normally passed to `App.use()`/registered per-group) is an **empty function
body** — `export default function (App) { }` — it does nothing. Instead, at
module load time the file runs:

```ts
if ( ! globalThis.Alert )   globalThis.Alert   = NAlertHandler;
if ( ! globalThis.Confirm ) globalThis.Confirm = NConfirmHandler;
if ( ! globalThis.Notify )  globalThis.Notify  = NNotifyHandler;
```

So as long as this module is loaded once (e.g. via the library's main entry),
`Alert`, `Confirm`, `Notify` exist as globals (`window.Alert` in a browser).
There is **no `App.component('n-alert', ...)`-style registration** and no
`<n-alert>`/`<n-confirm>`/`<n-notify>` template tag in the current source —
each is a plain class with a single relevant `static make()` method:

- `Alert` → `NAlertHandler` (`src/signal/js/alert/NAlertHandler.ts`)
- `Confirm` → `NConfirmHandler` (`src/signal/js/confirm/NConfirmHandler.ts`)
- `Notify` → `NNotifyHandler` (`src/signal/js/notify/NNotifyHandler.ts`)

The guard (`if (!globalThis.X)`) means a host app can pre-define its own
`window.Alert`/etc. before nano-ui loads to opt out of this global entirely.

## API

### Alert

| Method | Signature | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Alert.make` | `make(options: any = {}, type: string = null)` | `undefined` (see Gotchas) | Shows a blocking modal alert with an icon, message, and a single "Okay" button. |

`options` is either a **string** (shorthand for `{ text: options }`) or an
**object** merged over these defaults (`NAlertElement.options`):

```ts
{ uid: null, icon: null, text: null, theme: 'dark', size: null, type: null,
  closable: true, okayText: Locale.trans('Okay') }
```

If the second positional arg `type` is non-null, it overwrites `options.type`
(so `Alert.make('text', 'danger')` and `Alert.make({ text: 'text', type: 'danger' })`
are equivalent). `icon` (if set) overrides the type-derived default icon
entirely — confirmed in `NAlertElement.render()`:
`this.options.icon || Styler.icon(this.options.type, 'alert')`.

### Confirm

| Method | Signature | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Confirm.make` | `make(options: any = {}, type: string = null)` | `Promise<number>` | Shows a blocking modal with Cancel/Confirm buttons; resolves/rejects based on the user's choice. |

`options` string-shorthand and `type` override behave identically to `Alert.make`
(same `Mix.isString(options)` / `if (type != null) options.type = type` logic
in `NConfirmHandler.make`). Defaults merged in (`NConfirmElement.options`):

```ts
{ uid: null, text: null, theme: 'dark', size: null, type: null,
  cancelText: Locale.trans('Cancel'), confirmText: Locale.trans('Confirm') }
```

**How the yes/no result is delivered — confirmed from `NConfirmElement.promise()`:**
`Confirm.make(...)` returns a `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... })`.

- Clicking the **Confirm** button (or the modal being closed with `signal(true)`)
  calls `resolve(1)` — after the modal visually closes (via `Run.frame`).
- Clicking the **Cancel** button, closing the modal via its own close affordance
  (`modalProps.onClose = () => this.signal(false)`), or otherwise triggering
  `signal(false)` calls `reject(0)`.

So it is a **Promise**, not a callback: `await Confirm.make(...)` throws (with
value `0`) on cancel, and resolves to `1` on confirm. A caller that only wants
the "confirmed" path can do `Confirm.make(...).then(onYes)`, but must add a
`.catch()` (or wrap in try/catch) to avoid an unhandled-rejection warning on
cancel — confirmed in `demos/flex-basis.html`'s usage (`.then(...).catch(...)`).

There is no separate "onCancel"/"onConfirm" option in `NConfirmElement.options`
— only the Promise resolve/reject wires up both paths.

### Notify

| Method | Signature | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Notify.make` | `make(options: any = {}, type: string = null)` | `undefined` (see Gotchas) | Shows a non-blocking, auto-dismissing toast in a positioned stack. |

`options` string-shorthand and `type` override behave the same as the other
two. Defaults merged in (`NNotifyElement.options`):

```ts
{ text: null, theme: null, size: null, type: null, position: null, duration: 4500 }
```

`position` accepts the same 6-value notify-frame set used elsewhere in
`demos/overview.html`'s example (`top-start`, `top-center`, `top-end`,
`bottom-start`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-end`); `NNotifyHandler.frame()`
defaults `position` to `'bottom-start'` when `null`. `duration` is milliseconds
before auto-close (`Run.delay(() => this.close(), duration)`); the toast also
closes early if the user `pointerdown`s on it.

`NNotifyHandler` additionally exposes `create(position)`, `frame(position)`,
and `clear()` as internal helpers for managing the per-position stacking
container (`[data-notify="<position>"]` frame element in `document.body`) —
these aren't meant to be called directly to trigger a notification; use
`Notify.make(...)`.

## Type values

All three read `this.options.type` and resolve an icon via
`Styler.icon(type, '<alert|confirm|notify>')`, whose groups (per
`ai-docs/icons.md`) are keyed `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`
(same set for all three groups). `Styler.icon()` falls back to the group's
`default` icon for `null`/unrecognized `type` values. So:

- **Icon-mapped values** (each gets its own status icon): `info`, `success`,
  `warning`, `danger`.
- Any other string (including `primary`/`secondary`, or omitting `type`
  entirely) renders the `default` icon instead — it does **not** error, it
  just falls back visually.

Separately, `type` also feeds `Styler.bem(...)` for the root element's CSS
class (`n-type-{type}`) — so a "known default" type like `primary` still
produces a styled class (`n-type-primary`) even though its *icon* falls back
to `default`. Treat `type` here the same as elsewhere in nano-ui: an open
string (see `ai-docs/concepts.md`'s "Type and Size are open strings" section),
with `info`/`success`/`warning`/`danger` being the values that additionally
change the icon for these three globals specifically.

## Minimal example

```js
// Alert
Alert.make('Something happened.');

// Confirm
Confirm.make('Are you sure?', 'danger')
    .then(() => console.log('confirmed'))
    .catch(() => console.log('cancelled'));

// Notify
Notify.make('Saved.', 'success');
```

## Realistic example

From `demos/overview.html` and `demos/flex-basis.html`:

```js
// Alert.make(text, type)
methods.alert = function (type) {
    return window.Alert.make(
        'Lorem ipsum dolore Lorem ipsum dolore Lorem ipsum dolore', type
    );
};

// Notify.make(options-object)
methods.notify = function (type) {
    return window.Notify.make({
        text: 'Lorem ipsum dolore Lorem ipsum dolore Lorem ipsum dolore',
        type: type,
        position: randomNotifyPosition(),
    });
};

// Confirm.make(text, type) used as an async gate before an action,
// e.g. NDrawer's beforeClose hook:
data.n_drawer.beforeClose = () => {
    return window.Confirm.make('blabla', 'danger');
};

// Confirm.make(options-object) with .then()/.catch()
methods['showConfirm'] = function () {
    window.Confirm.make({
        text: 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consetetur sadipscing elitr...',
        type: 'danger',
    })
        .then(() => console.log('accept'))
        .catch(() => console.log('cancel'));
};
```

<!-- UNVERIFIED: demos/flex-basis.html's showConfirm example actually calls
`window.Confirm.make({ text, type: 'danger' }, () => { return this.disableConfirm; })`
— passing a function as the second positional argument. Per the confirmed
source (`NConfirmHandler.make(options, type)`), that second argument is only
ever used as `if (type != null) options.type = type`, i.e. it's treated as a
type string, not a callback/guard function. This looks like stale or
experimental demo code that doesn't match the current handler signature —
don't copy the two-argument-with-function-second-arg form; use a plain
`(text, type)` or `(options)` call as shown above. -->

## Common mistakes

- **There is no `<n-alert>`, `<n-confirm>`, or `<n-notify>` template
  component.** `demos/confirm/index.html` contains an `<n-confirm>` tag, but
  that demo is stale relative to current source: `src/signal/index.ts`'s
  install function body is empty, so nothing is ever registered via
  `App.component()`. Use `Confirm.make(...)` (etc.) from JS instead.
- Don't `import { Alert } from '@kizmann/nano-ui'` — these are not module
  exports, they're attached to `globalThis` as a side effect of loading
  `src/signal/index.ts`. Just reference `Alert`/`Confirm`/`Notify` directly
  (or `window.Alert` etc.) once the library has been loaded once.
- Don't treat `Confirm.make(...)`'s rejection as an error condition to log —
  cancelling is an expected path (`reject(0)`); always pair `.then()` with
  `.catch()` (or try/catch around `await`).
- Don't expect `Alert.make(...)`/`Notify.make(...)` to return a handle you can
  close later — see Gotchas.

## Gotchas

- **`Alert.make()` and `Notify.make()` return `undefined`.** `NAlertElement.open()`
  and `NNotifyElement.open()` have no `return` statement, so
  `NAlertHandler.make`/`NNotifyHandler.make` (which `return modal.open()` /
  `return notification.open()`) both hand back `undefined`. Only
  `Confirm.make()` returns something meaningful (the Promise). Don't chain
  `.then()` on `Alert.make()`/`Notify.make()`.
- **No programmatic dismiss API.** None of the three handlers expose a public
  method to close a specific alert/confirm/notification from outside once
  shown — dismissal only happens via: the Alert's Okay button, the Confirm's
  Cancel/Confirm buttons or its modal's own close affordance, or (Notify only)
  the user clicking the toast itself or the `duration` timeout elapsing. There
  is no `Alert.close(uid)` or similar.
- **They mount directly to `document.body`, not through Vue.** `NAlertElement`/
  `NConfirmElement` build a raw DOM tree via pico-js's `Dom.make(...)` and
  `root.appendTo(document.body)` — no Vue component instance, no Teleport.
  Alert/Confirm additionally register with `NModalHandler.append(el, props)`
  (the same modal-stacking system `NModal` uses) so they participate in
  modal backdrop/stacking behavior and get removed via
  `NModalHandler.remove(this.modal)` on close. Notify instead appends into a
  lazily-created, position-keyed frame element (`[data-notify="<position>"]`,
  also directly under `document.body`), which `NNotifyHandler.clear()` removes
  once it has no children left.
- `Alert`'s `closable` option (default `true`) is passed through to the modal
  as `modalProps.closable`; `Confirm` doesn't expose a `closable` option at
  all — its modal is always dismissible via the close affordance, which is
  wired to `signal(false)` (i.e. counts as a cancel, not a no-op).
- `theme` defaults to `'dark'` for both `Alert` and `Confirm` (not `null`/
  inherited), but `Notify`'s `theme` defaults to `null`.

## Related components

- `NModal` (`ai-docs/components/modal.md` if present) — `Alert`/`Confirm` are
  built on the same `NModalHandler.append`/`remove`/`openRun`/`closeRun`
  modal-stacking mechanism.
- `ai-docs/icons.md` — `Styler.icons.alert`/`.confirm`/`.notify` groups and
  `Styler.icon()` resolution used for these three globals' default icons.
- `ai-docs/concepts.md` — `ProtoController`'s `onSignal`/`fireSignal` pub/sub
  bus, the general mechanism these globals are conceptually adjacent to for
  decoupled, non-prop-driven triggering.


---

<!-- ===== components/slider.md ===== -->

# NSlider

A draggable-handle slider bound via `v-model`, supporting both a single-value mode and a two-handle range mode.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/slider/index.ts` as `NSlider` (`App.component(NSlider.name, NSlider)`). Source: `src/slider/js/slider/{NSlider,NSliderController,NSliderData,NSliderView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Size modifier, see concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Color/type modifier, see concepts.md. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Disables interaction (subject to `superDisabled`, see concepts.md). |
| `modelValue` | `[String, Number, Array]` | `null` | `NSlider.ts` (own prop) | Single-mode: a plain number (a numeric `String` is accepted by prop validation but the internal math (`Num.subtract`, array checks) is written for numbers — see Gotchas). Range-mode (`range: true`): a 2-element `[min, max]` array. Confirmed exact shape and dual behavior in `NSliderController.onPointerup`/`updateValues`. |
| `range` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NSlider.ts` (own prop) | Switches between single-handle mode (one draggable handle, `modelValue` is a number) and two-handle mode (`modelValue` is `[min, max]`). |
| `labels` | `Array` | `() => []` | `NSlider.ts` (own prop) | Tooltip labels indexed positionally against the `steps` array (only meaningful when `steps` is also an array — see Realistic example). Rendered as each handle's `data-tooltip` attribute. |
| `steps` | `[Number, Array]` | `1` | `NSlider.ts` (own prop) | As a `Number`: a fixed increment used to round the drag position. As an `Array` (e.g. `[100, 200, 300]`): an explicit list of allowed stop values — dragging snaps to the closest one, and `min`/`max` are then **ignored** in favor of the array's first/last entries (see `minfix`/`maxfix` below and Gotchas). |
| `min` | `Number` | `0` | `NSlider.ts` (own prop) | Minimum value. Only used when `steps` is a plain `Number` (overridden by `Arr.first(steps)` when `steps` is an `Array`). |
| `max` | `Number` | `100` | `NSlider.ts` (own prop) | Maximum value. Only used when `steps` is a plain `Number` (overridden by `Arr.last(steps)` when `steps` is an `Array`). |

`NSliderData` exposes the effective bounds as `minfix`/`maxfix` getters (`Mix.isArr(steps) ? Arr.first(steps)/Arr.last(steps) : min/max`) — read these, not raw `min`/`max`, to know the actual clamping range when documenting or debugging a `steps`-array slider.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `range: false` → the dragged handle's resolved number (`Arr.last(data.values)`). `range: true` → the full `[min, max]` array (`data.values`). | `NSliderController.onPointerup`, i.e. when the user releases a drag on either handle. Not fired continuously during drag — intermediate positions are tracked only in local `values` state, which powers the visual bar/handle rendering during the drag. |

## Slots

None — `NSliderView.default()` renders only `this.bar()` and `this.handles()`; it never calls `this.slot(...)`. Note: several demos pass slot content into `<n-slider>...</n-slider>` (e.g. `demos/overview.html`'s `<n-slider ...>Slider</n-slider>`) but this content is not rendered by the current source — see Gotchas.

## Exposed methods

None. `NSliderController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-slider v-model="value" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const value = ref(30);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` — a plain slider, a range slider, and a stepped slider with custom labels:

```vue
<template>
  <!-- single value, default 0-100 range -->
  <n-slider v-model="value" size="md" />

  <!-- two-handle range mode -->
  <n-slider v-model="rangeValue" :range="true" />

  <!-- fixed stop points with tooltip labels (min/max come from the steps array: 100 and 300) -->
  <n-slider
    v-model="stepValue"
    :steps="[100, 200, 300]"
    :labels="['Small', 'Medium', 'Big']"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const value = ref(30);
const rangeValue = ref([20, 60]);
const stepValue = ref(200);
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — standalone.

## Common mistakes

- Binding `modelValue` to a single number while `range="true"` (or vice versa): the two modes require different shapes (`Number` vs `[min, max]` `Array`); mismatching them means `updateValues()`'s `Mix.isArr(data.model)` check silently falls into the wrong branch.
- Setting `min`/`max` together with an array `steps` and expecting them to take effect: they're overridden by the array's first/last entries (`minfix`/`maxfix`).
- Expecting `labels` to map by value: they map by **index into `steps`** (`Arr.findIndex(data.steps, value)` then `Obj.get(data.labels, key, value)`), so `labels` only makes sense paired with an array `steps` of the same length.
- Putting slot content inside `<n-slider>...</n-slider>`: it is silently dropped (no slot rendering in `NSliderView`).

## Gotchas

- **External `modelValue` changes after mount don't move the handles.** `NSliderController.setup()` calls `updateValues()` exactly once (synchronously, at setup time) to derive the internal `values` array that drives handle/bar rendering. `cloneProp('modelValue')` does watch the prop and updates the underlying local value on external change, but nothing re-invokes `updateValues()` afterward — so programmatically reassigning the parent's bound value post-mount updates `data.model` but not the rendered handle position. Only user drags (`onPointermove`) update `values` afterward.
- <!-- UNVERIFIED: numeric `steps` (non-array) rounding appears to operate on the raw 0–100 pointer-percentage (`width` in `onPointermove`/`getClosestStep`) without rescaling into a custom `min`/`max` domain, unlike the array-`steps` branch which does rescale via `(Arr.last(steps) - Arr.first(steps)) / 100 * width`. This suggests a numeric `steps` slider with non-default `min`/`max` (e.g. `min="50" max="150" steps="5"`) may snap incorrectly — inferred from reading `NSliderController.getClosestStep`, not confirmed by running it. Default `min="0" max="100"` sidesteps this entirely since the percentage and value domains coincide numerically. -->
- `update:modelValue` only fires on pointer release, not during drag — don't rely on it for live/continuous feedback; the live-drag value lives in the component's internal (non-exposed) `values` state.
- The component measures its own pixel width via a `ResizeObserver` (`onMounted`/`onResize`) — if it's rendered while hidden (`display: none`, an inactive tab, etc.) its initial width can be `0`/stale until a resize occurs.

## Related components

None — NSlider has no composition relationship with other components (see task scope: documented independently from NSwitch).
