<!-- ===== components/switch.md ===== -->

# NSwitch

A toggle switch bound via `v-model`, switching its `modelValue` between an `onValue` and an `offValue`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/switch/index.ts` as `NSwitch` (`App.component(NSwitch.name, NSwitch)`). Source: `src/switch/js/switch/{NSwitch,NSwitchController,NSwitchData,NSwitchView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Size modifier, see concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Disables toggling (subject to `superDisabled`, see concepts.md). |
| `modelValue` | `[Number, Boolean, String, Object]` | `false` | `NSwitch.ts` (own prop) | The v-model value. Confirmed in source exactly as concepts.md states. Compared to `onValue`/`offValue` with strict `===`. |
| `onType` | `String` | `null` | `NSwitch.ts` (own prop) | Open string (same built-in set as `type`: `primary/secondary/info/warning/danger/success`). When set and the switch is "on", adds an `n-type-{onType}` class instead of the default on-color. |
| `offType` | `String` | `'default'` | `NSwitch.ts` (own prop) | Same open-string set. Adds `n-type-{offType}` class when the switch is "off". Note the default is the literal string `'default'`, not `null`. |
| `onValue` | `[Number, Boolean, String, Object]` | `true` | `NSwitch.ts` (own prop) | The value `modelValue` is set to when toggled on. |
| `offValue` | `[Number, Boolean, String, Object]` | `false` | `NSwitch.ts` (own prop) | The value `modelValue` is set to when toggled off. |
| `inline` | `Boolean` | `true` | `NSwitch.ts` (own prop) | <!-- UNVERIFIED: declared as a prop but not read anywhere in NSwitchController/NSwitchData/NSwitchView, and no `n-inline`-style class or CSS rule references it in src/switch/css/switch.scss. Appears to currently have no effect; do not assume it toggles inline/block layout. --> |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | the new `onValue` or `offValue` | The root element is clicked, calling `NSwitchController.toggle()`, which flips `modelValue` between `onValue`/`offValue` via `this.update('modelValue', value)`. |

`toggle()` logic (`NSwitchController.ts`): if current model strictly equals `onValue`, next value is `offValue`; if it strictly equals `offValue`, next value is `onValue`; if it matches neither, it snaps to `onValue`. On `setup()`, `resetValue()` runs once and forces `modelValue` to `offValue` if the initial value matches neither `onValue` nor `offValue`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none (no scope object passed) | Rendered inside the `.n-switch__label` element next to the toggle control — the switch's label text (e.g. `<n-switch v-model="x">Enabled</n-switch>`). |

## Exposed methods

None. `NSwitchController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-switch v-model="enabled" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const enabled = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/switch/index.html` and `demos/overview.html`, inside an `NForm`/`NFormItem`, with `size` and `on-type` variants:

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item label="Test">
      <n-switch v-model="form.test" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Test">
      <n-switch v-model="form.test" size="sm" on-type="success" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Test">
      <n-switch v-model="form.test" size="lg" on-type="warning" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Test">
      <n-switch v-model="form.test" on-type="danger" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item label="Test">
      <n-switch v-model="form.test" on-type="info" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ test: false });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — standalone. Works inside `NForm`/`NFormItem` (as shown above) purely for form layout/`superDisabled` purposes, not as a requirement.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `modelValue` must be boolean: it accepts `Number`/`Boolean`/`String`/`Object` and is matched against `onValue`/`offValue` with strict equality, so custom on/off values (e.g. `onValue="'active'"`, `offValue="'inactive'"`) work and are a supported pattern, not a hack.
- Passing an `onValue`/`offValue` pair by reference-typed object and expecting reactivity-friendly equality: comparisons are `===`, so two structurally-equal-but-different object references never match — `modelValue` would be reset to `offValue` by `resetValue()` on mount.
- Expecting `offType` to default to `null` like `onType`: it defaults to the literal string `'default'`.

## Gotchas

- `inline` prop exists but is not wired to any class or style in the current source — see the UNVERIFIED note in the props table.
- If the initial `modelValue` doesn't strictly match either `onValue` or `offValue`, `resetValue()` silently overwrites it to `offValue` on setup (no event emitted for this internal correction — only user toggles emit `update:modelValue`).
- The whole root `<div class="n-switch">` is the click target (`onClick` is bound at the root), not just the visual toggle knob — clicking the label text also toggles.

## Related components

None — NSwitch has no composition relationship with other components (see task scope: documented independently from NSlider).

<!-- ===== components/table-column.md ===== -->

# NTableColumn

Declares one column of an `NTable` — its cell renderer, filter UI, sort/filter behavior, width, and (for `select`/`matrix` types) a selection plugin. Renders no DOM of its own (`NTableColumnView.default()` returns `null`); it's read by the parent `NTable` via `NTable`'s `childs` list (see concepts.md's `GroupController`).

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/table/index.ts` as `NTableColumn` (tag `<n-table-column>`). Source: `src/table/js/table-column/NTableColumn.ts` / `NTableColumnController.ts` / `NTableColumnData.ts` / `NTableColumnView.ts`.

## Props

Spreads `Props.TrueText`, `Props.FalseText`, `Props.EmptyText`, `Props.UndefinedText` (all `TextProps.ts`, `Locale.trans(...)`-backed defaults — see concepts.md) and `Props.OptionsObject` (`options`/`optionsValue`/`optionsLabel` trio — see concepts.md's "Options resolution"), plus its own props declared in `NTableColumn.ts`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trueText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Yes')` | `Props.TrueText` | Used by the `boolean` cell renderer. |
| `falseText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No')` | `Props.FalseText` | Used by the `boolean` cell renderer. |
| `emptyText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('No items')` | `Props.EmptyText` | <!-- UNVERIFIED: not read anywhere in src/table's cell/filter renderers found so far — declared but apparently unused at the column level. --> |
| `undefinedText` | `String` | `Locale.trans('Undefined')` | `Props.UndefinedText` | Shown by the `option` cell renderer when `getOption(input)` finds no matching option. |
| `options` / `optionsValue` / `optionsLabel` | see concepts.md | `{}` / `'$index'` / `'$value'` | `Props.OptionsObject` | Powers both the `option` **cell** renderer (`NTableCellOption`, via `column.getOption(value)`) and the `option` **filter** renderer (`NTableFilterOption`, via `column.getOptions()`) — one config drives both. `options` may also be a `Function` (called as `options(this)`, resolved in `createOptionsMap()`) in addition to Array/Object. |
| `uid` | any | `null` | own | Optional explicit unique id for the column instance; falls back to an auto-generated uid (`makeUID()`) if not set. |
| `modelValue` | any | `null` | own | Only meaningful for `type: 'select'` / `type: 'matrix'` (drives the plugin — see "Plugins" below). Emits `update:modelValue` when the plugin toggles a row. Not used by the plain cell types (`string`/`boolean`/`datetime`/`image`/`option`). |
| `data` | `Object` | `null` | own | Generic per-column config bag, consumed differently per type: for `image` columns, `{ thumbProp: 'someField' }` picks a distinct thumbnail field off the row; for `select`/`matrix` plugin columns, `{ allowUncheck, matrix, prop }` (see "Plugins"). |
| `plugin` | `Object` | `null` | own | <!-- CONFIRMED DEAD PROP: declared in NTableColumnProps but never read by NTableColumnController/Data — the actual plugin class is looked up from `globalThis.NTablePlugins[data.type]`, not from this prop. Do not rely on it. --> |
| `type` | `String` | `'string'` | own | **Selects both the cell renderer (`NTableCells`) and, when `filter` is true, the filter-popover renderer (`NTableFilters`) — the same prop drives both**, resolved via `NTableView.resolve(column.data.type, scope)` (`src/table/js/table/NTableView.ts`). Full enumerated values below. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | own | Column header text. |
| `tooltip` | `String` | `null` | own | Header tooltip (`data-tooltip-inv` attribute). |
| `prop` | `String` | `null` | own | **Row-data key** (dot-path, resolved via pico-js `Obj.get(row, prop)`). Also the fallback for `sortProp`/`filterProp` when those are left `null`. |
| `sort` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | Whether clicking the header sorts by this column. |
| `sortProp` | `String` | `null`, falls back to `prop` | own | The property name reported in the table's `sort`/`update:sortProp` events; only relevant if different from `prop`. |
| `filter` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | Whether this column shows a filter icon/popover. |
| `filterProp` | `String` | `null`, falls back to `prop` | own | The `property` value written into the table's `filter` array entries; falls back to `prop`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean \| Function` | `false` | own | For `select`/`matrix` plugin columns: `Function` form is called as `disabled(item)` per row (`NTableSelectPlugin.disabled`/`NTableMatrixPlugin.disabled`) to disable individual row checkboxes. |
| `visible` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Static per-column visibility flag, checked first in `getVisibility()`. |
| `breakpoint` | `String \| Number` | `null` | own | If set, column auto-hides when the table's rendered width is below this number (`Mix.num(breakpoint) > width`), used only when `NTable`'s `visible` prop is left unset (auto-computed on mount). |
| `align` | `String` | `'left'` | own | Column/cell text alignment — plain string, not validated against a fixed set in source (treat as an open string similar to `type`/`size`, though only `left`/`center`/`right` appear to have matching cell/header CSS classes generated). |
| `width` | `String \| Number` | `null` | own | Flex-basis: `Number` → `${width}px`, `String` → used verbatim (e.g. `'20%'`). Ignored if `fixedWidth` is set. |
| `fixedWidth` | `Number` | `null` | own | Locks the column to a fixed, user-resizable pixel width (drives `n-resizer`'s `disabled`/`modelValue` wiring in `NTableView.column()`). |
| `minWidth` | `Number` | `60` | own | Only applied when `fixedWidth` is not set. |
| `maxWidth` | `Number` | `null` | own | Only applied when `fixedWidth` is not set. |
| `datetimeFormat` | `String` | `'LTSD'` | own | Format token passed to pico-js `Now.make(input).format(datetimeFormat)` in the `datetime` cell renderer. |

**`type` — full enumerated cell-renderer values** (`globalThis.NTableCells`, registered in `src/table/index.ts` from `src/table/js/table-cell/*.ts`; unknown values fall back to `'string'` per `NTableView.resolve()`):

| `type` value | Renderer file | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `'string'` (default) | `NTableCellString.ts` | Renders `Str.string(input)` as plain text. Also the fallback for any unrecognized `type`. |
| `'boolean'` | `NTableCellBoolean.ts` | Renders `trueText`/`falseText` via `Str.boolean(input, trueText, falseText)`. |
| `'datetime'` | `NTableCellDatetime.ts` | Renders `Now.make(input).format(datetimeFormat)`. |
| `'image'` | `NTableCellImage.ts` | Renders an `<n-preview>` for the value at `prop` (and optionally a distinct thumbnail from `data.thumbProp`). |
| `'option'` | `NTableCellOption.ts` | Resolves the row value against `options`/`optionsValue`/`optionsLabel` via `column.getOption(input)`; renders `undefinedText` if no match. |
| `'select'` | `NTableCellSelect.ts` | Renders a checkbox-style cell driven by `NTableSelectPlugin` (single-row selection into `modelValue`). |
| `'matrix'` | `NTableCellMatrix.ts` | Renders a checkbox-style cell driven by `NTableMatrixPlugin` (per-row bitmask toggle into `modelValue`). |

**`type` — full enumerated filter-renderer values** (`globalThis.NTableFilters`, from `src/table/js/table-filter/*.ts`; only consulted when `filter` is `true`; unknown values also fall back to `'string'`):

| `type` value | Renderer file | Filter UI / operators |
|---|---|---|
| `'string'` (default/fallback) | `NTableFilterString.ts` | Text input + operator select: `li` (Includes value, default), `nl` (Excludes value), `eq` (Equal value), `new` (Except value). |
| `'option'` | `NTableFilterOption.ts` | Checkbox group built from `column.getOptions()` (same `options`/`optionsValue`/`optionsLabel` as the cell) + operator select: `in` (Includes value, default), `ni` (Excludes value). |
| `'datetime'` | `NTableFilterDatetime.ts` | `n-datepicker` + operator select: `eq` (Exact date, default), `lt` (Before date), `gt` (After date). |

There is **no separate `filterType` prop** — a column with `type: 'boolean'`/`'image'`/`'select'`/`'matrix'` and `filter: true` will render the `'string'` filter UI (the fallback), which usually doesn't make semantic sense; only pair `filter: true` with `type: 'string'` / `'option'` / `'datetime'` for a matching filter UI.

**Plugins** (`globalThis.NTablePlugins`, from `src/table/js/plugin/*.ts`, keyed by the same `type` prop, instantiated in `NTableColumnController.setup()` when `type` matches a registered key):

| `type` value | Plugin class | `modelValue` shape | `data` config | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `'select'` | `NTableSelectPlugin.ts` | The single selected row object, or `null` | `{ allowUncheck: true }` (default) | Clicking a row's checkbox cell sets `modelValue` to that row (comparing rows via `table.uniqueProp`) or `null` if already selected (when `allowUncheck`); emits `update:modelValue`. Disables all other rows' checkboxes once one is selected. |
| `'matrix'` | `NTableMatrixPlugin.ts` | An array of rows, each carrying a bitmask field (default field name `'matrix'`) | `{ allowUncheck: true, matrix: 0, prop: 'matrix' }` | For multi-column bit-flag matrices (e.g. one `NTableColumn` per permission bit, all sharing the same `modelValue` array): toggling a cell flips bit `config.matrix` for that row's `config.prop` field via pico-js `Num.combine`/`Arr.toggle`, then emits `update:modelValue` with the updated array. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `select`: `(item \| null)`; `matrix`: `(rows: array)` | The column's plugin (`select`/`matrix` type only) toggles a row's checkbox — see "Plugins" above. Plain cell types (`string`/`boolean`/`datetime`/`image`/`option`) never emit this. |

## Slots

None — `NTableColumnView.default()` returns `null`; the component is a pure config/registration node, not something that renders its own markup or slot content.

## Exposed methods

None (`ctx.pass([...])` is never called for this component).

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-table :items="rows" style="height: 300px;">
  <n-table-column prop="name" label="Name" />
</n-table>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<template>
  <n-table :items="rows" style="height: 400px;">
    <n-table-column prop="name" label="Name" sort />
    <n-table-column prop="active" type="boolean" label="Active"
      true-text="Enabled" false-text="Disabled" />
    <n-table-column prop="role" type="option" label="Role" filter
      :options="{ admin: 'Administrator', user: 'Standard user' }" />
    <n-table-column prop="createdAt" type="datetime" label="Created"
      filter datetime-format="LL" />
  </n-table>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const rows = ref([
  { id: 1, name: 'Ada', active: true, role: 'admin', createdAt: '2026-01-04T00:00:00Z' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Grace', active: false, role: 'user', createdAt: '2026-03-11T00:00:00Z' },
]);
</script>
```

## Required composition

Must be a descendant inside an `<n-table>`'s default slot. `NTableColumnController.onMounted()`/`onUnmounted()` calls `this.ncx('table').append(this)`/`.remove(this)`, resolved through `injectRef(['table', 'NTable'])` — this only succeeds inside a component tree where an ancestor `NTable` has run `provide('NTable', this.instance)`.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `type` only affects the cell — it also selects the filter UI when `filter: true`, and (for `'select'`/`'matrix'`) activates a whole plugin. Picking `type: 'image'` with `filter: true`, for instance, silently gets the generic string-filter UI, not something image-aware.
- Passing a `plugin` prop expecting it to configure the select/matrix behavior — it is dead code; configure via `data` instead (see plugin table above).
- Forgetting each row needs a stable, unique value at the table's `uniqueProp` (default `'id'`) for `select`/`matrix` plugin equality checks and for row identity generally (see `table.md`).

## Gotchas

- `sortProp`/`filterProp` both silently fall back to `prop` (via `NTableColumnData`'s getter default arg) — you only need to set them when the sort/filter key genuinely differs from the display `prop`.
- The `align` prop is not validated against an enum in source (unlike, say, `Props.AlignLeft`) — any string is accepted structurally but only known values get matching BEM classes/CSS.

## Related components

- `NTable` — required parent.
- `NPaginator` — used alongside `NTable`, not related to `NTableColumn` directly.

<!-- ===== components/table.md ===== -->

# NTable

A virtualized, sortable, filterable, drag-reorderable data table built on top of `NDraglist` (tree/flat row rendering + virtual scroll) and `NScrollbar`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/table/index.ts` as `NTable` (tag `<n-table>`), alongside `NTableColumn` and `NPaginator`. Source: `src/table/js/table/NTable.ts` / `NTableController.ts` / `NTableData.ts` / `NTableView.ts`.

## Props

`NTable` uses the shared Controller/Data/View pattern (see `ai-docs/concepts.md`). It spreads `Props.Load`, `Props.Size`, `Props.Type` (open strings — see concepts.md), and the entire `Props.Draglist` mixin (`src/root/js/prop/DragProps.ts`), plus its own props declared directly in `NTable.ts`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Loading state, adds `n-load` class. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` | Open string, see concepts.md. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` | Open string, see concepts.md. |
| `items` | `Array` | `[]` | `Props.Draglist` (`DragProps.ts`) | **The row data.** See "Row data shape" below. Not cloned by the controller — read live via `data.items` (`DragData.get items()`). |
| `current` | `Object` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | The "current" (focused/keyboard-navigated) row. <!-- CONFIRMED GOTCHA: NTableView.body()'s `passed` prop-forwarding list (src/table/js/table/NTableView.ts) does NOT include `current` or `selected` — only `expanded`/`cascade` are forwarded into the internal `n-draglist`. So setting `:current`/`:selected` on `<n-table>` does not push a value down into the underlying draglist's selection state; only the `update:current`/`update:selected` events (draglist → table → your v-model) flow outward. Treat these as effectively read-only/output props, not true two-way v-model inputs, until proven otherwise. --> |
| `selected` | `Array` | `[]` | `Props.Draglist` | Selected row uids. Same one-way-out caveat as `current` above. |
| `expanded` | `Array` | `[]` | `Props.Draglist` | Expanded row uids (tree rows). Forwarded into the internal draglist and bindable both ways. |
| `cascade` | `Array` | `[]` | `Props.Draglist` | Ancestor-uid path of the current cascade selection (tree drill-down). Forwarded both ways. |
| `group` | `Array` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | Drag-and-drop group id list (defaults to `[this.uid]` internally). Forwarded. |
| `allowGroups` | `Array` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | Which drag groups may drop into this table. <!-- CONFIRMED BUG: `NTableView.body()`'s `passed` array contains the key `'allowGroup'` (singular, no `s`) — not `'allowGroups'`. Since `NTable` has no such prop, `scope.props['allowGroup']` is always `undefined`, so whatever you pass as `allow-groups` on `<n-table>` is never actually forwarded to the internal `n-draglist`. --> |
| `safezone` | `Number \| Function` | `0.6` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded as-is to the draglist. |
| `allowCurrent` | `Boolean` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `renderHandle` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `renderExpand` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. Needed to show the expand/collapse toggle for tree rows. |
| `renderSelect` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. Needed to show row checkboxes. |
| `allowSelect` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `allowDrag` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `allowDrop` | `Boolean \| Function` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `transformDrop` | `Function` | `null` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `insertNode` | `Boolean` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `removeNode` | `Boolean` | `true` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `uniqueProp` | `String` | `'id'` | `Props.Draglist` | Row key field. See "Row data shape". Forwarded. |
| `childProp` | `String` | `'children'` | `Props.Draglist` | Nested-rows field for tree tables. Forwarded. |
| `itemSkip` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `rootSkip` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Draglist` | Forwarded. |
| `filter` | `Array` | `null` | own (`NTable.ts`) | The **applied** filter state. Array of `{ value, type, property, operator }`. Cloned locally (`cloneProp('filter')`). See "Sort/filter are state-only" below — you own re-filtering `items`. |
| `sortProp` | `String` | `'id'` | own | Currently sorted column's `sortProp`/`prop`. Cloned locally. |
| `sortDir` | `String` | `'desc'` | own | `'asc'` or `'desc'`. Cloned locally. |
| `visible` | `Array` | `null` | own | Array of visible columns' `prop` values (controls which `NTableColumn`s render). If left `null`, is auto-computed on mount from each column's `getVisibility(width)` (breakpoint check against the table's rendered width). Cloned locally. |
| `itemHeight` | `Number` | `32` | own | Row height in px — required for virtual-scroll math (forwarded to `n-draglist`/`n-virtualbar`). |
| `itemOffset` | `Number` | `30` | own | Per-depth indent (px) for tree rows; also forwarded. |

**Row data shape** (`items` prop) — confirmed from `NTableView.cell()` (`Obj.get(node.item, data.prop)`, dot-path lookup) and `DragProps`/`NDraglistController` (`uniqueProp`/`childProp`):

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "label": "Row A",
    "amount": 42,
    "active": true,
    "createdAt": "2026-08-20T10:00:00Z",
    "children": [
      { "id": 2, "label": "Child of Row A", "amount": 7, "active": false, "createdAt": "2026-08-21T09:00:00Z" }
    ]
  },
  { "id": 3, "label": "Row B", "amount": 100, "active": true, "createdAt": "2026-08-19T08:00:00Z" }
]
```

- Every row needs a value at `uniqueProp` (default `'id'`) that is **unique across the entire tree** (including nested `children`), not just among siblings.
- `children` (or whatever `childProp` is set to) is optional per row — omit it for flat tables.
- Each `NTableColumn`'s `prop` is looked up on the row via `Obj.get(row, prop)` (pico-js dot-path getter), so `prop="user.name"` works for nested fields; it is **not** required to be a top-level key.
- No other keys are structurally required — everything else is whatever your columns' `prop`s point at.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:items` | `(items: array)` | The internal draglist reorders/moves/removes rows via drag-and-drop (`NDraglistController.onDragdrop`/`onDragend`). |
| `update:current` | `(node)` | The internal draglist's current-row pointer changes (passthrough from `n-draglist`'s own `update:current`). |
| `update:selected` | `(uids: array)` | Row selection changes (passthrough). |
| `update:expanded` | `(uids: array)` | A tree row is expanded/collapsed (passthrough). |
| `update:cascade` | `(uids: array)` | Drill-down cascade path changes (passthrough). |
| `update:filter` | `(filters: array)` | User clicks "Apply" or "Reset" in a column's filter popover (`applyColumnFilter()`/`resetColumnFilter()`). Payload is the array of **non-empty** `{ value, type, property, operator }` entries. |
| `update:sortProp` | `(prop: string)` | User clicks a sortable column header and the sort column changes. |
| `update:sortDir` | `(dir: 'asc'\|'desc')` | User clicks a sortable column header and the direction changes (toggles asc/desc on repeat clicks of the same column). |
| `update:visible` | `(props: array)` | User toggles column visibility via the built-in right-click context-menu checkbox group. |
| `filter` | — | **Declared in `emits` but never actually emitted anywhere in source** (`grep` of `src/table` finds no `emit('filter', ...)` call). Do not rely on it — use `update:filter`. |
| `sort` | `(prop: string, dir: 'asc'\|'desc')` | Emitted alongside `update:sortProp`/`update:sortDir` from `applySortColumn()`, called whenever a sortable column header is clicked (even if the resulting values are unchanged) — positional args, not an object. |
| `row-click` | `(node)` | A row is clicked (passthrough from `n-draglist`'s `onRowClick`). |
| `row-dblclick` | `(node)` | A row is double-clicked. |
| `node-click` | `(node)` | A tree node (any depth) is clicked. |
| `node-dblclick` | `(node)` | A tree node is double-clicked. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| default | — | `NTableColumn` children go here (required — this is how the table discovers its columns). |
| default (unnamed, passed to `n-scrollbar`) | — | `NTableView.default()` also renders `this.slot()` (unnamed) after the header/context/body — an extra unscoped default slot for arbitrary extra content inside the scrollbar viewport. |

## Exposed methods

None via `ctx.pass([...])` — no `pass()` call exists anywhere in `src/table`. The controller (`NTableController`) does define `toggleSelect()` and `getTotalSelect()` (select-all-rows helpers that delegate to the internal draglist via `this.ncx('draglist')`), reachable only through the internal `ncx()`/template-ref mechanism described in concepts.md, not as a documented public API.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-table :items="rows" style="height: 400px;">
    <n-table-column prop="label" label="Label" />
    <n-table-column prop="amount" type="string" label="Amount" />
  </n-table>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const rows = ref([
  { id: 1, label: 'Row A', amount: '42' },
  { id: 2, label: 'Row B', amount: '100' },
]);
</script>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<template>
  <div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 500px;">
    <n-table
      :items="rows"
      :sort-prop="sortProp"
      :sort-dir="sortDir"
      :filter="filter"
      style="flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0;"
      @sort="onSort"
      @update:filter="onFilter"
    >
      <n-table-column prop="name" label="Name" sort />
      <n-table-column prop="status" type="option" label="Status" filter
        :options="{ 0: 'Draft', 1: 'Published' }" />
      <n-table-column prop="createdAt" type="datetime" label="Created" filter
        datetime-format="LTSD" />
    </n-table>

    <n-paginator
      :page="page"
      :limit="limit"
      :total="total"
      @update:page="page = $event; reload()"
      @update:limit="limit = $event; reload()"
      style="flex: 0 0 auto;"
    />
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const rows = ref([]);
const total = ref(0);
const page = ref(1);
const limit = ref(100);
const sortProp = ref('name');
const sortDir = ref('asc');
const filter = ref(null);

function onSort(prop, dir) {
  sortProp.value = prop;
  sortDir.value = dir;
  reload();
}

function onFilter(value) {
  filter.value = value;
  reload();
}

function reload() {
  // NTable does not filter/sort `items` itself — you must refetch/re-derive
  // rows yourself from sortProp/sortDir/filter/page/limit and reassign `rows`.
}
</script>
```

## Required composition

- `NTableColumn` elements must be direct-or-nested descendants inside `<n-table>`'s default slot — each column's `NTableColumnController.onMounted()` calls `this.ncx('table').append(this)`, resolved via `injectRef(['table', 'NTable'])`, which only finds a provider if it is a descendant of an `NTable` (which calls `provide('NTable', this.instance)`). A column rendered outside an `NTable` will throw/fail to resolve its table.
- **`NPaginator` is not allowed inside `NTable`.** It is a fully separate component with no `inject`/`provide` relationship to `NTable` at all — use it adjacent to (e.g. below) the table, wiring `page`/`limit`/`total` yourself, as in the realistic example above.

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting to give `<n-table>` an explicit height.** `NTable` has **no `height` prop.** Internally it renders `n-scrollbar` → `n-virtualbar`, whose virtual-scroll window is computed from the *actual rendered* `el.clientHeight` (`NVirtualbarController.buildState()`, `src/scrollbar/js/virtualbar/NVirtualbarController.ts`). The scrollbar's inner content (`.n-scrollbar-content`) is `position: absolute; top/left/right/bottom: 0` (`src/scrollbar/css/scrollbar.scss`) — it fills its parent, but contributes **no** height of its own back up the DOM. If `<n-table>` (or a flex/grid ancestor sizing it) doesn't have a real CSS height (inline `style="height: …"`, a fixed-height class, or `flex: 1 1 auto` inside a sized flex column), the table renders at effectively zero height and appears empty/broken. Always set height via CSS/style, never via a prop.
- **Assuming the table filters/sorts `items` itself.** It does not. `sortProp`/`sortDir`/`filter` are purely UI state that `NTable` tracks and reports via `sort`/`update:sortProp`/`update:sortDir`/`update:filter` — there is no code path anywhere in `NTableController`/`NTableView` that reorders or filters the `items` array. Your app must react to those events (client-side re-sort/re-filter, or a server refetch) and pass back an already-sorted/filtered `items` array.
- Expecting `v-model="items"` (plain, unnamed) to work — `NTable` has no `modelValue`/`update:modelValue` pair at all. Bind with `:items`/`@update:items` (or Vue's named-slot v-model sugar `v-model:items="rows"`).
- Expecting `:current`/`:selected` to drive the table's selection from outside — see the confirmed gotcha in the props table above; only `expanded`/`cascade` are genuinely two-way.

## Gotchas

- The `filter` and `paginate`-style "semantic" event some might expect (`filter`) is declared in `emits` but dead code — never fired. Use `update:filter`.
- `allowGroups` is silently broken due to a `'allowGroup'` (singular) typo in the internal prop-forwarding list — see props table.
- `current`/`selected` are not forwarded down into the internal `n-draglist` — only their `update:*` events flow upward. Treat them as effectively read-only for now.
- `demos/table/index.html` in this repo is a stale, pre-rewrite (Vue 2) demo using prop names that do not exist in current source (`viewport-height`, `render-expand`/`render-select` as bare booleans without value binding oddities, `default-width`, `preview-prop`, `close-filter-on-enter`, `sort-on-label`, plain `v-model="items"`). Do not copy attributes from it — none of those extra props exist on the current `NTableProps`/`NTableColumnProps`. `ai-docs/` is written from `src/`, not from this demo.
- <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether NTableColumn's `emptyText`/`undefinedText` props affect anything besides NTableCellOption's `undefinedText` fallback for missing option matches — `emptyText` in particular is not referenced anywhere in src/table's cell/filter renderers. -->

## Related components

- `NTableColumn` — declares each column; must be a descendant.
- `NPaginator` — pairs with `NTable` for page/limit UI, but is never nested inside it.
- `NDraglist` (`src/draggable/js/draglist/`) — the underlying tree/virtual-list engine `NTable` builds on; most of `Props.Draglist` is a direct passthrough to it.
- `NScrollbar` / `NVirtualbar` (`src/scrollbar/js/`) — provide the custom scrollbar and virtual-scroll viewport measurement.


---

<!-- ===== components/tabs-item.md ===== -->

# NTabsItem

A single tab panel + header declared as a child of `NTabs`; identified by its `name` prop, which is matched against `NTabs`' `modelValue`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/tabs/index.ts` as `NTabsItem` (`<n-tabs-item>`), alongside `NTabs`. See `ai-docs/components/tabs.md` — the two are always installed together.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sort` | `[Number, String]` | `null` | own (`NTabsItem.ts`) | Sort key used by `NTabs` to order tabs (`Arr.sort(this.childs, 'data.sort')` in `NTabsController.updateTabs()`). |
| `name` | `String` | `'default'` | own | **The tab key.** Matched 1:1 against `NTabs`' `modelValue`/`update:modelValue` string. This is the prop that identifies which tab an `NTabsItem` represents. |
| `label` | `String` | `null` | own | Text shown in the tab header (rendered as `<span>{{ label }}</span>` by `NTabsItemView.header_label()`). |
| `icon` | `String` | `null` | own (redeclared here, **not** `Props.Icon` from the shared mixin — see Gotchas) | Icon shown in the tab header, rendered via `this.icon(data.icon)` only if non-empty. |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `null` | own | Whether the panel content is wrapped in an `n-scrollbar` component. `null` means "inherit from parent `NTabs`' `scrollbar` prop" (one-time copy at setup, see tabs.md Gotchas). |
| `lazy` | `Boolean` | `null` | own | Whether the panel defers rendering until first activated. `null` inherits from `NTabs`' `lazy` prop the same way. |
| `keep` | `Boolean` | `null` | own | Whether the panel stays mounted after being deactivated once shown. `null` inherits from `NTabs`' `keep` prop the same way. |

`NTabsItem` declares **no props from the shared `Props` mixins** at all (not even `Props.Icon` — its `icon` prop is a plain re-declaration with a different default: `null` here vs `''` for `Props.Icon`).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|

None — `NTabsItem.ts` declares `emits: []`. State changes go through the parent: `NTabsItemController.superOpen()` calls `tabs?.superToggle(name)`, which is what actually triggers `NTabs`' `update:modelValue`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The tab panel's body content. Rendered via `this.slot('default')` in `NTabsItemView.default()`. |

Only one slot exists on `NTabsItem`. There is **no separate "label/header" slot** — the header's icon and label are built entirely from the `icon`/`label` *props* (`NTabsItemView.header()`/`header_icon()`/`header_label()`), not from a slot. <!-- Confirmed by reading NTabsItemView.ts in full: only `this.slot('default')` appears anywhere in the file. -->

## Exposed methods

None. (No `pass(...)`/`ctx` exposure calls in `NTabsItemController`.)

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-tabs v-model="active">
    <n-tabs-item name="default" label="First">
      First panel content
    </n-tabs-item>
  </n-tabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const active = ref('default');
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html`:

```vue
<template>
  <n-tabs v-model="active">
    <n-tabs-item label="Default" icon="fa fa-ghost">
      Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit.
    </n-tabs-item>
    <n-tabs-item name="keep" label="Keep" :keep="true">
      <!-- stays mounted once shown, even after switching away -->
      <n-textarea></n-textarea>
    </n-tabs-item>
    <n-tabs-item name="bar" label="Headline in extra extra extra extra extra extra looooong" :lazy="false">
      <!-- rendered immediately, not deferred until first activation -->
      Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.
    </n-tabs-item>
  </n-tabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const active = ref('default');
</script>
```

## Required composition

`NTabsItem` **cannot exist outside `NTabs`**, by the same strict rule as `NRadio`/`NRadioGroup` and `NCollapse`/`NCollapseItem`. `NTabsItemController.setup()` injects the parent via `this.injectRef(['tabs', 'NTabs'])` and immediately calls `this.ncx('tabs')` without a null check to read `tabs.data.scrollbar`/`.lazy`/`.keep` — using `NTabsItem` without an ancestor `NTabs` throws rather than degrading gracefully. `NTabsItem` also registers itself with the nearest ancestor `NTabs` on mount (`this.ncx('tabs')?.append(this)`) and deregisters on unmount (`.remove(this)`), and separately `provide`s itself as `'NTabsItem'` so nested `NTabsItem`s (inside a nested `NTabs`) can find their nearest `NTabsItem` ancestor via `injectRef(['tabs-item', 'NTabsItem'])` — used by `superOpen()` to recursively open ancestor tabs before opening itself.

## Common mistakes

- Using `NTabsItem` standalone or under the wrong parent — it will throw when it tries to read `ncx('tabs').data.*` during setup.
- Expecting a header/label slot for custom header markup — there isn't one; only `icon` and `label` props control the header, and the only content slot is `default` (the panel body).
- Two sibling `NTabsItem`s sharing the same `name` — `NTabs` matches tabs by `name` string, so duplicates will be ambiguous (`Arr.has(names, value)` just checks membership, and header click handlers all key off `data.name`).
- Relying on `sort` for a stable/obvious visual order without setting it on every item — items with `sort: null` are still included in `Arr.sort(...)`, so mixing `sort` and un-sorted items may not order the way you expect. <!-- UNVERIFIED: exact tie-break/null-handling behavior of pico-js's Arr.sort when some items have sort: null — not traced into pico-js source. -->

## Gotchas

- `icon` here is **not** the shared `Props.Icon` mixin — it's a component-local prop with a different default (`null` vs `''`) and only feeds the tab header icon, not any built-in icon-position/disabled behavior (`Props.IconPositionBefore`/`IconDisabled` are not present on `NTabsItem` at all).
- `isActive()` (which gates whether the panel content renders at all) is not simply "am I the current tab" — it's `true` if `!data.lazy` (always render) OR `data.keep && data.init` (already been shown once and configured to persist), OR if the name matches the parent's current `value`. So a non-active, non-lazy tab's content is still mounted (just hidden via `isVisible()`'s inline `display: none`), while a lazy `keep` tab, once shown, stays mounted forever afterward even off-screen.
- `data.init` is a one-way flag: once a panel's `default()` render runs and `!data.init`, it's set to `true` immediately (`scope.set('init', true)`) — this is what makes `keep` "sticky" from then on.
- `scrollbar`/`lazy`/`keep` inheritance from `NTabs` happens **once**, at `setup()` time (`if (this.data.X === null) this.set('X', tabs.data.X)`) — changing the parent `NTabs`' `scrollbar`/`lazy`/`keep` prop after mount will not retroactively affect already-mounted `NTabsItem`s that inherited `null`.

## Related components

- `NTabs` — the only valid parent; see `ai-docs/components/tabs.md`.
- `NCollapseItem` — same strict-parent-child + `name`-keyed pattern for an accordion-style component.
- `NRadio` — same strict-parent-child composition rule under `NRadioGroup`.


---

<!-- ===== components/tabs.md ===== -->

# NTabs

Tabbed container that switches between `NTabsItem` children by a string key, with an animated active-tab indicator.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/tabs/index.ts` as `NTabs` (`<n-tabs>`), alongside `NTabsItem`. Both are installed together — there is no way to register one without the other via the plugin's `Install()` entry point.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shared loading-state flag; see concepts.md. |
| `size` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `xs, sm, md, lg, xl`. |
| `type` | `String` | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Open string. Known styled values: `primary, secondary, info, warning, danger, success`. |
| `modelValue` | `String` | `'default'` | own (`NTabs.ts`) | The active tab's `name`. Plain `v-model` (see concepts.md v-model conventions — confirmed here directly). |
| `float` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | Adds `n-float` class to root and to each active item's content wrapper (floats the tab header style). |
| `scrollbar` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Default `scrollbar` behavior inherited by child `NTabsItem`s that don't set their own (see `NTabsItemController.setup()` — item's own `scrollbar` prop defaults to `null` and falls back to this value). |
| `lazy` | `Boolean` | `true` | own | Default `lazy` behavior inherited by child items the same way as `scrollbar`. |
| `keep` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | Default `keep` behavior inherited by child items the same way as `scrollbar`. |
| `dragOpen` | `Boolean` | `false` | own | When `true`, dragging something over an inactive tab's header (`dragenter`) switches to that tab — useful for drag-and-drop workflows. |

`NTabs` does **not** spread `Props.Icon`, `Props.Disabled`, `Props.Color`, or `Props.Clearable` — only `Load`, `Size`, `Type` from the shared mixins.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `(value: string)` | A tab header is clicked/pointer-downed (`NTabsController.superToggle(value)` → `this.update('modelValue', value)`), or — if `dragOpen` is true — something is dragged over an inactive tab header. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | Must contain `NTabsItem` children — this is where all tab panels/headers are declared. Rendered via `this.slot('default')` inside the body wrapper (`NTabsView.body()`). |

## Exposed methods

None. (No `pass(...)`/`ctx` exposure calls in `NTabsController`.)

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-tabs v-model="active">
    <n-tabs-item name="default" label="First">
      First panel content
    </n-tabs-item>
    <n-tabs-item name="second" label="Second">
      Second panel content
    </n-tabs-item>
  </n-tabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const active = ref('default');
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html`:

```vue
<template>
  <n-select v-model="tabsSize" :options="sizes" />
  <n-select v-model="tabsType" :options="types" />
  <n-switch v-model="tabsFloat">Float</n-switch>

  <n-tabs v-model="active" :size="tabsSize" :type="tabsType" :float="tabsFloat">
    <n-tabs-item label="Default" icon="fa fa-ghost">
      Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit.
    </n-tabs-item>
    <n-tabs-item name="keep" label="Keep" :keep="true">
      <n-textarea></n-textarea>
    </n-tabs-item>
    <n-tabs-item name="bar" label="Headline in extra extra extra extra extra extra looooong" :lazy="false">
      Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.
    </n-tabs-item>
  </n-tabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';

const active = ref('default');
const tabsSize = ref('md');
const tabsType = ref('primary');
const tabsFloat = ref(false);

const sizes = { xs: 'XS', sm: 'SM', md: 'MD', lg: 'LG' };
const types = { primary: 'Primary', secondary: 'Secondary', success: 'Success', warning: 'Warning', danger: 'Danger', info: 'Info' };
</script>
```

Note the first `<n-tabs-item>` above omits `name` entirely — it relies on the default `name: 'default'` (from `NTabsItemProps`) matching `NTabs`' default `modelValue: 'default'`, so it's active on initial render with no explicit wiring.

## Required composition

`NTabsItem` **cannot exist outside `NTabs`** — same strict parent/child requirement as `NRadio`/`NRadioGroup` and `NCollapse`/`NCollapseItem`. Mechanically, `NTabsItemController.setup()` calls `this.injectRef(['tabs', 'NTabs'])` and then unconditionally dereferences it (`const tabs = this.ncx('tabs')`, immediately followed by `tabs.data.scrollbar`/`tabs.data.lazy`/`tabs.data.keep` reads) with no null-guard — an `NTabsItem` rendered without an ancestor `NTabs` will throw. Nesting also works: an `NTabsItem`'s content can contain another full `NTabs`/`NTabsItem` tree (see `demos/overview.html`'s `tabs1`/`tabs2` nested example).

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting that `modelValue` must match a child `NTabsItem`'s `name` exactly (string equality via `Arr.has(names, value)`); if it doesn't match any current child name, `NTabsController.updateTabs()` silently falls back to the first sorted child's name instead of throwing.
- Rendering `NTabsItem` outside of `NTabs` — it depends on injected `tabs`/`ncx('tabs')` context and has no standalone fallback.
- Assuming the header row renders when there's only one tab: `NTabsView.header()` returns `null` when `scope.childs.length < 2`, so a single-tab `NTabs` shows no clickable header at all (content still renders via the body slot).

## Gotchas

- The active-tab indicator (`updateIndicator()`) only runs/matters once there are 2+ children (same `childs.length < 2` guard as the header) and is recalculated on a `ResizeObserver` (debounced 50ms) plus after every `updateTabs()` call (`Run.frame`).
- `scrollbar`/`lazy`/`keep` set on `NTabs` are **defaults only** — each `NTabsItem` has its own same-named prop (default `null`) that, if left unset, is filled in once from the parent's value during the item's `setup()` (one-time copy, not a live link) via plain `if (this.data.X === null) this.set('X', tabs.data.X)`.
- `lazy` (per-item, effectively) controls whether the panel is mounted/rendered before it's first activated; `keep` (once activated) keeps the panel mounted/rendered even after switching away. See `NTabsItemController.isActive()`: renders if `!data.lazy || (data.keep && data.init)`, or if the tab is the current active tab.
- <!-- UNVERIFIED: `demos/overview.html`'s first `<n-tabs>` example passes a `:relative="false"` attribute, but no `relative` prop exists anywhere in `NTabsProps`. It is not consumed by NTabs and, since NTabs' root `div` doesn't spread `context.attrs`, likely has no effect at all — probably stale/dead markup in the demo rather than a real prop. -->
- `demos/tabs/index.html` is a legacy Vue 2 demo (loads `vue@2.5.13`) using a `preload` prop on `NTabsItem` that does not exist in the current source — do not treat it as representative of the current API; `demos/overview.html` and `demos/tabs.html` (Vue 3) are the reliable references.

## Related components

- `NTabsItem` — the only valid child; see `ai-docs/components/tabs-item.md`.
- `NCollapse`/`NCollapseItem` — same strict-parent-child pattern, same `GroupController`-based approach for a different (accordion-style) UI.
- `NRadio`/`NRadioGroup` — same strict-parent-child composition rule.

<!-- ===== components/tag.md ===== -->

# NTag

A small inline label/chip with an optional icon, styled by `type`/`color`/`size`.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/visuals/index.ts` as `NTag` (`App.component(NTag.name, NTag)`). Source: `src/visuals/js/tag/{NTag,NTagController,NTagData,NTagView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Size modifier, see concepts.md "Type and Size are open strings". |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known built-ins: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Styles the tag via `n-type-{type}`. The `demos/overview.html` overview demo also iterates `type` over `['neutral', 'primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info']` — **`neutral` is not one of the confirmed built-in styled values listed in concepts.md**. `NTag` itself has no code that special-cases `'neutral'` (unlike `NProgress`, which does map `state === 0` to a hardcoded `'neutral'` type internally — see `progress.md`). Treat `type="neutral"` on `NTag` as an arbitrary open-string value used in the demo, not a confirmed built-in with guaranteed CSS — <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether an `n-type-neutral` CSS rule exists anywhere in the stylesheet source; not checked here since CSS files are out of scope for this pass. --> |
| `color` | `[String, Number]` | `null` | `Props.Color` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Resolved through `Styler.wheel()` into `n-color-{$color}` (see `ProtoData.classRoot()` in concepts.md). Demo uses numeric values (`:color="index+40"`). |
| `icon` | `String` | `''` | `Props.Icon` (`IconProps.ts`) | Icon rendered via `ProtoView.icon()`. Only rendered if truthy (`NTagView` checks `data.iconPosition`, and `ProtoView.icon()` itself no-ops on falsy input). |
| `iconPosition` | `String`, validated in `['before','after']` | `'before'` | `Props.IconPositionBefore` (`IconProps.ts`) | Whether the icon renders before or after the default-slot content. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | `NTag.ts` declares `emits: []`. There is no interactive/emitting behavior anywhere in `NTagController`/`NTagView` — `NTag` is purely a display component. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | none | The tag's label content, wrapped in a `<span>` inside the root `<div class="n-tag">`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NTagController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-tag type="primary">New</n-tag>
</template>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/overview.html` — iterating tag `type`, and iterating numeric `color`:

```vue
<template>
  <template v-for="type in ['neutral', 'primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info']">
    <n-tag v-bind="n_tags" :type="type" icon="fa fa-ghost">Foo askd kasjdbnjka sjdkna</n-tag>
  </template>

  <template v-for="(value, index) in Array(30).fill(0)">
    <n-tag v-bind="n_tags" :color="index+40" icon="fa fa-ghost">Foo askd kasjdbnjka sjdkna</n-tag>
  </template>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const n_tags = reactive({ size: 'md' });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None — independent, standalone component.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `type="neutral"` to be a documented built-in styled value: it is used in the demo but is not among concepts.md's confirmed built-in `type` values (`primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) and `NTagData`/`NTagView` apply no special handling for it — it's just an open-string value passed through to `n-type-neutral`.
- Expecting `icon` alone to control position: `iconPosition` (`'before'`/`'after'`) determines where the icon renders relative to the slot content; the default is `'before'`.
- Expecting an emitted event on click/interaction: `NTag` has no click handlers and an empty `emits` array — it's non-interactive.

## Gotchas

- `color` accepts either a `String` or `Number`; numeric values are resolved through `Styler.wheel()` (see concepts.md `classRoot()`), which is how the demo generates 30 distinct color variants from `index+40`.
- The default-slot content is always wrapped in an inner `<span>` (`NTagView.default()`), separate from the icon element — useful to know if you're targeting the label text with CSS.

## Related components

None — NTag has no composition relationship with NRating, NMessage, or NProgress; documented independently per task scope.

<!-- ===== components/textarea.md ===== -->

# NTextarea

A multi-line text input bound via `v-model`, with optional row auto-growing; reach for this over `NInput` whenever the value is expected to span multiple lines (no icon-button, no inline label, and no `clearable`/`clear` support — this is a leaner component than `NInput`).

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/input/index.ts` as `NTextarea` (`App.component(NTextarea.name, NTextarea)`). Source: `src/input/js/textarea/{NTextarea,NTextareaController,NTextareaData,NTextareaView}.ts`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Adds the `n-load` loading class. |
| `size` | `String` (open string; known: `xs`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | See concepts.md. |
| `type` | `String` (open string; known: `primary`/`secondary`/`info`/`warning`/`danger`/`success`) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Same open-string rule. Note: this is also (harmlessly) passed straight through as the native `<textarea>`'s `type` attribute — see Gotchas. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Subject to `superDisabled` (concepts.md). |
| `modelValue` | `[String, Number]` | `''` | `NTextarea.ts` (own prop) | v-model value. Cloned locally via `cloneProp('modelValue')`. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `''` | `NTextarea.ts` (own prop) | Native placeholder text. |
| `autoRows` | `Boolean` | `false` | `NTextarea.ts` (own prop) | When `true`, the rendered `rows` attribute grows (up to `maxRows`) based on the number of newline characters currently in `modelValue`; recomputed on every render, so it also shrinks back down as lines are removed. |
| `minRows` | `Number` | `3` | `NTextarea.ts` (own prop) | Baseline `rows` attribute value, used regardless of `autoRows`. |
| `maxRows` | `Number` | `6` | `NTextarea.ts` (own prop) | Ceiling for the `autoRows` growth; ignored when `autoRows` is `false`. |
| `maxLength` | `Number` | `null` | `NTextarea.ts` (own prop) | Only applied as the native `maxLength` attribute when truthy (`if (data.maxLength) { props.maxLength = ... }`) — `null`/`0` mean no native character limit is set at all. |

Note: unlike `NInput`/`NInputNumber`, `NTextarea` does **not** mix in `Props.Clearable`/`Props.ClearValue`/`Props.Icon` — there is no icon, clear button, or `clearValue` support on this component at all.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | new `string` value (`e.target.value`) | Native `input` event on the `<textarea>` (`scope.update('modelValue', e.target.value)`). |
| `input` | native `Event` | Alongside `update:modelValue`, on every native input event. |
| `keydown` | native `KeyboardEvent` | Native `keydown` on the `<textarea>`. |
| `keyup` | native `KeyboardEvent` | Native `keyup` on the `<textarea>`. |
| `focus` | native `FocusEvent` | Native `focus` (sets internal focus state for the `n-focus` class). |
| `blur` | native `FocusEvent` | Native `blur` (clears the focus state). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| none | — | `NTextareaView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. |

## Exposed methods

None. `NTextareaController` never calls `this.pass([...])`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<template>
  <n-textarea v-model="value" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
const value = ref('');
</script>
```

## Realistic example

Adapted from `demos/form/index.html` (inside `NFormItem`) and `demos/overview.html` (`auto-rows` + `min-rows` variant):

```vue
<template>
  <n-form :form="form">
    <n-form-item label="Description" tooltip="Multi-line notes">
      <n-textarea v-model="form.notes" :auto-rows="true" :min-rows="1" :max-rows="8" />
    </n-form-item>

    <n-form-item prop="name" label="Bio">
      <n-textarea v-model="form.bio" :max-length="280" type="primary" placeholder="Tell us about yourself" />
    </n-form-item>
  </n-form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue';
const form = reactive({ notes: '', bio: '' });
</script>
```

## Required composition

None required — standalone. Optional: can be placed inside `NButtonGroup` (confirmed composition pairing).

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a `clearable`/`clear` button like `NInput`/`NInputNumber` have: `NTextarea` doesn't mix in `Props.Clearable` at all — there is no built-in clear control on this component.
- Setting `maxLength="0"` expecting an explicit zero-character limit: the prop is only applied when truthy (`if (data.maxLength)`), so `0` (and `null`) both mean "no native `maxLength` attribute set," not "zero allowed characters."
- Setting `autoRows` without also considering `maxRows`: growth is capped at `maxRows` (default `6`) — a long pasted block of text will not keep expanding the textarea past that, it'll start scrolling internally instead.

## Gotchas

- The native `<textarea>` element receives `type: data.type` as an attribute (the visual `type` prop, e.g. `'primary'`) — `<textarea>` has no `type` attribute in HTML, so browsers ignore it; this is a harmless no-op inherited from the same render pattern used elsewhere in this codebase, not a way to change the rendered element type.
- `autoRows`'s row count is recalculated fresh on every render directly from `modelValue`'s newline count (`(Mix.str(data.model).match(/\n/g) || []).length + 1`) — it is not driven by the actual rendered pixel height of wrapped (non-newline) long lines, only by explicit `\n` characters.
- `iconDisabled`/`icon`/`clearable`-style props from other input variants are simply absent from this component's prop set (`inheritAttrs: false`, so they don't exist here at all — passing them lands in `$attrs` and gets spread directly onto the inner `<textarea>` element via `Obj.except(scope.attrs, exclude, {...})`, i.e. as a raw, likely-invalid HTML attribute, not applied as a styled feature).

## Related components

`NInput` (single-line variant with icon-button/label/clear support), `NInputNumber` (numeric variant), `NInputFile` (file selection variant), `NFormItem` (form-layout wrapper providing labels/validation/`superDisabled` context).

<!-- ===== components/timepicker-panel.md ===== -->

# NTimepickerPanel

The hour/minute/second scroll-grid selector. It is used internally as
`NTimepicker`'s popover content (rendered directly by
`NTimepickerView.panel()`, not via a slot), but it is also registered
globally as its own component and rendered inline/standalone in
`demos/overview.html` (`<n-timepicker-panel v-bind="...">`) with no popover
involved — confirmed dual-purpose, not popover-only internal markup.

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/datetime/index.ts`:
`App.component('NTimepickerPanel', NTimepickerPanel)`. Source:
`src/datetime/js/timepicker-panel/NTimepickerPanel.ts`.
`NTimepickerPanelController` extends `GroupController`
(`src/root/js/controller/GroupController.ts` — see concepts.md), though
this component doesn't itself call `append`/`remove`/`watchChilds`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Loading state (`n-load` class). |
| `size` | `String` (open string) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Known defaults: `xs, sm, md, lg, xl`. |
| `type` | `String` (open string) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Known defaults: `primary, secondary, info, warning, danger, success`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Disables the component (`superDisabled`). |
| `modelValue` | `String` | `null` | own declaration | The bound value — a full date+time string formatted per `format`. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Select time'` | own declaration | Shown in the header when no value is set. |
| `format` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | own declaration | Format `modelValue` is stored/parsed in. |
| `displayFormat` | `String` | `'HH:mm:ss'` | own declaration | Controls the header display **and** which grid columns render: `hours()`/`minutes()`/`seconds()` each bail out (`return null`) unless `displayFormat` matches `/HH/`, `/mm/`, `/ss/` respectively. |
| `hoursInterval` | `Number` | `1` | own declaration | Step between hour-grid entries (`getHoursGrid(hoursInterval)`). |
| `minutesInterval` | `Number` | `1` | own declaration | Step between minute-grid entries. |
| `secondsInterval` | `Number` | `1` | own declaration | Step between second-grid entries. |

Unlike `NTimepicker`, this component has **no** `clearable`, `clearValue`,
or `position` props — those are popover/clear-button concerns owned
exclusively by `NTimepicker`.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `string` (formatted per `format`) | User clicks/pointerdowns an hour, minute, or second cell (`onMousedown(item)` → `this.update('modelValue', item.format(data.format))`). |

## Slots

None — `NTimepickerPanelView` never calls `this.slot(...)`.

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()`/`context.expose` calls in `NTimepickerPanelController`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-timepicker-panel v-model="time"></n-timepicker-panel>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<!-- demos/overview.html — used standalone, no popover -->
<n-timepicker-panel
  size="md"
  type="primary"
  v-model="form.time"
></n-timepicker-panel>
```

## Required composition

None. It does not require `NTimepicker` as a wrapper — it renders and
functions fully on its own, as shown above. Optional: `NButtonGroup` can
wrap it like any other control via its generic `default` slot.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a clear (×) button — not present on this component; only
  `NTimepicker` has `clearable`/`clearValue`.
- Passing a `displayFormat` that omits `HH`, `mm`, or `ss` silently drops
  that entire column from the grid (no warning).
- Confusing this component's `modelValue` (a formatted date+time
  **string**) with `NDurationpicker`'s (a plain **integer number of
  seconds**) — unrelated shapes despite sharing `src/datetime/`.

## Gotchas

- Each of the hours/minutes/seconds columns renders via `n-scrollbar` (not
  `n-virtualbar`) and auto-scrolls to the current value on mount via
  `ncx.scrollCenter(...)`, but only when `data.date.input` is truthy (i.e.
  a real value has been provided) — with no value yet, nothing is
  auto-centered.
- Uses `GroupController` as its base, but no child-registration behavior
  (`append`/`remove`/`watchChilds`) is exercised anywhere in this
  component's own Controller/View code.
  <!-- UNVERIFIED: whether GroupController's child-tracking is consumed
  by a parent/sibling elsewhere in the datetime group for this specific
  component, or is simply inherited unused. -->

## Related components

- `NTimepicker` — wraps this component as its popover content and adds the
  text-input + clear-button UX.
- `NDurationpicker` — different `modelValue` shape (seconds, not a date
  string).

<!-- ===== components/timepicker.md ===== -->

# NTimepicker

A text-input-plus-popover time picker: the input shows/edits a formatted
time string, and the popover's content is an internal `NTimepickerPanel`
scroll-grid. `NTimepicker` is the standalone, form-facing component; see
`ai-docs/components/timepicker-panel.md` for the grid it embeds (which is
also independently usable).

## Import / Registration

Registered globally by `src/datetime/index.ts`:
`App.component('NTimepicker', NTimepicker)`. Source:
`src/datetime/js/timepicker/NTimepicker.ts`. Controller
(`NTimepickerController`) extends `NPopoverPanelController`
(`src/popover/js/popover-panel/NPopoverPanelController.ts`), so it inherits
the `focus` state, `onFocus`/`onBlur`, and the `el`/`popover` refs described
there.

## Props

`NTimepickerProps` spreads `Props.Clearable`, `Props.ClearValue`,
`Props.PositionBottomStart`, then **all of `NTimepickerPanelProps`**
(`src/datetime/js/timepicker-panel/NTimepickerPanel.ts`), then overrides
`icon` locally.

| Prop | Type | Default | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clearable` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Clearable` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Shows the built-in × clear button once a value is set. |
| `clearValue` | `[String, Number, Boolean]` | `null` | `Props.ClearValue` (`BaseProps.ts`) | Value `modelValue` is reset to by `applyClear()`. |
| `position` | `String` (popover position enum) | `'bottom-start'` | `Props.PositionBottomStart` (`PositionProps.ts`) | Popover placement — full 12-value set in `ai-docs/concepts.md`. |
| `load` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Load` (`BaseProps.ts`), via `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Loading state (`n-load` class). |
| `size` | `String` (open string) | `null` | `Props.Size` (`BaseProps.ts`), via `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Known defaults: `xs, sm, md, lg, xl`. |
| `type` | `String` (open string) | `null` | `Props.Type` (`BaseProps.ts`), via `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Known defaults: `primary, secondary, info, warning, danger, success`. |
| `disabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | `Props.Disabled` (`BaseProps.ts`), via `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Disables the input and popover trigger. |
| `modelValue` | `String` | `null` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` (own declaration) | The bound value — a **full date+time string** formatted per `format`, not a bare time string. See Gotchas. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | `'Select time'` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Shown in the text input when empty. |
| `format` | `String` | `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Format `modelValue` is stored/parsed in (`Now.format`/`Now.make(value, format)`). |
| `displayFormat` | `String` | `'HH:mm:ss'` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Format shown/edited in the text input and panel header; independent of `format`. |
| `hoursInterval` | `Number` | `1` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Step between hour-grid entries in the panel. |
| `minutesInterval` | `Number` | `1` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Step between minute-grid entries. |
| `secondsInterval` | `Number` | `1` | `NTimepickerPanelProps` | Step between second-grid entries. |
| `icon` | `String` | `Styler.icon('clock')` | `NTimepicker`'s own declaration (`NTimepicker.ts`) — **not** the shared `Props.Icon` mixin | Leading icon in the display handle. No matching `iconPosition`/`iconDisabled` props exist on this component. |

All props above except `icon` are forwarded verbatim to the internal
`<n-timepicker-panel>` via `ProtoController.passProps(props, Mix.keys(NTimepickerPanelProps))`
(`NTimepickerView.panel()`).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Fired when |
|---|---|---|
| `update:modelValue` | `string` (formatted per `format`), or `clearValue` | (1) user types a time in the input and presses Enter — `onEnter()` parses `data.input` with `Now.make(input, displayFormat)` and, if valid, calls `this.update('modelValue', date.format(data.format))`; (2) user picks an hour/minute/second cell in the embedded panel — the panel's own `update:modelValue` is caught in `NTimepickerView.panel()` (`onUpdate:modelValue`) and re-emitted via `scope.update('modelValue', value)`; (3) the built-in clear (×) button is pressed (`applyClear()`, inherited). |

## Slots

None — `NTimepickerView` never calls `this.slot(...)`. Its `panel()` override
replaces `NPopoverPanelView`'s default slot-based panel rendering
(`this.slot('panel')`) with a hard-coded `<n-timepicker-panel>`, so there is
no user-facing `panel` slot on this component either.

## Exposed methods

None — no `pass()` or `context.expose` calls in `NTimepickerController`.

## Minimal example

```vue
<n-timepicker v-model="time"></n-timepicker>
```

## Realistic example

```vue
<!-- adapted from demos/timepicker/index.html and demos/overview.html -->
<n-form :form="form">
  <n-form-item label="Meeting time">
    <n-timepicker
      v-model="form.time"
      size="md"
      type="primary"
      minutes-interval="30"
      :clearable="true"
    ></n-timepicker>
  </n-form-item>

  <n-form-item label="Disabled">
    <n-timepicker v-model="form.time" :disabled="true"></n-timepicker>
  </n-form-item>
</n-form>
```

## Required composition

None required to work standalone. Optional: `NButtonGroup`
(`src/button/js/button-group/NButtonGroupView.ts`, a plain `div` rendering
`this.slot('default')`) can wrap an `NTimepicker` alongside other controls —
this is generic slot content, not a required or NTimepicker-specific pairing.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming `modelValue` is a bare time string (e.g. `'14:30:00'`). By
  default it is a **full date+time string** in `format`
  (`'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'`), e.g. `'2026-08-25 14:30:00'` — the date part
  defaults to today's date until a real date is supplied. `displayFormat`
  only controls what's shown/typed in the text field, not what's stored.
- Confusing this with `NDurationpicker`'s `modelValue`: that one is a plain
  **integer number of seconds**, not a formatted string at all — the two
  components have unrelated `modelValue` shapes despite both living under
  `src/datetime/`.
- Expecting `iconPosition`/`iconDisabled` to work on `NTimepicker`'s `icon` —
  it's a plain local prop override, not the shared `Props.Icon` mixin, so
  those companion props don't exist here.

## Gotchas

- `hoursInterval`/`minutesInterval`/`secondsInterval` only change the
  panel's scroll-grid step; they do not validate or round a typed value in
  the text input.
- Typing an unparseable string and pressing Enter silently reverts the
  input to the last valid `modelValue` display (`updateDates()`), with no
  emitted error/event.
- `displayFormat` also implicitly controls which grid columns the embedded
  panel renders (see `ai-docs/components/timepicker-panel.md`) since it's
  forwarded straight through.

## Related components

- `NTimepickerPanel` — the grid UI rendered inside this component's
  popover; also independently usable.
- `NDurationpicker` — a sibling `src/datetime/` component for relative
  durations (seconds), not absolute times.
- `NDatetimepicker`, `NDatepicker` — other `src/datetime/` pickers (not
  covered in this doc batch).
